# GenesisCA — Project Context for Claude Code

## Repository Context

This repository (https://github.com/rff255/GenesisCA) originally contained a Qt/C++ desktop application built in 2017 as an undergrad final project (Universidade Federal de Pernambuco). The `legacy_qt_cpp_solution` branch preserves that legacy code — a qmake project with `src/modeler` and `src/simulator` subdirectories, DearImGui-based node editor, and C++ code generation for model export.

**The current work is a complete rewrite.** `master` is the main branch and ships releases. Active development happens on feature branches off `master`. The `legacy_qt_cpp_solution` branch is frozen as historical reference — do not modify.

The old implementation in `legacy_qt_cpp_solution` serves as architectural reference. Key file for understanding the old compilation approach: `src/modeler/UpdateRulesHandler/node_graph_instance.h` — each node had an `Eval()` method that emitted C++ code snippets, stitched together into `.h`/`.cpp` files, then compiled to `.dll`/`.exe`. The new version follows the same pattern but targets JavaScript instead of C++.

---

## Commands

- `npm run dev` — Start Vite dev server (http://localhost:5173)
- `npm run build` — TypeScript check + production build to `dist/`
- `npm run preview` — Preview production build locally

---

## What GenesisCA Is

GenesisCA is an IDE for modeling and simulating Cellular Automata (CA). It uses a Visual Programming Language (VPL) — a node-based graph editor — so users can design arbitrarily complex CA models without writing code. The goals are **accessibility** (no programming required) and **performance** (grids up to 5000×5000+).

---

## The GenesisCA Model Definition

### Six Fundamentals

Every GenesisCA model satisfies these theoretical properties:

1. Cells have unlimited computing power
2. Cells have N internal attributes (of multiple data types), whose snapshot of values at a given generation is called its "state"
3. Cells are limited to only access (read) the states of cells in one of the neighborhoods defined in the CA model
4. **Writability** — In synchronous (classic) mode, cells can only modify their own attributes. In asynchronous mode, cells can also directly modify the attributes of neighboring cells, enabling movement and mass-conservation rules.
5. Space and Time are discrete (cells arranged in n-dimensional grid)
6. **Synchronicity** — The model can be either synchronous (all cells update simultaneously each generation — classic CA) or asynchronous (cells update sequentially using a single buffer, enabling number-conserving models where elements move across the grid without being created or destroyed). Async supports three update schemes: Random Order (Fisher-Yates), Random Independent (with replacement), Cyclic (fixed order from init).

### Simulation Essentials (Color Mappings)

Beyond the six fundamentals, two types of mappings enable visualization and interaction:

1. **Attribute-Color Mappings** — N ways to map cell state → colors (for visualization)
2. **Color-Attribute Mappings** — N ways to map colors → cell state (for user interaction and image-based initialization)

### Model Structure

A complete GenesisCA model definition consists of:

1. **Model Properties**
   - 1.1. Presentation (Name, Rule Author, GenesisCA Project Author, **Summary**, **Rule Description**, **Creation date**, Thumbnail, Tags...). `properties.createdDate?` (optional ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`) is the AUTHORED creation date behind the Models Library card stamp + its Newest/Oldest sort — see the "Model creation date" section. `properties.description` is the short **Summary** (UI label; the *only* presentation text shown on Models Library cards — internal id unchanged). `properties.ruleDescription?` (optional, additive — old files load without it) is the long-form **Rule Description** for elaborating at length on how the rule works; not shown on cards.
   - 1.2. Structure (Topology, Boundary Treatment, Grid Size...)
   - 1.3. Execution
     - 1.3.1. Initial Configuration (Attribute Initialization Mapping, Default Attribute Values)
     - 1.3.2. End Conditions (optional max generations + indicator rules with category support for linked-frequency) + in-graph Stop Event nodes

2. **Attributes** — each has a name, type (bool, integer, float, tag, color), description, and type-specific properties (integer range, tag options...)
   - 2.1. Cell Attributes (per-cell state)
   - 2.2. Model Attributes (global read-only parameters that all cells can access but not write; can be changed during simulation externally)

3. **Neighborhoods** — a list of neighborhoods, each being a list of N indexes relative to the central cell, a name, a description, and optionally tags for specific indexes (for easy reference in Update Rules)

4. **Color Mappings** — each mapping has a Name, Description, per-channel descriptions (R, G, B)
   - 4.1. Color-Attribute Mappings (input: for initialization and real-time interaction)
   - 4.2. Attribute-Color Mappings (output: for visualization modes)

5. **Update Rules** — a node graph defining what each cell computes per generation. The graph handles multiple event types:
   - Each Attribute Initialization Mapping event
   - New generation (the main update step)
   - Each Color-to-Attribute interaction event
   - When/how to update each Attribute-to-Color mapping

6. **Overseer (optional)** — a THIRD graph defining experiment orchestration AROUND the simulation: how executions are prepared, repeated, measured, and aggregated (replicate statistics, parameter sweeps, run-until-stop protocols, capture). Gated by `overseerConfig.enabled`; completely invisible when off. See the "Overseer (Experiment Orchestration)" major section.

## Architecture Decisions (Settled)

### Tech Stack

- **TypeScript + React** — the entire application
- **Vite** — build tool (replaces qmake)
- **React Flow** — node-based graph editor library (replaces DearImGui node editor)
- **Canvas2D** — grid rendering (initial target)
- **WebGPU** — future upgrade path for 5000×5000+ grids
- **Web Workers** — simulation engine runs off the main thread
- **GitHub Pages** — free static hosting, no server required

The app is **100% client-side**. No backend, no server, no paid hosting.

### Two Application Modes

- **Modeler** — UI for designing CA models (properties, attributes, neighborhoods, mappings, update rules graph). All editing panels are React components.
- **Simulator** — Runs and visualizes models. Grid rendering via Canvas, simulation loop in a Web Worker.

Both modes coexist in one app. The user can seamlessly switch between editing and simulating.

### Graph → Compile Strategy

This is the critical performance decision. At 5000×5000 (25M cells), the update function runs 25M times per generation.

**Approach: Compile the node graph at edit time to one of three ENGINES.** Chosen per model by the **Engine** radio in Properties → Execution — `Auto` (the default for new models) / WebAssembly / WebGPU, with **Debug (JS)** behind an Advanced reveal. See the "One Engine selector" section for the enum, the Auto policy and `resolveEngines`.

- **WebAssembly.** Hand-emitted WASM module, typically several times faster than JS on dense neighborhoods. Production engine for most models; exact + seedable (f64, one shared stream), bit-identical to the JS reference.
- **WebGPU.** WGSL compute shaders dispatched on the GPU. Best for very large grids and math-heavy per-cell work. Requires synchronous mode + a browser with WebGPU support.
- **Debug / Reference (JS).** Plain JavaScript via `new Function(...)`. The **semantic reference** the other two are verified against, the always-runnable fallback, and the source **Show Code always displays** (whatever engine runs) — but the slowest, so it is demoted behind Advanced rather than offered as a peer.

Each node type defines `compile()` (JS) plus per-target emitters (WASM / WGSL). The JS compiler:
1. Topologically sorts the graph
2. Resolves connections (output of node A → input of node B)
3. Stitches snippets into a flat function body with intermediate variables
4. Creates an executable function via `new Function(...)`

Example — the JS compile of a Game of Life graph emits a loop-wrapped step function (called ONCE per step, not per cell):
```js
(function(total, r_alive, w_alive, nIdx_moore, nSz_moore, modelAttrs, colors, activeViewer) {
  const _scr_n1 = new Array(nSz_moore); // scratch array (reused per cell)
  for (let idx = 0; idx < total; idx++) {
    const colorIdx = idx * 4;
    w_alive[idx] = r_alive[idx]; // copy prev state
    const _nb = idx * nSz_moore;
    for (let _n = 0; _n < nSz_moore; _n++) _scr_n1[_n] = r_alive[nIdx_moore[_nb + _n]];
    let _count = 0;
    for (let _n = 0; _n < _scr_n1.length; _n++) if (_scr_n1[_n] === 1) _count++;
    const _alive = (_count === 3 || (r_alive[idx] && _count === 2)) ? 1 : 0;
    w_alive[idx] = _alive;
    if (activeViewer === "default-viz") {
      colors[colorIdx] = _alive ? 76 : 13; colors[colorIdx+1] = _alive ? 201 : 27;
      colors[colorIdx+2] = _alive ? 240 : 43; colors[colorIdx+3] = 255;
    }
  }
})
```

This mirrors how the old Genesis worked — each node's `Eval()` produced C++ code, stitched into `.h`/`.cpp`, compiled by gcc into `.dll`/`.exe`. The only difference: the target language is JS instead of C++, and compilation is instant (no external toolchain). Grid uses Structure of Arrays (typed arrays per attribute) for cache-friendly access.

**Why not interpret the graph at runtime:** At 25M cells, even ~2μs overhead per cell = ~50 seconds per generation. Compiled JS with JIT optimization targets ~10-50ns per cell = ~0.25-1.25s per generation.

A "debug/step mode" that interprets the graph slowly with visual feedback (highlighting active nodes, showing intermediate values) is planned for when users are designing — then switch to compiled mode for simulation runs.

### Model File Format

Models are saved as `.gcaproj` files with a versioned schema. The JSON contains:
- Schema version (for future migration)
- All model properties, attributes, neighborhoods, color mappings
- The full node graph (nodes, connections, positions) as serialized React Flow state
- The compiled JS function string (optional, can be recompiled from graph)
- Optional `simulationState` — embedded simulation snapshot (included when user saves state in the simulator before saving the project)

Users can save/load these files locally (browser download/upload). No cloud storage.

### Simulation State Files (.gcastate)

Standalone simulation snapshots saved from the simulator transport bar. JSON containing:
- Generation, grid dimensions, all cell attribute arrays (base64-encoded typed arrays)
- Model attribute values, indicator state (standalone + linked accumulators), color buffer
- Simulator UI settings (activeViewer, brush, FPS, gens/frame)

Serialization: `fileOperations.ts` — `serializeSimState()`, `readStateFile()`, `arrayBufferToBase64()` / `base64ToArrayBuffer()`, `deserializeTypedArray()`

Worker messages: `getState` (worker copies and transfers all typed arrays), `loadState` (worker restores arrays and rebuilds neighbor indices). Dimension validation in `applySimulationState()` rejects mismatched state files.

Auto-save to localStorage strips `simulationState` to avoid exceeding quota on large grids.

### Presentation Export (standalone `.html` — SHIPPED)

File ▾ → **Export standalone simulation…** bundles the Simulator + one model into a **single self-contained `.html`** that runs in any browser — no install, no server, offline from a bare `file://`. The web rewrite's replacement for legacy Genesis's `.exe` export. Docs: [docs/IMPACT_MAP_PRESENTATION_EXPORT.md](docs/IMPACT_MAP_PRESENTATION_EXPORT.md) / [PLAN_PRESENTATION_EXPORT.md](docs/PLAN_PRESENTATION_EXPORT.md) (+ `.html` mockup).

- **Why it needs no binary assets:** WASM bytes + WGSL are generated in-JS from the model graph at load (works under `file://`); the `.gcaproj` IS the graph (recompiled at load). So embedding the model JSON alone runs the sim. Sprites (`SpriteAsset.dataUrl`/frames), thumbnail, presets, and the initial board (`simulationState`) are all already base64 inside the `CAModel`, so **one file carries everything — no folder**.
- **The build-time viewer template + runtime injection design.** A SECOND Vite build (`vite build --mode viewer`, the `mode==='viewer'` branch in [vite.config.ts](vite.config.ts)) produces `viewer-template.html` — a fully-inlined single file (`vite-plugin-singlefile`) mounting ONLY `<SimulatorView>` under a viewer `ModelProvider` ([src/viewer/{index=viewer.html at repo root, main.tsx, ViewerApp.tsx}](src/viewer/main.tsx)), NO PWA/library plugins. The template reads its model from the `<script id="genesis-model" type="application/json">` placeholder. `build:viewer` copies it to `public/viewer-template.html` (served at `/viewer-template.html` in dev, copied into `dist/` by the main build → PWA-precached for offline). `npm run build` runs `build:viewer` first.
- **The worker seam (the single blocker, solved).** The sim worker is code-split (`new Worker(new URL('./engine/sim.worker.ts', import.meta.url))` → its own chunk), which a single-file inliner won't fold in. Extracted into [createSimWorker.ts](src/simulator/createSimWorker.ts) (main app: `new URL`) + [createSimWorker.inline.ts](src/simulator/createSimWorker.inline.ts) (viewer: `import W from './engine/sim.worker?worker&inline'` → base64 Blob worker). The viewer build swaps them via a `resolve.alias` (`/^\.\/createSimWorker$/`; anchor BOTH ends — a partial regex mangles the leading `./` into the absolute path). Verified: the inlined worker boots + instantiates WASM from in-memory bytes + steps under a single-file HTML.
- **Export flow** ([src/export/exportPresentation.ts](src/export/exportPresentation.ts) + [FileMenu.tsx](src/components/FileMenu.tsx) `doExport` + [ExportPresentationDialog.tsx](src/components/ExportPresentationDialog.tsx)): capture live state via the existing `genesis-capture-sim-state` event (same seam as Save; `include: {grid, controls}`) → `serializeModel(modelWithState)` → `fetchViewerTemplate()` (`${BASE_URL}viewer-template.html`) → `assemblePresentationHtml` injects the escaped JSON → `downloadHTML`. **Injection gotcha:** the placeholder sentinel `__GENESIS_MODEL_JSON__` appears TWICE in the built file (the `<script>` placeholder AND the bundled `EMBEDDED_MODEL_PLACEHOLDER` JS constant), so a bare string-replace hits the wrong one — target the `<script id="genesis-model">` element with a regex. Escape `<`→`<` (+ U+2028/9) so a `</script>`/`<!--` inside a string value can't break the tag. **Share previews:** `assemblePresentationHtml` also personalizes the `<title>`, injects og:/twitter: meta from the model's name/summary (+ the thumbnail as a data-URL og:image when ≤300 KB — most scrapers ignore data URLs, so hosted shares reliably show title+description only), and prepends a **human-readable HTML comment banner** right after the doctype (name / wrapped summary / authors / "open in a browser" / genesisca.online). The banner exists because messengers never OG-scrape file ATTACHMENTS — Discord/Slack preview an attachment's FIRST LINES as raw text (WhatsApp shows nothing for .html documents; unfixable), so those first lines must read as a title card, not minified code. Comment-safety: `commentSafe` replaces `--` runs with an en dash (a `-->` in a model name would terminate the banner). Verified incl. hostile names + the extractEmbeddedModel round-trip. Presets + the whole graph + sprites + metadata are ALWAYS embedded; grid/controls are the only opt-outs (grid defaults OFF past 250k cells — a big base64 board dominates the file).
- **R1 — dual artifact (recoverable model source).** The `.html` embeds the COMPLETE `CAModel`, so the logic is never lost. The viewer's About panel has "⤓ Download model (.gcaproj)"; the IDE's Load accepts a presentation `.html` — `extractEmbeddedModel(html)` + the shared `parseModelJSON(text)` (the `readModelFile` body was refactored to expose both, [fileOperations.ts](src/model/fileOperations.ts)); `readModelFile` auto-detects HTML (extension / `<!doctype` / the `genesis-model` marker) and extracts first. FileMenu Load `accept` = `.gcaproj,.json,.html,.htm`. Verified round-trip: export → re-import → editable model recovered.
- **R2 — metadata display.** [ViewerApp.tsx](src/viewer/ViewerApp.tsx)'s About/Info panel (ⓘ, auto-open on first load) shows Title (`name`), Rule author (`author`), Project author (`modelAuthor`), Summary (`description`), Rule description (`ruleDescription`), Tags, Thumbnail — a lean read-only render (NOT coupled to the editing `InfoPanelContent`).
- **DEV helpers** (not shipped): [scripts/inject-test-model.mjs](scripts/inject-test-model.mjs) (inject a `.gcaproj` into the template for manual testing) + [scripts/static-serve.mjs](scripts/static-serve.mjs) (serve the single file — the Browser pane can't open `file://`, so verify over http; the runtime is identical). `dist-viewer/` + `public/viewer-template.html` are gitignored build artifacts.
- **WebGPU under `file://`** may not init (secure-context gating) — the worker falls back to JS/WASM automatically, so an exported WebGPU model runs on WASM; no COOP/COEP needed (non-shared `WebAssembly.Memory`).

## Development Guidelines

- Language: TypeScript (strict mode)
- All new code and documentation in English
- **Type-name display convention:** the UI never shows the raw type ids `bool` / `float` — they render as **Binary** / **Decimal** (general-public vocabulary). Route every user-visible type name through `typeDisplayName()` in [typeLabels.ts](src/model/typeLabels.ts) (badges, dropdowns showing `name (type)`, hints); `<option value>` keeps the internal id, only the option TEXT uses the display name. Prose in HelpView/README/NODES_REFERENCE says binary/decimal too (NODES_REFERENCE's port-type table maps id → UI name). Internal ids in schema/configs/compilers/`.gcaproj` are NEVER renamed.
- The original undergrad thesis (in Portuguese) exists as reference material but is not part of the codebase
- Prefer modular, readable code. Each node type is its own file. The compiler is separate from the editor.
- Do not assume file structure beyond what's documented here — ask if uncertain
- When building new node types, follow the established pattern of existing nodes (compile method, port definitions, UI component)
- `NodeTypeDef` includes optional `description` (one-line summary of what the node does). Include it in new node definitions for Add Node menu tooltips.
- **AN ENABLED CONTROL MUST DO SOMETHING — hide it when it structurally cannot, grey it when it temporarily cannot (user rule, 2026-08-05).** A control that is visible AND interactable but internally inert is the single most confusing thing the UI can do (the user's report: *"if the option doesn't work for certain targets because of theoretical reasons then it should be hidden… many other options are left visible and interactable when in reality they are internally disabled"*). Two dispositions, and the test is **can the user reach the working state from this panel?**
  - **STRUCTURALLY impossible for the current model / dimension / render path ⇒ HIDE.** The user cannot flip it from here, so a greyed row is just clutter that raises "why is this here?". Examples now enforced: gridlines with no CA grid or in 3D · infinity canvas in 3D · agent Glow / Background / Metaballs(2D) / Vision in 3D · agent Glue/Cut/Bond with `resolveMaxBonds === 0` · Outlines while Metaballs replaces the bodies · Draw-agents-in-front / Cell gaps / Occlusion on an agents-only model · smooth scaling under the E2 composite.
  - **TEMPORARILY unavailable, or one setting away in an adjacent control ⇒ DISABLE IN PLACE with the reason in the tooltip.** Examples: capture settings while recording (locked for the run) · infinity canvas on a non-torus boundary (Boundary is right there in the Settings panel) · the WebM-only Quality / overload rows under GIF (a format choice away) · the Overseer's Run button mid-experiment · the WebGPU stop-check interval on a non-WebGPU model.
  - **A hidden control needs its STATE handled too, not just its markup**: coerce a stranded selection when the model changes (the agent brush falls back to `add`; the CSV `none` delimiter falls back to `auto`), and drop it from any keyboard / wheel CYCLE (Alt+wheel steps `agentBrushModesRef.current`, never the full `AGENT_BRUSH_MODES`). A cycle that lands on a hidden mode is the same bug wearing a different hat.
  - **Do NOT hide on a state the user just set in the same panel** (Show-agents off, a colour mapping not selected) — the causal link is visible, and hiding half a panel per checkbox is worse than the disease.
- **Illustrated plans (HTML mockups) — required for UI / behavior changes:** Whenever a plan involves a non-trivial UI change OR any change in behavior, produce a self-contained HTML representation of the plan (inline CSS + inline SVG, no external assets) saved alongside the plan `.md` file, IN ADDITION to the written markdown plan. Use visual mockups to illustrate the proposal — before/after states, interaction gestures/sequences, and data-/control-flow diagrams — so the user can SEE the change, not just read it. **Exempt (trivial):** renames, color tweaks, minor repositioning, copy edits, and pure-internal refactors with no observable behavior change.
- **2D AND 3D dual impact (mandatory for EVERY change now that both grid kinds ship):** the engine is "incremental 3D" — 2D is the byte-identical fast path and 3D adds the layer axis (`total = W*H*D`, the `_layer` decode, `coords3d`, the 10-bit NI codec). Most code is shared, so a single edit usually touches both, and it's easy to fix/extend one dimension while silently regressing the other (real examples: the dimension-reset drop-guard checked only W/H → 3D-only loop; the soft-recompile `dimsModel` carried only W/H → stale WebGPU `total` after a 3D depth-resize). Before finishing ANY change ask: does it run in a 3D model? a 2D model? Are the grid-dim / `total` / per-cell-coordinate assumptions right for each? **Verify both** (the dev harness + a 3D sample like Life3D AND a 2D sample). This composes with compiler-lockstep — a change must be correct across the **3-target (JS/WASM/WebGPU) × 2-dimension (2D/3D)** matrix.
- **ALL-TARGET DELIVERY (non-negotiable — never ship a JS-only / single-target feature):** every feature MUST run on **all three compile targets (JS / WASM / WebGPU)**, on both the cell grid AND (where applicable) the agent loop, across 2D and 3D. The targets exist for performance (WASM/WebGPU are several-x faster on dense work) — shipping a feature on JS alone, or "clamping to JS when X is used", silently throws that performance away for any model that touches the feature, and is a **regression, not an acceptable shortcut**. "It's harder to emit on WASM/WebGPU", "the value type isn't native there", or "I'll do the other targets later" are **NOT** valid reasons to clamp. The ONLY acceptable single-target restriction is a **fundamental incompatibility** — a property the target's execution model genuinely cannot express — and the bar is the documented set: **async update mode + the async-only neighbour-write nodes on WebGPU** (WebGPU runs cells in parallel; a write visible to a later cell this step is inherently serial), and **order-dependent indicator ops** (`updateIndicator` toggle/next/previous on WebGPU; non-commutative mutation of one shared accumulator by parallel writers). f32-vs-f64 precision and per-cell-PCG-vs-shared-RNG are *documented intentional differences*, not reasons to clamp. When a target lacks NATIVE support for a value/operation, the correct move is one of: **(a) lower it to primitives the targets already compile** — a shared pre-compile graph transform that rewrites the feature into existing nodes BEFORE per-target compile, exactly like [macroExpand.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/macroExpand.ts) (macros → flat nodes), [rerouteCollapse.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/rerouteCollapse.ts) (reroutes → direct edges), [linkedOutputMappings.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/linkedOutputMappings.ts) (linked OM → real colour-pass nodes), and **[expandComposites.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/expandComposites.ts)** (vector/color → scalar nodes); or **(b) emit it natively in each target's compiler** (the WASM encoder + the WGSL builder). Both keep all targets in lockstep with one source of truth. **Before declaring a feature done, prove it compiles + runs on JS, WASM, AND WebGPU** (the dev harness `compileAll` + a real worker run / parity check) — a green tsc + a JS-only check is NOT done. If you ever feel tempted to add a node type to a `JS_ONLY` set or a `detect*Incompatibilities` clamp, STOP: that is the partial-delivery anti-pattern this rule exists to prevent — lower it or emit it instead.
- **Documentation consistency (keep ALL sources of truth in sync — do this after every feature change, not as an afterthought):** A change isn't done until every layer that describes it is updated, because future context-gathering relies on them agreeing. Update: (1) the **code itself** — structure + the comments/docstrings near what you changed; (2) **this `CLAUDE.md`** — extend/add the relevant feature section AND the Project Structure tree when files are added/moved; (3) `src/help/HelpView.tsx` (in-app Help tab); (4) the root `README.md` (whose `## Features` section is DELIBERATELY high-level — short product-page groups with screenshot placeholders, no per-node/per-target inventories; a new feature belongs there only if it changes one of those one-to-three-sentence summaries, and its detail goes in HelpView/`docs/` instead); (5) for node-system changes (new nodes, port types, redundancies) also `docs/NODES_REFERENCE.md` (table + node count + Mermaid diagrams). Drift between any of these silently degrades every later change, so treat them as one atomic update.
- **Pre-commit type check:** Vite dev server does NOT type-check — always run `npx tsc -b` before committing to catch TypeScript errors that will fail the CI build. Note: `npx tsc --noEmit` (without `-b`) silently checks nothing because the root tsconfig has `"files": []` and only project references. If `tsc -b` itself errors with a phantom `Cannot read file '.../nodes/tsconfig.json'` (a transient incremental-build / file-lock glitch — seen right after parallel workflow agents touch the tree), just retry it, or run `npx tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit`, which reliably type-checks the app project (the `--noEmit`-checks-nothing caveat above applies only to the ROOT tsconfig, not the app one).
- **Debugging blank-screen React crashes:** When the app whites out (React unmounts on uncaught error), console usually only shows generic "error in `<X>` component" warnings without stack traces. Install a `window.onerror` handler via preview_eval BEFORE reproducing, then read captured errors after — this surfaces the real stack trace.
- **Dismissing a user bug report requires concrete contradicting evidence**, not a plausible-sounding alternative narrative. Byte-level "the data round-trips correctly" is necessary but not sufficient — when the user is certain something is wrong, step the simulation end-to-end and inspect observable behavior (e.g., post-load `getState` + per-step NI histograms). Plausible-sounding stories ("the saved data already has bias, the simulation just preserves it") cost iterations when the actual bug is one indirection away from where you're looking.
- **Version display:** When bumping version, update ALL FOUR places: `package.json`, `package-lock.json` (root + first `packages.""` entry), the hardcoded version string in `src/App.tsx` header (`v1.X.Y`), and the badge in `README.md` (`<sup>v1.X.Y</sup>`). Easy to miss; sweep with `grep -rn "v1\.[0-9]"` after bumping. The **`/updateversion`** slash command ([.claude/commands/updateversion.md](.claude/commands/updateversion.md)) automates this: pass an explicit `X.Y.Z` or `major`/`minor`/`patch` and it updates all four files.
- **PR descriptions:** Never include "Built with Claude Code" or similar Claude/Anthropic attribution lines. User handles all attribution decisions.

---

## Performance Targets

- Target grid size: up to 5000×5000 (25 million cells)
- Target generation time: under 2 seconds for typical rules at max grid size
- The UI must never freeze during simulation (Web Worker isolation)
- Grid rendering must maintain interactive frame rates for pan/zoom at large sizes

---

## What NOT to Do

- No server-side computation. Everything runs in the browser.
- No paid hosting dependencies. GitHub Pages or equivalent free static hosting.
- No external compilation toolchains. The graph compiles to WASM (default), WebGPU, or JS inside the browser instantly — all three compilers are hand-rolled in TypeScript.
- Do not modify the `legacy_qt_cpp_solution` branch. It is frozen as historical reference.
- All new work goes on feature branches off `master` (e.g., `ux_improvements`).

## Current Implementation Status

The app is functional with these major systems:

### State Management
- `src/model/ModelContext.tsx` — React Context + useReducer holding entire CAModel
- `src/model/defaultModel.ts` — `EMPTY_MODEL` seeds the app on every load; `src/model/archetypes.ts` (C7/P6) builds the File→New archetype seeds on top of it (`buildArchetypeModel('empty')` returns `EMPTY_MODEL` itself)
- `src/model/fileOperations.ts` — Save (.gcaproj) / Load / Download utilities
- No model auto-save / auto-restore across reloads — stripping partial state (`simulationState` / `presets` were too big for the ~5 MB localStorage quota) led to misleading restore-then-silently-lose-preset/grid flows. Explicit `.gcaproj` save only.
- `beforeunload` warning (ModelContext) fires when `state.isDirty` is true so accidental close/reload prompts the user. `isDirty` is reset by `NEW_MODEL`, `LOAD_MODEL`, and `MARK_SAVED` (FileMenu's Save handler calls `markSaved()` after a successful download).
- Default tab is always `library` (every tab/reload) — no first-launch flag. A one-shot cleanup in `ModelProvider` removes stale `genesisca_autosave` and `genesisca_has_launched` keys left over from older builds.
- **`ModelState.loadedFileName`** (display-only, NEVER serialized — it lives on `ModelState`, not `CAModel`): the source file name shown in the top bar in parentheses after the project name. Set by `LOAD_MODEL` (the file/library file name), updated by `MARK_SAVED` to the downloaded filename, cleared (`null`) by `NEW_MODEL`. `loadModel(model, fileName?)` / `markSaved(fileName?)` carry it; it's threaded through the context value + both `useMemo` dep arrays. Helps disambiguate multiple files of the same project.
- **Loading lands on the Simulator + a confirmation toast** (App.tsx `afterLoad`): both load paths (FileMenu's `onLoaded` callback and a Library card) switch the top-level tab to `simulator` and show a 3.5 s auto-dismiss toast (`pointer-events: none`; the timer ref is cleared on unmount and on re-fire). The unsaved-changes confirm path (`pendingLibLoad`) also routes through `afterLoad`.

### Visual Programming Language (VPL)
- `src/modeler/vpl/GraphEditor.tsx` — React Flow-based node graph editor
- `src/modeler/vpl/CaNode.tsx` — Custom node component with per-type config UI
- `src/modeler/vpl/nodes/` — 154 node types (151 selectable from the Add Node menu + 3 hidden macro boundary nodes), each in its own file with `compile()` method. Canonical list: `ALL_NODES` in [registry.ts](src/modeler/vpl/nodes/registry.ts). Async-only nodes (6): SetNeighborhoodAttribute, SetNeighborAttributeByIndex, MarkCellUpdated, SetFacingOrientation, SetNeighborOrientationByIndex, MoveSelfToNeighbor. Includes `StopEventNode` (flow input only, text widget for stop message — compiles to `if (_stopFlag[0] === 0) _stopFlag[0] = <1-based idx>;` first-match-wins; WASM emitter mirrors this via `i32.store` at `layout.stopFlagOffset`).
- Five "event" entry-point nodes: GenerationStep (per-gen logic), InitEvent (runs once PER CELL on simulator Reset — see Variegated Cells section), **GridInit** (runs ONCE GLOBALLY on Reset — free-form procedural seeding; see the "Grid Init Event" section), InputMapping C→A (brush), OutputMapping A→C (color pass)
- `src/modeler/vpl/compiler/compile.ts` — Two-pass compiler: hoists values, then emits flow
- Multi-output nodes (InputColor, GetColorConstant, MacroNode, ColorScale, FilterNeighbors, JoinNeighbors, GetFacingLabels, BreakDownNeighborIndex, InitEvent, GetCellPosition, GroupOperator with position output) use `_v${nodeId}_${portId}` naming
- **Get Cell Position** ([GetCellPositionNode.ts](src/modeler/vpl/nodes/GetCellPositionNode.ts)): a value node (data) that outputs the current cell's `row`/`col` (+ `layer` in 3D, hidden via `hiddenPorts` in 2D) — a controlled, OWN-cell-only break of locality so a cell can behave by position (spatial gradients, region rules, coordinate-aware Output Mappings). Works in every event: the compiler already decodes per-cell `_row`/`_col`/`_layer` (JS), `rowLocalIdx`/`colLocalIdx`/`layerLocalIdx` (WASM, reused zero-copy), and `idx`-derived coords (WebGPU: `idx%W`, `(idx%WH)/W` or `idx/W`, `idx/WH`); the node just exposes them. Registered in `MULTI_OUTPUT_TYPES` AND **`NEVER_INVARIANT`** ([loopInvariant.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/loopInvariant.ts)) — it has no value inputs, so without the latter loop-invariance hoists it to the function preamble ABOVE the per-cell coordinate decode (`_row is not defined`). 2D/3D + 3-target verified (JS runtime row/col/layer 0 mismatches; WASM/WebGPU compile clean with the right per-dim formulas).
- Switch node: flow control with dynamic case ports, compiler emits if/else-if chain
- Aggregate node: accepts multiple connections on one isArray input port, operations: Sum/Product/Max/Min/Average/Median
- ProportionMap, Interpolation, ColorScale, ValueSwitch: math/color/select utility nodes (ColorScale replaced the legacy `colorInterpolation` node)
- GetNeighborAttributeByTag: resolves neighborhood cell tags to indices at compile time
- Multi-root support: Step (per-generation), InitEvent (per-cell init on Reset), InputColor (brush interaction), and OutputMapping (color pass) compile separately
- OutputMapping functions: loop-wrapped, always sequential (no shuffle), no copy lines; run once after all generation steps complete; skipped in unlimited gens mode via `skipColorPass` flag
- Paint with OutputMapping: prefers `runColorPass()` over `runStep()` so painting doesn't advance the simulation
- Right side panel: tabbed via `src/modeler/RightActivityBar.tsx`, two tabs — Explorer (existing) and Palette (`src/modeler/panels/PalettePanelContent.tsx`). Drag-drop from Palette to canvas via custom MIME `application/genesisca-palette`; payloads: `{kind: 'node'}`, `{kind: 'macro-default', file}`, `{kind: 'macro-project', macroDefId}`. Floating chevron tab on the graph area's right edge reopens the last-active panel.
- **Spacebar quick-add**: Space (ModelerView capture-phase keydown) opens the **unified in-canvas add-node menu at the cursor** — the SAME `pane`-target context menu a blank-canvas right-click shows (see "Unified add-node menu" below) — via `quickAddApi.openQuickAddMenu()`. It no longer opens the Palette. GraphEditor positions the menu from the cursor's last canvas screen position (`lastClientMousePos`, fallback wrapper-centre), freezes the drop flow position, and the menu's focus effect focuses the search. `quickAddApi` lives in [graphState.ts](src/modeler/vpl/graphState.ts) (GraphEditor registers `{getCursorFlowPos, addFromPalette, openQuickAddMenu}` on mount — `addFromPalette` = `spawnPalettePayload`). The Palette panel still has its own keyboard quick-add when opened manually (its `onQuickAdd` → `quickAddApi.addFromPalette` at the live cursor pos), just no longer Space-triggered.
- **Unified add-node menu** (`pane` context-menu target): blank-canvas **right-click** AND **Spacebar** open one menu — the action options (Paste [if clipboard] / Add Comment / Add Group / Import Macro…) on top, an `<hr>`, then a **focused search field** + the **category-grouped, keyboard-navigable node list**. This is the SAME search/keyboard machinery as the connection-drop menu (`dropMenuSearch` / `dropMenuSelIdx` / `dropSearchRef`, the re-anchor-on-filter effect, ↑/↓-wrap + Enter + Esc, the flat category-headered rows), extracted into one `renderQuickAddSearch(placeholder, emptyText)` helper used by BOTH the `pane` and `connection-drop` branches. `dropMenuItems` builds per target: pane = every node `isNodeAvailable` to the model (minus `HIDDEN_FROM_DROP_MENU` + placed Step/Init singletons), no Reroute, no port-compatibility filter; connection-drop = compatible nodes + Reroute (unchanged). `commitDropMenuItem` for a pane item → `addNodeAtPosition` (no wiring). The old `Add Node ›` hover-submenu (and its `categories`/`addNode` helpers) is removed. The node-list region is wrapped in a `.dropList` (`max-height` + `overflow-y`) so the pinned options + search stay visible while the full catalogue scrolls.
- `addNodeAtPosition(nodeType, position, configOverrides?, label?)` in GraphEditor is the shared node-creation helper used by BOTH context menu Add Node AND palette drop. New flows that create nodes should call it (gets the Step-singleton check + pushSnapshot for free). Pass `label` for macro instances so the user-facing name appears above the "Macro" header.
- **`addNodeAndConnect` adds the node even when no compatible port exists under the DEFAULT config**: a node can be offered as compatible because SOME configuration exposes a matching port (e.g. Get Random's `Options`/`probability` inputs only exist in options/bool mode) while `def.defaultConfig` hides it. Rather than silently doing nothing when the user clicks such a node in the connection-drop menu, `addNodeAndConnect` now drops the node UNWIRED (returns its id, builds no edge) and lets the user configure it. The single-connection-replace gate and snapshot/sync still fire only on the wired path.
- `addNodeAndConnect` (recommended-nodes / connection-drop + single-option panel-drop) builds its edge DIRECTLY (bypassing `isValidConnection`), so it must self-enforce the single-connection limit: when the drag origin is a value, non-array INPUT (`origin.kind==='input' && category==='value' && !origin.isArray`) it FILTERS any existing edge into that same target handle out of the list passed to `addEdge` — i.e. the new node REPLACES the prior wire. Without this, dragging a new link off an already-connected single-input and picking a recommended node silently left the input double-connected. (Direct drops on a port are already rejected by `isValidConnection`; panel-drag never snaps to an occupied input because `computeCompatibleHandlesForDrag` excludes occupied handles — so this gate only bites the connection-drop-from-input path.)

### Simulation Engine (SoA Architecture)
- `src/simulator/engine/sim.worker.ts` — Web Worker owns grid as Structure of Arrays
- Grid storage: one typed array per attribute (`Uint8Array` bool, `Int32Array` int/tag, `Float64Array` float), double-buffered (sync) or single-buffer (async)
- Tag attributes: `Int32Array`, value = index into `tagOptions` string array
- Model attribute bounds: optional `hasBounds`, `min`, `max` fields on `Attribute` type (integer/float model attrs only). When both min & max set, simulator shows range slider alongside spinbox. Values clamped at UI level, no worker enforcement.
- Color model attributes: stored as 3 entries (`attrId_r`, `attrId_g`, `attrId_b`) in cachedModelAttrs
- Neighbor access: pre-computed `Int32Array` index tables (built at init, handles torus/constant boundary once)
- Step function is LOOP-WRAPPED: `(total, r_<attrs>..., w_<attrs>..., nIdx_<nbrs>..., nSz_<nbrs>..., modelAttrs, colors, activeViewer[, order])` — contains the for-loop, called ONCE per step
- Async mode: `order` param is an Int32Array of shuffled/random cell indices; loop uses `idx = order[_i]` instead of `idx = _i`; r_ and w_ params point to same typed arrays (single buffer); copy lines are skipped; buffer swap is skipped after step
- Async schemes: `random-order` (Fisher-Yates shuffle per step), `random-independent` (N random picks with replacement), `cyclic` (one-time shuffle at init)
- InputColor functions remain per-cell: `(_r, _g, _b, idx, r_<attrs>..., ...)`
- **Get Random — EVERY parameter is an input PORT with an inline widget** ([GetRandomNode.ts](src/modeler/vpl/nodes/GetRandomNode.ts)), so a rule can drive the interval / the distribution parameters / the vector reference from a wire (a model attribute, an expression, a neighbour read) instead of a fixed number. Modes: `bool` (`P` port) · `integer` (`Min`/`Max`) · `float` ("Decimal") · `orientation` · `options` (`Options`/`Fallback`) · **`vector`**. `hiddenPorts` gates every port on the mode AND the distribution — the whole matrix lives once on the def.
  - **`distribution` config (DECIMAL only)** — `uniform` (absent/default ⇒ `min + u·(max−min)`, byte-identical to the historical emit) · **`normal`** (`Mean`/`Std Dev`, Box-Muller `mean + sd·(sqrt(−2·ln(1−u1))·cos(2π·u2))`) · **`exponential`** (`Mean`, inverse-CDF `mean·(−ln(1−u))`). Integer stays uniform-only (a discrete Gaussian is a separate feature) and `randomDistribution()` enforces that.
  - **THE DRAW-COUNT CONTRACT — every distribution is FIXED-COUNT, never a rejection loop**: normal = **2** stream advances, everything else = **1** (`randomDrawCount`, exported and asserted by the harness). That is what keeps the shared xorshift32 (JS/WASM) and the per-cell/per-agent PCG (WebGPU) advancing in lockstep. **`1 − u` (not `u`) is the log argument on every target** — `u ∈ [0,1)` so `1−u ∈ (0,1]` and `ln` can never see 0; exponential takes a MEAN rather than a rate so there is no divide, hence no ÷0 guard to keep in step across six emitters (Mean 0 degenerates to exactly 0).
  - **`vector` mode is MULTI-OUTPUT** — `X` / `Y` plus a composite `Vector` port. ONE draw picks an angular offset uniform in ±`Span°`/2, applied as a screen-clockwise ROTATION of the reference unit vector; `Norm` scales it. **Compass convention: 0° = north = −y, 90° = east = +x** (the sprite `atan2(dx, −dy)` heading convention), so a reference unit is `(sin θ, −cos θ)`. The reference is a compass `Angle°` OR (config `refSource: 'vector'`) a wired `Dir X`/`Dir Y`; a ZERO wired direction falls back to north via a single select over an eps-guarded normalise (`1/max(len, 1e-30)` ⇒ `0·1e30 = 0`, never NaN). **ROTATING rather than adding to a computed reference ANGLE is load-bearing: it needs only sin/cos of the OFFSET, so the wired-direction path needs no `atan2` — which the cell WASM module does not import** (and adding an import would shift every module's func indices). Planar (XY) even in a 3D model; a spherical mode is a follow-up. Registered in `isMultiOutput` (config-conditional, like `getModelAttribute`'s `isColorAttr`) + the Overseer's `refFor`; the JS emit also aliases `_v<id>_value` to X so a stale edge from a previous mode can't ReferenceError.
  - **The composite `Vector` output costs NO extra draw**: `expandComposites`' `vecComponentsOf` lowers it to plain wires back to THIS node's `x`/`y` ports (never to synthesized arithmetic), so both components resolve through the one multi-output emit.
  - **BYTE-IDENTITY is preserved by folding at compile time when the range is UNWIRED.** All five compiled surfaces keep the historical constant-fold (`f64Const(max − min)` / the baked WGSL literal) when neither `min` nor `max` is wired, and only take a runtime-span path when one is — so all 29 shipped models are byte-identical on every surface. Wiredness is read from `inputToSource` (WebGPU/agents) or `isInline()` (cell WASM), never from the presence of `inputs[...]`, because an unwired inline port still arrives as a constant ValueRef.
  - **Migration** [getRandomRangeMigration.ts](src/model/getRandomRangeMigration.ts) (LOAD_MODEL + `macroImport` + `migrateForHarness`) re-keys legacy `config.min`/`config.max` onto `_port_min`/`_port_max` across the cell / agent / overseer graphs + every macroDef, value-for-value and idempotent. Without it the UI would show the port default while the compiler used the legacy value.
  - **⚠ PRE-EXISTING (not introduced here, deliberately out of scope): a CELL graph holding SEVERAL RNG nodes where at least one has a WIRED value input assigns the draws in a different ORDER on JS (flow order) than on WASM (sink-analysis topo order)** — reproducible today on the untouched bool + wired-`probability` path, so it is not specific to the new ports. The AGENT compilers are immune (RNG nodes are flow-ordered via the volatile seeding). Fixing it would move the emit order of essentially every existing model, so `scripts/test-get-random.mjs` isolates ONE Get Random per model instead.
  - **Gates**: [scripts/test-get-random.mjs](scripts/test-get-random.mjs) (node def + hiddenPorts matrix + draw counts + the migration + CELL JS-vs-REAL-WASM values and bit-parity for every mode + the compass convention + the WGSL emit + an Overseer driver run) and the permanent `[synthetic] Get Random …` entry in [scripts/parity-agent-wasm.mjs](scripts/parity-agent-wasm.mjs), whose VALUE invariant is stream-INDEPENDENT (σ=0 ⇒ exactly the mean; span 0 ⇒ an exact direction; |v| = Norm) so a mutation applied identically to BOTH targets — which parity cannot see — is still caught.
- **Mode-dependent dead ports are hidden DECLARATIVELY via `NodeTypeDef.hiddenPorts?(config) => string[]`** ([types.ts](src/modeler/vpl/types.ts)): each node def returns the ids of STATIC ports that carry no meaning under the current config, and BOTH CaNode's render path AND [effectivePorts.ts](src/modeler/vpl/effectivePorts.ts) `getEffectivePorts` apply the SAME hook as a final filter — so the rule lives **once on the node def** and can't drift between the two (this replaced the parallel inline `if`-block filters that previously had to be hand-kept-in-sync). Current `hiddenPorts` users: `getModelAttribute` (R/G/B vs Value by `isColorAttr`), `logicOperator` (hide B for NOT), `updateAttribute` + `updateIndicator` (hide Value for the unary `toggle`/`next`/`previous` ops), `getRandom` (the full mode x distribution matrix: probability only for bool, options+fallback only for options mode, Min/Max only for integer + uniform decimal, Mean/StdDev only for the normal/exponential decimal distributions, the vector block + the X/Y/Vector OUTPUTS only for vector mode -- which in turn hides the scalar `value` output, and swaps Angle for Dir X/Y by `refSource`), `statement` + `groupCounting` (hide the upper bound unless a between-family op), `groupOperator` (hide `Position`/`index` unless `max`/`min`/`random`/`weightedRandom` — those are the only ops that pick a real index; the rest emit a constant `-1`, the op set is `GROUP_OPERATOR_POSITION_OPS` in [GroupOperatorNode.ts](src/modeler/vpl/nodes/GroupOperatorNode.ts)), `arithmeticOperator` (Math — hide Y for the unary ops, the set `ARITHMETIC_UNARY_OPS` in [ArithmeticOperatorNode.ts](src/modeler/vpl/nodes/ArithmeticOperatorNode.ts): `sqrt`/`abs`/`negate`/`floor`/`ceil`/`round` + the transcendentals). Hiding is **UI-only** (inputs AND outputs): the compilers ignore the dead port, and any pre-existing edge into/out of it simply goes unread, so it's always safe. **Nodes that ADD or TRANSFORM ports per config — `switch` (case_N + value-widget swap + hide value in conditions mode), `sequence` (then_N), `expression` (slice to visibleCount + relabel) — keep that logic inline in both files** (the hook only REMOVES static ports). When adding a new node whose port set depends on a mode, add `hiddenPorts` to its def rather than a new inline filter. (The audit that produced this — `audit-mode-dependent-ports` workflow — checked all 71 nodes against all 3 compile targets and found Math + Update Indicator were the only un-gated cases.)
- GetNeighborsAttribute uses `_scr_<nodeId>` scratch arrays declared before the loop — never allocate in hot path
- **varName() registration**: Any node whose `compile()` emits a non-default output variable (e.g., `_v${id}_result`, `_v${id}_vals`, `_scr_${id}`) MUST have a matching special case in `varName()` in compile.ts. Without this, downstream nodes reference the wrong (undeclared) variable. Also register scratch arrays in all three locations: main pass, macro inline, nested macro inline.
- NEVER use `fn(...args)` in per-cell loops — V8 megamorphic spread kills performance
- Play pipeline chains from worker message handler (not rAF): receive result → draw → send next step
- Color output: the merged `setCellLooks` node (plain mode, or glyph mode with `setBackground`) writes directly to the RGBA `colors` buffer, checks `activeViewer` for multi-viewer support. See the "Set Cell Looks" major section for the full node shape.
- **`setCellLooks` "Current Simulator Selected"** (`config.mappingId === CURRENT_VIEWER_SENTINEL` = `'__current__'`, exported from [SetCellLooksNode.ts](src/modeler/vpl/nodes/SetCellLooksNode.ts)): writes WHICHEVER output mapping is active instead of one fixed mapping, so one graph can serve several viewers. **Changes compiled CA code on all three targets** — each emits the writes (colors AND/or glyph) WITHOUT the `activeViewer` guard for the sentinel: JS's `_isV_` hoist (`collectViewerRefs`) skips it (no `_isV___current__` identifier emitted); WASM emits `emitWrites()` unconditionally (the sentinel never enters `viewerIds`, so the `viewerInt!` assertion can't fire); WebGPU drops the `control.activeViewer` step-shader guard AND, inside an output-mapping shader, bypasses the `currentMappingId === viewerId` match (every OM shader writes — harmless since each OM pass is dispatched only for its own mapping, so the sentinel's real flexibility is in the Step color pass). `nodeValidation` accepts the sentinel for `setCellLooks` (the `inputColor`/`outputMapping` case still requires a real mapping). Verified byte-shape on all three via dev-server compiler imports.
- Bool constants use `1`/`0` (not `true`/`false`) for typed array compatibility
- Paint: after InputColor writes to writeAttrs, copy back to readAttrs before runStep()
- Worker mutation handlers (paint, importImage, reset, writeRegion, clearRegion): after mutating cell attributes, refresh the display via `if (hasColorPass) runColorPass(); else if (stepFn) runStep(); else writeDefaultColors(); sendColors();`. Without the fallback, users without an Output Mapping see no visual feedback. **NB for verification:** for a no-Output-Mapping model (GoL, Wireworld, Gray-Scott colour-in-step) this runs a STEP, so a `getState` right after a `writeRegion` reads the POST-step cells — use a model with a real Output Mapping (`hasColorPass`) or an immovable cell value to observe the raw written region.
- **Shape-aware cell copy/paste** (Ctrl+C/V/X), **2D AND 3D**: the region is read as the **bounding BOX** of the current brush footprint (so Circle/Ring copy their disc/annulus, the volumetric brush copies its sphere/shell/box; Line at a single cursor point resolves to its width-dot; no special-casing), but a **shape mask** (Uint8, length `w*h*d`, indexed `(dl*h + dr)*w + dc`) travels with the clipboard so **paste writes only the shape's cells**, leaving the surrounding cells at the target intact (a circle pastes a disc, not a square). `clipboard.{mask,hotL,hotR,hotC}` carries the mask + the cursor's offset within the box so paste re-centres on the cursor exactly the way copy did (rect: `hotR/hotC` = the old `halfH/halfW`, so rectangle copy/paste is byte-identical). Cut (Ctrl+X) clears only the masked cells.
  - **ONE clipboard shape serves both dimensions — 2D is simply the `d === 1` case** (`d`/`hotL` stay absent and default to 1 / 0). The three worker messages (`readRegion` / `writeRegion` / `clearRegion`) gained optional `layer?` + `d?`, and `cellIndexOf(0, r, c) IS r*width+c`, so **the 2D path is byte-for-byte the historical single-layer rectangle**. A 2D clipboard pasted into a 3D model lands as one slice at the hovered layer; a 3D clipboard pasted into a 2D model is clipped by the worker. A clipboard carrying attributes the target model lacks skips them (the write loop iterates the MODEL's `cellAttrs` and looks each up in the payload).
  - **In 3D the anchor is the BRUSH-PLANE cursor** (`hover3dRef`), never the 2D `cursorGrid` (an inert fit-mapping in 3D — driving a region write from it corrupted layer-0 cells far from the plane, which is why the shortcut used to be gated off there). **With the brush plane disabled or no hovered cell the shortcut is a no-op + a hint toast**, never a write. The footprint is EXACTLY what the 3D brush would paint at that cell: the same `currentStampOffsets3d()` through the same plane-axis permutation, now factored into the shared **`planeAxisDelta(axis, dr, dc, dl) → [dLayer, dRow, dCol]`** that `mapStampToPlane` also uses (so the copied set cannot drift from the painted set).
  - **The box is measured in ABSOLUTE grid axes and pasted in the same axes whatever the plane is set to afterwards** — the plane only supplies the ANCHOR cell, it never reorients the contents (a plane-relative reorientation is deliberately out of scope). Deltas are taken **UNWRAPPED** (like 2D), so a footprint straddling a torus seam yields a compact box rather than a grid-spanning one; out-of-range cells read as the attribute DEFAULT on copy and are CLIPPED on paste, on every axis — the 2D behaviour, generalized.
  - **In 3D a copy/cut TOASTS what it grabbed** (`Copied 179 cells (7×7×7 box)`). 2D stays silent on purpose: there the silhouette cursor already shows the footprint and the paste is immediately visible, while a 3D volume is occluded and may be deeper than the plane.
  - Worker `writeRegion`/`clearRegion` skip cells where `mask[local] === 0` in BOTH the attr-write loop AND the WebGPU per-cell `idxs` patch loop. **The `gpuOwnsAttrs` trap is already handled by `patchWebGPUCells`** (it forces the per-cell strategy whenever the CPU mirror may be stale, so the batched `[minIdx..maxIdx]` upload can never clobber evolved cells between masked ones) — a 3D mask spans a much wider index range, so that guard is load-bearing here.
  - **DEV hook `window.__sim3dHover(layer,row,col)`** sets (or, with no arguments, reads) the hovered plane cell — the `__sim3dPaint` precedent, since `pickOnPlane` is unreachable from a synthetic pointer event and that cell is the anchor for everything plane-relative.
  - Verified through the real worker: 3D copy→paste of a volumetric sphere is cell-for-cell exact across a tag + bool + integer attribute (179/179 cells, **0** of the other 7821 cells touched); cut clears exactly the mask to each attribute's default and the re-paste carries the pre-cut values; the y-plane permutation is confirmed by a NON-cubic 5×3×2 box reporting `5×2×3` (a z-plane would say `5×3×2`); flat mode gives a `7×7×1` box with the 15 out-of-grid source cells read as defaults; destination clipping writes only the 22 in-bounds cells. **On the WebGPU target after 5 un-read GPU steps**, the paste landed the copied values and ALL 13 824 cells matched an independently computed Bays-5766 evolution (0 stale-clobbered); the cut likewise. **2D regression** (Game of Life 300², WebGPU): paste is exactly the 37-cell disc, hotspot-aligned, values exact; cut clears exactly the disc; the re-paste carries the pre-cut values; nothing else changes.
- `src/simulator/SimulatorView.tsx` — Canvas rendering via ImageData + zoom/pan, LMB=brush/RMB=pan
- Simulator settings persisted to localStorage (`genesisca_sim_settings`)
- Bottom transport bar (simulation TIME only): save/load state │ the two ADJACENT speed readouts (FPS, G/F — both vertical-slider popovers) │ play/pause/step/reset. Top viewer bar: mapping tabs; collapsible side panels. **Capture (screenshot + recording) is NOT on the bar** — see the capture-cluster bullet below.
- **Capture cluster + the bottom-right stack** ([SimulatorView.tsx](src/simulator/SimulatorView.tsx) `.bottomRightStack` / `.captureCluster` / `.capturePopover`; plan+mockup [docs/PLAN_CAPTURE_UI.md](docs/PLAN_CAPTURE_UI.md)/`.html`): all six capture controls left the transport bar (they were ~470 px of mostly-configuration, and the WebM-only pair UNMOUNTED for GIF, reflowing everything to their right). They now live at the canvas's bottom-right as `📷 ⏺ [format · area · quality ▾]`. **PURE PRESENTATION** — `recordFormat`/`captureScope`/`recordQuality`/`recordOverload` and their `genesisca_sim_settings` round-trip are untouched, and NOTHING in `recording/*` / the encoder / the capture caps / the recording state machine changed (`git diff --stat` = SimulatorView.tsx + its CSS). Load-bearing details:
  - **ONE bottom-anchored flex column (`.bottomRightStack`) owns the stats overlay AND the cluster.** `.statsOverlay` lost its own `position:absolute` and is now a plain flow child — two independently bottom-anchored overlays would collide the moment the stats grew (an agent model adds several lines). Measured gap: exactly 4 px on a 5-line grid model AND a 6-line agent model, at 900×620 and 1400×900.
  - **`bottom: 68px`, NOT `--space-6`** — the transport bar is CENTRED and grows with the model, so on a narrower canvas it reaches the right edge. The stats overlay used to sit in that band (a covered READOUT is merely ugly); a covered BUTTON is broken. 68 = the bar row's ~51 px + its 12 px inset + margin. `.zoomControls` uses the same trick (60px) on the left edge.
  - **Popover = the `speedPopup` pattern, anchored bottom-right and opening UPWARD-LEFT** (`bottom:100%; right:0`, flush — a visual gap is a hit-test hole that fires `pointerleave`; verified 0 px). The chip has its OWN `position:relative` wrapper so hovering 📷/⏺ does not pop the settings open. `overlayPopup` (renamed from `speedPopup`) is `'fps'|'gpf'|'capture'|'shot'|'diagnostics'|null` — ONE state + ONE wrapper ref = one popover at a time for free.
  - **📷 has a Save / Copy menu, and a plain CLICK is still Save** (2026-08-06). Its own `.captureBtnWrap` (`position:relative`, the `.captureChipWrap` twin) so the menu anchors to the camera and hovering it opens THAT rather than the settings popover; `.shotMenu` opens flush upward (`bottom:100%`, `left:0` — the cluster is already at the canvas edge, so growing rightward can never overflow). It joins `overlayPopup` as `'shot'`, inheriting the outside-pointerdown + Escape dismissal, and opens on **hover OR right-click** (`onContextMenu` + `preventDefault`). **Copy is not a second capture path** — `handleScreenshot(action)` takes the disposition as a PARAMETER and the whole pipeline (3D `readPixels`, the simulation-scope `requestColorsSnapshot` round-trip, the view-scope overlay composite) is shared; only the final `downloadBlob` branches to `copyBlobToClipboard`. That is what makes a Copy of a simulation-scope shot identical to a Save of one (**measured: both 720×720 on a 100² grid**). `navigator.clipboard.write` needs a secure context AND a **focused** document and may be refused outright by WebView2, so EVERY failure toasts (`showAgentNotice`) — a silent no-op is indistinguishable from a successful copy until the user tries to paste. A Tauri clipboard plugin is the follow-up if the desktop build refuses.
  - **Two rules that outlive this change: (1) inside THIS popover, never UNMOUNT an inapplicable control — disable it in place, with the reason in its TOOLTIP** (GIF → quality/overload; 3D → the area row). **This is the popover-local form of the general rule below — the popover is a fixed-size configuration surface whose rows must not reflow mid-interaction, and every row here is either one FORMAT choice away or explained on hover.** **(2) a binary choice is a two-state SEGMENT, never a dropdown** (`captureSegment()`, a module-level helper). `PICK_OPT_STYLE` (the dark `<option>` workaround) died with the last `<select>`.
  - **EVERY EXPLANATION IS A TOOLTIP; ROWS NEVER REFLOW.** The popover is a control surface, not a manual — a row is a **label + a control**, nothing else. The detail is exposed **on demand** via native `title`, in two layers: the **row wrapper** says what the setting is (or, when greyed, WHY), and each **option** says what that choice does. Putting the reason on the row WRAPPER is load-bearing, not tidiness: a browser fires no mouse events on a **disabled** button, so a disabled option's tooltip resolves to the nearest titled ancestor — which is exactly where the "why is this greyed?" reason has to live. **This REPLACED always-visible prose** (2026-08-07, user: *"way too much explanatory text always visible, bloating the popup dialog"*): 5 rows carried ~930 characters of `.captureWhy` sentences, and swapping a long explanation for a short reason slid every row ~125 px out from under the cursor — the same defect class as unmounting — which is why `.captureWhyStack` used to stack both variants in ONE grid cell (`grid-area: 1/1` + `visibility`) to equalise their heights. **A tooltip changes no geometry at all, so that machinery is gone and the invariant now holds by construction.** Measured: **480 → 178 px tall (−302 px, −62.9 %) at the same 270 px width**, visible text 930 → 167 chars, and **dY = 0 on every row** across a WebM↔GIF flip, an enabled↔disabled Cursor-row swap, and a 2D↔3D switch (identical 178 px and identical row offsets `[30,55,93,119,144]`). **Do not reintroduce visible prose here** — add a `title`.
  - **Everything is `data-sim-overlay`** (on the `.bottomRightStack` wrapper, so `closest()` covers every descendant) — without it `canvasBrushActive` lets a click fall through and PAINT CELLS. Verified with a worker-postMessage spy: a canvas click emits `paintManual` (positive control), while clicks on the cluster padding, the stack gap, the stats strip and inside the popover emit **zero**.
  - **Locked at Start**: while recording the chip is `disabled` and keeps showing the FROZEN configuration (clicking it does not open the popover — verified mid-recording), and ⏺ becomes `⏹ <frames> −<skipped> ⏳`.
- **Capturing the CURSOR OVERLAY LAYERS — `captureOverlays` (`'off'` default / `'highlights'` / `'all'`, persisted in `genesisca_sim_settings`).** Since the cursor-overlay rework the brush cursor + highlight rings live on two canvases ABOVE the scene canvas, while every capture reads the SCENE canvas — so a recording / screenshot never contained them (correct by default; a tutorial recording needs them). **`compositeCaptureOverlays(ctx, dw, dh)`** ([SimulatorView.tsx](src/simulator/SimulatorView.tsx), defined next to `drawCursorLayer`) replays the BROWSER'S OWN compositing onto the destination: `cursorHl` source-over, then `cursorNeg` under **`globalCompositeOperation = 'difference'`** — the Canvas2D equivalent of the layer's CSS `mix-blend-mode: difference`, and correct because the layer is transparent everywhere else (difference with 0 is identity, so ONLY the silhouette pixels invert). ONE call site per capture path: the recording's view-scope branch (into the CPU-backed `recordScratch`, BEFORE `getImageData` — so GIF, buffered WebM and the streaming `makeVideoFrame` all inherit it) and `handleScreenshot`'s view-scope branch. **`drawImage` from the live overlay canvases is a texture READ — it does NOT de-optimise them** (the recording-slowdown rule bans `getImageData` on a live canvas, not `drawImage`).
  - **THREE-state ladder, not two booleans**: the rings mark what the brush is ABOUT to affect, so "cursor without rings" is not a state anyone wants — `Off < Highlights < All` is monotone and fits ONE popover row.
  - **VIEW SCOPE ONLY, by construction** — the overlay is positioned by the LIVE pan/zoom, while the "simulation" scope renders a fit framing of the whole world; pasting view-space pixels onto a differently-framed image would put the cursor in the wrong place. With the capture area set to Simulation the row is disabled in place with that reason as its tooltip (`overlaysSimArea`). **2D ONLY** — in 3D the brush outline / hovered cells / inspect rings are drawn INSIDE the gl3d scene, so every 3D capture already contains them; `compositeCaptureOverlays` early-returns on `is3dRef` and the row is disabled with that reason as its tooltip.
  - The chip appends `· +rings` / `· +cursor` (it is LOCKED for the run like every other capture setting, so it has to say what is being captured).
  - **Verified through the real UI** (Game of Life + Particle Life, real downloaded files decoded in-page): a view-scope PNG differs from the `off` baseline in **exactly the 550 non-transparent pixels of the `cursorNeg` layer**, `maxΔ = 765` (a full inversion); with an empty highlight layer `highlights` is **byte-identical** to `off` (same 22 025-byte PNG). Real **GIF recordings** decoded with `ImageDecoder`: 6 frames each, off-vs-off **0 px / identical 5 139 bytes** (the negative control proving the sim is deterministic across the two runs) vs off-vs-all **126 px, maxΔ 762**. On Particle Life (agent Remove brush, 2 609 ring px + 548 silhouette px): `off→highlights` **2 604 px**, `highlights→all` **exactly 548 px**, sizes strictly increasing 1 343 645 → 1 346 146 → 1 347 273. Popover geometry: **every row top identical (dY = 0)** across the enabled↔disabled reason swap.
- Keyboard shortcuts: Space=step (also pauses), Enter=play/pause, Esc=reset
- **Brush shapes** ([SimulatorView.tsx](src/simulator/SimulatorView.tsx)): the stamp is shape-selectable — `Rectangle` (W×H, byte-identical to the historical double-loop, even-size off-centre bias preserved), `Circle` (filled euclidean disc by radius), `Ring` (annulus, radius ± width/2), `Line` (two clicks define a capsule segment of a chosen thickness — first click stages an anchor that paints nothing, second commits; RMB / Escape cancel a staged anchor). The right-panel size row adapts per shape (Rect W/H, Circle Radius, Ring Radius+Width, Line Width). `brushShapeOffsets()` returns the stamp's cell offsets; `lineStampCells()` is the capsule walk (point-to-segment ≤ width/2); both fold to the torus-shortest path in infinity mode like the existing drag-paint. Offsets + silhouette edges are cached by a shape/param key (`stampCacheRef`). State: `brushShape` / `brushRadius` / `brushRingWidth` / `brushLineWidth`, persisted in `genesisca_sim_settings` AND serialized into `.gcastate` (alongside `brushW/H`).
- **Brush cursor = negative silhouette**: the cursor outlines the EXACT cell-silhouette of the current stamp (`cellSilhouetteEdges()` — every cell edge bordering a non-member cell), stroked with `globalCompositeOperation = 'difference'` + white so it renders as the photographic negative of whatever colors are behind it (visible on any palette — the Windows-cursor trick; `ctx.save`/`restore` so the composite mode doesn't leak). Drawn once per visible tile in infinity mode. `Ctrl+LMB` drag resizes the active shape's params (Rect W/H, Circle radius, Ring radius+width, Line width).
- **Recording — WebM STREAMS (encode-as-you-go), GIF buffers.** Four settings in the capture chip's popover (bottom-right of the canvas — see the capture-cluster bullet above) — **format**, **area**, and (WebM only) **quality** + **on-overload** — with the chip `disabled` while recording, so **format, scope, quality and overload policy are locked for the run**, which is what lets the recorder commit to a streaming encoder AND to a single overload policy at Start. Worker tracks a `recording` flag (`setRecording` message) so direct render still ships colors when capturing. Investigation + all the measurements: [docs/INVESTIGATION_STREAMING_RECORDING.md](docs/INVESTIGATION_STREAMING_RECORDING.md); the options round: [docs/PLAN_RECORDING_OPTIONS.md](docs/PLAN_RECORDING_OPTIONS.md) (+ `.html`).
  - **QUALITY = the keyframe cadence, and GOP-30 is the DEFAULT** (`RecordQuality` + `keyFrameIntervalFor` in [webmEncoder.ts](src/simulator/recording/webmEncoder.ts), consumed by BOTH encoders — that sharing is load-bearing): `standard` = a keyframe every **`GOP_STANDARD`(30)** frames, `archival` = all-intra (the historical behaviour, now opt-in). Measured on 60 real Kelp War frames at 810×912 through the shipped `encodeFramesToWebM`: **6.35× smaller (38.8 → 6.1 MB) and 3.06× faster (6111 → 1994 ms)**. **A DROPPED FRAME IS SAFE UNDER GOP-30** — a drop happens BEFORE submission, so the encoder only ever sees the frames it was given, in order, and codes each delta against the previously *submitted* frame; nothing can reference a frame that was never encoded. Verified, not asserted: a 122-chunk GOP-30 recording taken **with 351 drops** decoded through `VideoDecoder` to exactly 122 frames, 0 errors (chunk types `K` at 0/30/60/90/120). The BITRATE rule is deliberately unchanged (the investigation's 40 Mbps option carries an unmeasured quality cost).
  - **OVERLOAD POLICY — `drop` (default) or `lossless`.** Drop is unchanged: `addFrame` refuses at `QUEUE_CAP`/the duty gate and the caller counts it. **Lossless ("never skip") slows the SIMULATION instead** — `addFrame(frame, force)` bypasses the cap+gate so a captured frame is ALWAYS submitted, and the **rAF `tick` at the tail of the `stepped` handler** (the one part of the loop that is already asynchronous — `draw()` is synchronous and cannot await, which is *why* drop exists) refuses to issue the next step batch until `enc.readyForNextFrame()`. Because a frame is captured exactly once per issued step and a step is only issued when the queue is below the cap, **the queue stays bounded by CAP+1** — no unbounded (invisible, GPU-memory) queue, and no frame refused. Three anti-hang guards: `LOSSLESS_HARD_CAP`(8) for submissions outside the throttled loop (manual Steps — which force-submit, so they never silently lose a frame); `LOSSLESS_STALL_MS`(8000) after which the run **one-way degrades to `drop`** + a toast (never flaps); and `⏳ waiting for encoder` in the stats overlay + `⏳` on the Stop button so a slowed run never reads as a hang. The throttle also holds while the async codec probe is in flight (else the bounded pending array would drop). Measured on dense content: **0 dropped vs 250, simulation 4.92× slower**, throttle visible 52% of the time, max main-thread gap 252 ms. `recordOverloadActiveRef` is the run's LOCKED policy (drop unless streaming WebM); pausing clears the throttle flag (the tick that would clear it never runs again).
  - **THE VP9 PROFILE-1 GUARD IS A RESIDUE TEST, NOT A MAX WIDTH** (`isVp9Profile1Safe`) — this REPLACED `VP9_444_MAX_WIDTH = 960`, which was the wrong SHAPE and let widths that freeze **today** through. Bisecting the original 900-OK/960-FREEZE bracket (13 standalone measurements, zero contradictions) showed the failure tracks the **coded width mod 32** (`cw = ceil(w/8)*8`): **`0` → FREEZE** (renderer starved indefinitely; 960² held >150 s and only released on navigating away — 640, 864, 896 froze too), **`16` → FAST** (~50 ms/frame, responsive), **`8`/`24` → SLOW** (~800 ms/frame, ~1 s main-thread stalls — a third regime the original probe never saw). **Width-driven, confirmed twice**: 928×540 (501k px) freezes while 920×920 (846k px) does not, and 912×**928** is fast. **Profile 0 is IMMUNE** (1280×720 = 32 ms/frame, the fastest measured), so the fallback is sound. The guard requires the ONE fast residue — merely avoiding `≡0` would leave half of all widths at 800 ms/frame. `isConfigSupported` reports every frozen config as `supported: true`.
  - **CAPTURE CAPS: `RECORD_MAX` 960 → 912, new `RECORD_MAX_3D` = 1280** (both in webmEncoder.ts, co-located with the residue rule because the coupling IS the reason). 912 ≡ 16 (mod 32), so **the default 2D recording is now genuinely 4:4:4** instead of silently falling back to 4:2:0 (whose chroma subsampling bleeds exactly the 1-px colour transitions CA output is made of) — verified in-app: a 150-frame Kelp War recording selects `vp09.01.10.08.03` at 912×912 with a **303 ms** max main-thread gap. `snapRecordWidth(w)` lowers arbitrary capture widths (portrait canvases via the view-scope crop, tall grids via `renderSimulationFrame(…, snapWidth=true)`) into the fast class, deriving the height from the SAME scale so the aspect is exact; it engages only above 320 px. **3D capture is capped in the RECORDING block only** (`downscaleCapture` — putImageData onto a never-displayed source canvas, drawImage-scaled onto a never-displayed `willReadFrequently` scratch, `getImageData` that; NEVER getImageData a live canvas); screenshots keep full display resolution. 1280 ≡ 0 → profile 0, i.e. **3D records in 4:2:0** by design. Verified: a 1480×964 GL buffer captures at 1280×834 (aspect preserved), −25% bytes/frame at DPR 1 and ~−81% at DPR 2 where the uncapped cost was 23 MB/frame.
  - **CAPTURE RESOLUTION — `captureResolution: 'auto' | '480' | '720' | '1080' | 'native'`** (persisted; `captureMaxFor` / `gifMaxSizeFor` in [SimulatorView.tsx](src/simulator/SimulatorView.tsx)), a **Resolution** row in the capture popover below the dividing rule (recording-only) and a chip part whenever it is not `auto`. `auto` resolves to the historical caps (`RECORD_MAX` 912 / `RECORD_MAX_3D` 1280, GIF `GIF_MAX_DEFAULT` 512) so it is byte-for-byte today's behaviour; a number caps the long edge at BOTH capture sites and replaces the GIF cap (ceiling `GIF_MAX_HARD` 1024 — a GIF buffers every frame); `native` means no rescaling, bounded by `CAPTURE_MAX_NATIVE` (2048), and for the SIMULATION scope specifically it means **one pixel per cell** (`renderSimulationFrame`'s new `noUpscale`, which caps the scale at 1 — that scope normally UPSCALES a small grid). **Screenshots are deliberately untouched** (full display resolution).
    - **⚠ THE FREEZE GUARD IS NOT THIS SETTING'S JOB.** `pickVp9Config` calls `isVp9Profile1Safe` on the ACTUAL width every time, so no user-chosen number can reach the freezing coded-width residue — it falls back to the immune profile 0. `snapRecordWidth` buys **QUALITY** (4:4:4 instead of 4:2:0), so it is applied where the capture is rescaling anyway: the 2D view crop, the 2D simulation render, and — via a new optional 3rd param on `downscaleCapture` — the 3D downscale **for an explicit choice only** (`auto` in 3D keeps the documented RECORD_MAX_3D/profile-0 trade; `native` means don't touch my pixels). Verified on a 980×864 3D viewport: `720` → **720×635, profile 1**; `auto` → **980×864, profile 0**.
    - **Verified end-to-end** (2D 300² grid, simulation scope): GIF `480`→**464×464** · `720`→**720×720** · `1080`→**1024×1024** (capture snapped to 1072, then the GIF 1024 ceiling) · `Native`→**300×300** (1 px/cell) · `Auto`→**512×512**; WebM `Auto`→**912×912** · `480`→**464** · `720`→**720** · `1080`→**1072** · `Native`→**300**, **every one with `vp9CodedWidth(w) % 32 === 16` and the shipped `pickVp9Config` selecting VP9 profile 1 (4:4:4)**, all loading in `<video>` with correct dims + finite duration and decoding real content.
  - **Tier 2 (streaming to disk / FSA / OPFS) is DEFERRED BY DECISION** — see the investigation's §7; do not re-litigate it.
  - **WebM** → [webmStreamEncoder.ts](src/simulator/recording/webmStreamEncoder.ts) `WebMStreamEncoder`: each captured frame goes to the `VideoEncoder` immediately, so only the COMPRESSED bytes accumulate. The muxer path is unchanged (`addVideoChunk` was ALREADY called from the encoder's `output` callback — muxing was always incremental; only frame SUBMISSION moved). **The encoder configuration is shared** — `pickVp9Config` / `vp9EncoderConfig`, now exported from [webmEncoder.ts](src/simulator/recording/webmEncoder.ts) and used by BOTH paths, so a streamed file is configured byte-for-byte like a buffered one (VP9 p1 4:4:4 → p0 fallback, all-intra, `max(4 Mbps, w·h·fps·6)`, `contentHint:'text'`).
  - **Why:** raw frames are 2.9 MB (2D) to 33 MB (3D at 4K — `readPixels` is UNCAPPED at `cssW·dpr`) EACH; measured ceiling ~**9.3 GB / 4094 frames** then `RangeError` from `ImageData` (uncaught, inside the `stepped` handler → the simulator stops repainting). That is ~1m46s of 2D or **under 15 s of 3D on a HiDPI display**. Measured retained cost after: **670 KB/frame** dense (Kelp War 898×821) / **5.3 KB/frame** sparse (GoL) — compression spans **4.4×–541×**, so never quote a single number. Stop went from a full encode (10 fps on dense content ⇒ minutes) to a flush: **87 ms** / 3.1 MB, **1.28 s** / 87.8 MB.
  - **A PRE-EXISTING Chrome bug this work surfaced (SUPERSEDED — see the residue-guard bullet above).** The original fix was `VP9_444_MAX_WIDTH = 960` ("profile 1 only below width 960"), from a two-point 900-OK/960-FREEZE bracket. A later bisect showed that model was WRONG — the failure is periodic in the coded width, so widths far below 960 froze under that guard. Kept here only so the history reads correctly; the live rule is `isVp9Profile1Safe`.
  - **Backpressure is MANDATORY; the DEFAULT policy is DROP** (the opt-in `lossless` alternative throttles the step pipeline instead — see the overload-policy bullet above). `encode()` is non-blocking; measured with no cap the queue grows linearly forever (+7.5/s) and **queued `VideoFrame`s are NOT on the JS heap** (GPU/media memory) — an INVISIBLE memory sink, worse to diagnose than the `RangeError`. `draw()` is synchronous and cannot await, so `addFrame` returns **false** when `encodeQueueSize >= QUEUE_CAP` (**2**) and the caller counts a drop. A second limit, the **`DUTY_FACTOR` (1.5) duty-cycle gate**, additionally refuses a frame until 1.5× the rolling-average encode time has passed since the last submission — the encoder is never held 100% busy, so it always leaves the renderer wall clock (a deep queue alone does NOT protect the main thread; on cheap content the gate never binds). Safe because a drop happens BEFORE submission, so the encoder only ever sees the frames it was given, in order — the sequence is shortened, never corrupted, under any keyframe cadence — and because the file is timed from the WALL CLOCK (see the timing bullet below), so a drop reads as the pause it actually was. The drop count renders next to the REC counter — never silent. **A frame the encoder would refuse is no longer CAPTURED either**: the capture site asks `readyForNextFrame()` first (the exact predicate `addFrame` would have used) and skips the whole `drawImage`+`getImageData` — 3 MB in 2D, a full `readPixels` in 3D — on 50-70% of frames on the heavy models, which is the investigation's own §3.2 recommendation ("do not even `getImageData`") finally applied. Same frame skipped, same drop counted; gated on the DROP policy and on a LIVE encoder (lossless force-submits, and before the async codec probe resolves there is nothing to ask). **It must not `return`** — the next-step scheduler is later in the same `stepped` handler and bailing out of it stalls the run.
  - **THE FILE IS TIMED FROM THE WALL CLOCK, NOT FROM THE FRAME INDEX** (fixed 2026-08-05 — the user-reported *"recording webm 'view' videos doesn't seem to be working well unless using 'never skip' and 'archival'"*).
