Every captured frame carries the `performance.now()` at which it was CAPTURED (`acceptRecordedFrame` stamps it once and threads it through `addFrame(frame, force, captureTimeMs)`, through the bounded pending array — those are submitted in a BURST when the probe resolves, so timing them at SUBMISSION would squash the start of every recording — and through `encodeFramesToWebM`'s optional `captureTimesMs`), and the block timestamp is that offset from the first frame. **The old rule was `timestamp = encodedIndex × 1/fps`, whose premise — that the pipeline sustains the nominal fps — is false on anything but the cheapest content.** MEASURED before the fix, all at the DEFAULT settings: Particle Life view-scope 10.1 s → a **0.754 s** file (13× too fast), Growing Graphs **19×**, the *simulation* scope **22×**, and even Game of Life **5×**; `archival`+`never skip` did NOT fix the speed (10.0 s → 0.622 s) — it only made the motion CONTINUOUS, which is why it read as "the working combination". After: the same runs give **9.73 / 9.65 / 9.95 s** for 10 s. Fast content where the encoder keeps up is unaffected (consecutive captures are ~1/fps apart, exactly what the index formula produced). `duration` per chunk is the previous inter-frame gap — a hint only, since block spacing is what players use. Timestamps are forced strictly increasing (`performance.now()` is monotonic, but two captures in one microsecond would be rejected by the encoder).
  - **THE FPS SLIDER IS NOT A FRAME RATE — clamp it** (`clampRecordFps` / `MAX_RECORD_FPS` = 120, applied in `pickVp9Config` so BOTH encoders and the GIF delay inherit it). Its "unlimited" position resolves to the sentinel **999999**, which reached both derived quantities and destroyed each: `bitrate = w·h·fps·6` became **4.4 Tbit/s** (rate control collapsed — 71 frames in 0.13 MB, against 9.3 MB for the same content at a finite fps) and the timing base `1e6/fps` became **1 µs**, so a whole recording's blocks landed inside ~70 µs and `<video>` reported **`duration = NaN`, i.e. an unplayable file** (the GIF delay likewise rounded to 0 ms). Verified after: FPS ∞ now configures 120 fps / 528 Mbps and an 8.2 s recording yields a **7.76 s** playable file. **Any new consumer of `targetFpsRef` in a capture path must clamp** — it is a UI slider, not a rate.
  - **Honest cost:** the encoder competes for CPU, so a dense model's capture/display rate drops (measured **24 fps buffered → 11 fps streaming** on Kelp War). The buffered path would pay that same encode time at Stop anyway, and dies at ~136 s.
  - **The VideoFrame is built from the RGBA BUFFER, never a canvas** (`makeVideoFrame`): `putImageData` into an OffscreenCanvas + `new VideoFrame(canvas)` round-trips every frame through the GPU (upload + synchronous readback), which contends with a WebGPU model already driving the GPU. `new VideoFrame(imageData.data, {format:'RGBA',…})` touches no GPU; the canvas path is kept only as a fallback for engines without BufferInit.
  - **`recordDimsRef`** is the dimension lock for BOTH paths (it used to be `recordedFrames.current[0]`, which stays empty while streaming). `acceptRecordedFrame` is the ONE disposition point for a finished frame (stream → buffer → count exactly once). The encoder is built **lazily on the first frame** (its dims are only known then) via the async `isConfigSupported` probe; frames captured meanwhile are held in `webmStreamPendingRef` (cap `WEBM_STREAM_PENDING_MAX` = 8) and drained on resolve — **any failure degrades to the historical buffered path**, never loses the recording. `resetRecordingState()` (start / stop / every abort site / unmount) `cancel()`s the encoder — abandoning one leaks a hardware encoder session.
  - **`fps` is locked at Start** (the encoder needs it at `configure()`); it used to be read at Stop, which silently retimed the whole file if the slider moved mid-record.
  - **GIF still BUFFERS** — `gifenc` needs the raw RGBA of every frame for its per-frame palette, so a GIF recording retains `ImageData` (verified: zero `encode()` calls during a GIF recording). Short clips only. Its ENCODE now lives in [gifEncoder.ts](src/simulator/recording/gifEncoder.ts) and is delta-optimised — see the next bullet.
- **GIF DELTA FRAMES + identical-frame delay merging** ([gifEncoder.ts](src/simulator/recording/gifEncoder.ts) `encodeFramesToGif`; the encode was lifted out of `stopRecording` into its own module). The old path wrote every captured frame WHOLE — quantize 256 → `applyPalette` → `writeFrame` — consulting nothing about the previous frame, so a frozen simulation cost exactly as much as a churning one. Two optimisations, and **one rule that makes them safe**:
  - **Identical-frame merge**: a run of byte-identical frames is written ONCE with the summed delay. GIF timing IS per-frame delay, so this is exactly equivalent — and it is the biggest single win (a motionless 40-frame recording: **36 039 → 939 B, 38×**). It also *improves* timing accuracy: the centisecond rounding happens once per RUN instead of once per frame (measured 1240 ms vs 1200 ms against a true 1333 ms).
  - **Transparent-index deltas**: pixels already on screen become a reserved index, `dispose: 1` ("do not dispose"). Full-size frames — what shrinks is the LZW payload.
  - **⚠ THE COMPARISON IS AGAINST THE DECODED IMAGE, NEVER THE SOURCE RGBA.** Each frame has its own quantised palette, so an unchanged source colour can land on a different palette entry and therefore a different RGB. `prevRgb` tracks what the decoder actually holds; a pixel goes transparent only when the new frame would paint the identical RGB. **Measured on a palette-drift fixture: a naive source compare would have left 119 570 pixels stale.** With the decoded compare the delta output is **DECODE-IDENTICAL** to writing every frame whole (verified 0 differing channel values, max delta 0, on both the sparse and the drift fixtures).
  - **⚠ A DELTA IS NOT ALWAYS SMALLER, so the choice is MEASURED per frame, not assumed.** The transparent index is a new symbol that FRAGMENTS the runs LZW was already compressing; where changes are scattered the delta comes out bigger — measured on the shipped **Chromatography** (~32 % of pixels change, spread across the column): 194 999 B full-frame vs **204 057 B all-delta, i.e. −4 %**. So each frame is encoded BOTH ways into a throwaway probe encoder (`probe.reset()` + `bytesView().length`) and the smaller is written, making the path **non-regressive by construction** and adaptive *within* one recording. A cheap predictor was evaluated first (adjacent-symbol transition counts called all 11 Chromatography frames correctly) and REJECTED: a wrong prediction ships a bigger file, and the exact answer costs ~2 extra LZW passes — **LZW is ~2.0 ms of a ~6.2 ms per-frame encode**, paid ONCE at Stop (measured 173 → 365 ms for a 30-frame GIF).
  - **⚠ `dispose` MUST be explicit.** gifenc's default `-1` means "you pick", and its pick for a TRANSPARENT frame is 2 = restore to background — it CLEARS, the exact opposite of a delta.
  - **⚠ The transparent slot is appended only AFTER `applyPalette`.** Its nominal colour is `[0,0,0]`; present during palette application, real black pixels would map onto it and silently vanish. Quantisation targets `GIF_DELTA_COLORS` (255) to leave the slot free — one colour of 256, and **nil on CA content** (verified: Chromatography's 5-colour palette re-encodes **byte-for-byte identical** to the 256-colour baseline).
  - **Global-palette reuse**: a frame whose palette equals the first frame's passes `palette: null`, so it carries no local colour table. The common case for CA content (measured 29 of 30 frames on Chromatography, 39 of 40 on GoL).
  - **SUB-RECT frames are NOT expressible and are not attempted**: gifenc's `encodeImageDescriptor` hard-codes the frame position to (0,0), so a changed-region rectangle could only sit in the top-left corner. Emitting one means writing the image-descriptor bytes around gifenc's LZW output, i.e. forking the encoder. The transparent-index delta already collapses the untouched area into one LZW run; what a sub-rect would additionally save is a few bytes of per-frame descriptor.
  - **Measured spread (honest — the win is entirely about WHERE the change is, not how much):** motionless **38×** · settled GoL 300² (5 % of pixels) **1.33×** · synthetic sparse (1 %) **6.9×** · palette-drift fixture **2.03×** · **live GoL soup 300² (20 %, scattered) 1.00×** (all 39 deltas rejected, +0.0007 %) · Chromatography **1.00×** (all 29 rejected, byte-identical) · synthetic dense noise **1.00×**.
  - **DEV hook `window.__lastGifFrames`** (`import.meta.env.DEV` only) retains the captured frames after a GIF save so the optimisation can be A/B'd on REAL content by re-encoding the same frames with `{delta:false, mergeIdentical:false}`. `encodeFramesToGif` also takes `maxColors` so a test can hold the palette policy fixed while flipping `delta` — which is what isolates the delta logic exactly.
  - **The investigation's remaining phases are now RESOLVED:** capping 3D capture (DONE — `RECORD_MAX_3D`), a recording quality selector (DONE — and the DEFAULT moved to GOP 30), and Tier 2 streaming straight to disk (**DEFERRED BY DECISION**; the measurements stand — OPFS at 207 MB/s with a working seek-back and a 10 GB quota, `ArrayBufferTarget` doubling then `slice()`ing so the in-memory target peaks at ~3x the file — but it is not planned).
- Screenshot exports at display canvas resolution (not grid resolution) with nearest-neighbor upscale
- Recompile optimization: structural changes reinit worker, graph-only changes send `recompile` message (preserves grid state)
- Load Preset (`handleLoadPreset`): only pauses playback when the preset forces a structural worker reinit (grid dimensions or boundary-treatment change) — the predicate mirrors `applySimulationState`'s `boundaryChanged`/`dimsChanged` check. Parameter-only / matching-dims presets (the common case — e.g. the chemistry models' interaction-table parameter sets) apply LIVE via `updateModelAttrs` / `updateLookupTable` without interrupting a running simulation. (Previously it unconditionally `setPlaying(false)` on every preset load.)
- **A preset's BOARD is the cell grid AND the agent population — `serializePreset` captures `agents` inside its `includeGrid` block, exactly like `serializeSimState`** (the checkbox reads "Include board state"; `PresetSaveDialog` takes `hasCells`/`hasAgents` so its hint names the layers the model actually has). **The bug this fixed:** `serializePreset`'s `workerState` type had no `agents` field and its grid block never called `serializeAgentState`, so a preset saved WITH board state dropped the population — and since an **agents-only** model has NO cell attributes at all (`attributes` is `{}`, `colors` is zero-length), such a preset captured *literally nothing* (measured: 2 657 bytes for a 1 200-agent Particle Life 3D board, vs **126 337** after). On load `hasGrid` is still TRUE (`{}`/`''` are non-null), so it posted `loadState` with no agent payload and the worker's **no-agents else-branch re-seeded the population** — the user-reported *"loading it just started from a reset state"*. **The two documented preset semantics are untouched**: a parameter-only preset stays grid-less, so `applySimulationState` returns at `if (!hasGrid)` and never touches the running population; a grid-only model's preset gets no `agents` key at all (payload byte-identical). **Back-compat**: an existing preset saved before this carries no `agents` and keeps taking the legacy re-seed branch — the same rule `.gcastate` documents.
- Save/Load State: transport bar buttons (left side) save `.gcastate` / load `.gcastate`. Worker `getState` copies all typed arrays via `.slice()` and transfers them. Worker `loadState` restores arrays and rebuilds neighbor indices. `applySimulationState()` validates grid dimensions match before loading. Auto-save strips `simulationState` from localStorage to avoid quota overflow. Saving state also stores it in model context so next `.gcaproj` save includes it. On `.gcaproj` load, `pendingSimStateRestore` ref triggers restore after first worker `stepped` message.
- **An explicit Reset is AUTHORITATIVE over a deferred snapshot restore (`9e464fb`).** `model.simulationState` (armed by a Save-with-grid) re-arms `pendingSimStateRestore` on every reinit at matching dims, and a PAUSED reinit replies `colors` (not `stepped`) so the arm LINGERS. `handleReset` posts `reset` (the worker reseeds cleanly from the model's Init Events) but used to leave the arm set, so the next Play's first `stepped` fired `applySimulationState` and clobbered the fresh reseed with the saved snapshot — "Reset" silently restoring a stale/edited board. Fix: `handleReset` clears `pendingSimStateRestore.current = null` before posting. ONE line covers BOTH layers (the deferred restore carries cells AND agents). The `.gcastate`/preset Load path is unaffected (it routes through the `adaptDims:true` restore, not this deferred one). (Distinct from the Particle-Life brush-revert, which needed no save — that was the stale-present bug above.)
- **`applySimulationState(state, opts?: { adaptDims? })` — the embedded snapshot is NOT authoritative for the model's grid (dimension-reset-loop fix).** When the saved boundary/dims differ from the current model, the function's "adapt-model-to-state" branch dispatches `updateProperties` to change the model's `gridWidth`/`gridHeight`/`gridDepth`/`boundaryTreatment`/`dimension` to the snapshot's. That's correct ONLY for **authoritative loads** — a `.gcastate` file (`handleLoadState`) or a preset (`handleLoadPreset`), which now pass **`{ adaptDims: true }`**. The **embedded auto-restore** path (`pendingSimStateRestore` → `applySimulationState(state)` after a structural reinit) passes the default `adaptDims: false`: there the **model is the source of truth**, so a snapshot whose dims no longer match was invalidated by a user edit and is **DROPPED** (`pendingSimStateRestore = null` + `setSimulationState(undefined)`), never used to revert the edit. The bug it fixes (reported in 2D *and* 3D): a model saved with **Simulator controls / grid** carries a `simulationState`; editing Grid Width/Height/**Depth** (or Boundary Treatment) re-armed the stale snapshot, whose adapt branch then **reverted the edit on the next step**, so the dimension "kept resetting" and couldn't be typed (workaround was toggling Boundary back and forth, which hit the drop-guard). **Two layers, both dimension-agnostic:** (1) the model-effect **drop-guard** (`model.simulationState && !pendingSimStateRestore.current`) now checks **all** structural fields — width, height, **and `gridDepth ?? depth ?? 1` (the previous miss — it only checked w/h, so 3D depth edits slipped through)** — dropping a stale snapshot immediately at edit time; (2) `applySimulationState`'s `!adaptDims` drop branch is the backstop if a stale snapshot is ever consumed. Verified at runtime: 3D depth 24→12 and 2D width 300→150 both stick (no revert) after a Save State. **Grid-less states never adapt AT ALL (2026-07 fix):** even under `adaptDims: true`, a state with NO embedded grid (a **parameter-only preset** / a controls-only save) is barred from adapting dims/boundary — `boundaryChanged` and `dimsFromState` are gated on `hasGrid` at all THREE mirrored predicate sites (applySimulationState + handleLoadPreset's pause check + the Overseer `loadPreset` needs-reinit check). `serializePreset` always writes `gridWidth`/`gridHeight`/`gridDepth` (worker dims at save time) even for parameter-only presets, so before the gate a param-only preset saved at other dims RESIZED the grid AND overwrote the model's default dims via `updateProperties` (the reported "parameter preset changes the grid and then the default" bug); those fields are now metadata-only on grid-less states. Verified: Chromatography resized 43×200→43×100 keeps 43×100 through a param-preset load, model default stays 200.
- **Right-panel brush/indicators splitter**: a draggable row-resize handle (`.rightSectionSplitter`) sits between the ACTIVE brush section and the Indicators section, only rendered when the model has indicators. **It governs whichever brush is active** — the **Input Mapping** section (CA-grid brush) OR the **Agent Brush** section (agents) — since the two are mutually exclusive and BOTH carry `brushSectionRef` + the `.rightSectionBrush` class, so exactly one renders and the ref points to it. **Section order is `[Input Mapping | Agent Brush] → Splitter → Indicators`** — the agent brush renders in the SAME slot as the CA-grid brush (ABOVE indicators), NOT below them (the old bug: the Agent Brush section was placed AFTER Indicators with no splitter, so on an agents+indicators model the indicators filled `flex:1` and the brush was pushed to the bottom, unresizable). Dragging sets `brushSectionH` (px, min 60, max `panel - 140` clamped to ≥ 60 so a very short panel can't let the brush section eat the indicators); double-click resets to `null` = auto. **Default cap:** the CA-grid brush shrinks-to-content (short); the AGENT brush is tall, so when `brushSectionH` is null AND indicators exist it gets a `maxHeight:'55%'` default so the indicators stay visible without a drag (the body scrolls within; the splitter's explicit height overrides). Persisted in `genesisca_sim_settings` as `brushSectionH` (localStorage-only — panel layout, NOT serialized into `.gcastate`, mirroring how panel widths are treated).
- Save Project options: `genesis-capture-sim-state` CustomEvent carries `detail.include = { grid?: boolean; controls?: boolean }` (defaults to both true). SimulatorView resolves immediately when neither is wanted, or skips the worker round-trip for controls-only. All `SimulationState` fields are optional; `applySimulationState` restores grid and controls independently. When making new shared-serialized fields optional, also audit `readStateFile` validation and every consumer that reads them unconditionally.
- **Save-dialog defaults are PER-LOADED-MODEL, not a program-wide last choice** (`deriveSaveOptions(model)` in [FileMenu.tsx](src/components/FileMenu.tsx); replaced the removed global `localStorage['genesisca_save_options']` whose cross-model leakage silently dropped data). **Presets** — checked iff `model.presets?.length` (a durable model property, so a save never drops the presets a loaded model carries [the reported bug: load a model WITH presets, edit its description, save with presets unchecked because a prior save of a *different* model had omitted them] and never offers "include presets" for a model with none). **Board state / simulator controls** — LIVE-session captures, so the rule is snapshot-aware, NOT a blanket "checked iff already present": when the model carries an embedded `simulationState`, reflect its composition (`attributes` present ⇒ grid ON, `modelAttrs` present ⇒ controls ON — `serializeSimState` writes each only inside its own `wantGrid`/`wantControls` block, so their presence records which layers were last saved for THIS model AND respects a prior explicit omission); when there is NO embedded snapshot (fresh/from-scratch model, or one saved definition-only) default **both ON** — matching the historical convenience default so building a model from scratch, evolving its board / tuning its attributes, and hitting Save still captures that live work. **The ON-fallback is deliberate** (`s ? s.attributes !== undefined : true`, not `s?.attributes !== undefined`): a fresh/evolved model never mirrors its live board+controls into `model.simulationState` until a save actually captures them, so deriving OFF there would silently discard the user's evolved board+tuned attributes on the common "build → evolve → Save" path (an adversarial-review-confirmed regression). Every in-session save rewrites `simulationState` to the chosen composition. **The user's CONFIRMED choice is additionally remembered per loaded model (`sim_agent_fixes` batch)**: `ModelState.lastSaveOptions` (in-session only, never serialized; reset by NEW_MODEL/LOAD_MODEL, recorded via `markSaved(fileName, opts)` on a successful save) — the dialog opens with `lastSaveOptions ?? deriveSaveOptions(model)`, so repeated saves keep the explicit choice (all boxes OFF stays OFF — previously a definition-only save left no snapshot and the deliberate ON-fallback re-checked grid+controls every time), while a freshly loaded model still derives from its own content.
- **The Save dialog also EDITS the model's presentation fields (Name / Rule Author / GenesisCA Project Author), and an edit is a MODEL edit — not a file-only override.** The three fields (`SaveMetadata` in [SaveProjectDialog.tsx](src/components/SaveProjectDialog.tsx), labels copied verbatim from the Info panel, which owns the same three properties) are seeded from the LIVE model by `useState` — safe because the dialog is conditionally mounted, so every open re-seeds. `doSave(opts, meta)` diffs them against `modelRef.current.properties` into a `metaEdits` patch and, **when the patch is non-empty**, does BOTH: `updateProperties(metaEdits)` (so the navbar / Info panel / a later save agree) AND a local merge into `toSerialize` — because `updateProperties` is a dispatch, so reading `model` back inside the same handler would still see the pre-edit values. **The local merge is the authority for the file**, which also makes the write-back independent of whether React flushed during the `genesis-capture-sim-state` await; the capture flow and its `wantsAny`/presets composition are untouched (the merge is applied to the already-composed object). **`modelFilename` reads `toSerialize`, not `latest`**, so the default filename follows the edited name. **An empty name is barred at the dialog** (Save disabled + the Enter handler guarded) rather than silently ignored — a blank name would strip the navbar title and collapse the filename to `model.gcaproj`. **No edits ⇒ no dispatch and no merge**, so a save with the fields untouched is byte-identical to before (verified: two consecutive saves produce the same 857 427-char JSON) and can't flip `isDirty`; when there ARE edits the dispatch precedes the awaits and `markSaved` follows them, so the run still ends clean. The include-what checkboxes and `deriveSaveOptions`/`lastSaveOptions` are untouched.
- Save/load `ATTR_TYPE_MAP` ([fileOperations.ts](src/model/fileOperations.ts)) MUST list every cell-attr runtime type `createTypedArray` (sim.worker.ts) returns. A missing entry silently falls through to `'float64'`, mislabeling int32 buffers. Round-trips fine for some grid sizes, but constant-boundary's +1 sentinel makes attrs N+1 elements long, so 4(N+1) bytes is non-multiple-of-8 for ~half of all grid sizes — `new Float64Array(buffer)` throws `RangeError: byte length must be a multiple of 8` and `applySimulationState` (no try/catch around `deserializeTypedArray`) aborts the entire load silently. Failure mode: "click load, nothing happens" and the grid stays at the default state. When adding a new cell-attr type, register it in BOTH places at the same time.
- Save/load typed-array views: cell-attrs / colors / `orderArray` / `stopFlag` / `rngState` are all initialised as typed-array VIEWS over `wasmMemory` at baked-in offsets (see initGrid). Any restore handler that reads from a load message MUST copy into the existing view (`for i { dst[i] = src[i] }`) — never reassign the JS reference (`orderArray = new Int32Array(...)`). The WASM step reads through the baked-in memory offset, not the JS reference, so reassigning orphans WASM from JS-side mutations. orderArray hit this in 4d82145 and stayed latent until d581232's NI load fix made loads succeed for affected models — symptom was sequential cell iteration in async mode after load, producing strong directional bias in any rule that writes per-cell during the step.

### Busy / progress overlay — one indicator for every multi-second operation (branch `polishing`)

ONE shared indicator so a long operation always says what it is doing and that the app has not frozen. Store: [src/components/busyState.ts](src/components/busyState.ts) (module-level + pub/sub — the `graphState.ts` pattern, so `App`, `SimulatorView`, `FileMenu`, `ModelsLibrary` and any plain module can all call it with no prop drilling); component: [BusyOverlay.tsx](src/components/BusyOverlay.tsx), mounted ONCE in `App`. API: `beginBusy(label, {determinate?}) → { progress(fraction?, detail?), setLabel(), end() }`; `end()` is idempotent and order-independent.
- **THE PAINT-HONESTY RULE (the whole point).** A progress UI is worthless unless it PAINTS. An operation covered here must either be genuinely async (the work is in the worker, or it awaits) or be made to YIELD between chunks via **`yieldToPaint()`** — a MessageChannel round-trip, NOT `requestAnimationFrame` (rAF is part of the rendering steps, so it is suspended in a hidden/occluded tab and would stall a long encode forever *and* make the operation unverifiable in an automation pane). **Wrapping a still-synchronous block in `beginBusy`/`end` buys NOTHING** — the show-delay timer cannot even fire while the main thread is blocked.
- **`BUSY_SHOW_DELAY_MS` (150) applied uniformly**, so an operation that finishes promptly never flashes a bar. Measured in the real UI: a library-model fetch and four short GIF encodes correctly showed nothing.
- **Overlap policy**: entries are a STACK and the MOST RECENTLY begun visible one shows (the innermost, most specific thing). No queueing or merging.
- **`getBusySnapshot` returns a CACHED object** — `useSyncExternalStore` demands a stable reference, and rebuilding the view per call is an infinite render loop.
- **Covered operations.** Recording stop — **GIF is DETERMINATE** (`encodeFramesToGif` became `async`, taking `onProgress` + a `yieldBudgetMs` [default 16 ms]; the bar tracks frames encoded), WebM is indeterminate (streaming stop is a flush; the buffered path encodes at Stop). Worker reinit — `initWorkerWithDimensions` is the single funnel, so ONE handle covers **grid resize / manual Recompile / model load / image-import resize / CSV-import resize**, ended by the first `stepped`|`ready`|`error` from the fresh worker (`beginWorkerBusy`; ends any previous handle first, so back-to-back reinits cannot strand a bar, plus a 120 s safety net and an unmount teardown). Also: model file read/parse (FileMenu, drag-drop, PWA file handler, library card), `.gcastate` load, the paste-centred image import and the keep-grid CSV import. **A structural preset load** (the pre-existing `boundaryChanged || dimsChanged` predicate) announces itself; **a live parameter-only preset deliberately does NOT** (verified: no bar).
- **GIF byte-identity is STRUCTURAL, not luck** — all encoder state is in locals of `encodeFramesToGif`, the loop never mutates `frames`, and `stopRecording` clears `recordingRef` synchronously before awaiting, so no capture can append mid-encode. Guarded by [scripts/test-gif-encode-yield.mjs](scripts/test-gif-encode-yield.mjs) (21 checks): yield-every-frame AND the shipped 16 ms budget are byte-identical to `yieldBudgetMs: Infinity`, over a fixture that provably exercises the merge / delta-win / delta-reject / global-palette branches, plus a proof the event loop really does run during a yielding encode (and really does NOT without), and two negative controls.
- **⚠ The top-centre slot is SHARED** by the busy card, the load toast and the SW update banner — the latter two take `.loweredForBusy` while a card is up. That rule is **deliberately a doubled class** (`.loweredForBusy.loweredForBusy`): `.updateBanner` is declared later at equal specificity and won on ORDER, so the offset silently did nothing until the specificity was raised.

### Interruptible step batches (the high-G/F responsiveness fix — branch `updates`)

A `step` batch runs `count` generations back to back. At a high Gens/Frame that is SECONDS of uninterrupted work, and measuring it found **three separate costs**, only one of which was where it looked:

| | measured BEFORE | measured AFTER |
|---|---|---|
| Pause latency, WebGPU grid (MNCA 700², G/F 200, batch ≈ 3.2 s) | 1780 / 1595 / 1621 ms | **108 / 93 / 93 ms** |
| Pause latency, CPU grid (Amphiphile 500² async→WASM, batch ≈ 6.9 s) | **> 5000 ms** (probe timed out, 3/3) | **119 / 104 / 117 ms** |
| rAF during a WebGPU batch | **8–14 fps, max gap 2590 ms**, 15 gaps > 200 ms | **97 fps, max gap 94 ms, 0 > 200 ms** |
| Throughput cost | — | WebGPU **≈ +5 %** batch time; CPU **+0.3 %** (6859 → 6879 ms) |

- **RC1 — CONTROL LATENCY (every target).** Pause is main-thread state and a lower G/F is only read at the next `sendNextStep`, so both waited out the whole in-flight batch.
- **RC2 — FRAME STARVATION (WebGPU grid only).** With no stop event the WebGPU loop never awaited, so it ENCODED all `count` generations in a few ms and the GPU queue saturated; the browser could not composite for the entire batch, which is why the nav/transport bar itself felt frozen while **JS was only 4 % busy**. The CPU-target control (same batch length) showed 75 fps / 92 ms worst gap — that contrast is what identifies this half as GPU-specific, and it is why the fix needs GPU backpressure, not just a yield.
- **RC3 — a ~72 ms main-thread React commit per `setGeneration`** (canvas work in it: 11 ms of 5260 ms). NOT the reported regression and deliberately out of scope — it is *worse* at low G/F (67 % blocked at G/F 1 vs 27 % at G/F 200, since the commit is throttled to 10 Hz) — but it is the reason the worst rAF gap lands at ~90 ms rather than ~35 ms. Dev-build figure; a production build will be lower.

**The mechanism.** Every multi-generation batch loop now runs in **time-budgeted chunks** (`STEP_CHUNK_BUDGET_MS = 32`), yielding via `yieldToEventLoop()` — a **MessageChannel** round-trip, chosen over `setTimeout(0)` because it is a macrotask with no timer clamping (~0.05 ms vs 1–4 ms), which is what makes ~100 yields per multi-second batch cost nothing measurable. Four sites: the sync JS/WASM loop, the WebGPU grid loop, the per-gen agent-WebGPU loop, and the GPU-**resident** agent batch (sliced, so residency is preserved *within* a slice).
- **The WebGPU grid boundary is driven by SUBMISSION DEPTH, not wall time.** A wall-clock pacer never fires there (encoding is fast; the batch's whole duration is the GPU draining), so it drains every `gensPerDrain` generations with `device.queue.onSubmittedWorkDone()` — the backpressure IS the compositor fix. `gensPerDrain` is *measured*, not guessed: it extrapolates the previous drain's real cost to the budget, and instrumentation confirmed it converges to 2 generations / 34 ms on the 700² model (so a batch that fits in one chunk never drains at all).
- **A chunk boundary is NOT a batch boundary.** The indicator scan, the colour pass and the single `stepped` all still happen exactly once at the true end of the batch, so nothing an observer can see (chart history, end conditions, recording cadence, the Overseer) changes.
- **G/F 1 takes the literal old fully-synchronous path** (`msg.count > 1` gates the new one) — no promise, no deferral, no chunk bookkeeping.
- The deferral this arms is **not a new restriction**: in the old synchronous loop those same messages simply waited in the event loop until the batch's task ended, and `endAsyncStepBatch` replays them after `stepped` is posted — the same observable sequence.

**`cancelStep`** ([sim.worker.ts](src/simulator/engine/sim.worker.ts)) is the control-plane escape hatch, posted by SimulatorView when the user **pauses** (the single `useEffect([playing])` seam covers button / Enter / Esc / an end condition / a Stop Event) and when **G/F is LOWERED while playing** (only a decrease — raising it asks for more work). Two rules make it safe:
- **It is handled BEFORE the `asyncStepBatchInFlight` deferral guard** — deferring it would replay it after the very batch it was meant to shorten. Safe there precisely because it is pure control plane: it sets a flag the loops poll at chunk boundaries and touches no state.
- **An Overseer batch (`reqId` set) is never cancelled.** `ovRunGenerations` is a FIXED-count run (the ensemble's fixed developmental time point), so a short batch would silently bias the statistics. Verified: the replicate experiment is bit-identical across runs before and after (30 replicates, mean 263.2 / std 70.352 / min 149 / max 374), with 0 cancels posted.

**⚠️ THE NON-OBVIOUS HALF — a cancel must also DISCARD step batches already QUEUED.** The main thread can legitimately have **more than one** batch outstanding: *every* `sendColors()` posts a `stepped` — including ones from init / reset / a colour pass / a mutation — and the play loop's handler treats any `stepped` as "my batch finished", clearing `pendingStep` and issuing another step. Harmless while batches merely run back to back; but once a batch can be cancelled, that stale queued batch is replayed immediately afterwards and runs to completion. Measured symptom: a cancel correctly cut its own batch to 54 generations, then the simulation lurched **200 more generations over a 3.2 s stall** with the worker's event loop fully responsive the whole time (all pings 0 ms — which is what proved it was a queued message, not a block). So `cancelStep` filters `deferredDuringAsyncBatch`, dropping `step` messages **without** a `reqId` (Overseer batches are kept — the runtime awaits that exact reqId and would hang). Filtering *at the moment the cancel is processed* is what makes it precise: it removes exactly the batches issued under the intent the user just revoked, while a step arriving afterwards is the new intent and survives.

### Key Patterns
- Connected-handles pub/sub: graphState.ts exports `subscribeConnectedHandles` / `getConnectedHandlesForNode(id)` / `setConnectedHandlesFromEdges(edges)`. CaNode subscribes once via `useSyncExternalStore` instead of `useStore(edges)` per node. GraphEditor rebuilds the map in `useLayoutEffect([edges])`; rebuild is diff-aware (reuses Set identity for unchanged nodes) so only affected nodes re-render. Any future per-node derived data should follow this pattern. **The per-node set now records BOTH target (input, `input_*`) AND source (output, `output_*`) handle ids** — handle ids are kind-prefixed so the two never collide, and existing `input_*`-only consumers (`detectMissingConfig`, inline-widget visibility) are unaffected. The collapsed-port fan-out (below) reads the output entries too.
- CaNode `memo` uses reference equality on `data` (plus id/selected/dragging/parentId). React Flow's `updateNodeData` swaps only the mutated node's data ref, so other nodes skip re-render. Don't add deep comparators unless profiler demands.
- Node config validation: `src/modeler/vpl/nodes/nodeValidation.ts` exports `detectMissingConfig(nodeType, config, model)` returning issue strings. CaNode renders an amber `!` badge in the header when issues exist. New node types with required configs (attributeId, neighborhoodId, mappingId, indicatorId, tagName, etc.) MUST add a case to that switch — otherwise the compiler silently emits `_undef` placeholders.
- Vite dev server picks up new `public/<subdir>/` directories ONLY at startup. Adding a new folder (e.g. `public/macros/`) and fetching `/<subdir>/index.json` will return the SPA index.html until you restart the dev server.
- `window.confirm/prompt/alert` block `preview_eval` (the JS thread freezes; the eval times out and the page becomes unresponsive — even subsequent reload eval times out). Stub them BEFORE clicking buttons that trigger dialogs: `window.confirm = () => true; window.prompt = () => 'value'; window.alert = () => {};`. The "New" button in the navbar uses `window.confirm` for unsaved-changes prompts. Same trap applies to dispatching a synthetic `beforeunload` event — if the app's handler sets `e.returnValue = ''`, Chromium shows the real leave-site dialog and eval hangs. Assert the listener is wired via a different signal (e.g. track `addEventListener` calls) instead of dispatching the event.
- `preview_fill` (and plain `input.value = ...` assignment in eval) does NOT trigger React's `onChange` — React tracks the last-known value and skips the event if the setter wasn't the native one. Use the native setter + manual event: `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(HTMLInputElement.prototype, 'value').set.call(input, 'text'); input.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));` (or `'change'` for `<select>`). Otherwise the controlled component's state stays stale and submit buttons gated on non-empty fields remain disabled. For `<input type="file">`, neither of those paths works — build a `DataTransfer`, populate `.items.add(file)`, assign `input.files = dt.files`, then `dispatchEvent(new Event('change', { bubbles: true }))`.
- `preview_console_logs` returns a persistent buffer — it accumulates across page reloads and is NOT cleared by `console.clear()`. To verify whether a specific error is still firing after a fix, hook `console.error` fresh in an eval (push to `window.__newErrors` and reset), run the reproduction, then inspect `__newErrors`. Don't trust "errors found in logs" as current evidence.
- `preview_eval` that RETURNS a Promise serializes as `{}` (the resolved value is lost). Split async work into a fire-and-forget eval that stashes to `window.__x`, then read `window.__x` in a follow-up eval (the natural delay between tool calls covers the await).
- **Reproducing a model-specific / large-grid bug in the preview**: a `.gcaproj` stores grid DIMS as plain numbers (the grid itself isn't serialized) and the thumbnail is the file's bulk — so a faithful full-scale repro (e.g. 300×300×100 = 9M cells) is ~65 KB: `delete properties.thumbnail`, edit `gridWidth/Height/gridDepth` (+ `useWebGPU`), write to `public/models/`. Load it WITHOUT a dev-server restart via `fetch('/models/x.gcaproj').then(r=>r.text())` → inject into the FileMenu `<input type=file accept=".gcaproj,.json">` (DataTransfer + a `change` event); a restart is only needed for the library LIST (index.json), not direct file access. WebGPU bugs especially hide by SCALE (the dispatch limit blanks grids >4.2M cells) and by STATE (`gpuOwnsAttrs` is only true POST-step, so the readback-before-paint path is untested at gen 0) — repro at the real size AND after a step.
- `window.__sim3dPaint(layer,row,col)` IGNORES the `layer` arg for a z-plane brush — it paints on `plane3dRef.pos` (the brush-plane position). When verifying a 3D paint, check the painted cells at `plane.pos`, not the layer you passed.
- Never call another component's state dispatch (prop callback, dispatched action) inside a `setState(updater => {...})` function — React treats the updater as render work, so external dispatches fire mid-render and throw "Cannot update a component while rendering a different component". Clear your own state first (`setState(null)`), then compute and dispatch externally; track any value you need in a local ref so pointerup/async handlers don't race with async React state.
- Destructuring swap `[arr[i], arr[j]] = [arr[j], arr[i]]` fails strict-mode type checks because TS can't prove array access is defined, so each side resolves to `T | undefined`. Use a temp variable: `const tmp = arr[i]!; arr[i] = arr[j]!; arr[j] = tmp;`. Applies anywhere we swap array elements in-place.
- React Flow's `onPaneContextMenu` doesn't respond to plain `dispatchEvent('contextmenu')` because of internal pointer-event filtering. Tests that need to verify pane right-click menus should set state directly or rely on the source-level diff. Node right-click DOES work via dispatchEvent on the .react-flow__node element. Ctrl+click for multi-select and pointer-drag box-select ALSO don't fire via synthetic events — for tests that need multi-selection, mutate the nodes array directly (adding `selected: true`) or accept source-level review. React's `onMouseEnter`/`onMouseLeave` are synthesized from `mouseover` with `relatedTarget` tracking, so a naive `dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('mouseenter'))` doesn't fire them either. Escape hatch for any of these: grab the attached props via the internal key — `const props = el[Object.keys(el).find(k => k.startsWith('__reactProps$'))]` — then call `props.onMouseEnter?.({ currentTarget: el })` directly. React Flow CONNECTION drags (onConnectStart/onConnectEnd via XYHandle) also ignore synthetic pointer events — even invoking the handle's `__reactProps$` onPointerDown won't start a connection. Add a DEV-only `window.__<x>` hook that sets the resulting state directly (precedent: `window.__openConnectionDropMenu(origin,x,y)`, `window.__simWorker`).
- `fileOperations.ts` uses a custom `stringifyCompact` for .gcaproj output (coords, edges, and nodes are inlined per item). It MUST filter `undefined` object properties and map `undefined` array entries to `null` — matching native `JSON.stringify` — otherwise files emit `"key": undefined`, which is invalid JSON and breaks load. `readModelFile` has a recovery path that strips `"<key>": undefined` patterns for files saved by older buggy builds + strips a UTF-8 BOM + surfaces parse errors with `position N` and a 40-char snippet.
- Canvas chart components (`IndicatorSparkline` / `IndicatorMultiLineChart` / `IndicatorStackedAreaChart`) ALWAYS mount the outer `<div ref={wrapRef}>`; only the inner `<canvas>` is gated on data availability. Early-returning `null` when `data.length < 2` leaves `wrapRef.current` null when the mount-time width-measurement effect runs, `width` stays at 0 forever, and the chart never appears even after data grows (remounting via collapse/expand is what "fixes" it). A `useLayoutEffect` fallback re-measures width on renders where `ResizeObserver` was lazy (common when parent transitions from `display:none`).
- **NodeTypeDef.`requirements`** (`{ async?: boolean, variegated?: boolean }` in [types.ts](src/modeler/vpl/types.ts)) is the unified per-node capability gate — it REPLACED the old hardcoded `ASYNC_ONLY_TYPES` set. `detectCapabilityRequirements` + `isNodeAvailable` in [nodeValidation.ts](src/modeler/vpl/nodes/nodeValidation.ts) drive: palette filtering, Add-Node menu, connection-drop menu (all hide nodes the current model can't satisfy), and the CaNode amber badge on already-placed violators. The compiler reads `def.requirements.async` directly. Async-only nodes (6): `setNeighborhoodAttribute`, `setNeighborAttributeByIndex`, `markCellUpdated`, `setFacingOrientation`, `setNeighborOrientationByIndex`, `moveSelfToNeighbor` — compiler emits an error if used in sync mode. (The neighbor-write ones would have copy lines overwrite neighbor writes; `markCellUpdated` has no scheduling meaning under parallel sync updates.) `getNeighborAttributeByIndex` is read-only and works in both modes. Both `setNeighborAttributeByIndex` and `getNeighborAttributeByIndex` accept an array index input (loops over all elements / takes element 0 respectively) — never coerce array→scalar via `(arr | 0)` because it silently returns 0 for any multi-element or empty array.
- Mark Cell Updated flag (`markCellUpdated` node, async-only): writes `1` into a per-cell Uint8 region at `layout.skippedOffset` (allocated `total` bytes, view in worker as `skippedArray`). The async cell loop emit injects `if (_skipped[idx] !== 0) continue;` at the top of every iteration (JS) and `i32.load8_u offset=skippedOffset` + `br 1` from inside `ifThen` (WASM — increment outerCounter BEFORE the `br` so the loop doesn't spin on the skipped cell). Worker clears the array via `.fill(0)` at the top of every step (transient, not persisted to save state). Also added `_skipped` to `buildLoopParams` after `order` so the JS step signature matches. WebGPU rejects the node automatically via `requirements.async` since async mode itself is rejected on the WebGPU target.
- JoinNeighbors is multi-output (`result` NI array + `count` scalar), same shape as FilterNeighbors. Both ops (union + intersection) now use the multi-output `_v<id>_result` / `_v<id>_count` variable convention in JS; the union path used to emit `const _v<id>` (single-output) and is now consistent. Scratch is allocated unconditionally for both ops (was intersection-only). `isMultiOutput()` in `compile.ts` includes `joinNeighbors`. WASM array emitter caches the count port via `setCachedPort(ctx, id, 'count', { localIdx: outLenLocal, valtype: I32 })`; WebGPU emitter caches via `setCachedPort(ctx, id, 'count', { expr: out.lenName, type: 'i32' })`. Both targets also expose a value-emitter entry that calls `compileArrayNode` then returns the cached count, mirroring filterNeighbors' dispatch.
- Neighbor-write nodes use `if (_ni < total)` guard to protect constant-boundary sentinel from corruption
- Graph state sync: single debounced sync (100ms) via refs — never use multiple setTimeout callbacks
- Graph editor mouse: RMB click=context menu, RMB drag=pan (`panOnDrag={[2]}`), LMB click=select, LMB drag=box select (`selectionOnDrag`); simulator: LMB=brush, RMB=pan
- **Ctrl-drag alignment guides** (PowerPoint-style): hold Ctrl/Cmd while dragging any node/comment/group and it snaps so its edges/center line up with nearby nodes, with dashed guide lines. Pure geometry lives in [alignmentSnap.ts](src/modeler/vpl/alignmentSnap.ts) (`computeAlignmentSnap(movingUnionBox, targets, thresholdFlow) → {dx,dy,guides}` + `sameGuides` diff); GraphEditor's `handleNodesChange` runs it (gated on `ctrlHeldRef`, which a window keydown/keyup listener tracks — mouse-move events don't carry the modifier) BEFORE the group-drag intercept so a snapped group position propagates to members, applies dx/dy to every moving `position` change, and over­rides the 20px grid rounding while engaged. Anchors on the UNION bbox of the moving node(s) so multi-selections align their outer box. Guides render in `<AlignmentGuidesOverlay>` (a child of `<ReactFlow>`) which subscribes to the live viewport `transform` via `useStore` and maps flow→screen as `flow*zoom+translate` (verified pixel-exact). Threshold is `ALIGN_SNAP_PX(6)/zoom` so it feels constant at any zoom. **Note:** the board's `multiSelectionKeyCode="Control"` means a Ctrl+drag also runs RF's add-to-selection on the grabbed node (pre-existing RF behavior; harmless for the single-node case — the node still drags via `getDragItems`' `node.id === nodeId`). React Flow node drags can't be driven by synthetic pointer events (verify the pure function via `import('/src/modeler/vpl/alignmentSnap.ts')` in `preview_eval` instead).
- Shared mutable state: `graphState.ts` holds module-level variables (`isConnectingGlobal`, `showPortLabelsGlobal`, `connectingFrom`) to avoid circular imports between GraphEditor↔CaNode
- Module globals that drive memoized React components (e.g. `showPortLabelsGlobal` → CaNode): wire them through `useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, snapshot)` with a `Set<() => void>` listener list; setters must notify listeners. Without pub/sub, memoized consumers don't re-render on toggle and the global can drift out of sync with local React state across remounts.
- Canvas view toggles (port labels / background grid / snap-to-grid) persist via `graphState.ts` module globals (`showPortLabelsGlobal` / `showGridGlobal` / `snapEnabledGlobal`) with localStorage write-through (`genesisca_graph_view_settings`). GraphEditor seeds its useState from the globals (it unmounts on every Modeler↔Simulator tab switch) and each toggle writes both the local state and the global. New view settings should join this block, not plain `useState(default)`.
- **Modeler panel/layout state survives tab switches** via the same module-global pattern: [modelerUiState.ts](src/modeler/modelerUiState.ts) holds a single mutable snapshot (`activePanel`, `activeRightPanel`, `lastLeftPanel`, `lastRightPanel`, `selectedByPanel`). `ModelerView` is conditionally rendered in App.tsx (UNMOUNTED when the user switches to the Simulator / another top-level tab), so without this its useState would reset every time. ModelerView seeds those five useState from the snapshot on mount and writes them all back in one `useEffect` on every change, so which left tab is focused, which side panels are open, and which item is being edited in each all persist across a Simulator round-trip. In-memory only (resets on full page reload, like graph viewport's runtime parts). Any new ModelerView layout useState should join this snapshot, not be a plain `useState(default)`.
- Connection validation: `isValidConnection` on ReactFlow prevents flow↔value, self-connections, occupied value inputs, and cycles (BFS from target)
- Connection highlighting: `connectingFrom` in graphState stores `{ category, kind, nodeId }`. CaNode checks BOTH category match AND opposite direction (`kind !== 'input'` for input ports, `kind !== 'output'` for output ports).
- Port labels render outside nodes (absolute positioned left/right of handles); controlled by `showPortLabelsGlobal` toggle
- **Flow ports = right-pointing triangles (Unreal-blueprint style)**: `.handleFlow` ([CaNode.module.css](src/modeler/vpl/CaNode.module.css)) uses `clip-path: polygon(0% 0%, 100% 50%, 0% 100%)` + `border-radius:0` + a dark `drop-shadow` outline (a real `border` would be clipped into the triangle). Both input AND output flow handles point right (flow runs left→right). `clip-path` clips `box-shadow`, so the magenta compatibility glow is re-expressed as a `drop-shadow` filter via the compound selector `.handleFlow.handleCompatible` (covers connection-drag + panel-drag highlight). Value ports stay round. Reroute flow relays inherit the triangle (they reuse `caStyles.handleFlow`).
- **Main flow ports pinned to the header centre**: the primary flow input (`mainFlowIn` = the single flow-category input) and primary flow output (`mainFlowOut` = the `next` port, else the first flow output — covers Step/InitEvent/OutputMapping roots + Sequence's FIRST) are rendered by `renderMainFlowHandle` ([CaNode.tsx](src/modeler/vpl/CaNode.tsx)) INSIDE the `position:relative` header (`style top:50%` → header centre, robust to the optional userLabel/header height). The body port maps iterate `bodyInputPorts`/`bodyOutputPorts` (the full lists minus the two lifted ports), so the data ports + branch flow ports (THEN/ELSE/BODY/CASE_N…) reindex from body row 0 and `maxPorts` (height) is computed on the body arrays. Result: one exec-in pin top-left + one exec-out pin top-right at header level (a horizontal through-line), everything else below — the UE blueprint layout. Value-only nodes (no flow ports) are unchanged. Collapsed nodes still collapse all handles to `top:50%`.
- **Body-port spacing is uniform across ALL node types** (`PORT_TOP_BASE = 30 + (userLabel ? USER_LABEL_HEIGHT : 0)`, `portSpacing = 22` in [CaNode.tsx](src/modeler/vpl/CaNode.tsx)). `isCompact` (step/conditional/sequence) now ONLY drives the `compactNode` min-width class — it no longer tightens port spacing/base. (Before: compact nodes used base 24 / spacing 16, which — once the main flow ports moved to the header — left Conditional's THEN/ELSE and Sequence's THEN/Then-N sitting higher and closer together than the identical branch ports on Loop/ForEach/Switch. Unifying the grid makes every node's Nth body port land on the same row.) **`USER_LABEL_HEIGHT = 21`**: body-port handles are absolutely positioned from the NODE's top, so a rename's `.userLabel` strip (height ≈21px, measured) shifts the header+body down — without adding that to the base, the data/branch ports ride UP onto the header and overlap the main flow pins (the reported "renamed node ports conjoined" bug). The main flow pins need no adjustment — they're inside the header (`top:50%`) and move with it.
- **Palette flow-port previews are green triangles too**: `.previewDotFlow` ([PalettePanelContent.module.css](src/modeler/panels/PalettePanelContent.module.css)) overrides the round `.previewDot` with the same `clip-path` triangle + `#4caf50` fill as the canvas `.handleFlow`, so the Palette's VISUAL mini-previews (NodePreview) match what lands on the graph. (It previously used the warm-yellow theme token `--color-port-flow` as a circle.) Value-port previews keep the grey Blender-socket circle. The preview is a row-based schematic, so it does NOT lift the main flow ports into the header (canvas-only layout).
- Inline port widgets: stored in node config as `_port_${portId}` keys; compiler reads via `getInlineValue()` helper
- Node collapse: `isCollapsed` flag in node data. Collapsed nodes **fan their CONNECTED handles** out vertically around the node centre at a tight 11px spacing (`spreadTop()` in [CaNode.tsx](src/modeler/vpl/CaNode.tsx)) so the user can still tell which wire lands on which port without expanding; UNconnected handles stay stacked at `top: 50%` (they're only drag targets). The connected set is read from the connected-handles pub/sub (which now carries output handles too). Because the spread shifts handle positions WITHOUT a node-size change, CaNode calls `useUpdateNodeInternals(id)` whenever it's collapsed and the connected set (or collapse state) changes — otherwise React Flow wouldn't re-measure handle bounds and edges would render to stale positions. `isConnectingGlobal` triggers hover-to-uncollapse. The hover-expand is **disambiguation only** (`onMouseEnter`): it force-expands the collapsed node only when the COMPATIBLE side has >1 category-matching port (inputs when the drag origin is an output, outputs when it's an input). A single compatible port → no expand (releasing on the collapsed node lands on it directly), so approaching e.g. a one-input action node with a wire no longer pops it open.
- **Config-driven port-set changes re-measure handle bounds** ([CaNode.tsx](src/modeler/vpl/CaNode.tsx)): a node whose visible ports change via `hiddenPorts`/dynamic-port config — Vector Op's `op` (add `[a,b]` → scale `[a,s]`, or add → dot swapping the `result`→`value` OUTPUT), Get Agent Position's `mode`, Switch/Sequence dynamic ports — can keep the node HEIGHT the same, so React Flow's ResizeObserver never fires and the newly-shown handle keeps STALE/absent bounds → it silently **rejects connections** until something else forces a remeasure (the reported "Vector Op input port sometimes won't accept input" bug — H3-confirmed by the `vectorop-input-bug` workflow: NOT a validation issue, the connection paths resolve the ports fine). Fixed by a `useEffect` keyed on the visible port-id signature (`inputPorts`+`outputPorts` ids) that calls `updateNodeInternals(id)` on every port-set change — one place covering every config-driven port change (distinct from the collapsed-fan-out effect above, which handles the connected-set case).
- Group node RMB passthrough: CSS `:global(.react-flow__node-groupNode) { pointer-events: none !important; }` with `[data-drag-handle]` re-enabled
- Context menu: pane menu uses hover submenu (`.contextSubmenuTrigger` > `.contextSubmenu`); paste uses `pasteFlowPos` ref for right-click position
- ReactFlowProvider lifted to ModelerView (not inside GraphEditor) so NodeExplorer can access useReactFlow/useStore
- Simulator overlays: ALL overlay elements on the canvas (stats, transport bar, viewer bar, zoom controls, panel expand buttons) MUST have `data-sim-overlay` attribute. Mousedown handler sets `canvasBrushActive` flag; mousemove brush painting checks this flag to prevent accidental painting when interacting with overlays.
- Hide React Flow's persistent selection rect: CSS `:global(.react-flow__nodesselection-rect) { display: none !important; }`
- Groups use React Flow's native `parentId` — auto-resize requires manual bounding box computation in `handleNodesChange`
- Use `NodeResizer` for resizable nodes (comments, groups) — CSS `resize: both` conflicts with React Flow drag. NodeResizer updates `node.measured.width/height` and top-level `node.width/height` on resize end — NOT `node.style.width/height`. To persist across save/load: (1) `toRFNodes` seeds `rfNode.style = { width, height }` from `data` for the initial render, (2) the resizer's `onResizeEnd` callback writes back to `data` via `updateNodeData`, and (3) `toGraphNodes` reads `measured.width ?? node.width ?? style.width` (measured wins) when serializing. Without all three, mid-session resizes are lost on save.
- MacroNode, MacroInputNode, MacroOutputNode are hidden from Add Node menu via `HIDDEN_FROM_MENU` set
- Undo/redo: `graphHistory.ts` module-level undo/redo stacks (max 50 snapshots). Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y redo. Snapshot pushed BEFORE each mutation. History cleared on scope change.
- `isMultiOutput()` helper in compile.ts replaces raw `MULTI_OUTPUT_TYPES.has()` — also checks `getModelAttribute` with `isColorAttr` config
- CaNode config: NEVER call `updateConfig()` twice in sequence — second call uses stale `nodeData.config`, losing the first update. Instead, build the merged config object and call `updateNodeData(id, { ...nodeData, config: newConfig })` once.
- CSS gotcha: `flex: 1` on buttons inside flex-column containers causes them to stretch vertically. Remove `flex: 1` from buttons that should have fixed height.
- Nullish coalescing: never mix `??` with `||` or comparison operators without explicit parens — Babel/esbuild will warn or error.
- Simulator lifecycle: SimulatorView is always-mounted (wrapped in `display:none` div when not visible). Simulation auto-pauses when leaving the tab. Canvas redraws via `requestAnimationFrame` when `visible` transitions to true. The `useEffect([model, compileModel])` fires on every model change (even while hidden), handling full reinit or soft recompile as appropriate. When `model.indicators` changes during soft recompile, an `updateIndicators` message is sent to the worker alongside the `recompile` message.
- Simulator save integration: FileMenu dispatches `genesis-capture-sim-state` CustomEvent with `detail.resolve` callback. SimulatorView captures worker state via `getState` and calls `resolve()` after `setSimulationState()`. FileMenu `await`s the Promise before serializing. 5-second safety timeout.
- Copy/paste: Ctrl+C/V/X + context menu. Strips macroInput/macroOutput, remaps IDs. **The clipboard SPANS BROWSER TABS** — see the "Cross-tab graph clipboard" section below.
- Group paste: parentId must be remapped to new IDs, children keep relative positions, groups sorted before children
- React StrictMode double-mount: effects run mount→cleanup→mount in dev. When terminating resources (Web Workers), always null out the ref (`workerRef.current = null`) after `.terminate()` so the second mount detects it needs a fresh init instead of reusing a dead reference.
- Indicator values use a ref (`indicatorValuesRef`) not React state — avoids extra re-renders on every worker step message. The existing `setGeneration` re-render reads the ref naturally.
- Linked indicator aggregation is always post-loop (not in-loop) to avoid async mode single-buffer corruption where mid-loop reads see a mix of old and new cell values.
- Neighborhood tags: `Neighborhood.tags?: Record<number, string>` maps coord index to tag name. Tags are optional per-cell labels for neighbor positions. **Tag keys are coord-array INDICES** — any code that removes coords MUST remap surviving tags or later tags silently shift onto the wrong cells. `toggleCellsChanges` in [NeighborhoodsPanelContent.tsx](src/modeler/panels/NeighborhoodsPanelContent.tsx) is the single batch-toggle helper that does this (the one-cell Point click routes through it too).
- Neighborhood shape tools (Point/Circle/Ring/Line in the grid editor): tool + paint mode (mark/unmark/toggle) + symmetry toggles (**h/v/d/d2** — horizontal, vertical, main-diagonal `r↔c`, anti-diagonal `r,c→-c,-r`; any three generate the full 8-fold D4) + staged clicks + hover live in component state; pure helpers `annulusCells` (euclidean disc/ring, clipped to margin box) / `lineCells` (integer Bresenham) / `shapeCells` / `expandSymmetry` (mirror closure over the enabled mirrors, mirrors of in-grid cells stay in-grid so no clipping) compute the affected set; everything applies through `applyCellsChanges(nbh, cells, mode)` as ONE updateNeighborhood (`cellEffect` decides add/remove/none per covered cell; a covered center drives `includeCentralCell` by the same mode; tag-index remap on removal lives here). Hover preview is outcome-split: `.gridCellPreviewAdd` (accent tint — visible on empty), `.gridCellPreviewRemove` (dim + warm outline — visible on filled), `.gridCellPreview` (covered no-op, faint outline); staged anchors `.gridCellStaged`; right-click cancels staging (falls through to the tag right-click only when nothing is staged). Center cell fills like a normal cell with a persistent inset ring (`.gridCellCenter`/`.gridCellCenterIncluded`).
- `inputToSources` (plural) map in compile.ts: collects ALL edges targeting the same value port. Used for multi-connection `isArray` ports on Aggregate node.
- Connection validation: `isValidConnection` allows multiple edges to the same target handle when the target port has `isArray: true`.
- Switch node dynamic ports: case output ports generated from `caseCount` + `case_N_value` config keys, similar to macro dynamic ports.
- Context menu: clamped to viewport bounds via `useLayoutEffect` + ref measurement after render. Initial render with `visibility: hidden`.
- Modeler PanelShell: resizable via drag handle on right edge (200-600px range). Pattern matches simulator right panel.
- Group shrink-to-fit: `resizeGroupsToFit(nds, allowShrink)` runs on graph load with `allowShrink=true`. Prevents stale bloated groups.
- Input drag fix: `stopDrag` callback checks `e.button === 0` (LMB only) to allow RMB pan through nodes. `stopAll` stops all buttons (for double-click). Body div uses `onDoubleClick={stopAll}` to prevent collapse; inline widgets use both `onMouseDown={stopDrag}` and `onDoubleClick={stopAll}`.
- Compiler: in `compileFlowChain`, EVERY `varName()` call MUST be preceded by `compileValueNode(source.nodeId)` to ensure the value variable is declared. This applies to ALL flow node handlers (conditional, loop, switch, regular). Missing this causes undefined variables at runtime.
- Model element cleanup: `ModelContext.tsx` reducer uses `patchAllNodes()` / `clearDeletedId()` helpers to update node configs when attributes/neighborhoods/mappings/indicators are deleted. Tag option deletion remaps indices in getConstant, switch, and setAttribute nodes. Always scan both `graphNodes` and `macroDefs[*].nodes`.
- Graph nodes are heterogeneous: comment nodes (`type: 'commentNode'`) have `data: { text }` and group nodes have `data: { label, width, height, nodeType: 'group', config: {} }`. Any code iterating `model.graphNodes` must guard against `n.data.config` being undefined (e.g., `patchNodes` in ModelContext).
- **Comment node editing** ([CommentNodeComponent.tsx](src/modeler/vpl/CommentNodeComponent.tsx)): the textarea is INERT (`readOnly`, `pointer-events: none`) until the user **double-clicks** to edit — only then does it get the `nodrag` class so native click-drag and shift-click text selection work (without `nodrag`, React Flow's drag swallows the pointer and selection is impossible). `onBlur` exits edit mode. A NEW comment (Add Comment from the context menu) is created `selected: true` with `data.autoEdit: true`; CaNode's effect focuses + select-all's the textarea and clears the one-shot flag via `updateNodeData(autoEdit: undefined)` so it never persists into a saved graph.
- Switch node: two modes (`conditions` = user-wired bool inputs per case; `value` = comparison ops per case with int/float/tag/**neighborIndex** types). `firstMatchOnly` toggle: true = if/else-if chain, false = independent if blocks with `_sw{id}` guard variable. Tag mode uses equality against tag index; int/float mode uses configurable comparison op (==,!=,>,<,>=,<=). **`neighborIndex` value type** (CaNode dynamic ports): the `value` port and each `case_N_val` port are WIRED (no inline widget — there's no packed-NI editor), equality-only (no op dropdown). Needs NO compiler change — it routes through the existing non-tag `value`-mode path: JS emits `===`, WASM compares as F64 (exact for all i32 NIs), WebGPU casts to i32. Wire NI sources (Get All Neighbor Indexes → Get Array Element, Neighbor Index From Tag/Offset, Get Facing Orientation, …) into the cases.
- Compare node (`statement`): a `compareType` config (`numerical` default / `bool` / `tag` / `neighborIndex`) swaps the inline operand widgets (CaNode extends the same dynamic `effectiveWidget` swap used by setAttribute-family: bool→`InlineBoolSelect`, tag→`InlineTagSelect` from the node's own `tagAttributeId`, neighborIndex→no widget/wired, numerical→number). Non-numerical types restrict the op dropdown to ==/!=, and changing the type resets `_port_x`/`_port_y`/`_port_y2` to type defaults. No emit change for numerical/bool/tag (`getInlineValue`/`parseInlineNum` already coerce `true`/`false`→1/0 and tag-index strings→numbers, and small ints are exact in f64/f32); neighborIndex adds an i32-equality branch in WebGPU only (JS `===` and WASM F64 are already exact for NIs). `nodeValidation` requires `tagAttributeId` when `compareType==='tag'`. Collapsed-node title formats the inline operands by `compareType` (`fmtOperand` in CaNode's collapsed block): tag→the `tagOptions` NAME (not the index), bool→`True`/`False` — mirrors Get Constant's collapsed resolution.
- PanelShell `side` prop: `'left'` (default) puts resize handle on right edge; `'right'` puts it on left edge with inverted drag math. NodeExplorer uses `side="right"`. Simulator left panel has its own resize handle (`.leftPanelResizeHandle`).
- **Show Code emits a PORT-READY MODEL DOCUMENT, not just the compiled functions** ([showCode.ts](src/simulator/showCode.ts) `buildModelDocument(model, result, opts)`, wrapped by SimulatorView's `referenceSourceFor` + the single `refreshShowCode` call site). The old `buildFullCode` concatenated the step + inputColor + outputMapping bodies with section headers — but those functions are **NOT self-sufficient**: they are the *rule*, and the WORKER supplies everything around them, so a reader could not port the model. The document is three parts: **(1) MODEL DEFINITION** — grid geometry + the flat index convention, the per-attribute typed-array table (storage/default/boundary/sub-attribute rules), model-attribute CURRENT values (live when available), **the full dense contents of every lookup table** with its axis dims/mins/strides, the neighbourhood offset lists + the table-build algorithm (torus wrap / constant sentinel), the NI codec, variegation, colours/viewers, the RNG spec, the indicator slot order, stop events + end conditions, and for agent models the RESOLVED centerBased physics + the agent SoA + bond/field attribute tables; **(2) DRIVER SKELETON** — a generated `init()` / `reset()` / `runGeneration()` outline of the engine's call order and buffer discipline (sync swap vs async order-shuffle + the three schemes, sub-attr scrub, when the colour pass / indicators / stop flag run) plus, for agents, the full per-generation phase order with the force LAWS written out (soft-sphere `mu*(d-s)*rhat` with `s = r_i + r_j`, cutoff/global charge, per-bond springs, the integrator, positional projection, the structural phase + the bond request-queue lane encoding). **Only the branches the model actually takes are emitted**; **(3) COMPILED FUNCTIONS** — unchanged, each preceded by a numbered table naming every argument.
  - **THE DISCIPLINE (C1): every displayed fact comes from the function that ENFORCES it.** Signatures come from the REAL emit builders — `buildLoopParams` / `buildCellParams` / **`buildOutputMappingParams`** (the OM list was inline at its compile site and was extracted into that exported function; the extraction is byte-identical, `check-compile-identity` 29/29) — so the parameter documentation can never drift; table geometry/data from `resolveAxes` + `buildLookupTablePayload`, stored values from `encodeAttrValue`, agent physics from `resolveMaxBonds` / `effectiveAgentDt` / `chargeParamsOf` / `layoutIterationsOf` / `collisionMode` / `usesEngineSprings|Growth` / `agentMotionMode` / `resolveAgentFieldGates`, agent signatures from `buildAgentAbiParams(kind, agentAbiShapeOf(model))`. **NEVER hand-write a parallel param list or re-derive a resolved value here.** Note the doc therefore shows the RESOLVED number, not the raw field (Boids stores `maxBonds: 2` but its Bonds capability is off, so the document correctly reads `0 (no bond store allocated)`).
  - **`computeDefaultModelAttrs` moved out of SimulatorView** into [modelAttrDefaults.ts](src/model/modelAttrDefaults.ts) so the document's fallback values come from the SAME resolver the worker seeds from (the doc prefers the LIVE `runtimeModelAttrs` and falls back to it).
  - The agent bundle reaches the document through `agentCodeRef` + `refreshShowCode(model, result, agentResult)`, re-run at BOTH compile sites right after `compileAgentModel` (the init path compiles cells first, so the first pass would otherwise show only the cell half).
  - **Acid-tested**: the generated Game of Life document was ported by hand into a from-scratch Node driver (geometry, storage, the neighbour-table build, the 16-argument order, the sync swap — all transcribed from the document alone) and matched an INDEPENDENT hand-written Conway implementation **cell-for-cell over 3 generations on a 300² torus, 0 mismatches**, including a deliberate torus-seam cluster. Nothing was missing.
  - `.codeBlock`'s `max-height` went 250px → `max(250px, 50vh)` — the document runs to thousands of lines and 250px was a keyhole.
- `inlineWidget: 'number'` ports on `setAttribute` / `updateAttribute` / `setNeighborhoodAttribute` / `setNeighborAttributeByIndex` / **`setAgentAttribute` / `setAgentsAttribute`** (the by-id agent writers) can carry `'true'`/`'false'` strings in config: CaNode dynamically swaps the rendered widget to a bool `<select>` (or a tag `<select>` from the picked attribute's `tagOptions`) when the chosen attribute is bool/tag, but the static port def stays `'number'`. The swap membership is a **hardcoded nodeType OR-chain in [CaNode.tsx](src/modeler/vpl/CaNode.tsx)** (~`effectiveWidget`, keyed on `port.id === 'value'`) — add a node type there to give it the type-adaptive value widget; the target attribute resolves via the graph-aware `ownAttrList` (= `model.agentAttributes` on the Agents graph, so the agent-only by-id writers resolve their AGENT attribute automatically). A neighborIndex/color/vector attribute falls to the `else → undefined` arm (wired-only, no widget). `getInlineValue` must map `'true'→'1'` / `'false'→'0'` BEFORE `parseFloat` (matching `parseInlineNum`) — otherwise NaN falls back to `defaultValue '0'` and every model that writes a bool attr via the inline widget breaks on ALL THREE targets (JS/WASM/WebGPU all chain through `getInlineValue` / the per-target `getInlineNum` clones, which key off the STATIC `'number'` inlineWidget and already accept `'true'`/`'false'`/tag-index — so the swap is **editor-only, no compiler change**). `setAgentsAttribute`'s array `agents` port is untouched (the swap only targets `value`).
- Inline `<input type="number">` widgets MUST set `step="any" lang="en" inputMode="decimal"`. Default `step="1"` makes decimals step-invalid; on some Chromium/locale combinations `.value` returns `""` for `0.2`-style entries → `getInlineValue` falls back to `defaultValue '0'` → "always-true" comparison bug (Compare's `>= 0.2` was the canonical reproducer).
- `onConnectEnd` signature in xyflow v12 is `(event, connectionState)`. `connectionState.toHandle == null` is the canonical "released not on a port" signal — works for releases on the pane AND on a node body. If onConnectEnd sets context-menu state (e.g., the connection-drop compatible-nodes menu), beware: the same LMB-up that fires onConnectEnd ALSO fires the editor wrapper's synthesized `click`, which closes the menu the moment it opens. Use a one-shot `suppressNextEditorClickRef` flag set in onConnectEnd and consumed by the wrapper's onClick.
- **Searchable connection-drop menu** (drag a wire onto empty canvas → compatible-nodes menu): a focused `.contextSearch` input + a persistent keyboard selection (`dropMenuSelIdx`) over the flat `dropMenuItems` list (Reroute first when origin is an output, then compatible nodes grouped by category). Same quick-add UX as the Palette: typing re-anchors the selection to the best LABEL match (prefix→substring→0), ↑/↓ wraps, mouse-move syncs, Enter → `commitDropMenuItem` (→ `addRerouteAndConnect` / `addNodeAndConnect`), Esc closes. The compatibility filter (`HIDDEN_FROM_DROP_MENU`, step/init singletons, `isNodeAvailable`, `nodeHasCompatiblePort`) is unchanged — search is layered on top. Items are flat with interleaved `.contextCategory` headers (flat index drives ↑/↓). **This same search/keyboard UI is now shared with the pane quick-add menu** (Spacebar / blank-canvas right-click) via the `renderQuickAddSearch` helper and the dual-target `dropMenuItems` / `commitDropMenuItem` — see "Unified add-node menu" above; the connection-drop branch just adds a `.contextTitle` and passes a wire origin (Reroute + compatibility filter), the pane branch passes no origin. DEV-only `window.__openConnectionDropMenu(origin,x,y)` test hook exists because React Flow's connection drag ignores synthetic pointer events (same limitation as box-select — see the synthetic-event gotchas).
- A new flow-control node with DYNAMIC flow outputs (Switch-style `case_N`, Sequence-style `then_N`) requires edits in ALL of: NodeTypeDef (+ defaultConfig counter), CaNode dynamic-port derivation + +/- UI, [effectivePorts.ts](src/modeler/vpl/effectivePorts.ts) (consumed by panel-drag + connection-drop helpers), `compile.ts` × 2 sites (compileInnerFlow + compileFlowChain), `wasm/compile.ts` × 2 sites (compileFlowChain + visitFlow), `webgpu/compile.ts` × 3 sites (preEmitValueNodes + compileFlowChain + analyzeAlwaysWritten), and `sinkAnalysis.ts` if the node belongs in `TRANSPARENT_FLOW_TYPES`.
- **Flow pass-through port (`next` — NEXT/DONE)**: every flow-input node except `sequence` + macro boundaries/instances has a static `next` flow OUTPUT in its def.ports (label NEXT on action nodes — their only output; label DONE on conditional/loop/forEachInArray/switch — rendered FIRST/top among outputs, aligned with the flow input so chains stay horizontal; the def lists `next` before the branch ports, and a CaNode+effectivePorts reorder re-hoists it to the FRONT above switch's dynamic `case_N`). Port order is purely visual — the compilers look ports up by id, so reordering is free. Semantics: targets run right after the node / after the whole construct, at the SAME scope, before the parent port's next sibling (depth-first, UE-style); `A.next → B` compiles byte-identically to `parent → [A, B]` fan-out on all three targets. Hooks (see [docs/IMPACT_MAP_FLOW_PASSTHROUGH.md](docs/IMPACT_MAP_FLOW_PASSTHROUGH.md)): each compiler's `compileFlowChain` walks `next` at the end of the per-target dispatch (+ the switch `caseCount===0` `continue` paths in WASM/WebGPU); `sinkAnalysis`/`volatileHoist` walk `next` at parentScope (transparent — no new scope); `asyncWriteHazard` walks it with prefix = entry ∪ own-writes (actions) / entry ∪ branch-body writes (control nodes) — its `writesInSubtree` covers next-subtrees automatically via the `${nodeId}:` prefix scan; WASM `visitFlow` + WebGPU `preEmitValueNodes` recurse into `next` (safe for forEach — the next chain is OUTSIDE the loop); WebGPU `analyzeAlwaysWritten` unions `next` for every target type (a loop's body gives no guarantee but its DONE chain always runs). A forEach with NO array wired skips body AND DONE (`continue` on both compilers). Any new flow-walk MUST handle `next` or chained nodes silently vanish from that analysis.
- **Loop `index` output (all compile surfaces)**: the Loop node exposes its 0-based iteration counter as an `index` value output — body-only scope, exactly like ForEachInArray's `element`/`index`. Per-surface wiring: **JS** `varName` maps `loop.index` → the `_li<id>` for-counter + the loop flow-emit activates the forEach-style body-emit context (`findElementDependents(node.id, ['index'])`); **sinkAnalysis** registers `loop` in `elementDependentsByForEach` and `hoistPastLoops` now consults it for `loopBody` scopes too (index-dependents stay pinned inside the loop; everything else still hoists past); **loopInvariant** `NEVER_INVARIANT` includes `loop` (its Count input is typically invariant, so the composite rule would otherwise hoist index consumers to the function preamble where `_li` is undefined); **WASM** caches the counter local via `setCachedPort(node.id, 'index')` inside the loop (mirrors forEach); **WebGPU** `loopIndexRef` mints the counter's WGSL name ON DEMAND (cached on the node's `index` port) so consumers compiled during `preEmitValueNodes` and the later `for (var …)` declaration agree — their `let`s flush inside the loop via the loopBody sink scope; **agentWasm/agentWebgpu** use a `loopStack` frame (mirrors `forEachStack`), seed `loop` in `computeVolatile` (consumers re-emit per iteration) and list it in `AGENT_VALUE_NO_HOIST`; **overseer** `refFor` resolves `_l<id>` with a `loopScopes` in-body guard (outside use = compile error). Index used outside the BODY chain is undefined-behaviour parity with forEach (JS ReferenceError / WGSL unknown identifier). **Range mode** (`config.mode: 'count' | 'range'`, default `'count'`): `hiddenPorts` swaps the Count port for `from`/`to` integer inputs, and the counter runs **From..To INCLUSIVE** (ascending; From > To = zero iterations) on every surface — JS `for (let _li = (from)|0, _liEnd = (to)|0; _li <= _liEnd; …)` (the `|0` matches the WASM/WebGPU i32 truncation), WASM `li = from` + exit-on-`OP_I32_GT_S` (count keeps `GE_S`), WGSL `for (var li = from; li <= to; …)`, agent compilers + overseer mirror it. COUNT-mode byte-identity is guarded by resolve-before-alloc ordering (WASM: the bound ref resolves BEFORE `li`/`lc` are allocated; agentWebgpu: the bound resolves before `fresh('lpI')` mints the counter — a lazily-compiled bound source mints its own locals/names, so swapping that order changes existing modules). Verified: [scripts/test-loop-index.mjs](scripts/test-loop-index.mjs) (JS+WASM runtime values + bit-identity for BOTH modes — count 25/7, range 3..7=25 + empty 5..2 skipped + −2..2=5; WGSL counter-inside-loop + inclusive headers; overseer driver runs log 0..2 and 2..4; agent WebGPU shader both modes) + the permanent `[synthetic] Loop index` entry in [scripts/parity-agent-wasm.mjs](scripts/parity-agent-wasm.mjs) (now includes a range loop, acc3 += 2..4); check-compile-identity: all 23 library models byte-identical (loops without index consumers / in count mode emit verbatim pre-change output on every surface).
- Worker `self.onmessage` is sync — `await` directly inside a `case` body is a syntax error. Wrap async work in `void (async () => { ... })()` IIFE (same pattern as `setUseWasm`), OR keep the await out of the message handler entirely.
- Module-level `let` exports from `graphState.ts` are LIVE bindings — reading the imported identifier inside a callback always sees the current value at call time (no ref needed). Used for `compatibleHandlesForDrag` and `currentModelElementDrag`. Safer than refs when the consumer is a pure function or non-React module.
- Panel-drag drop on a port (Attribute / Neighborhood / Mapping → canvas): `onPaletteDrop` in GraphEditor.tsx computes the snap target via `findNearestCompatibleHandle` (DOM query at the drop point), then calls `resolveDropCandidates(payload, snap)` to filter `RELATED_NODES` by port-compatibility. When `resolved.length === 1`, the menu is skipped and the node is auto-created via `addNodeAndConnect`.
