## Macro System (Implemented)

### Architecture:
- MacroInput/MacroOutput are boundary nodes inside macro subgraphs (teal, `#00897b`)
- MacroInput has OUTPUT ports (data flows into subgraph); MacroOutput has INPUT ports (data flows out)
- Ports are dynamic — derived from `MacroDef.exposedInputs`/`exposedOutputs` at render time
- Port editing UI on boundary nodes: add/remove/rename ports, value/flow category selector
- Changes propagate automatically — MacroNode's external handles re-derive from the same MacroDef arrays
- Boundary nodes cannot be deleted (filtered in `handleNodesChange` and `deleteSelection`)

### Create Macro from Selection:
- Auto-creates MacroInput (left of bbox) + MacroOutput (right of bbox) inside the subgraph. **Boundary positioning uses the selection's FULL-extent bbox** (`bMinX/bMinY/bMaxX/bMaxY` via `nodeSize(n)` → `position + measured width/height`), NOT bare `position.x`: MacroInput's right edge sits `BOUNDARY_GAP` (120px) left of the bbox left edge (`x = bMinX − GAP − EST_BOUNDARY_W`), MacroOutput's left edge sits `BOUNDARY_GAP` right of the bbox right edge (`x = bMaxX + GAP`), both vertically centred on the bbox. **Vertical centring estimates each boundary node's height from its exposed-port count** (`estBoundaryH(portCount) = 46 + max(1,portCount)*22`) — applied per side (`exposedInputs.length` for MacroInput, `exposedOutputs.length` for MacroOutput) so a tall many-port boundary node still centres on the selection instead of riding high. The old code used `maxX + 100` on the rightmost node's *top-left corner*, so MacroOutput landed ON TOP of that node whenever it was wider than 100px (nearly always — the user's "boundary nodes on top of the graph" report). Positions are stored relative to the selection centroid (`avgX/avgY`) like the internal nodes. DEV-only `window.__openSelectionMenu(nodeIds, x, y)` test hook ([GraphEditor.tsx](src/modeler/vpl/GraphEditor.tsx)) opens the selection context menu (box-select can't be driven by synthetic events — same limitation as `__openConnectionDropMenu`).
- `exposedInputs[i].internalNodeId` points to MacroInput node ID (not the actual internal target)
- Bridging edges connect MacroInput output ports → original internal targets
- Bridging edges connect original internal sources → MacroOutput input ports
- External edges are sorted by `internalNode.position.y * 1000 + portIdx` BEFORE building exposedInputs/exposedOutputs, so port order matches the visual top-to-bottom layout instead of arbitrary edges-array order. Port index resolves via `def.ports.filter(p => p.kind === kind).findIndex(p => p.id === portId)`, falling back to MacroDef.exposedInputs/Outputs for nested macros.

### Default Macros & Import/Export:
- `.gcamacro` file format: `{ schemaVersion: 1, name, description?, macroDef: MacroDef }`. Single MacroDef per file.
- `public/macros/*.gcamacro` is auto-indexed into `public/macros/index.json` by `macrosLibraryPlugin()` in vite.config.ts (mirrors `modelsLibraryPlugin`). Palette's "Default Macros" section fetches from `index.json` and lists each one as draggable.
- Right-click macro node → "Export Macro…" downloads a `.gcamacro` (filename derived from macro.name).
- Right-click canvas → "Import Macro…" (top-level item) opens a hidden `<input type="file">` and inserts the imported macro at the right-click position.
- `cloneMacroWithFreshIds(raw)` in `src/model/macroImport.ts` is REQUIRED for any macro import path. Regenerates: MacroDef.id, every internal node.id (with parentId remap), every edge.id, MacroPort.internalNodeId references, AND `config.macroDefId` on `macroInput`/`macroOutput` boundary nodes (this last one is easy to forget — without it, boundary nodes still point at the old MacroDef and macros break across imports).
- `importMacro(raw): string` action on ModelContext wraps clone + addMacro and returns the new id.
- MacroNode `data.label` is the user-facing name shown above the "Macro" header. `createMacroFromSelection` sets it; palette drops and file imports also pass `name` as the label argument to `addNodeAtPosition`. Always set the label when creating a macro instance.
- Project Macros section in palette filters `model.macroDefs` to only those referenced by at least one MacroNode (in `model.graphNodes` OR in any `model.macroDefs[*].nodes`). Stale defs (last instance deleted) don't appear; no auto-cleanup of model state itself.

### Undo Macro:
- Filters out boundary nodes and bridging edges when restoring
- Traces through bridging edges to find actual internal nodes for edge reconnection
- **Positioning** (`undoMacro` in GraphEditor.tsx): restored nodes are centered on the macro node by aligning the internal cluster's bounding-box center to the macro node's center (`offset = macroCenter − clusterCenter`). Do NOT just add `macroNode.position` to each internal `n.position` — that assumes internal coords are relative to (0,0), which only holds for `createMacroFromSelection` (stores `pos − centroid`). Macros from `.gcamacro` import or palette drop carry absolute coords, so the naive offset flung them far from the macro node. The bbox-center alignment is origin-independent.

### Macro Compilation (shared `expandMacros`, all three targets):
- **All three compilers flatten macros UP FRONT** via the shared `expandMacros` ([macroExpand.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/macroExpand.ts)) before any analysis. Each `macro` instance is replaced by its MacroDef's internal nodes (ids prefixed `m<instanceId>_`) + rewritten bridge edges; boundary nodes (`macroInput`/`macroOutput`) are dropped; recurses with a depth-20 guard. After expansion NO `macro`/`macroInput`/`macroOutput` nodes remain, so sink analysis, loop-invariance, accessor-CSE AND volatile hoisting all see one uniform flat graph — there is no "inside a macro" special case on any target.
- **JS used to have a SEPARATE lazy macro-inliner** (`inlineMacroValues` / `inlineMacroFlow` / `inlineNestedMacroValues` + `emitMacroLine` + `expandingMacroDefs`) that ran NONE of those analyses on macro internals. It was DELETED in favour of `expandMacros` (call at the top of `compileGraph`, before reroute-collapse / linked-OM / CSE / `buildAdjacency`). This closed two real bugs: (a) the lazy flow-inliner never emitted a flow node's internal value-input deps (a macro of `getNeighbors→count → setVariable` referenced undeclared `_m…_count` vars); (b) macro internals bypassed sink/loop-invariance/volatile analysis entirely. The per-target macroDef-iteration pre-resolve loops (indicators/stopEvents/move/variegated/viewer-refs) and the per-macroDef reroute-collapse are gone too — the flattened top-level nodes cover everything.
- Bridge rewiring: MacroInput output ports → wired directly to the outer source feeding the matching instance port. MacroOutput inputs → the internal source is wired directly to each outer consumer of the macro instance's output port.
- `expandMacros` is a structural graph transform only — purely id-prefix + edge-rewrite, no per-target logic. The `forEachInArray`-body element-dependent analysis (`findElementDependents` / `forwardValueConsumersMulti`) now never sees a macro node (always flat), so its edge-map output-port discovery is only exercised by genuinely dynamic-output value nodes.

### Linked vs Independent Copies (v1.16):
- **The data model already supports sharing** — a macro instance is just a graph node whose `config.macroDefId` points at a `MacroDef`. Two instances sharing one `macroDefId` are **linked** (mirror copies): the MacroDef is the single source of truth (edit-inside writeback via `updateMacro`; all three compilers expand by `macroDefs.find(d => d.id === macroDefId)`), so editing any instance's internals updates ALL of them with **zero compiler changes**. Independent copies each own a separate MacroDef.
- **Creation paths (intentionally mixed):** Palette "Project Macro" drop = **linked** (reuses the existing `macroDefId`); right-click → **Duplicate → "Duplicate Linked"** = **linked**; right-click → **Duplicate → "Duplicate Independent"** + copy/paste + default-macro drop + Create-from-selection = **independent** (clone the def via `importMacro`/`cloneMacroWithFreshIds`).
- **`duplicateNode(linked = false)`** in [GraphEditor.tsx](src/modeler/vpl/GraphEditor.tsx): when `linked && srcType === 'macro'` it SKIPS the def-clone block so the duplicate keeps the source `macroDefId`. The single-node context menu renders **Duplicate as a hover submenu for macro nodes** (`.contextSubmenuTrigger`/`.contextSubmenu`, same pattern as Align/Distribute) — "Duplicate Independent" calls `duplicateNode(false)`, "Duplicate Linked" calls `duplicateNode(true)`. Non-macro nodes get a plain "Duplicate" button (`duplicateNode()` → independent). Don't pass `duplicateNode` directly as an `onClick` handler (the event would land in `linked`).
- **Count badge** ([CaNode.tsx](src/modeler/vpl/CaNode.tsx), `.linkBadge`): rendered as the first child of the macro `.header` (left of the "MACRO" title), shown ONLY when `countMacroInstances(model, macroDefId) >= 2` (Blender-style — single-user macros show nothing). Click → `.linkMenu` popover → **"Make Independent Copy"** = `importMacro(srcDef)` then `updateNodeData(id, {config:{macroDefId: newId}})` for THIS node only; other linked instances stay on the original (their count decrements). Keeps the node's `data.label` (no rename/suffix).
- **`nodrag` gotcha:** the badge + popover live in the `.header`, which is a React-Flow drag handle (only the `.body` carries the `nodrag` class). Interactive elements in the header MUST add the `nodrag` class or mousing down on them initiates a node drag — `onMouseDown` `stopPropagation` does NOT prevent it because React Flow's d3-drag attaches a native listener on the node element that fires before React's root-delegated handler. (`.linkBadge` + `.linkMenu` both carry `nodrag`.)
- **`countMacroInstances(model, macroDefId)`** in [macroImport.ts](src/model/macroImport.ts): walks `model.graphNodes` + every `model.macroDefs[*].nodes` counting macro instances with that `macroDefId`. Same traversal as the palette Project-Macros filter and `undoMacro`'s ref-check.
- **Undo asymmetry (accepted, harmless):** "Make Independent" does a model dispatch (`importMacro` → ADD_MACRO, sets `isDirty`) AND a graph-only node retarget. Ctrl+Z (graph-only history) reverts the retarget but leaves an **orphan MacroDef** — hidden from the palette (`usedMacroIds` filter) and never removed out from under a live instance by `undoMacro`'s ref-count. This exactly mirrors the existing independent-`duplicateNode` behavior. Don't build a combined ModelContext action (it would have to own React-Flow graph state).

### Remaining:
- No def-switching dropdown — a macro instance can't be repointed to a different existing MacroDef from the UI (only linked-copy / make-independent).

### Thumbnails
- `ModelProperties.thumbnail?: string` stores a PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP **or `video/webm`** data URL (≤2 MB, validated in [InfoPanelContent.tsx](src/modeler/panels/InfoPanelContent.tsx)). Travels inside `.gcaproj` — no sidecar for user-saved files. **The schema is unchanged (still one data URL string)**; WebM is accepted because the simulator RECORDS WebM, so a short recording is the most natural thumbnail a model can carry.
- **AN `<img>` CANNOT DISPLAY A WEBM — every render site MUST go through [`<ThumbMedia>`](src/components/ThumbMedia.tsx)**, the ONE place the branch lives (a `<video autoPlay loop muted playsInline>` vs an `<img>`; the caller's `className`/`style` apply to both, so sizing/`object-fit` rules are shared). `muted` + `playsInline` are REQUIRED for autoplay without a user gesture, and `controls` is deliberately absent (a thumbnail is decoration, not a player). The three consumers: the Info panel preview, the Models Library hover popover, and the standalone viewer's About panel. [thumbnail.ts](src/model/thumbnail.ts) owns `isVideoThumbnail` (`data:video/…` for embedded URLs, an exact `.webm` extension for library sidecars — NB `.webp` (still) and `.webm` (clip) differ only in the last character), plus the shared `THUMBNAIL_ACCEPT` / `THUMBNAIL_MAX_BYTES` / `THUMBNAIL_FORMATS_LABEL`.
- **The ONE graceful degradation: the presentation export's `og:image`.** [exportPresentation.ts](src/export/exportPresentation.ts) gates on `thumb.startsWith('data:image/')`, so a WebM thumbnail is simply SKIPPED for the social tags (a link scraper needs an image) while still travelling inside the embedded model and playing in the viewer's About panel. Verified through the real export: `og:title` present, `og:image`/`twitter:image` absent.
- `modelsLibraryPlugin` in `vite.config.ts` extracts `properties.thumbnail` from each library `.gcaproj` into `<file>.thumb.<ext>` sidecars, records the sidecar path in `index.json`, and sweeps stale `*.thumb.*` on every run. Sidecars are gitignored (`public/models/*.thumb.{png,jpg,jpeg,gif,webp,webm}`). **The extension list appears in FIVE places that must stay in sync**: the plugin's `cleanThumbnails` sweep regex, its `extractThumbnail` data-URL regex + ext map, the PWA `globPatterns` precache entry, the PWA `runtimeCaching` thumb regex, and `.gitignore`.
- Plugin runs only at `configureServer` / `closeBundle` — adding a thumbnail to a library `.gcaproj` while the dev server is running requires a restart before it shows up. **Pre-existing dev-server gotcha (bit the WebM verification):** a sidecar written during `configureServer` can miss Vite's initial public-dir scan, so on the FIRST dev start after a NEW sidecar appears the request falls through to the SPA `index.html` (`content-type: text/html`) instead of the file. A second restart fixes it; the production build is unaffected (it copies `public/` into `dist/`). If a thumbnail mysteriously 404s-as-HTML in dev, restart before debugging the code.
- `ModelsLibrary` renders a fixed-position TWO-PANE popover on `onMouseEnter` — [title + auto-scrolling description | thumbnail], both 320×240, side by side — centered ON the hovered card (both axes, overlaying it; viewport-clamped near edges; `pointer-events: none` keeps the card's hover + clicks working underneath); `image-rendering: pixelated` + `object-fit: contain` so small grid GIFs scale up crisply (a WebM clip inherits the same box + fit).

### Model creation date (`properties.createdDate`)
- **`ModelProperties.createdDate?: string`** — an ISO calendar date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) the AUTHOR sets in the Info panel ("Creation date", with **Today** / **Clear** buttons). Additive + optional, travels inside `.gcaproj` like the rest of the presentation metadata; **no migration** (old files simply have no date).
- **WHY AUTHORED AND NOT DERIVED — the bug this replaced.** The library card stamp + the Newest/Oldest sort used to read a plugin-emitted `modified` = the `.gcaproj`'s **file mtime**, which every build / checkout / `git switch` churns — so the date said "when this working copy was written", never "when the model was made", and the sort was meaningless. **Filesystem birthtime is no better** (a checkout recreates the file). There is no derivable ground truth on disk, so the date is a field, not an inference.
- **A model with NO date shows NO date** — the card omits the stamp entirely (and its tooltip), and the entry sorts **LAST in BOTH Newest and Oldest** (then by name; `byCreated` in [ModelsLibrary.tsx](src/library/ModelsLibrary.tsx)). Silence beats a misleading number, and an undated model has no place on a time axis.
- **[createdDate.ts](src/model/createdDate.ts) is the ONE parse/format module** (`parseCreatedDate` / `createdDateTimestamp` / `formatCreatedDate` / `todayCreatedDate`), shared by the library, the standalone viewer's About panel ("Created", rendered only when set) and the Info panel. **Two traps it exists to close:** `new Date('2026-04-07')` parses as **UTC** midnight and renders as the PREVIOUS day west of Greenwich (so it builds a LOCAL-midnight date from the components), and `toISOString()` for "today" is likewise UTC (so `todayCreatedDate` formats local parts). It also round-trip-validates the components, rejecting overflow dates the `Date` constructor would silently roll forward.
- **The Vite plugin (`modelsLibraryPlugin`) emits `createdDate` only when `properties.createdDate` matches `YYYY-MM-DD`**, and **omits the key otherwise** — so an unset/garbage value can never become a card stamp. `index.json` is build-generated + gitignored, so the field swap needed no back-compat shim. As with thumbnails, the plugin runs at `configureServer` / `closeBundle` — **editing a shipped model's date needs a dev-server restart** before the library reflects it.
- **The 29 shipped library models are stamped with their FIRST-ADDED commit date** (`git log --diff-filter=A --format=%as -- <file>`; **NOT `--follow`**, whose rename heuristic misattributes a new model to a similar deleted one — it dated four GRA samples two months early). Each **generator script carries the same date** as a `createdDate:` literal in its properties object, so a re-run preserves the stamp.

### UpdateAttribute Node
- Complements SetAttribute: in-place modify via increment/decrement/max/min (int/float), toggle/or/and (bool), next/previous (tag)
- Unary operations (toggle, next, previous) hide the `value` input port via `inputPorts.filter()` in CaNode.tsx
- Uses `w_${attr}[idx]` for read-modify-write (reads current write-buffer value, not read-buffer)
- Tag operations store `_tagLen` in node config for modulo wrap; updated when attribute selection changes

### Key Patterns:
- When adding new fields to CAModel type, always add migration guards in ModelContext's `createInitialState`
- `Attribute.boundaryValue?: string` (cell attrs only, shown in UI only when `properties.boundaryTreatment === 'constant'`). Worker's `buildNeighborIndices` writes `boundaryCellValue(attr) ?? defaultValue(attr)` into the sentinel cell at index `total`. WASM reads the same memory — no compile-path change needed.
- Align / Distribute submenu on the multi-selection context menu (`alignNodes(mode)` / `distributeNodes(axis)` in GraphEditor.tsx). Align modes: left/centerH/right, top/centerV/bottom. Distribute: sort by axis, fix first and last, equalize inter-node gaps. Uses the standard `pushCurrentSnapshot()` + `scheduleSync()` pattern.
- Node config UI: when a config field changes type (e.g., constType), reset dependent fields to prevent stale values
- Compiler: all value declarations hoisted to function scope (Pass 1) before control flow (Pass 2) to avoid block-scoping issues
- Web Worker in Vite: `new Worker(new URL('./file.ts', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' })` — no config needed
- Worker postMessage with transfer: use `{ transfer: [buffer] }` options format (not positional arg)
- ID generation: NEVER use counter-based IDs (`nextId++`) — they collide after page reload with saved models. Always use `Date.now().toString(36) + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2,5)`
- Worker message types: adding new messages requires updating the `WorkerMsg` union type in sim.worker.ts
- Vite base path: `const base = process.env.GHPAGES ? '/GenesisCA/' : '/'` — the production site is served at the ROOT of the custom domain **genesisca.online** (pinned by [public/CNAME](public/CNAME)), so the deploy ([deploy.yml](.github/workflows/deploy.yml)) builds with base `/` — the same as `npm run dev`, local `npm run build`/`preview`, and the Tauri shell. `GHPAGES` is an opt-in fallback: set it to rebuild under the `/GenesisCA/` subpath ONLY if the custom domain is removed and the bare `rff255.github.io/GenesisCA/` project URL is used directly. Don't hardcode `/GenesisCA/` for local builds.
- Reset must run one step via compiled stepFn so model-defined color mappings apply (not hardcoded fallback)
- Models Library: Vite plugin in vite.config.ts auto-generates `models/index.json` from `public/models/*.gcaproj` — no manual manifest; card metadata comes from `ModelProperties`

## WASM Compile Target (Wave 2 — current default)

WASM has full node-catalogue coverage including the multi-source `groupOperator.random` path. **C4 note**: new models no longer name WASM directly — `EMPTY_MODEL.properties.engine = 'auto'` and the Auto policy picks WebGPU where the gates pass, else WASM (`useWasm: true` remains in EMPTY_MODEL only as the static legacy MIRROR). The Properties radio reads **Auto (recommended) / WebAssembly / WebGPU**, with Debug (JS) behind Advanced.

- 4-file structure under `src/modeler/vpl/compiler/wasm/`: `encoder.ts` (hand-rolled WASM binary encoder, no wabt.js), `layout.ts` (memory layout: attrs/colors/nbrs/modelAttrs/indicators/rngState/activeViewer/order/scratch), `emitter.ts` (`WasmEmitter` class + `ValueRef`/`ArrayRef` types), `compile.ts` (orchestrator + per-node emitters)
- One module exports all entry points: `step`, `inputColor_<sanitisedMappingId>`, `outputMapping_<sanitisedMappingId>`. Host math functions WASM lacks native opcodes for are imported from JS (`env.pow/exp/log/sin/cos/tan/tanh`) at contiguous funcIdx `POW_FUNC_IDX=0 … TANH_FUNC_IDX=6` (`NUM_IMPORTED_FUNCS=7`); module-defined funcs start at funcIdx `NUM_IMPORTED_FUNCS` (export funcIdx = `NUM_IMPORTED_FUNCS + i`). The import-entry order, the `*_FUNC_IDX` consts, and `instantiateWasmModule`'s `env` object MUST stay in sync. sqrt/abs/**neg**/floor/ceil/min/max use native f64 intrinsics — so a Math op that maps to one (e.g. `negate` → `f64.neg`, an IEEE sign flip that is bit-identical to JS `-x` and WGSL `-x` incl. -0/NaN) needs NO import entry and NO funcIdx change. The Math node (`arithmeticOperator`) and Expression node share this transcendental set: JS emits `Math.*`, WGSL uses native intrinsics, WASM calls the imports — adding one means editing `expression/parser.ts` (FN_ARITY), all three `expression/emit{JS,Wasm,Wgsl}.ts`, `ArithmeticOperatorNode.ts` (+ `ARITHMETIC_UNARY_OPS` if unary) and its WASM/WebGPU emitters in `wasm/compile.ts` + `webgpu/compile.ts`, plus (WASM only) a new import entry + `*_FUNC_IDX` const + `env` entry. `log` = natural log.
- Multi-output value cache: `valueLocals: Map<nodeId, Map<portId, LocalRef>>`. Single-output nodes get the named port aliased to `'value'` automatically; multi-output emitters call `setCachedPort` for each named port
- Array-producing nodes (`getNeighborIndexesByTags`, `filterNeighbors`, `joinNeighbors`, `getNeighborsAttrByIndexes`, `groupCounting` hybrid) live in a separate `ARRAY_NODE_EMITTERS` table. They allocate via per-cell scratch (bump-pointer reset at top of every cell iteration). Array consumers (aggregate/groupCounting/groupStatement) dispatch through `isArrayProducer` to the array path
- Entry-point nodes (inputColor/step/outputMapping) have NO `VALUE_NODE_EMITTERS` entry. InputColor's CHANNEL outputs resolve via the `paramRefs` map (a `LocalRef` per channel — legacy r/g/b are param indices 1/2/3 as i32; a declared parameter list mints one f64 param per channel, see Parameterized Input Mappings); skipping them in `preEmitValueNodes` is required
- Skip `port.isArray` during scalar input resolution in `compileValueNode` / `compileArrayNode` / `compileFlowChain` — array consumers fetch sources via `inputToSources` + the array dispatch path; trying to value-emit an array source hits "no value emitter" errors
- Sync mode WASM↔JS interop: WASM uses baked-in `attrReadOffset`/`attrWriteOffset` so worker `runStep()` does pre-step `readAttrs→attrsA` normalize + post-step bulk `attrsB→attrsA` copy. JS-mode swap path is untouched. Same normalization needed in `paint`/`importImage`/`runColorPass` when WASM is active
- WASM compiler is self-sufficient — does its own `_resolvedTagIndexes` and `_indicatorIdx` pre-resolve (mirrors JS compiler). Don't assume the JS compiler ran first
- `window.__simWorker` is exposed in DEV (`SimulatorView.tsx`) for direct postMessage testing — far more reliable than standalone parity harnesses, which have subtle setup mismatches with the worker (activeViewer string vs i32, indicators Float64Array vs wasmMemory region, etc.)
- Cross-target compiler changes are verifiable in `preview_eval` WITHOUT driving the UI: `await import('/src/modeler/vpl/compiler/compile.ts')` (+ `wasm/compile.ts` `compileGraphWasm` with `computeLayoutFromModel`, + `webgpu/compile.ts` `compileGraphWebGPU`), build a minimal `{graphNodes, graphEdges}` + `EMPTY_MODEL`-derived model, and compare `.stepCode` / `.bytes` / `.shaderCode`. Ideal for proving a refactor is byte-identical (flow-port reorders, sink-analysis tweaks, etc.) — far cheaper than driving the canvas, and catches WGSL/WASM emit regressions the JS path wouldn't.
- Big WASM-emitter refactors: implement EVERY emitter first, do a static review pass over the whole compiler, THEN run a single end-to-end test sweep. Iterative implement-test-fix-test cycles thrash because each new node type tested exposes structural issues (config-key mismatches, value-hoist scoping, sync-mode buffer swap, sentinel handling). One focused pass converges much faster
- Post-loop computation must stay in sync across JS and WASM targets. The JS-compiled step embeds post-loop aggregation (generated by `buildLinkedIndicatorCode` in `compiler/compile.ts`); the WASM step doesn't emit that code — instead the worker runs `computeLinkedIndicatorsFromBuffer()` after `wasmStepFn()` and replicates the aggregation against the shared typed-array buffer. Any new post-loop compute (new indicator kind, new metric, anything that reads the final-state buffer and writes to `linkedResults` / similar) needs both the JS-compile emit AND a matching branch in the worker-side fallback, or it'll silently work in JS mode and be empty in WASM mode.
- **Scratch-top snapshot for loop-invariant scratch allocations** (the Amphiphile NI-poisoning bug): `emitInvariantValueNodes` allocates scratch via `allocArrayInScratch`, which reads `scratchTopLocal`. But `scratchTopLocal` was only initialised inside `emitBody` (per-cell), so loop-invariant scratch allocations (e.g. a hoisted `getAllNeighborIndexes`) ran with the local at WASM's default 0 — their writes landed on top of the kind buffer at `memory[0..]`. Per-cell `getCellAttribute` reads then read NI bytes back as kind values, and `setNeighborAttributeByIndex` propagated the poison across cells until WASM eventually blew its memory bounds. Fix: seed `scratchTopLocal = layout.scratchOffset` BEFORE `emitInvariantValueNodes`, snapshot the post-invariant top into a new `perCellScratchBase` local, and reset per-cell scratch from `perCellScratchBase` (not the bare `scratchOffset` constant) so per-cell scratch starts ABOVE the invariant region. Models with no loop-invariant scratch are byte-identical (snapshot == `scratchOffset`). InputColor's single-shot entry seeds `perCellScratchBase = scratchOffset` directly (no invariant pass).

## WebGPU Compile Target (Wave 3)

**Status: functional.** WebGPU is the third compile target alongside JS (default) and WASM. The compiler emits a single WGSL shader module containing the `step` entry point + one `outputMapping_<sanitisedId>` per Attribute→Color mapping, dispatched as compute pipelines on the GPU. Verified on Game of Life (with macros), Coagulation, MNCA (model-attribute-driven trace gradient), and Wireworld (array-producing nodes + linked-frequency indicators) — paint, reset, play, save/load, indicator readback, stop events, GIF + WebM recording all work. Direct OffscreenCanvas render (transferControlToOffscreen + a `presentColors` compute pipeline) skips the per-step colors readback. GPU-side reductions cover eligible linked-indicator aggregations. Pipeline cache short-circuits rebuild when the WGSL source is byte-identical (`shaderHashOf` check at `sim.worker.ts:294`).

### Architecture
- `useWebGPU?: boolean` on `ModelProperties`. Mutually exclusive with `useWasm` enforced by the UI 3-way radio (Properties → Execution → Compile Target) and a worker-side safety net (WebGPU wins if both flags arrive true on a hand-edited file).
- `webgpuStopCheckInterval?: number` on `ModelProperties` (default 1) — opt-in throughput knob on WebGPU only. Worker checks the stop flag every K generations AND always on the last step of any batch (so the user never overshoots a stop event past the current play batch). K=1 preserves exact behaviour. JS / WASM ignore the setting.
- 4-file compiler under `src/modeler/vpl/compiler/webgpu/`:
  - `encoder.ts` — WGSL string helpers (bindings, struct decls, per-cell copy preamble, attr read/write helpers, PCG functions).
  - `layout.ts` — 8-binding GPU buffer layout (attrsRead/attrsWrite/colors/nbrOffsets/modelAttrs/indicators/rngState/control). Bool/int/tag/float attrs are stored as one u32 word per cell with bitcast on read/write. `nbrOffsets` holds only the per-neighbourhood (dRow, dCol) i32 pairs (a few KB total) — neighbour cell indices are computed inline by the WGSL `nbrCellIdx(cellIdx, baseOffset, k)` helper using grid-width/height/sentinel literals baked into each shader. Replaces the legacy per-cell `total × nbrSize` index table that hit multiple GB on huge grids (see docs/HUGE_GRID_OPTIMIZATIONS.md §2.1).
  - `emitter.ts` — `WgslEmitter` shell (legacy; current orchestrator builds lines directly).
  - `compile.ts` — orchestrator. Macro expansion (`expandMacros`) runs first to flatten the graph. Then `preEmitValueNodes` walks the flow chain to compile every referenced value node at the entry-point's top scope (avoids the "var declared in `if` branch but referenced in sibling `else` branch" WGSL scoping issue). Per-node dispatch via `VALUE_NODE_EMITTERS` and `FLOW_NODE_EMITTERS`.
- `src/simulator/engine/webgpuRuntime.ts` owns adapter/device/buffers/pipelines. `setupBuffersAndPipelines()` builds the step pipeline plus one pipeline per output mapping. Helpers: `uploadAttrs` / `uploadAttr`, `uploadNeighborOffsets`, `uploadModelAttrs`, `uploadActiveViewer`, `uploadIndicators`, `dispatchStep`, `dispatchOutputMapping`, `readbackAttrs`, `readbackColors`, `readbackIndicators`, `readbackStopFlag`, `seedRngState`.
- Worker integration:
  - `runStepWebGPU()`: resets stop flag, syncs per-generation indicators to GPU, dispatches step pipeline.
  - `runColorPassWebGPU()`: dispatches the active viewer's output mapping pipeline.
  - `finalizeStepWebGPU({needAttrs?, needColors?})`: async tail that reads back colors / indicators / stop flag (and optionally cell attrs for linked indicators or save state). Standalone integer/tag/bool indicators decode as bitcast<i32>; everything else as bitcast<f32>.
  - Mutation handlers (paint, importImage, reset, writeRegion, clearRegion) mutate CPU `readAttrs` then upload via `uploadAttrs` and dispatch `runColorPassWebGPU`.
  - `getState` does `readbackAttrs` first when `gpuOwnsAttrs`. `loadState` uploads everything after CPU restore.
  - On WebGPU init (`startWebGPUInit` then `setupBuffersAndPipelines`), the worker uploads CPU state, seeds per-cell RNG, dispatches an initial output mapping pass, reads back colors, and posts a `stepped` message so the canvas paints the initial state.

### Atomics
- Stop events: `atomicCompareExchangeWeak(&control.stopFlag, 0u, idxU)` — first-cell-wins matches JS/WASM semantics.
- UpdateIndicator (integer/tag): `atomicAdd` for increment/decrement, `atomicMax` / `atomicMin`. `bitcast<u32>(i32)` to encode.
- UpdateIndicator (bool): `atomicOr(&ind, 1u)` for `or` when value is true; `atomicAnd(&ind, 0u)` for `and` when value is false.
- UpdateIndicator (float): `loop { atomicLoad → bitcast<f32> → compute → bitcast<u32> → atomicCompareExchangeWeak; if exchanged break }`. CAS loop on the f32-bitcast u32 word.
- `toggle`/`next`/`previous` on indicators: rejected at compile time (order-dependent under parallel cell execution).

### Compile-time rejections
`detectWebGPUIncompatibilities()` and `detectWebGPUModelIncompatibilities()` in [nodeValidation.ts](src/modeler/vpl/nodes/nodeValidation.ts) catch async mode, the async-only nodes (`setNeighborhoodAttribute` / `setNeighborAttributeByIndex` / `markCellUpdated` / `setFacingOrientation` / `setNeighborOrientationByIndex` / `moveSelfToNeighbor`), and `updateIndicator` with `toggle`/`next`/`previous`. The variegated READ nodes + `setOrientation` + `lookupInteraction`/`interactionTableMap` + Init Event ARE supported on WebGPU. CaNode warning badges surface rejections in the modeler when `useWebGPU` is on. The compiler returns an `error` and the worker stays on JS.

### Aggregate / GroupOperator median + uniform random (FULL COVERAGE — DONE)
`aggregate.median` and `aggregate`/`groupOperator` uniform `random` now run on the WebGPU GRID target (they're per-cell-LOCAL + order-INDEPENDENT, already on JS/WASM — never fundamentals). [webgpu/compile.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/webgpu/compile.ts) `emitAggregateOrCount`: a shared **`materialiseFoldInput`** lifts the value-input materialisation out of the `weightedRandom` block (single-array source / sub-attr-FILTERED nbr-path / multi-source scalars) into one f32 `var<function>` scratch (sized by `maxArraySize`), so median / uniform-random / weightedRandom stay in lockstep. **median** = per-thread insertion-sort the materialised prefix, then median-pick (empty 0; even = mean of two middles; odd = middle — matches AggregateNode JS). **random** = advance the per-cell PCG once (always, JS/WASM always-advance) → `idx = floor(u*len)` → clamp → pick; empty → index -1/result 0; result+index ports. The picked index DIFFERS cross-target by design (per-cell PCG vs shared xorshift32 — same documented statistical-parity stance as `getRandom`). Sub-attribute nbr-path filters non-matching neighbours so the sort/pick run over the filtered prefix. GPU-verified: both shaders compile 0 errors + run end-to-end (a median-of-Moore rule smooths a sparse field to death; a random-pick rule preserves density).

### Not implemented on WebGPU (compile-time rejected, worker falls back to JS) — the genuine fundamentals ONLY
- Async update mode and async-only nodes (`setNeighborhoodAttribute`, `setNeighborAttributeByIndex`, `markCellUpdated`, `setFacingOrientation`, `setNeighborOrientationByIndex`, `moveSelfToNeighbor`). Async = "a write is visible to a later cell this step" — fundamentally serial, no parallel-GPU representation. The user keeps async by picking WASM/JS.
- `updateIndicator` with `toggle` / `next` / `previous` (order-dependent non-commutative mutation of one shared accumulator by parallel writers — the lone node-op-level fundamental; or/and/max/min/inc/dec ARE supported via atomics).

These two are the **complete** WebGPU-grid reject set. f32 precision + per-cell PCG bar NO node.

### Known target-specific differences (intentional, documented)
- WGSL has no f64. Float arithmetic runs in f32 — small precision differences vs JS/WASM accumulate over many generations on chaotic models. Bit-exact parity is NOT a goal.
- RNG: WebGPU uses per-cell PCG state seeded from a global seed. JS/WASM use a single shared xorshift32 stream. Same global seed → different sequences. Statistical behaviour matches; deterministic replay across targets does not.

### Key gotchas
- **A WGSL FLOAT LITERAL IS PARSED AS f64 AND THEN RANGE-CHECKED AGAINST f32 — never hand-write a rounded f32::MAX** (a real shipped defect, 2026-07-31). Both WebGPU compilers seeded a `min`/`max` fold with `3.4028235e38`, the *rounded* spelling of f32::MAX. That decimal is **340282349999999991754788743781432688640**, which is LARGER than f32::MAX (340282346638528859811704183484516925440), so Naga rejects the WHOLE shader — `value … cannot be represented as 'f32'` — and the model **silently falls back off the WebGPU target** (`[agents] WebGPU runtime build failed, falling back to JS`). Use the shared **`WGSL_F32_MAX`** (`'3.4028234663852886e38'`, the shortest decimal that round-trips f32::MAX) exported from [webgpu/compile.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/webgpu/compile.ts) — imported by [agentWebgpu/compile.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/agentWebgpu/compile.ts) so the two cannot drift. It fed **6 emit sites** (cell-grid `aggregate`/`groupOperator` min+max; the agent `readCellsUnder` reduce, `groupOperator` best-of, and `aggregate` min+max). **Why it escaped every gate:** `check-compile-identity` HASHES emitted text without ever handing it to a device, and the one shipped model that used `aggregate.min` (`Cubic GRA`) ships on the WASM agent target. `Ant Necrophoresis` was latently broken the same way (a `readCellsUnder` `max` reduce). Guarded permanently by [scripts/verify-wgsl-float-literals.mjs](scripts/verify-wgsl-float-literals.mjs) — Tier A scans every shipped model's emitted WGSL (grid step + agent behaviour + agent OM + the force pass in all 4 variants; 160 surfaces) for any literal that does not fit f32, Tier B forbids the rounded spelling in `src/` outside its documenting comment, and `--self-test` is the negative control. **The general lesson: emitted text that compiles in TypeScript is not a shader that compiles on a device — a numeric constant crossing into WGSL must respect f32, not f64.**
- WebGPU types are NOT in the default DOM lib. The project uses `@webgpu/types` (dev dep) referenced via `/// <reference types="@webgpu/types" />` at the top of `webgpuRuntime.ts` — do NOT add `"types": ["@webgpu/types"]` to tsconfig.app.json because that switches off auto-loading of all OTHER `@types/*` packages.
- WGSL struct definitions must come BEFORE the `var` declarations that reference them. `Control` struct is emitted before `var<...> control: Control` in `emitBindings()`.
- WGSL `var`/`let` are block-scoped. Cross-branch references (a value computed in `then` cannot be read in `else`) used to be solved by an eager `preEmitValueNodes` pass that hoisted every value to function-top scope. Post-sinking (see "Value sinking" section below) the analyzer guarantees every value's emit scope dominates all its uses, so block-scoped declarations inside an `if`/`case` block work naturally for single-branch values, and multi-branch values keep their LCA at the parent (function-top in the worst case) for cross-branch visibility.
- Value emitters that resolve **array-port sources INSIDE their `routeEmissionForNode` wrapper** (e.g. `getRandom` "options", `aggregate`/`groupOperator` over multi-source scalars) violate the "inputs resolved upstream" contract. `compileValueNode` therefore pre-resolves an array port's **multi-source scalar** inputs BEFORE the wrapper (warming the cache at the proper scope). Without this, a CSE-shared `getConstant` (sink scope `CELL_TOP`) first compiled inside the wrapper lands in that node's temporary branch buffer, so a sibling switch case reading it hits `unresolved value '_v…'` at WGSL shader-compile (the kelp_war **`_ki10`** crash: options-mode `getRandom` fed by duplicate tag constants that CSE merged). Single array-PRODUCER sources are left to the emitter so `aggregate`/`groupOperator` **fusion** is preserved; `getVariable` is skipped (dual scalar/array, resolved at use site). WASM is immune (function-scoped locals); JS uses `branchValueLines` and was already correct here.
- Storage buffers must be ≥4 bytes. `layout.ts` clamps `attrsBytes` / `nbrBytes` to a 4-byte minimum so degenerate models don't fail buffer creation.
- Worker-side mutual-exclusion safety net: in `init` and `setUseWasm`/`setUseWebGPU` handlers, when both flags would be true the worker silently demotes WASM. Keep both UI and worker enforcement — UI for live edits, worker for legacy `.gcaproj` files saved before the radio existed.
- `gpuOwnsAttrs = true` after `runStepWebGPU` runs. Mutation handlers AND save/load MUST upload-after-write OR readback-before-read. CRITICAL distinction: handlers that overwrite ALL cells (reset, importImage) call full `uploadAttrs(rt, readAttrs)`. Handlers that touch only a subset of cells (paint, writeRegion, clearRegion) MUST patch the GPU buffer at per-cell offsets via `device.queue.writeBuffer(attrsBuf, byteOffset + idx*4, ...)` — full `uploadAttrs` would clobber the post-Play evolved state with the stale CPU mirror. The bug symptom is "brushing seems to reset the board to random/initial".
- The Resize button (`handleApplyDimensions`) calls `initWorkerWithDimensions(w, h)` directly with the new dimensions WITHOUT updating `model.properties.gridWidth/Height`. The compilers must therefore receive a `dimsModel` with overridden dimensions — passing the unmodified `model` makes `compileGraphWebGPU` bake the OLD `total` into the WGSL bounds check (`idx >= ${total}u`), causing only the first N cells of the new larger buffer to evolve. WASM is tolerant because it takes `total` as a runtime function arg. Symptom: half the grid shows live evolution, half stays at the initial randomize.
- `adapter.requestDevice()` defaults to a conservative 128 MB `maxStorageBufferBindingSize` even when the adapter supports 2 GB. Large grids (multi-attribute models at 5000²+) can exceed the default for the attrs / colors buffers. Request `requiredLimits` matching the adapter's max so larger grids work. `setupBuffersAndPipelines` also defensively checks each region against the device's actual `maxStorageBufferBindingSize` and throws a clear error before the lower-level GPU validation error fires (which is hard to attribute back to a specific buffer). The neighbour-index buffer is no longer a concern post-§2.1 — it now stores only the relative offsets (a few KB total).
- **`maxComputeWorkgroupsPerDimension` is 65535 — a FLAT 1-D `dispatchWorkgroups(ceil(total/64))` silently no-ops past ~4.19M cells** (= `65535 × 64`). No error is raised — the kernel simply never runs, so the **whole WebGPU sim goes blank** (step + colour pass + init + reductions all skipped) on any grid above the threshold: a 5000×5000 (25M) 2D grid OR a 3D volume past ~4.2M cells (the canonical repro was a **300×300×100 = 9M** 3D model — display blank, brushing appeared to "do nothing" because painted cells were never coloured). Requesting the adapter max for this limit doesn't help — 65535 IS the hardware/spec ceiling. **Fix: tile the dispatch into a 2-D workgroup grid** via `dispatchCells(pass, total, wg)` ([webgpuRuntime.ts](src/simulator/engine/webgpuRuntime.ts)) — `x = min(groups, 65535)`, `y = ceil(groups/65535)`, `dispatchWorkgroups(x, y)`. Used at ALL 5 per-cell dispatch sites (step / init / output-mapping ×2 / reductions); the present pass + glyph-clear are unaffected (texture-dim dispatch / `clearBuffer`). The per-cell shaders recover the linear index from the 2-D global id: `let idx = gid.y * (nwg.x * 64u) + gid.x;` with `@builtin(num_workgroups) nwg` — emitted by `emitEntryPoint` ([webgpu/encoder.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/webgpu/encoder.ts)) for step/init/OM and by the reduction-shader builder ([webgpuReduce.ts](src/simulator/engine/webgpuReduce.ts)). **For grids ≤ 65535×64 cells `y==1` → `gid.y==0` → `idx==gid.x`, byte-behaviour-identical to the old 1-D path** (verified: a 40×40×12 model renders unchanged; the 9M model went from 0 → 3.6M rendered instances + brushes correctly post-step). The `64u` literal MUST track `@workgroup_size(64)` — change both together. Any NEW per-cell compute dispatch over `total` MUST go through `dispatchCells` + use this 2-D index recovery.
- **The dead CPU neighbour table is DROPPED on the WebGPU grid target (the wasm32-4-GiB grid-ceiling fix; branch `optimize`).** The worker's `wasmMemory` is ONE backing store shared by every target, and even on WebGPU `initGrid` used to reserve the FULL per-cell neighbour tables (`total × nSz × 4` — **2.81 GB at 300³ 26-Moore, 6.66 GB at 400³**) — the DOMINANT per-cell cost and what blows the 4 GiB `WebAssembly.Memory` cap (`value 127930 above the upper bound 65536` resizing the shipped Accretor to 400³). But the **WebGPU runtime NEVER reads that table** — the GPU computes neighbours inline in WGSL from the compact `nbrOffsets` buffer (§2.1); `runStep()` returns via `runStepWebGPU()` BEFORE ever calling `buildLoopArgs`. So on the WebGPU target the table is dead weight. **Fix ([sim.worker.ts](src/simulator/engine/sim.worker.ts), worker-only — no compiler touched → JS/WASM byte-identical):** the `init` handler computes **`nbrTableDropped`** = `msg.useWebGPU` (INTENT — the layout is baked here, before the async runtime is known to succeed) `&& gridCells && !SIE-on && !cpuIndexesNbr`, where **`cpuIndexesNbr` = does any COMPILED CPU function that runs on this target — init / gridInit / OM / inputColor, but **NOT the STEP** — index a neighbour table (`codeIndexesNeighbourTable`, regex `/nIdx_\w*\[/` over the code strings; a compiled param decl is `nIdx_<id>,` so `nIdx_<id>[` appears only at a real read site)**. When dropped, `computeMemoryLayout` gets `layoutNeighborhoods = []` (no nbr region) and `buildNeighborIndices` fills ONLY the constant-boundary sentinel (`fillBoundarySentinel`, uploaded to the GPU with the attrs) — `nbrIndices` stays `{}`, so `buildLoopArgs` pushes an `undefined` table arg the (guaranteed-non-indexing) CPU fns never read. **The STEP is deliberately EXCLUDED from the check** = its JS/WASM CPU fallback is the ONE reader we drop: a WebGPU model whose GPU runtime FAILS can no longer silently fall back to a CPU step (a grid too large for the GPU table is too large for JS/WASM anyway). `runStep` guards this — when `nbrTableDropped` it returns without running the JS/WASM step (transient no-op while the runtime inits; a genuine failure — `webgpuGridFailed`, set in every `startWebGPUInit` failure branch — surfaces a one-time clear "runs on WebGPU only" error). A soft **recompile** that ADDS a neighbour read to a CPU function while the table is already dropped can't reallocate; it posts a one-time "reload to apply" error. **Trade-off:** a WebGPU model on a non-WebGPU browser now surfaces that honest error instead of silently running the (impractical-at-scale) JS fallback. Measured ceiling: 300³ dead-table 2.81 GB → gone; **400³ (the user's error) now inits + plays; the WebGPU-target ceiling moves from ~320³ past ~860³** (bounded now by attrs+colours, not the table — 512³ hits the browser tab's contiguous-ArrayBuffer budget, a recoverable env limit, NOT the WASM cap). **Guarded by [scripts/verify-webgpu-nbr-table.mjs](scripts/verify-webgpu-nbr-table.mjs)** (layout-delta == Σ total·nSz·4; 400³/512³ dropped fits + full overflows the 65536-page cap; the Accretor's CPU fns don't index nbr → dropped; a synthetic neighbour-reading-init model → table KEPT). **NB the edge case: a WebGPU model with a Grid Init Event forces the CPU init path (`useWebGPUInit` false when `gridInitFn !== null`), so a per-cell Init Event that reads neighbours KEEPS the full table** — the `codeIndexesNeighbourTable(initCode)` arm covers exactly this; its full-table path is byte-identical to pre-change.
- **The dead CPU sync attribute WRITE buffer is DROPPED on the WebGPU grid target too (the 600³ sequel to the neighbour-table drop; branch `optimize`).** After the neighbour table is gone, the next dead-weight on a large 3D WebGPU grid is the CPU sync **double-buffer**: in sync mode `initGrid` reserves a SEPARATE per-attr `attrWriteOffset` region (the step reads `r_<attr>`, writes `w_<attr>`, then swaps). But on the **WebGPU target the STEP runs on the GPU** (`runStepWebGPU` does its OWN attrsBufA/B ping-pong), so the CPU `w_<attr>` region (≈9 B/cell for the Accretor = state+Boundary+Fade ≈ **1.9 GB at 600³**, ~30k of 89k pages) is never read/written — the residual dead weight that (after the nbr drop) still kept 600³ over the 4 GiB cap (`value 88990 above the upper bound 65536`). **Fix ([sim.worker.ts](src/simulator/engine/sim.worker.ts) + [wasm/layout.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/wasm/layout.ts), no compiler EMIT touched → JS/WASM byte-identical, `check-compile-identity` clean on all 25 models):** the `init` handler computes **`attrWriteAliased`** = `msg.useWebGPU` (INTENT) `&& gridCells && !async`. Unlike `nbrTableDropped` this is **INDEPENDENT of what CPU functions read** — the ONLY reader that needs a distinct write buffer is the sync STEP, which never runs on WebGPU (so it's BROADER than `nbrTableDropped`, with its own flag). `computeMemoryLayout` gained a trailing `webgpuGridWriteAliased` param that reserves NO write region (`attrWriteOffset[id] = attrReadOffset[id]`, 0 extra bytes — the SAME aliasing the async + agents-only paths use), and `initGrid`'s attr-view loop sets `attrsB[id] = arrA` (write view === read view). **Correctness surface (all write FINAL values, correct with write===read):** `runInit` writes `r_` directly (its post-init `w→r` copy is a self-copy no-op); `runGridInit` likewise; paint/paintManual/writeRegion/clearRegion write the single shared buffer (`dstB[i]=v` becomes a redundant self-write) then upload/patch to the GPU; `resetGrid` fills both (same slot twice). The **STEP guard is shared with the nbr drop** — `runStep` returns early when `nbrTableDropped || attrWriteAliased` (transient no-op while the runtime inits; a genuine `webgpuGridFailed` surfaces the one-time honest "runs on WebGPU only" error, since a dropped-resource model can't fall back to the CPU step). **No WASM-desync risk**: on the WebGPU target SimulatorView sends EMPTY `wasmStepBytes`, so `tryInstantiateWasmModule` early-returns — no WASM module is instantiated against the (now-smaller) `wasmMemory`; `computeLayoutFromModel` (the WASM-compile layout) NEVER passes the alias flag → the WASM module keeps its separate write region → JS/WASM byte-identical. **Documented edge (accepted, same class as the STEP tradeoff):** a WebGPU model with a Grid Init Event (forces the CPU init path) whose per-cell Init Event READS-BACK a cell attribute would see intra-pass writes (r===w) — the Accretor's init only writes position-derived `border`/gridInit-scatters seeds (no attr read-back), so it is provably safe. **Verified in-browser (WebGPU, DISPLAYED):** 300³ plays unchanged (Gen 141, the dendritic accretion structure growing); resizing to **600³ now CLEARS the WASM cap** — `initGrid` succeeds (the `value 88990` error is GONE; the layout is 59327 ≤ 65536 pages), and on this test device the NEXT limit is the honest GPU-device `maxStorageBufferBindingSize` (2048 MB < the GPU's own 2471.9 MB attrs read+write ping-pong — a device-specific limit my fix cannot address, surfaced as a clear `[webgpu] init failed: Grid is too large for WebGPU on this device` message from `startWebGPUInit`, which runs AFTER `initGrid`). **Guarded by [scripts/verify-webgpu-attr-write.mjs](scripts/verify-webgpu-attr-write.mjs)** (layout-delta full−aliased == Σ writeable-attr-bytes at 300³/400³/600³; the aliased 600³ FITS the 4 GiB cap [59327p] while the full one OVERFLOWS [88990p — the exact reported error]; the aliased layout reserves NO separate write region while the full one does; the Accretor's worker predicate `attrWriteAliased === true`). **New practical WASM ceiling:** dropping the write buffer cuts the Accretor's WebGPU per-cell WASM cost from ~27 B/cell → ~18 B/cell, so the WASM-cap cube ceiling moves further past ~860³; the real-device ceiling is now GPU-storage-buffer-bound (~560³ on a 2048 MB device), NOT the WASM cap. **Next dead-weight follow-on (NOT done):** the async-only `orderArray` (`total×4`) + `skippedArray` (`total`) are reserved even in sync mode for layout stability — 5 B/cell dead on a sync WebGPU model; and the CPU `colours` buffer (4 B/cell, needed only for frame-mode readback) — both candidates if the WASM ceiling must move further, but out of scope here (600³ is already GPU-bound, not WASM-bound).
- DO NOT add fake/hardcoded "default viz" output shaders as placeholders for un-implemented per-node emit. The honest path: leave colors uninitialised on GPU, return a clear compile error, let the worker fall back to JS.
- Macros must be expanded BEFORE compile. `expandMacros` walks the graph, replaces each `macro` instance with the macroDef's internal nodes (prefixed ids) plus rewritten edges. Recursion guard depth=20 mirrors WASM. The compileValueNode / compileFlowChain code only sees flat post-expansion graphs.
- Vite serves stale dev-server modules aggressively when `@webgpu/types` arrives via reference. After heavy edits to the webgpu/ files, a hard reload is sometimes needed before the browser sees the new shader code.
- Under direct render, the visible canvas is `drawImage`'d from an OffscreenCanvas owned by the worker — main-thread `getImageData` on the visible canvas can return all-(0,0,0,0) even when the user sees content. Don't trust getImageData for verification under direct render; use `preview_screenshot` to read what the user actually sees.
- Soft-recompile direct-render: reusing the salvaged OffscreenCanvas across `startWebGPUInit`'s unconfigure+reconfigure-with-new-device leaves the canvas in a state where no subsequent `dispatchColorPassAndPresent` produces visible output (viewer switches and Play don't recover; manual Recompile button "works" only because it creates a fresh canvas via Phase 1/2). The main thread sets `recompilePendingCanvasRefresh.current = true` when sending a recompile under direct render; the useWebGPUStatus handler allocates a NEW canvas + `transferControlToOffscreen` + `attachCanvas` on the post-rebuild ack so Phase 2 commits a fresh canvas. Worker isn't torn down — all state survives.

## Target Compatibility readout + resolved-config annotations (C1 — branch `GRA`)

Phase C1 of the Clarity & Simplification initiative ([HANDOFF_CLARITY_SIMPLIFICATION.md](docs/HANDOFF_CLARITY_SIMPLIFICATION.md) §C1, implementing [PROPOSAL_CLARITY_SIMPLIFICATION.md](docs/PROPOSAL_CLARITY_SIMPLIFICATION.md) **P2** + the **P4 core**; plan + mockup [docs/PLAN_CLARITY_C1.md](docs/PLAN_CLARITY_C1.md)/`.html`). **READ-ONLY — zero behaviour change** (`check-compile-identity`: 29 models byte-identical on every surface; the only worker edit is an import swap to shared helpers computing the same numbers).

### The doctrine — four limitation classes, three principles
Every restriction is one of four classes, and the reasons the UI shows carry the class as a tag: **S** semantics (the engine's execution model cannot express it — a blocker), **R** reproducibility (runs, not bit-reproducibly — a note), **F** fast path (runs identically; only ms/generation differ — never an error), **C** capacity (a resource bound, stated WITH its number — a blocker). They derive from three sentences: (1) **sequential vs parallel** — CPU engines run both, the GPU runs only parallel; (2) **CPU is exact, GPU is statistical**; (3) **speed paths are eligibility, not correctness**. The motivating misread this fixes: *"bonds prevent WebGPU"* is FALSE — bonds forfeit GPU **residency** (class F) and `Graph Metrics - Growth Sweep` ships on WASM for **sweep reproducibility** (class R). Two invisible facts reading as one wall.

### `diagnoseTargets(model)` ([src/model/targetDiagnosis.ts](src/model/targetDiagnosis.ts), pure)
Per layer (grid / agents) × per engine (js / wasm / webgpu) a verdict `{ ok, blockers: Reason[], notes: Reason[] }` + the layer's `requested` / `resolved` / `demotionReason`. **THE RULE: every VERDICT is produced by the function that ENFORCES it** — `detectWebGPUIncompatibilities` / `detectWebGPUModelIncompatibilities` / `detectWasmIncompatibilities` (grid), `isAgentGraphWasmSupported` / `isAgentGraphWebGPUSupported` / `agentTargetOf` (agents), `residencyModelBlockers` (the class-F note), `resolveMaxBonds`. This module NEVER re-implements a gate, so the readout cannot drift.
- **A gate that only answers for the CURRENTLY-selected target is asked HYPOTHETICALLY** via a shallow probe clone with that target selected (`{...model, properties:{...properties, useWebGPU:true}}`) — the honest way to answer "could I use WebGPU?" without duplicating its logic. `detectWebGPUModelIncompatibilities` early-outs on `!useWebGPU`, so without the probe the readout would say "no problem" for every non-WebGPU model.
- **REASON TEXTS are a diagnostic layer ON TOP of the verdict.** The agent gates return a bare boolean, so when one says no the module explains it by reading the gate's OWN tables (`AGENT_WASM_SUPPORTED_TYPES` / `AGENT_WEBGPU_SUPPORTED_TYPES`, `AGENT_NEARBY_SCRATCH_SLOTS` = 4, `AGENT_WEBGPU_NEARBY_SLOTS` = 6) plus exact detectors for the documented op-level fundamentals (median / uniform-random aggregate, toggle/next/previous indicators, a cross-agent overwrite aimed at a WIRED non-spawn id — mirroring the gate's own 4 node types / port names / Create-Agent exemption), and falls back to a generic honest sentence otherwise. **A reason can at worst be unhelpfully generic — never wrong about ✓/✗**, because the verdict never depends on it. Swept: all 29 library models satisfy `verdict ⇔ blocker` consistency.
- **Behaviour-SCOPED walks matter** (`walkAgentBehaviourNodes` / `behaviourReachedIds` — flow edges OUT of a reached node + value edges INTO it, exactly the compilers' `behaviourReachableNodeIds`): `divisionEvent` / `agentInit` / `agentOutputMapping` are compiled separately on the CPU on EVERY engine, so a Create Agent in the **Init Event** must NOT read as a residency blocker — **Particle Life spawns its whole population there and IS resident**. Whole-graph scans got this wrong (and named `agentInit` as an unsupported node type on Ant Necrophoresis). The FIELD term stays whole-graph, matching the worker's `agentUsesField`. Following value edges OUTWARD would be wrong too — a value producer shared with the Division Event would drag that CPU-only subtree in.
- All walks are **macro-aware** (the compilers flatten macros up front), and `LOWERED_AWAY` excludes the pre-compile lowering sources (census / periodic step / composites / …) so a lowered node is never reported as unsupported.

### `residencyModelBlockers` ([src/model/agentResidency.ts](src/model/agentResidency.ts)) — the shared residency terms
`agentResidentEligible()` mixed RUNTIME terms (`rt.ready`, the resolved target, `simulateAgents`) with MODEL-derivable ones. The model half moved here and **the worker CALLS it** (`sim.worker.ts` keeps only its runtime terms), so the engine's decision and the explanation the user reads are ONE predicate — the `resolveMaxBonds` single-source discipline; the main thread never imports the worker. Blockers are ordered most-fundamental-first (structural rewriting → bonds → field → sync attrs → positional → growth → spawn/stop/indicators) so a surface showing only the first reason shows the most explanatory one.
- **`ResidencyGraphFacts.bondSlots` is passed IN, not re-derived**: the worker passes its store's real `s.maxBonds` (what was actually allocated), the UI passes the prediction `resolveMaxBonds(cfg)` — the same number by construction (`createAgentStore` calls that resolver), but the worker reports the allocation it HOLDS so a live config edit that has not yet re-allocated can never make engine and readout disagree.

### `effectiveAgentDt(cfg)` ([centerBased.ts](src/model/centerBased.ts)) — the Δt clamp, explained
The Mathias-2020 bound `Δt ← min(Δt_user, 0.2/μ_eff)`, `μ_eff = μ_R + λ`, extracted verbatim from the worker's `clampAgentDt` (which now calls it — same operands, same order, byte-identical engine) and returning `{ requested, dt, muEff, bound, clamped }`. `clamped` is true only when the bound actually REDUCES the value, so a model sitting exactly on the bound reads as unclamped. **Most agent models ARE clamped and never said so** — e.g. Growing Tissue runs 0.0625, not the 0.1 the panel showed (μ_eff = 3.2); Chemotaxis 0.125 from 0.25.

### `capabilityClosureDrivers(profile)` ([agentCapabilities.ts](src/model/agentCapabilities.ts)) — "(required by X)"
DERIVED from `computeCapabilityClosure`, never a hand-written table: close a baseline containing ONLY capability J at the profile's value and record which OTHER keys the closure raised — those are J's requirements; invert to get each row's drivers. `capStrength` ranks the 3-state modes so "did the closure RAISE it?" is decidable for `motion`/`bonds`/`collision` too. Edit the closure and the annotations follow automatically. (Verified: Growing Tissue → `Motion ← Collision, Bonds, Auto-bond`, `Body ← Collision, Growth, Division`, `Bonds ← Auto-bond`.)

### UI surfaces
- **Properties → Compatibility** (`CompatibilityBlock` in [PropertiesPanelContent.tsx](src/modeler/panels/PropertiesPanelContent.tsx)) — its OWN `CollapsibleSection id="compatibility"` directly under Execution (which it explains), rather than nested inside that already-long body. Per layer: the requested→resolved line + one row per engine (✓/✗, "running" marker, class-tagged reasons) + a doctrine footer. Memoised on `model` (the agent gates flatten the agent graph).
- **Effective Δt** — an amber `→ effective Δt … — clamped from … (μ_eff = …)` line under the Time Step row, plus the bound stated when it is NOT binding.
- **Capability rows** — a `(required by …)` accent suffix + a tooltip naming what to turn off to release the row.
- **Simulator chip** — amber for EVERY `resolved ≠ requested` state (previously only a failed WebGPU *device*; a compile-gate demotion reached the console only), with a `⚠` suffix and the classified reason in the tooltip.
- **⧉ Copy** — see "Copying the readouts" below (shared with C2).

### Copying the readouts (Compatibility + Generation Pipeline)
Both sections are report text users paste into bug reports and chats, so each `CollapsibleSection` header carries a **`⧉ Copy`** button (`CopyButton` + the new optional `action` slot on `CollapsibleSection`) that renders the WHOLE section as plain text.
- **THE ROOT CAUSE WAS NOT A `user-select: none`.** Audited live: the ONLY `user-select:none` in the Properties panel is on the click-to-toggle section TITLE rows (+ their chevrons + the Execution "Advanced" toggle) — every readout body computed `user-select: auto` and was already selectable. What made copying impractical is the LAYOUT: each block is a dense stack of flex rows whose ✓/✗ marks, `S`/`R`/`F`/`C` class tags, tempo chips and row indices interleave with the prose, so a hand-drag yields `…rules.⏎✓⏎WebGPU⏎running⏎R⏎Statistical parity…` in a ~300 px column that has to autoscroll. `styles.selectableText` (`user-select: text` + a text cursor) is pinned on the two block roots anyway — explicit intent, an advertised affordance, and insulation from any future inherited `none`. It is scoped to READOUT bodies only; the title rows stay unselectable because they are pure toggles, and no control/slider/reorder-handle region is touched.
- **`compatibilityToText(model)` / `pipelineToText(model)` live directly beside the components they mirror** and are built from the SAME `diagnoseTargets` / `analyzeGeometryTaint` / `describeGenerationPipeline` / `describePipelineGroups` results — **never by scraping the DOM** (a scrape drifts the moment a chip moves). `getText` is called ONLY on click, so the macro-aware, gate-calling derivations cost nothing per render (no second `useMemo` beside the block's).
- **The button sits INSIDE the click-to-toggle header, so its `onClick` MUST `stopPropagation`** or copying collapses the section. `navigator.clipboard.writeText` needs a secure context AND a focused document; a rejection falls back to a hidden-textarea `execCommand('copy')`, and the label flashes `✓ Copied` / `✗ Failed` for 1.5 s (timer cleared on unmount).
- Styling follows the `.dragHandle` lesson recorded below: the glyph takes `--color-text-tertiary` (NOT `--color-text-muted`, which collapses on both shipped panel surfaces) and the outline the canonical `--color-widget-border`.
- **Verification gotcha:** in an OCCLUDED Browser pane `document.hasFocus()` is false, so `navigator.clipboard.writeText` rejects with `NotAllowedError` (the fail branch is verifiable for real; the success branch needs a resolving stub), and `getComputedStyle` on DESCENDANTS returns a frozen pre-HMR snapshot — read the live `document.styleSheets` rule TEXT instead of a computed colour when checking theme reactivity.

### Gotchas
- `NodeConfig` lives in [modeler/vpl/types.ts](src/modeler/vpl/types.ts), NOT `model/types.ts` (the per-node config record vs the model schema).
- `detectWasmModelIncompatibilities` is DEPRECATED (it wraps the obsolete `detectAgentTargetRestriction`, which keys off the GRID flags and would falsely block every agent model) — the readout deliberately does NOT call it; it calls the live per-node `detectWasmIncompatibilities` so a future WASM-only gap surfaces with no edit here.

## Generation Pipeline panel (C2 — branch `GRA`)

Phase C2 of the Clarity & Simplification initiative ([HANDOFF_CLARITY_SIMPLIFICATION.md](docs/HANDOFF_CLARITY_SIMPLIFICATION.md) §C2, implementing [PROPOSAL_CLARITY_SIMPLIFICATION.md](docs/PROPOSAL_CLARITY_SIMPLIFICATION.md) **P3** + its tempo tags from Appendix A; plan + mockup [docs/PLAN_CLARITY_C2.md](docs/PLAN_CLARITY_C2.md)/`.html`). **READ-ONLY — zero behaviour change**: one new pure module + one Properties section + one harness; nothing in the engine, the compilers or the worker was touched (`check-compile-identity`: 29 models byte-identical on every surface).

**The gap it closes** (proposal §1.3): the CA-grid contract is legible — *the graph is the rule; the engine double-buffers and runs the colour pass.* The AGENT generation is ~20 interleaved phases, only two or three of which are the user's graphs, and NOTHING showed that sequence, which phases were active for their model, or which resolved values each phase reads. The capability work had already made the GATING real; what was missing was making the PIPELINE visible.

### `describeGenerationPipeline(model)` ([src/model/generationPipeline.ts](src/model/generationPipeline.ts), pure)
Returns `PipelinePhase[]` in EXECUTION order — `{ id, title, owner: 'graph'|'engine', tempo: 'generation'|'event'|'frame'|'reset', active, capability?, detail?, group?, presentation? }`. Companion `describePipelineGroups(model)` gives the bracket headers (the force loop's `×N iterations` from `layoutIterationsOf`) and `integrationFormula(cfg)` the resolved `v = m·v + (Δt/η)·ΣF · cap` line.
- **THE RULE (inherited from C1): every `active` bit and every number comes from the function the ENGINE consults** — `usesSoftCollision` / `usesPositionalCollision` / `usesEngineSprings` / `usesEngineGrowth` / `usesCharge` / `chargeParamsOf` / `chargeMaxDistOf` / `layoutIterationsOf` / `resolveMaxBonds` / `cbNum` / **C1's `effectiveAgentDt`** / `sparseSteppingEnabled`. Never a parallel hand-written truth.
- **Where a GRAPH-CONTENT question has an engine usage gate, that gate is called** rather than scanned locally: `agentGraphUsesBondRequests(model)` (the gate that SIZES the request queue) drives the drain row, `dividePartitionTableForModel(model)` (the table the engine INDEXES at runtime) drives the divisions row + its partition/daughter-bond detail, and `periodicParams(config)` (the lowering's OWN clamp) produces the cadence note. **The one deliberate exception, stated in the module header**: "does the graph contain a Kill Agent / a Division Event root / a sprite / an Output Mapping" has no resolver — the engine simply runs the phase and it no-ops — so those come from the macro-aware `walkNodes` scan (the C1 discipline).
- **Phase order mirrors the shipped loops exactly** (`sim.worker.ts` `runAgentStep` → `runAgentStructuralPhase` → `runStep`, the step-message batch loop, the reset handler's `runInit` → `runGridInit` → `runAgentInit`). **Agents step BEFORE cells** (Decision D-FIELD, the closed agent↔grid loop) — a field-using model additionally gets *"reads/writes the cell field here — your deposit is what the cell step below then sees"* on the behaviour row, which is exactly WHY that order holds.
- The canonical order (a grid-only or agents-only model is an ordered PROJECTION of it, asserted by the harness): `init.cell` `init.grid` `init.agent` → `agent.forceReset` `agent.spatialHash` `agent.primeAttrs` `agent.behaviour` `agent.commitAttrs` → [forces group] `agent.charge` `agent.softCollision` `agent.springs` `agent.integrate` `agent.growth` → `agent.positional` → [structural group] `structural.drain` `structural.death` `structural.divide` `agent.divisionEvent` `structural.autoBond` `structural.sweep` → `agent.sprites` → `cell.asyncOrder` `cell.step` `cell.sparse` `cell.swap` → `indicators` → `color.cells` `color.agents`.
- **`presentation?` is RESERVED and never written by C2** — C8 (the geometry taint check) sets it on the force/motion/layout phases so they can render *"presentation only — does not affect your rule"*. Shipping the field now means C8 needs no shape change.
- **Scope**: it answers what the model ASKS FOR, from the model alone. Whether a fast path actually ENGAGED at runtime is C3's diagnostics popover, deliberately not mixed in. The panel is **not editable** (proposal §4 — a user-orderable engine pipeline reopens every cross-target verification).

### UI + Help
- **Properties → Generation Pipeline** (`GenerationPipelineBlock` in [PropertiesPanelContent.tsx](src/modeler/panels/PropertiesPanelContent.tsx)) — its own `CollapsibleSection id="pipeline"` directly under Compatibility (C1 answers *which engine*, C2 answers *what does it do*). A coloured left RAIL carries owner attribution (accent = your graph, grey = engine); a per-row tempo CHIP carries the Appendix-A question; inactive rows render struck + dimmed as `off — needs <capability>` (they are NOT hidden — seeing that bond springs exist and are off IS the clarity win); consecutive same-`group` rows render inside a dashed bracket with the group's own resolved number.
- **⧉ Copy** — `pipelineToText` renders the ordered list as plain text (group brackets become `-- Force loop (×N iterations) --` header lines + an extra indent; an inactive phase reads `off — needs X`). See "Copying the readouts" in the C1 section above for the shared mechanism and the root-cause finding.
- **HelpView's "What runs each generation"** renders `<GenerationPipelineReference/>`, which calls **the same function** over a synthetic everything-on model (`FULL_AGENT_PROFILE` + `charge:'on'`, so a NEW capability appears there automatically). There is deliberately **NO hand-written duplicate table** — the runbook forbids one, and a duplicate is how the earlier docs drift happened.

### Drift guard — [scripts/test-generation-pipeline.mjs](scripts/test-generation-pipeline.mjs)
**3401 checks.** (1) **Activity ⇔ resolver** over a 288-combination synthetic matrix (bonding × collision off/soft/positional × bonds off/data/physics × growth × charge × auto-bond × sync/async × growthRate), the harness re-deriving each truth from the engine's OWN resolver so a drift in EITHER direction fails; (2) **phase ORDER** against a hard-coded list (+ sub-lists must be ordered projections of it); (3) every shipped model produces a pipeline, with the same resolver spot-checks on REAL configs + per-model assertions for the five verification models; (4) **six in-harness negative controls**. Proven live by **source mutation**: hard-coding `active: true` on soft collision → 198 failures; swapping the death/divide rows → the order check reports the exact diff. Run it after ANY change to the module, the resolvers it reads, or the worker loops it describes.
