### Scene geometry is rasterized at the SAME sample count on every path (branch `polishing`)

User report: *"Moving the cursor out and back to the canvas on 3D Particles makes the Grid (if toggled on) change its brightness."* Render-layer only — **`git diff --stat` = [sceneWireframe.ts](src/simulator/engine/sceneWireframe.ts) + [webgpuRuntime.ts](src/simulator/engine/webgpuRuntime.ts) + [agentWebgpuRuntime.ts](src/simulator/engine/agentWebgpuRuntime.ts) + the harness; no compiler / worker / engine / gl3d file.**

**THE LESSON, and the companion to the ownership rule below: SHARING THE GEOMETRY IS NOT ENOUGH — the DRAW STATE has to match too.** The brush-plane pass established that the three renderers build the wireframes from one builder; this one closes the other half. The **cursor going in and out of the canvas flips free↔frame** (the UI-sync hover pin), and gl3d's WebGL2 context is created with **`antialias: true`** while the two worker WGSL passes sat at WebGPU's **default sampleCount 1** — so the same 1-pixel line was multisampled in one mode and single-sampled in the other.

- **MEASURED, not inferred** (Particle Life 3D's floor grid: the SAME 274 vertices through the SAME MVP at 500×500, rendered through gl3d, then through a WebGPU rig reproducing the shipped line pipeline at both sample counts):

  | | lit px | fully covered | mean α | Σα vs gl3d | per-scanline error |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | gl3d (frame mode) | 38 493 | 48 % | 198.15 | — | — |
  | **worker, sampleCount 1 (the BUG)** | 20 420 | 100 % | 255 | **0.683×** | **32.09 %** |
  | **worker, SCENE_MSAA_SAMPLES (the FIX)** | 37 677 | 52 % | 202.5 | **1.0003×** | **1.61 %** |

  The alpha histogram is the tell: gl3d's is exactly `{255, 191, 127, 64}` = 4/4…1/4 coverage of a **4×** MSAA buffer. The per-scanline figure is the phase-insensitive one (mean |Δ| of Σα per row over the 229 rows the grid touches) — a 20× reduction, and no fully-lit reference pixel goes dark in either direction (1-px tolerance).
- **`SCENE_MSAA_SAMPLES` (4) lives in [sceneWireframe.ts](src/simulator/engine/sceneWireframe.ts)** — beside the geometry the three renderers already share, because it is the same class of thing: a value that must not drift between them. Both worker passes now render into an MSAA colour texture and **RESOLVE onto the swap-chain texture** (`storeOp: 'discard'` on the multisampled attachment — only the resolve is ever read), with their depth attachment at the same count (a mismatched pairing is invalid) and `multisample: { count }` on **every** pipeline drawing into that pass.
- **WHY 4 and not "whatever WebGL picked":** WebGPU core guarantees sampleCount 1 and 4 only, and `antialias: true` resolves to 4 on the overwhelmingly common configuration. A driver choosing a different WebGL count leaves a small residual — vastly smaller than the 1-vs-4 gap — and there is no portable way to ask WebGPU for it.
- **Two things ride along, both wanted:** the voxel **cubes** now antialias their silhouettes the way gl3d's already did (a second free↔frame alignment), and the **sphere impostors are unchanged** — their silhouette is a `discard`, which kills the whole fragment and all its samples, so MSAA cannot smooth it (the documented reason `antialias: true` buys gl3d nothing there either). The voxel **shadow** pass keeps its own single-sampled depth target and is deliberately untouched.
- **Verified on the real GPU**: the pixel table above (the rig's 4× column matches gl3d to 0.03 % of total light) plus, in the running app, Particle Life 3D on the WebGPU agent target (`agentEngineActive: 'webgpu'`, `directActive: true`, 100 generations, **0 fallback events, 0 console errors**) and Life3D on the WebGPU grid target (voxel free mode `active: true`, `uiSync: false`, **15 presents**, compaction 1073/13824 instances, 0 errors) — a present only completes if the multisampled pass validates. Pinned by the **B17** block in [scripts/verify-agent-render.mjs](scripts/verify-agent-render.mjs) (19 checks: the shared constant, gl3d's `antialias: true` premise, both colour+depth attachments, both resolves, every pipeline's `multisample`, both teardowns, and the shadow pass staying single-sampled); **negative-controlled by SOURCE MUTATION — 3 mutations, 4 failures, each naming exactly the check that covers it** (drop the agent line pipeline's multisample, drop the voxel resolveTarget, revert both depth textures).

### The brush plane is depth-tested on every path (branch `updates`)

User report: *"3D CA Grid when using brush Plane it is always being drawn in front of the 3D cells."* Render-layer only — **`git diff --stat` = [gl3d.ts](src/simulator/render/gl3d.ts) + [sceneWireframe.ts](src/simulator/engine/sceneWireframe.ts) + [webgpuRuntime.ts](src/simulator/engine/webgpuRuntime.ts) + [agentWebgpuRuntime.ts](src/simulator/engine/agentWebgpuRuntime.ts) + [sim.worker.ts](src/simulator/engine/sim.worker.ts) + [SimulatorView.tsx](src/simulator/SimulatorView.tsx) + the harness; no compiler / node / engine file.**

**THE RULE THIS SETTLES, and the one to apply to anything added to the 3D viewport: geometry that sits at a definite place IN the volume is WORKER-OWNED and depth-tested in free mode; CURSOR/UI meant to be seen THROUGH the scene stays in gl3d with depth off.** The scene wireframes (bounds/grid/axes) and the brush interaction PLANE are the first group; the brush footprint OUTLINE, hovered/inspected cell cubes, agent rings, axis labels and the gizmo are the second.

- **ROOT CAUSE — one per path.** **FREE mode (both of them) was the bug**: it is a TWO-CANVAS split (the worker presents its scene into the canvas underneath, gl3d draws on a TRANSPARENT canvas above), the two share no depth buffer, so anything gl3d draws there composites in front of every cell/agent unconditionally. `46e0954` moved the WIREFRAMES into the worker's depth-tested line passes for exactly this reason and left the plane behind — the same defect, one group later. **FRAME mode was already CORRECT** and is unchanged: `renderBrushPlane` runs BEFORE the voxel/agent passes into the SAME depth buffer, so the `LESS` test lets nearer geometry overwrite it (measured: a plane at layer 12 of Life3D is 89.1 % occluded by the structure). Note the tie-break differs by mode (frame draws the plane FIRST, the worker draws it AFTER the cubes), which only matters for exactly co-planar depths — the plane sits at a layer CENTRE and cube faces at ±0.5, so no ties arise.
- **ONE builder, so the flip cannot move a line**: **`buildBrushPlaneVerts(W,H,D,{axis,pos})`** in [sceneWireframe.ts](src/simulator/engine/sceneWireframe.ts) is now what gl3d's `renderBrushPlane` CALLS (a stronger guarantee than `renderOverlays`' documented lockstep pair — there is no second copy to drift). gl3d gained its one import of that dependency-free geometry leaf.
- **The plane rides the EXISTING line pass in both workers — no new pipeline, no new binding, no new uniform.** `ensureVoxelLineBuffer` / `ensureAgentLineBuffer` CONCATENATE `[wireframes, plane]` into the one vertex buffer and one draw (identical pipeline state — line-list, depth-test + depth-write, `less` — and the same rebuild triggers), and the rebuild SIGNATURE carries `axis|pos` so moving the slider actually rebuilds. **The agent pass's GL→WebGPU clip-z remap is inherited automatically** (its spheres write `frag_depth`; the voxel pass needs none) — measured, see below.
- **`plane` rides `setGridViz` / `setAgentViz`** (optional field, `null` = off) — the messages that already mean "what scene-anchored geometry does the worker draw", so every re-apply site (attach ack / refresh / status) carries it for free. Worker module state `gridPlane3d` / `agentPlane3d`. The main thread posts from `gridPlaneMsg()` inside `postGridViz`/`postAgentViz`, and the `plane3d` effect re-posts both on any axis / position / enable change (the refs are assigned above the posts, so both helpers read the new value).
- **gl3d skips it via the EXISTING `wireframesExternal` flag**, whose meaning widened from "the worker draws the wireframes" to "the worker owns the depth-tested scene geometry" — one `sceneExternal` guard now covers `renderOverlays()` AND `renderBrushPlane()`. The `agentsInFront` depth-restore re-draw (frame mode) still re-draws both, unchanged.
- **VERIFIED ON THE REAL GPU** (occluded pane ⇒ gl3d `readPixels` + a WebGPU offscreen rig, never composited pixels). **Frame-mode ground truth** (Life3D 24³, 1119 cells, gl3d): plane at z0/z6 = 0 % occluded, z12 = **89.1 %**, z18 = 74.7 %, z23 = 57.6 %. **The WebGPU arrangement** — an offscreen rig rendering the SHIPPED `buildBrushPlaneVerts` through the shipped line-pipeline descriptor against the EXACT 1119 cells the worker's compaction produced (read out with `__voxelReadback`), same `sceneCameraMatrices` mvp: z0 = 0 %, z12 = **90.5 %**, y12 = 48.6 %, x12 = 46.6 %, x0 = 47.8 % — **within 1.5 points of frame mode on all five**, and **0 of every rig plane pixel falls outside the frame-mode plane mask** (1-px dilated for gl3d's MSAA), i.e. the free render never shows plane where the depth-correct render doesn't. The pre-fix behaviour is the same rig's voxels-off column (0 % occluded, 14980 px at z12 against 1418) — a **10.6×** difference. **The concatenation is lossless**: the combined buffer's mask is EXACTLY the union of wire-only ∪ plane-only (10457 = 10457, 0 missing, 0 extra). **The agent-sphere pass** (spheres writing `frag_depth` like the shipped `SPHERE_FS`): shipped remap ⇒ 16.8 % occluded, **negative control without the remap ⇒ 2.0 %** — the 46e0954 failure mode reproduced, so the plane genuinely needs (and gets) that pass's remap. **gl3d in free mode contributes 0 plane pixels** with `wireframesExternal` true and the full plane (36917 px on Life3D, 102223 px on the 300³ Accretor) with it false — the skip is the flag, not a deletion — while the cursor set still renders (2385 lit px). **Through the real UI**: the Brush plane checkbox, the three axis buttons and the position slider each post exactly one `setGridViz`/`setAgentViz` with the right spec (`null` when unticked) on a grid model (Life3D) and on an agents-only 3D model (Particle Life 3D, which does show the control), the worker's present counter advances, `pickOnPlane` still resolves every ray to the plane's layer, and the 300³ Accretor takes the plane with **0 console errors** on a clean load.
- **⚠ Verification limits worth remembering**: the worker's WebGPU swap-chain image is **unreadable from the main thread while the pane is occluded** — `drawImage`/`createImageBitmap` on the transferred voxel canvas return fully transparent (measured), which is why the offscreen rig exists. And a paint can't be driven end-to-end there either (`flushPaintBatch` is rAF-coalesced, and rAF is suspended) — `pickOnPlane` was exercised directly instead. Also: React re-renders the plane block on every change, so DOM nodes captured before a click are STALE — re-query the controls between steps.

### 3D depth precision — bonds no longer draw in front of agents (branch `updates`)

User report: *"In 3D, bonds (edges), when zoomed out, end up being drawn in front of all agents … extremely hard to visualize when the model has many bonds."* Render-layer only — **`check-compile-identity`: 29 models byte-identical on every surface**; nothing in the worker, the engine or any compiler was touched (`git diff --stat` = [gl3d.ts](src/simulator/render/gl3d.ts) + the new harness).

**ROOT CAUSE — the near plane was a FIXED 0.05, so the depth buffer's world resolution collapsed as you zoomed out.** A bond is a LINE between two agent CENTRES; an agent is a sphere impostor whose FS writes its FRONT SURFACE depth. Bonds draw FIRST (`render()`), so the only margin a sphere has to cover a bond is its own `radius`. A perspective depth buffer's world-space quantum is `Δz ≈ z²/(near·2²⁴)`, so with a fixed `near` it grows with the SQUARE of the camera distance and overtakes the agent radius at

> `dist ≈ sqrt(radius · 2²⁴ · near) / maxGridDim`

— **≈5.8 for the shipped 200³ 3D Tissue, and ≈1.3 for a 600-unit Graph-Rewriting world with 0.7-unit nodes, i.e. TIGHTER THAN THE DEFAULT ZOOM.** Past it the sphere's front surface and the bond quantize into the SAME 24-bit bucket, GL_LESS rejects the sphere, and the bond mesh punches through every agent. **Measured through the real renderer on the shipped 3D Tissue** (1635 agents / 7659 bonds): agent ink lost to bonds **0.1% at dist 1 → 4.7% at dist 5 → 34.4% at dist 8**; on a GRA-shaped lattice (600³ world, 0.7 nodes, 1344 bonds) **60% at dist 1 → 90% at dist 1.9**. There is no error and no wrong-looking buffer — only pixels.

**THE FIX — three layers, in order of impact.**
1. **`sceneNearPlane(r, W, H, D, target, forward)`** (gl3d.ts, exported) makes the near plane ADAPTIVE — a quarter of the clearance between the eye and the nearest thing we draw, floored at the historical `MIN_NEAR_PLANE` (0.05) when the camera is inside the scene. It feeds the SHARED `sceneCameraMatrices`, so the WebGL renderer and BOTH worker WGSL free-mode paths move together and can never disagree. Quantum at dist 1.9 on the 3D Tissue: **0.172 → 1.7e-4 world units (~1000×)**.
   - **THE 0.25 FACTOR IS LOAD-BEARING, not a taste knob.** The WGSL passes feed this GL-convention matrix straight into WebGPU, whose clip volume keeps only `z_clip ∈ [0, w]` — it discards everything closer than the `z_ndc = 0` plane at `2fn/(f+n) ≈ 2·near`. A quarter of the clearance puts that plane at ~half the distance to the nearest geometry, a 2× margin. **Never raise it past 0.5 without also remapping z in every WGSL vertex shader.**
   - **`sceneReachTowardCamera` uses the box's exact SUPPORT along the view axis** (`Σ half_i·|forward_i|`), not the half-diagonal — a 600³ cube seen down an axis reaches 300, not 520, which is what keeps the adaptive plane engaged at close zoom. Padded by the overlays' `ext` (must match renderOverlays / renderAxisLabels / the worker's `buildVoxelOverlayVerts`) and by `|target|` for panning.
2. **The agent-surface passes compare LEQUAL** (`beginSurfaceDepth`/`endSurfaceDepth`, wrapping the sphere, metaball and sprite draws), so a residual quantized tie resolves toward the SURFACE. Sound because the window-depth mapping is strictly increasing in eye distance: a genuinely nearer point can never land in a larger bucket, so `bucket(sphereFront) ≤ bucket(bondPoint)` ALWAYS. **Scoped and restored** — left on globally, the BOND pass (which draws after the voxels) would win ties against the CA-grid cubes and bleed through the volume.
3. **Bonds now meet the agent SURFACE, not its centre** (`uploadAgents` trims each end by that agent's radius, clamped to 45% per side so an overlapping pair can't invert). GL rasterises a line at a MINIMUM of one pixel however far away it is while an agent's disc shrinks with distance, so a centre-to-centre bond covers its own endpoints outright once an agent is a pixel or two across — ink that is geometrically ON the agent, which no depth fix can reach. Also simply the correct ball-and-stick geometry.

**Measured after** (same models, true before/after with the old projection reconstructed in-page): 3D Tissue **34.4% → 0.5% at dist 8** (70×) and **4.7% → 0.5% at dist 5**, flat across the whole zoom range instead of exploding; GRA lattice **90.1% → 54.2% at dist 1.9**. The GRA residual is the honest floor — at that zoom each node is under a pixel while 1344 one-pixel bonds cross it, so there is genuinely more line ink than node ink (zoom in, or use the Show-bonds toggle).

**Gate: [scripts/verify-3d-depth-precision.mjs](scripts/verify-3d-depth-precision.mjs)** (25 checks) — the occlusion margin (radius ≥ 8 depth buckets at every zoom outside the scene), the WebGPU clip-safety margin, "never worse than the old fixed near" over the whole shipped camera range, the resolver's own contract, and that every shipped 3D model has a CASES entry. **`--old` is the negative control** and fails assertion 1 on all six model shapes. Run it after ANY change to the projection, the near-plane resolver, or the agent-surface depth state.

**Verified in-browser**: the 3D Tissue A/B above; a magnified side-by-side on a GRA lattice at dist 1.9 (before = a near-uniform white blob, after = the node array clearly visible through the mesh); clip interval (slab + camera axis) cuts correctly; alpha blend, agent alpha blend, metaballs and agents-in-front OFF all render with `glError 0`; **`depthFunc` is back at `LESS` after every render** (no state leak); and the two WGSL free-mode paths are unaffected by the new projection — **Life3D (voxel free mode, `overlaysOnly:true`) and the Accretor 300³ render at dist 0.3 through 8 with nothing clipped**, and Particle Life 3D (agent-sphere free mode, 1200 agents) renders at dist 1.9 and 6. Zero console errors throughout.

### 3D viewport — Lighting controls + Cell gaps toggle (branch `sim_agent_fixes`)
Plan + mockup: [docs/PLAN_LIBRARY_3D_VIEW_UX.md](docs/PLAN_LIBRARY_3D_VIEW_UX.md) / `.html` (also covers the Models Library browse tools). Render-layer only — zero compiler/worker/schema impact; 2D untouched.
- **Lighting** ([gl3d.ts](src/simulator/render/gl3d.ts)): the voxel FS + agent-sphere FS no longer hardcode `L=normalize(0.4,0.8,0.6)` / `0.45+0.55·n·L` — they take uniforms `uLightDir`/`uAmbient`/`uDiffuse`/`uSpecular`(+`uViewDir` on the voxel FS), shade = `ambient + diffuse·max(0,n·L)` + an optional white Blinn-Phong `specular·max(0,n·H)³²`. **`Light3D`** (exported, + `DEFAULT_LIGHT3D`): `{ mode:'camera'|'world', bx, by, wx, wy, wz, ambient, diffuse, specular }`. **THE DEFAULT IS A VIEW-ANCHORED KEY LIGHT AT THE BALL'S MAX TOP-LEFT POINT** (`mode:'camera'`, `bx = −LIGHT_BALL_MAX_R/√2`, `by = +LIGHT_BALL_MAX_R/√2` — the 45° top-left point on the edge of the dot's travel disc, i.e. exactly where a drag to the widget's top-left corner lands) — a deliberate **user-requested default change (2026-08)**; it previously reproduced the historical hardcoded shade exactly (world mode, `normalize(0.4,0.8,0.6)`). The INTENSITIES are unchanged (.45/.55/0), and `wx/wy/wz` keep the historical world vector as the world-mode fallback, so only the light's ANCHOR + DIRECTION moved. Screen-space the default projects to `right −0.6364 / up +0.6364 / toward-viewer +0.4359`, **invariant under orbit** (that IS camera mode); on the shipped Z-up remap the three visible cube faces come out screen-up 0.874 (brightest) / screen-left 0.668 / screen-right 0.450 (pure ambient) — a textbook top-left key. **`LIGHT_BALL_MAX_R` (0.9) lives in gl3d.ts, not the widget** — it is BOTH the widget's drag clamp (`LightBallWidget` imports it) and the radius the default sits at, so a widget re-tune can never leave the default out of range. A **SAVED `genesisca_sim_settings.light3d` is never clobbered**: `sanitizeLight3d` falls back to the default only per MISSING/malformed field (its `mode` arm accepts either literal and otherwise takes `d.mode`), so a user who tuned their light keeps it across the default change. `setLight()` + the per-frame `lightWorldDir()`: **camera** mode combines the ball position (bx,by, implied bz=√(1−bx²−by²) toward the viewer) with the CURRENT camera basis each frame (light rides the view — headlight/matcap); **world** mode returns the stored unit vector (scene-fixed — sun). `setLightUniforms` runs inside `setCommonUniforms` + `setSphereUniforms` (null locations on the pick programs no-op per GL spec). `cameraBasis` is now EXPORTED — SimulatorView's `applyLightBall`/`setLightMode` convert a world-mode drag (and the camera→world switch, which freezes the current view-relative dir so switching NEVER jumps the shading) through it. UI ([SimulatorView.tsx](src/simulator/SimulatorView.tsx) 3D View panel): a **Lighting** block — [LightBallWidget.tsx](src/simulator/LightBallWidget.tsx) (an SVG "sun position" ball: radial-gradient highlight + dot track the light; window-level pointer listeners like ClipIntervalSlider) + Ambient/Light/Shine range sliders + View/World mode buttons + Reset. State `light3d` (sanitized on load via `sanitizeLight3d`) persists in `genesisca_sim_settings.light3d`. **NB the state is declared with the other persisted view options ABOVE the settings-persist effect** (declaring it in the 3D-controls block below TDZ-crashes the persist dep array); the ball/mode HELPERS stay in the 3D block (they close over `cam3dRef`). Verified: ambient slider brightens; Reset restores the baseline sum bit-exactly; ball drag changes shading with identical lit-pixel count; View→World switch = 0 pixel change; orbit-away-and-back in World mode ≠ the original (light stayed put) — the mode semantics proof.
- **Cell gaps** ([gl3d.ts](src/simulator/render/gl3d.ts) `setCellGaps(on)`): the voxel `uCubeScale` is no longer the hardcoded 0.92 — ON (the historical look) = 0.92; OFF (**default since the occlusion round** — flush cubes = the seamless-solid look AND the mode where buried-cell culling engages; the state default is `saved.cellGaps3d === true` so an explicitly saved ON is respected) = **1.001**, deliberately NOT 1.0 (exactly-coplanar shared faces of adjacent cubes z-fight along seam edges; the 0.001 overlap keeps every interior face strictly behind a neighbour's outer face → seamless solid volume). The pick pass shares the uniform via `setCommonUniforms`, so clicking "between" cells matches what's drawn. UI: a "Cell gaps" checkbox next to Alpha blend (the 3D analogue of the 2D gridlines toggle), persisted as `genesisca_sim_settings.cellGaps3d`, **gated on `gridCellsOn`** — it only affects the CA-grid voxels, so it's hidden for an **agents-only** model (no grid to render); Alpha blend by contrast stays (it also drives the agent-sphere blend via `setAgentAlphaBlend`). Verified: gaps OFF fills more pixels (156716→160497 lit on Life3D), back ON restores exactly; hidden on Morphogenesis — 3D Tissue (agents-only), shown on Life3D.

#### Global lighting — cast shadows + occlusion AO (opt-in; branch `sim_agent_fixes`)
Two opt-in "global lighting" toggles so cells/agents shade EACH OTHER instead of each surface being lit only by its own normal (the reported "each cell/agent is independently lit" flatness). Both DEFAULT OFF → **byte-identical to the historical shade** (verified: off = exact baseline luminance; strength 0 == off). Render-layer only ([gl3d.ts](src/simulator/render/gl3d.ts) + the [SimulatorView.tsx](src/simulator/SimulatorView.tsx) Lighting panel) — zero compiler/worker/schema impact; 2D untouched. `Light3D` gained `{ shadows, shadowStrength, ao, aoStrength }` (defaults false/0.6/false/0.7; `sanitizeLight3d` clamps them; persisted in `genesisca_sim_settings.light3d`).
- **Cast shadows (shadow map)** — voxels + agents both CAST and RECEIVE. A depth-only pass renders the cubes + agent sphere impostors from the light's ORTHO POV into a `DEPTH_COMPONENT24` `sampler2DShadow` texture (`renderShadowMap`, first in `render()`, no-op when off); the voxel + sphere FS PCF-sample it (shared `SHADOW_GLSL` `shadowFactor(fragWorld, ndl)` — 3×3 taps over hardware-2×2 compare) to attenuate the diffuse+specular. **The light matrix** (`computeLightMVP`) fits the volume's bounding SPHERE (radius R from the origin-centred world), eye at `2R·L`, ortho `±R`, near/far `0.5R/3.5R` — stable at ANY light angle; up-vector degeneracy guarded (`|L.z|>0.99 → [0,1,0]`). **Two dedicated depth programs**: `CUBE_SHADOW_VS/FS` (decodes the cell centre EXACTLY like the main VS — col→+X/row→-Y/layer→-Z) and `SPHERE_SHADOW_VS/FS` (a LIGHT-facing billboard — axes ⟂ L via cross products — raycast to the light-facing sphere hemisphere + `gl_FragDepth`). Both clip-aware (a clipped-open view's interior is lit as if the removed shell weren't casting). **Scale-relative bias** `uShadowBias = 0.9/(3R)` (a ≈1-cell world bias mapped into the light's [0,1] depth range) + slope term — avoids acne on small grids AND peter-panning on huge ones. `SHADOW_SIZE=2048`, on `SHADOW_TEX_UNIT=1`; a 1×1 dummy depth-compare texture (`ensureDummyShadowTex`) is ALWAYS bound to unit 1 so the `sampler2DShadow` stays valid when shadows are off (the FS branches out on `uShadowEnabled=0`). Depth-only FBO completeness is checked → `shadowUnsupported` quietly disables shadows on a driver that can't do it. `sampler2DShadow` needs an explicit `precision highp sampler2DShadow;` in GLSL ES 3.00 (the compile error that first surfaced).
- **Ambient occlusion (voxel occupancy)** — each cell is darkened by how many of its 6 face-neighbours are filled (crevices/interiors → darker), computed in `uploadColors` INSIDE the existing per-step cell scan (an incremental `(col,row,layer)` walk + 6 bounded neighbour alpha reads, ONLY when AO is on — the off path stays as cheap as before). Stored in a PARALLEL `aoBuf` (attrib 4 on the cube VAO; the pick/shadow cube programs don't declare it → ignored) and applied to the AMBIENT term (`uAmbient*(1 - aoStrength*vAO)`), so shadows own the diffuse and AO owns the ambient. `sortBackToFront` reorders `aoData` in step with the alpha-blend instance reorder. `aoBuf` is kept finite across every off→on→off + capacity-grow path (grow allocates zeros; on = refresh; off+no-grow = skip, ×0 in the FS). Because AO is BAKED at upload, toggling it forces a re-upload (`prevAoRef` resets `lastUploadedColors3dRef` in the light3d effect — colours are unchanged so `draw()` would otherwise skip `uploadColors`). Agents get their "no longer independently lit" from the cast shadows, not occupancy AO (spheres already read as 3D; a screen-space / agent-cluster AO is a possible follow-up).
- **UI**: two rows (Shadows / Occlusion) in the 3D-View Lighting panel — a checkbox + a strength slider each (dimmed when off), below the View/World mode buttons. **The Occlusion row is gated on `gridCellsOn`** (hidden for an agents-only model, like Cell gaps): occupancy AO is computed from CELL face-neighbours in `uploadColors`, so it does nothing for agents — Shadows stays (agents cast + receive).
- **Verified on the GPU (readPixels luminance; screenshots time out on this heavy page)**: all shaders compile + the renderer inits; AO on darkens Life3D meanLum 97.82→85.57 (same pixel count) and off restores EXACTLY 97.82; shadows scale with strength (97.82 → 95.09 @0.6 → 93.32 @1.0) and off restores 97.82; a 200-agent dense cluster receives shadows (scales 0→1); zero console errors throughout. tsc + `npm run build` clean. (The planned adversarial-review workflow's agents hit the session limit — replaced by a manual adversarial self-review across the same dimensions; no defects.)

#### Agent Metaballs — implicit-surface agent rendering, 2D + 3D (opt-in; branch `sim_agent_fixes`)
Render the agent population as a **fused implicit surface** (Blender-metaball semantics) instead of discrete circles / sphere impostors — each agent contributes a Wyvill falloff `w = (1 − (d/R)²)³` over `R = influence · radius`, the fields SUM, and the surface is the isosurface at `threshold`, so overlapping agents bulge toward each other and MERGE (the natural look for tissues/morphogenesis). **Purely a RENDER mode** — picking/brushing/inspect (the sphere pick FBO), bonds, physics, engine, compilers, schema all untouched; sprite-agents are EXCLUDED from the field and keep drawing as billboards on top. Plan + deviations: [docs/PLAN_AGENT_METABALLS.md](docs/PLAN_AGENT_METABALLS.md) (+ `.html` mockup). DEFAULT OFF → byte-identical baseline (verified: off = exact sphere lit-pixel counts).
- **Config**: `Metaballs3D { enabled, influence 1–3, threshold 0.02–0.9, resolution 1|2|4 }` + `DEFAULT_METABALLS3D` + **`metaballAutoThreshold(influence) = (1 − 1/influence²)³`** — the threshold at which a LONE agent renders at EXACTLY its own sphere radius (verified pixel-exact: 585 = 585 px) — all exported from [gl3d.ts](src/simulator/render/gl3d.ts). ONE shared, persisted user setting (`genesisca_sim_settings.agentMetaballs`, state `agentMetaballs` + `sanitizeAgentMetaballs` in [SimulatorView.tsx](src/simulator/SimulatorView.tsx)) drives BOTH the 3D and 2D views. UI: a **Metaballs** block in the 3D View panel (checkbox + Influence/Threshold sliders + a ⟲ auto-threshold button + a 1×/2×/4× Detail control, agent models only) and a **Metaballs** block in the 2D agent common-controls ("Fuse agents into blobs" + the two sliders).
- **3D = bake a density field into a 3D texture, then raymarch it** ([gl3d.ts](src/simulator/render/gl3d.ts) `bakeMetaballField`/`renderMetaballs` + `META_VS`/`META_FS`): the CPU splat reads the **packed `agentInstData`** (already alive-compacted, colours 0..1, and sprite-agents flagged by a NEGATIVE radius — NB the SNAPSHOT's radius is always positive, so a snapshot-based bake would misclassify sprites) into an RGBA8 `TEXTURE_3D` over the agents' influence bbox (A = Σw/`META_F_MAX`(2.0), RGB = density-weighted colour → colours blend smoothly across fused tissue); the fullscreen-quad FS reconstructs the world ray from `inv(MVP)`, slab-tests the field box, marches (≤512 steps, half-voxel step) to the first threshold crossing, bisects ×5, shades with the SAME lighting model incl. `shadowFactor()` (the blob RECEIVES cast shadows; the sphere casters approximate the blob's own shadow), and writes `gl_FragDepth` with the SPHERE_FS formula so it depth-interleaves with voxels/bonds/sprites. Clip interval reads as density-0 → the blob is cut OPEN (matching the voxel cut). **The bake is LAZY on a `metaDirty` flag** (set by `setMetaballs` param changes / `uploadAgents` / `clearAgents`) — camera-only frames re-render without re-baking (measured 0.3 ms vs 9–37 ms bakes at 1500 agents); NO SimulatorView snapshot invalidation needed. **Field cap** ~2M voxels (`META_MAX_VOXELS`, ≈128³) with a CONTINUOUS per-axis effective resolution; **torus worlds bake the FULL world with modulo-wrapped splats** (verified: a seam-hugging agent's blob renders on both sides). **The mirroring gotcha**: `uFieldA`/`uFieldB` are the SIGNED world coords of the field's cell-min/cell-max corners — NOT a numeric min/max (the Z-up remap negates row/layer; per-axis `(p−A)/(B−A)` with a negative span is exactly what keeps the texture un-mirrored, and the slab test is order-robust). Texture unit **2** (0 = sprite atlas, 1 = shadow map), bound AFTER `setLightUniforms` (which resets the active unit to 0).
- **2D = an approximate "gooey" filter** ([SimulatorView.tsx](src/simulator/SimulatorView.tsx) `drawAgentsOverlay` + `ensureGooFilter`): non-sprite agent discs draw into an offscreen scratch (`gooScratchRef`, drawn-to only — never `getImageData`'d), then ONE blit through `ctx.filter = 'url(#genesisca-agent-goo)'` — an injected SVG filter of feGaussianBlur (σ = `(influence−1)·avgRadPx·0.85`) + a steep feColorMatrix alpha threshold. **The threshold is anchored to the blurred-disc PEAK alpha** (`1 − exp(−r²/2σ²)`) — without this, lone agents VANISH at high influence because blur flattens their peak below a fixed threshold (found in verification); with it, fusion is monotonic in influence (verified: 5 discs → 1 blob) and the full threshold range stays usable. Sprite-agents draw normally on top (a second `'sprites'` stamp pass); falls back to plain circles when `ctx.filter` is unsupported. `ensureGooFilter` ADOPTS an existing `#genesisca-agent-goo` element by id before creating one — a re-evaluated module (Vite HMR) must not append a duplicate id, since `url(#…)` resolves the FIRST match and the duplicate's params would never reach the canvas (a real debugging trap hit during verification).
- **Verification recipe** (screenshots time out on the 3D page — use `readPixels` via `window.__sim3dRenderer()` + direct `r.setMetaballs(...); r.render()` calls, and count connected components of the lit mask WITH OVERLAYS OFF — the bounds box/gizmo lines otherwise contaminate the component count): off = exact baseline; influence sweep monotonic; threshold monotonic; comps drop to 1 on fusion; pick id identical on/off.

### Post-PR8 — camera/viewport overhaul + interaction-plane brush (feedback round 1)
- **Z-up Blender camera** ([gl3d.ts](src/simulator/render/gl3d.ts)): the world remap is now **Z-up** — XY is the horizon (the 2D-CA plane), `z = uHalf.z - layer` (layer increases DOWNWARD), so a top-down view shows the grid like a 2D CA. `Camera3D` = `{ yaw, pitch, dist, target:[x,y,z] }` (target replaces panX/panY). `cameraBasis()` derives forward/right/up; **`panCamera(cam, dx, dy, scale)`** (exported) pans the target along the camera's right/up axes (screen-space pan, tracks the viewpoint). Input scheme (SimulatorView pointer effect): **MMB-drag OR Alt+LMB-drag = orbit**, **Shift+(MMB/Alt+LMB) = pan**, **wheel = zoom**, **plain LMB = brush** (interaction plane), **Ctrl/Cmd+LMB click = inspect**. (LMB is the brush, so orbit is on MMB/Alt+LMB, Blender-style. **Round 3 adds RMB-drag = pan.**)
- **Scene overlays + gizmo** (`Viz3D = {axes, grid, bounds, gizmo}`): a 2nd unlit line program draws toggleable RGB **axes**, an XY floor **grid** (stepped if >100 cells/axis), and the volume **bounds** box; a corner **gizmo** viewport shows the axes rotating with the camera (orthographic, `camDir`). `setViz()` per frame from `viz3dRef`. (**Round 3 makes the gizmo clickable** — 6 ± endpoints snap to the main POVs — see "feedback round 3".)
- **Clip plane gained a `'camera'` axis** — discards fragments past a plane perpendicular to the view direction (`uClipForward` = camForward); peels toward the viewer. X/Y/Z unchanged.
- **Interaction-plane brush** (the 3D brush): `pickOnPlane(cssX, cssY, cssW, cssH, axis, pos)` unprojects the cursor through `inv(MVP)` to a world ray and intersects the axis-aligned slice plane at grid index `pos`, returning the nearest in-bounds `{layer,row,col}` (or null). LMB-drag ray-traces onto the plane → `paint3dRef`, which **stamps the full brush shape on the plane + interpolates the drag** (see PR8 "Brush shape on the plane"). Controlled by the **Brush plane** toggle (axis + position slider). `mat4Invert`/`unproject`/`mat4Ortho` added.
- **Auto-orbit** (`orbit3d {on, speed}`): a rAF loop spins `cam.yaw` while enabled + 3D + visible. **Collapsible 3D View panel** (`controls3dOpen`) — Reset view, Axes/Grid/Bounds/Gizmo toggles, Auto-orbit+speed, Clip plane (X/Y/Z/View + slider), Brush plane (axis + slider), Alpha blend.
- **Verified** (readPixels): orbit/pan change the image; axes/grid/bounds/gizmo add pixels; camera-axis clip reduces pixels; `pickOnPlane` resolves the correct cell for top-down + 3/4 views on X/Y/Z planes (passing the drawing-buffer dims — the GL canvas's CSS layout size can read 0 in a headless eval, but the real pointer handler uses `getBoundingClientRect`).
- **Live 3D neighbourhood preview** ([NeighborhoodPreview3D.tsx](src/modeler/panels/NeighborhoodPreview3D.tsx)): a small orbiting canvas in the 3D neighbourhood editor that reuses `Gl3DRenderer` to show the centre cell (amber) + neighbour offsets (green) inside a bounds box (auto-orbit + drag + wheel). Rebuilds a synthetic `(2·maxAbs+1)³` colours buffer on `coords3d` change. Verified: the preview canvas lays out + renders (295×170, GL context constructs clean), Generate (Moore r1) → 26 cells reflected.

### PR9 — save/load + indicators + inspector 3D consumer-scan (done)
- **Save/load** ([fileOperations.ts](src/model/fileOperations.ts)): the worker getState payload echoes `depth` ([sim.worker.ts](src/simulator/engine/sim.worker.ts)); `serializeSimState`/`serializePreset` write `gridDepth` (always) + `depth` (inside the grid block); `readStateFile` normalizes `depth`/`gridDepth` → 1 for legacy files. `applySimulationState` deserializes at `total = W*H*depth` (a 3D state would otherwise truncate to its first layer), threads `depth` through `dimsFromState`/`dimsChanged` (adapting the model + flipping it to `dimension:'3d'` when `depth>1`), and the hard dim-validation rejects a depth mismatch with a `W×H×D` message (3rd dim shown only when either side is a volume). The preset-load dim check mirrors it. **`gridDepth.current`** is set beside `gridWidth/Height.current` (init + applySimulationState).
- **Spatial `'layers'` axis**: `computeSpatialIndicators` ([sim.worker.ts](src/simulator/engine/sim.worker.ts)) accepts `xAxis==='layers'` (axisLen = depth; the posBin decode is now 3D-correct — layer=⌊i/WH⌋, row/col within the layer — behaviour-identical in 2D); the `hasSpatialIndicators` gate + the post-loop linked-skip + the WebGPU-reduction-skip all include `'layers'`. `IndicatorSpatialChart` widens `axis` to `'layers'` (axisName 'layer'); `IndicatorDisplay` gained a `gridDepth` prop (axisLength = depth for layers) + its three `isSpatial` checks include `'layers'`; the IndicatorsPanelSection X-axis dropdown offers **Layers (spatial, 3D)** only when `dimension==='3d'`. **Verified**: a per-layer frequency indicator's `true` series matches an independent re-bin by ⌊i/WH⌋ with 0 mismatches.
- **Inspector** ([InspectCellPopover.tsx](src/simulator/InspectCellPopover.tsx)): the `neighborIndex` value decode was 2-axis `(dr, dc)` in PR9; **PR10 made it dimension-aware** — 3D models decode `(dr, dc, dl)` via `unpackNI3` (an `is3d` prop threaded from SimulatorView).
- **Verified**: 3D getState `depth=24`; serialized `gridDepth/depth=24` + the `alive` buffer base64-decodes to the full 13824 bytes (not truncated to W*H); spatial-layers 0 mismatches. `ATTR_TYPE_MAP` needs no change (a longer buffer base64's automatically).

### PR10 — 3-axis NeighborIndex offsets + un-gate the NI family in 3D (done; lockstep)
- **Why:** PR4 gated the whole `neighborIndex` family off in 3D because the packed codec carried only two 16-bit `(dr, dc)` halves. PR10 adds a 3-axis codec and un-gates the family, so offset-based neighbour access (the imperative `getAllNeighborIndexes → filter/pick/forEach → get/setNeighborAttributeByIndex` style) works on the 3D lattice. User decision: "enable 3D offsets, defer the rename" (the `neighborIndex` type id + node labels are unchanged; only 3D support added).
- **Codec** ([niCodec.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/niCodec.ts)): 3D packs three sign-extended **10-bit** fields (`dr<<20 | dc<<10 | dl`, ±511/axis); 2D keeps the verbatim 16-bit codec → **2D output byte-identical**. `INVALID_NI = 0x80000000` stays valid in BOTH (bit 31 free in 3D's bits 0-29; consumers compare the bit pattern before decoding). New: `packNI3`/`unpackNI3`; the emit helpers `niDrExpr`/`niDcExpr`(+`is3d`) / `niDlExpr` / `niPackExpr`(+`is3d`,`dlExpr`) / `niCellExprStmts`(+`is3d` → a 3D branch using `_layer`/`D`/`WH`). `is3dModelLike(model)` — a lightweight 3D check for node files (avoids importing `is3dModel` from compile.ts → circular).
- **Per-model codec selection (single source of truth per target):** JS = `CompileContext.is3d` (= `is3dModel(model)`), threaded into every NI node's `compile(...ctx)`. WASM = `ctx.layerLocalIdx >= 0`. WebGPU = `ctx.layout.gridDepth > 1`. All three resolve the cell via the layer (`(nl*H+nr)*W+nc`, torus wrap or constant→`total` sentinel).
- **JS** ([compile.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/compile.ts)): pre-pass `packCoord(nbr, slot)` packs from `coords3d`+`packNI3` in 3D (for getAllNeighborIndexes / getNeighborIndexesByTags / neighborIndexFromTag); `niCellExprStmts` callers (get/getNeighborsAttr/filter/set/markCellUpdated/moveSelfToNeighbor) pass `ctx?.is3d`; `neighborIndexFromOffset` / `breakDownNeighborIndex` / `flipNeighborIndex` use the dim-aware helpers.
- **WASM** ([wasm/compile.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/wasm/compile.ts)): `pushNiCellIdx` 3D branch; `neighborIndexFromOffset`/`breakDown`/`flip` + `getAllNeighborIndexes` emit the 10-bit codec; the tag pre-pass now packs `_resolvedTagIndexes`/`_resolvedPacked` 3D-aware (this also **fixed a latent bug**: the WASM-only path emitted bare *slot indices* instead of packed NIs — masked whenever the JS pre-pass resolved the config first).
- **WebGPU** ([webgpu/encoder.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/webgpu/encoder.ts) + [compile.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/webgpu/compile.ts)): `nbrCellIdxFromNi` 3D form in the encoder; same three node emitters + `getAllNeighborIndexes` 3D. (Tag NIs read the JS/WASM-resolved packed config, as before.)
- **Un-gate**: removed `requirements.lattice2d` from all 13 NI nodes; the flag is kept as generic 2D-only infra (no current users — comment updated in types.ts). `neighborIndexFromOffset` + `breakDownNeighborIndex` gain a `dl` port, hidden in 2D via `hiddenPorts(_config, model) => is3dModelLike(model) ? [] : ['dl']`. `breakDownNeighborIndex`'s `dl` resolves via the multi-output `_v<id>_dl` convention (already in MULTI_OUTPUT_TYPES); `flipNeighborIndex` preserves dl (the flips are XY-plane). The `neighborIndex` value-type in Switch/Compare needs no change — it compares the packed bit pattern (dimension-agnostic) and now has real sources in 3D.
- **UI**: `NeighborIndexValuePicker` + `NeighborIndexDefaultEditor` ([NeighborIndexDefaultEditor.tsx](src/modeler/panels/NeighborIndexDefaultEditor.tsx)) take an `is3d` prop → pack/decode 3 axes + a `dl` (layer) stepper, grid hint-membership per layer (`coords3d`), 10-bit clamp (±511). Threaded from AttributesPanelContent (default/boundary/undefined editors), ManualBrushPanel, the simulator model-attr panel, and the cell inspector (`unpackNI3`) — all keyed on `dimension==='3d' && (gridDepth??1)>1`.
- **Verified**: tsc + full build clean; cross-target compile parity via the harness (all three emit the 10-bit codec; 2D byte-identical); JS direct-runtime 0 mismatches on a layer-up shift; and the **real worker on all three targets** — a "copy the cell one layer below" rule (`neighborIndexFromOffset(0,0,-1) → getNeighborAttributeByIndex`) rose a seeded ring exactly one layer per step on WASM (L0→L3), JS (L0→L5), and WebGPU (L0→L4), confirming cross-target 3D-NI runtime parity. (This was driven by a throwaway `Shift3D` demo model + a `gen-shift3d.mjs` generator — both **removed** afterward as too specific to ship in the Models Library; the NI-3D code is regression-covered by the dev harness, which needs no shipped model.)

## Reroute Links (wire reroute points)

Movable relay dots placed on a wire (Blender / Unreal blueprint style) so users can bend connections around nodes and fan one output out to many consumers without long crossing wires. Two layers, deliberately decoupled.

### Editor layer (visual-only node)
- React Flow `type: 'rerouteNode'` (in the `nodeTypes` map), rendered by [RerouteNodeComponent.tsx](src/modeler/vpl/RerouteNodeComponent.tsx) — a tiny ~16px dot. It is **NOT** a registry `NodeTypeDef` (like comment / group nodes); it has no `compile()` and never reaches a compiler.
- `data: { nodeType: 'reroute', portCategory: 'value'|'flow', dataType?, config: {} }`. `portCategory` is **locked at creation** from the relayed output (flow ≠ value). One input handle `input_<cat>_in` (left) + one output handle `output_<cat>_out` (right); colored by category (value cyan / flow green / NI amber), with the same compatible/incompatible glow as CaNode handles (subscribes to `connectingFrom`).
- **A reroute always relays an OUTPUT, never an input** → exactly one inbound edge, any number of outbound. So it's a single-input / multi-output relay. **Composes freely:** many reroutes per output port (ordinary fan-out) and chains of reroutes on one link (`A → R1 → R2 → R3 → B`). **Single-incoming is enforced** in `isValidConnection`: a reroute's input rejects a second incoming wire (for BOTH value and flow — a reroute is not a merge point; the collapse pass would otherwise silently keep only the first inbound). `collapseReroutes` keeps "first inbound wins" purely as a defensive fallback for hand-edited files.
- **Normal draggable node:** reroutes are NOT `draggable: false`. They move individually AND as part of a multi-selection (drag a selection of nodes and reroutes go with it) — the earlier `draggable: false` approach broke selection moves and was removed. The press-and-hold gesture is ONLY for creating a reroute on a wire, never for moving an existing one (moving is a plain drag).
- Serialization round-trips like comment/group: `toRFNodes`/`toGraphNodes` map the `rerouteNode` type (the shared type-mapping ternary in [GraphEditor.tsx](src/modeler/vpl/GraphEditor.tsx) was extended at all 4 sites: load, paste, duplicate, undo-macro). `nodeSize` has a 16px case. No schema/`types.ts` change (GraphNode/GraphEdge already round-trip arbitrary node types).

### Creation (press-and-hold gesture, edges only)
- A capture-phase `pointerdown` handler in [GraphEditor.tsx](src/modeler/vpl/GraphEditor.tsx) (mirrors the RMB-through-edges handler). LMB-press on a `.react-flow__edge` and hold ~550ms (staying within ~6px) → split the wire and drop a reroute that then follows the cursor until release (`insertRerouteOnEdge`). Early movement / quick release before the threshold cancels, so wire double-click-delete, edge selection, and RMB-pan are untouched. The handler targets `.react-flow__edge` ONLY — it never intercepts reroute nodes, so repositioning stays a normal RF node drag (and thus works inside a multi-selection).
- Secondary path: the connection-drop menu (drag a wire off a port, release on empty canvas) gains a **"Reroute"** entry, shown only when `origin.kind === 'output'` (`addRerouteAndConnect`). `getOriginPortInfo` has a `reroute` branch so dragging from a reroute carries its category/dataType (chains keep their type + highlight).
- **A freshly created reroute is the SOLE selection.** Both creation paths (`insertRerouteOnEdge` for the press-and-hold, `addRerouteAndConnect` for the menu) deselect every other node (and, for the wire-split path, every edge) when appending the new reroute — `makeRerouteNode` marks it `selected: true`. Pressing on a wire to start the hold does NOT otherwise clear a prior node selection, so without this the reposition drag that immediately follows the hold would drag along whatever the user had selected before (the reported "another node was wrongly moved along" bug).
- Delete = plain delete (the reroute + all its links); React Flow's `deleteElements` removes connected edges, and `deleteSelection` does NOT filter reroutes (only macro boundary nodes).

### Dissolve — remove the dot, KEEP the wiring (the editor inverse of insert-on-wire)
**`dissolveReroute(nodeId)`** ([GraphEditor.tsx](src/modeler/vpl/GraphEditor.tsx)) rewires every consumer of a reroute's output straight to the reroute's **IMMEDIATE upstream source**, then deletes the reroute and its now-dead edges — Blender's term for the same operation, and the exact inverse of the press-and-hold insert gesture. Reached two ways: **"Dissolve Reroute"** in the single-node context menu (which titles itself `Reroute` for a reroute), and a **double-click on the dot** (reroutes had no double-click behaviour, and "double-click a wire element to take it out" is already the editor's idiom — `onEdgeDoubleClick` deletes an edge; `onNodeDoubleClick` branches `macro → enter` / `rerouteNode → dissolve` / `caNode → collapse`). Multi-selection is deliberately out of scope — the single-node menu only.
- **Only the CLICKED reroute dissolves**: its consumers land on whatever fed it, which may be another reroute, so a chain stays intact minus one link (`A → R1 → R2 → B`, dissolve R1 ⇒ `A → R2 → B`). Simpler and less surprising than resolving transitively, and the result is exactly what `collapseReroutes` would then produce.
- **Target handles are preserved verbatim**; the new edge's `source`/`sourceHandle` come from the reroute's single inbound edge (first inbound wins — reroute inputs are single-occupancy, the same defensive rule `collapseReroutes` uses). Fresh edge ids follow the `e_<ts>_rd<n>_<rnd>` convention of `insertRerouteOnEdge`; the consumer's own `style` rides along (a dissolve can't change the wire's category).
- **Degenerate shapes fall out**: NO inbound ⇒ the reroute just deletes and its consumers' edges go too (they were relaying nothing — exactly `collapseReroutes`' `if (!real) continue`); no outbound ⇒ plain delete.
- **Duplicate suppression** (flow-only in practice): a flow input accepts several incoming edges, so a consumer wired BOTH directly from the source AND through the reroute would otherwise end up with two identical edges. A rewritten edge is dropped when an identical `(source, sourceHandle, target, targetHandle)` already exists. A value input can't hit this at all (single-occupancy, enforced by `isValidConnection`), and the compiled result is unchanged either way.
- Standard mutation discipline — `pushCurrentSnapshot()` first (Ctrl+Z restores the dot **and** the original wiring, verified), then `setEdges`/`setNodes` + `scheduleSync()`. The inbound edge is resolved INSIDE the `setEdges` updater, so it can never read a stale edge list.

### Compiler layer (collapse pass — zero per-target emit changes)
- [rerouteCollapse.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/rerouteCollapse.ts) — `collapseReroutes(nodes, edges) → { nodes, edges }`. Removes reroute nodes and rewrites each real consumer's edge to the real source it ultimately relays from, resolving chains transitively (memoized + cycle-guarded). Mirrors `injectLinkedOutputMappings` / `canonicalizeAccessorEdges`. **Hot-path no-op** (returns the same arrays) when no reroutes — the overwhelmingly common case.
- Sound in BOTH sync and async modes (a reroute is a pure wire relay — collapsing changes neither read/write ordering nor any value), so unlike accessor-CSE there is **no async gate**.
- Wired into all three compilers BEFORE linked-OM / CSE / `buildAdjacency` so nothing downstream sees a reroute: **JS** at the top of `compileGraph` (+ also collapse each `MacroDef`'s internal graph, since JS inlines macros lazily); **WASM** / **WebGPU** right after `expandMacros` (so in-macro reroutes, now flattened, collapse for free). `A → R → B` compiles byte-identically to `A → B`. Verified: collapse unit (chain / fan-out / dangling / no-op), JS full-compile byte-identical on Game of Life, and WASM + WebGPU worker runs of a reroute model with zero errors.

## Cross-tab graph clipboard (copy/paste BETWEEN models — branch `updates`)

Copying a piece of graph in one tab and pasting it into a **different model open in
another tab** — the small-scale alternative to the save-a-`.gcamacro` /
import-a-`.gcamacro` round trip the user previously had to perform for two nodes.
Editor-layer only: **no compiler / worker / engine file is touched**, so compile
identity holds by construction.

### Transport — TWO copies, and the fresher one wins ([graphClipboard.ts](src/modeler/vpl/graphClipboard.ts))
Copy/cut writes the **in-memory** module-level clipboard (the historical same-tab
path) **AND** a serialized payload under `localStorage['genesisca_graph_clipboard_v1']`
(same-origin tabs share it; it also survives a reload). Both carry the SAME `at`
stamp, and `readGraphClipboard()` returns the newer — **memory wins a tie**, so a
same-tab flow is unchanged, while a copy performed in another tab afterwards has a
later stamp and wins. **No `storage` event listener**: both the paste and the pane
context menu read lazily, so a tab that never copied anything still lights up Paste.
- **Payload** `{ v: 1, at, kind, nodes, edges, macroDefs? }`. `kind` keeps the
  existing graph-kind rule verbatim (a `cells` payload pastes only on Cells; the
  cross-kind case renders the same DISABLED *"Paste (from X graph)"* item — now with
  an **Overseer** label, which the old two-way ternary mislabelled as "Agents").
- **Malformed entries are IGNORED, never thrown from** — `validate()` shape-checks
  `v`/`at`/`kind`/`nodes`/`edges` and the parse is wrapped, because the pane menu
  reads the clipboard **during render**. A corrupt entry falls back to the in-memory
  clipboard. The parse is cached by the raw string so a re-render of an open menu
  does not re-parse a large payload.
- **Size guard `MAX_STORED_CHARS` (2 MB)**: past it the write is SKIPPED **and the
  existing key is REMOVED** (so another tab can never paste a stale selection
  believing it is this copy) with one `console.warn`; the in-memory clipboard still
  holds it, so same-tab paste is unaffected. `setItem` is also try/caught (quota /
  private mode).

### MacroDefs travel with the selection
A copied `macro` node's `config.macroDefId` names a def in the SOURCE model, which
the pasting tab cannot reach — so **`collectMacroDefBundle` walks the referenced defs
TRANSITIVELY** (a macro nested inside a macro travels too; `seen` guards a cycle) and
bundles them into the payload.
- **Paste is per-node and per-def**: a def **this model already has** takes today's
  path unchanged (`importMacro(srcDef)` once per pasted node = independent copies —
  the Undo-Macro rationale). A def it has **never seen** comes from the bundle: the
  defs referenced from INSIDE the bundle (`nestedMacroDefIds`) are cloned **once per
  paste and shared**, then the directly-referenced def is cloned **per node**,
  mirroring the local rule.
- **The nested import is TWO-PHASE** — every clone's id is registered before
  `remapNestedMacroRefs` retargets the references, because a nested def can itself
  nest another. `cloneMacroWithFreshIds` regenerates ids but does NOT rewrite a
  nested `macroDefId` (correct for the same-model case, where the nested def exists),
  which is exactly why the remap is needed here.
- A bundled def that is missing (hand-edited payload) leaves the instance pointing at
  its stale id and badging — never a crash.

### Dangling model-element references are EXPECTED
A pasted node may name an attribute / neighborhood / mapping / indicator / variable id
the target model lacks. That is the **macro-import experience**: `detectMissingConfig`
badges it (verified: a Game-of-Life `getCellAttribute` pasted into Wireworld shows the
amber `!` with *"Select an attribute"* and the dropdown offers Wireworld's attributes).
**No name-based auto-mapping** — deliberately out of scope; a possible follow-up.

**A DANGLING REFERENCE COMPILES TO AN ERROR — IT MUST NEVER THROW.** The user-reported
crash (paste Kelp War's whole generation step into a fresh model → switch to the Simulator
→ **white screen**) had two independent layers, both fixed:
- **[danglingRefs.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/danglingRefs.ts) — the JS compilers now
  report by name.** The WASM and WebGPU compilers already returned `"getCellAttribute:
  unknown attr …"`; the JS reference compiler silently emitted `_undef` / `nSz_<missing>`
  and only blew up at RUN time inside the worker (`nSz_… is not defined`, with **no banner
  at all on the JS engine**). `detectDanglingRefs(nodes, model)` runs in BOTH `compileGraph`
  and `compileAgentGraph`, right after `expandMacros` (so it sees the FLAT graph the
  compiler actually emits — an uninstantiated `macroDef` can never fail a compile) and
  BEFORE the lowering chain (which rewrites ids). **Only a NON-EMPTY id that resolves to
  nothing is reported** — an unset id (`''`/absent) is the "still building" state and keeps
  compiling exactly as before, which is what makes this byte-identical for all 29 shipped
  models. Membership is a UNION over every id space a key may legally name (cell ∪ model ∪
  agent ∪ bond attributes for `attributeId`; cell ∪ agent mappings + the
  `CURRENT_VIEWER_SENTINEL` for `mappingId`; …) — deciding WHICH space a node type may use
  is `nodeValidation`'s job, so the union keeps the compile gate conservative.
- **`srcCanvasTransferredRef` — the actual crash** ([SimulatorView.tsx](src/simulator/SimulatorView.tsx)).
  `draw()`'s CPU `putImageData` branch reused `srcCanvasRef.current` whenever its dimensions
  matched, and called `getContext('2d')` on it. Under WebGPU **direct render** that canvas has
  had its control TRANSFERRED to the worker, so `getContext` throws `InvalidStateError` — and
  since `draw()` is invoked from a `useLayoutEffect`, the throw unmounted React (white screen).
  **`directRenderActiveRef` is NOT a safe proxy for "was it transferred"**: it goes false while
  `srcCanvasRef` still holds the transferred canvas whenever the worker reports
  `useWebGPUStatus { ready: false }` — which is exactly what a failed recompile does, and a
  pasted graph with dangling references fails the shader compile. The dedicated flag is set
  where the transferred canvas is committed, cleared at every point a fresh canvas is
  installed, and consulted by draw()'s recreate condition; the `ready:false` and
  transfer-failure branches now also RELEASE the transferred canvas. **Any future path that
  turns direct render off must release it too.**
- **Defence in depth**: `safeCompileGraph` (module-scope, next to `withPipelineModel`) wraps
  the JS reference compile at both call sites, and `compileAgentModel` wraps
  `compileAgentGraph` — the WASM/WebGPU compiles were already try/caught at every call site,
  so these were the only compiles whose exceptions could reach React. An unexpected throw now
  becomes the red banner (`Compile failed: …`), never a white screen.

Verified end-to-end through the real UI (Kelp War → copy → File→New → paste → Simulator):
20 amber badges in the Modeler, a named red compile-error banner in the Simulator, **zero
uncaught errors**, the app stays fully usable (tab round-trips, manual Step, loading another
model clears the banner and runs), and re-pointing one node's attribute dropdown drops the
badge count 20 → 19. The agents-graph twin (Boids' agent graph pasted into a Flocking
archetype that lacks its agent variables) degrades the same way, with an `[agents] …` banner.

### Same-tab behaviour is preserved exactly
The singleton-root strip (`step`/`initEvent`/`behaviourStep`/…) still MUTATES the
in-memory clipboard when the paste consumed it (`setMemoryClipboardNodes`); a payload
read from storage belongs to another tab and is left alone. Everything downstream —
the id remap, the group `style`/`zIndex` rebuild, the edge rewrite — is the original
code operating on a payload variable instead of the module global.

### Verified (two real tabs, real UI)
Tab A = Game of Life, tab B = Extended Wireworld, both on the Cells graph: 4 wired
nodes cross-paste with fresh ids and all 3 edges intact; a **macro** pastes with its
def imported (entering it in B shows the 7 internal nodes and the Palette's *Project
Macros* lists it); a **nested** macro round-trips (`Root › Outer Nest › Decide Life
State`) with the inner reference retargeted at a fresh id; a mixed selection (group +
children + comment + reroute + macro) round-trips with sizes/labels/text preserved and
the `step` singleton correctly DROPPED; the **freshness rule** holds (tab B pastes tab
A's newer copy over its own older in-memory one); cross-kind shows the disabled item
and Ctrl+V is a no-op; a fresh third tab that never copied shows an ENABLED Paste and
pastes; four malformed payloads are ignored with no throw; the 2.6 MB guard removes
the key, warns once, and still pastes in-tab. Zero console errors in all three tabs.

## Composite Value Types — Vector & Color + Get Self Handle

Two new **bundled value port types** (the Unreal/Blender Make-Break pattern) so a graph passes a whole vector or colour on ONE wire instead of per-component scalars, plus a small agent node exposing the self id.

### Data types ([types.ts](src/modeler/vpl/types.ts) `PortDataType`)
- **`vector`** — a 2D/3D vector value (the Z component exists only in a 3D model; the Z port is hidden via `hiddenPorts` keyed on `is3dModelLike`).
- **`color`** — RGBA (0–255 channels, A defaults 255).
- Both are **EDITOR SUGAR**, not a runtime value type — they're LOWERED to scalar nodes before any per-target compile (see "All-target lowering" below). So the compilers carry **zero** vector/colour-specific emit; vectors run NATIVELY on JS / WASM / WebGPU via the verified scalar emitters (NOT a JS-only clamp — this is the ALL-TARGET DELIVERY rule).

### Nodes (6)
- **Get Self Handle** ([GetSelfHandleNode.ts](src/modeler/vpl/nodes/GetSelfHandleNode.ts), `getSelfHandle`, agent/`bondGraph`): outputs the current agent's own id (`const _v<id> = idx`). Feed it to the by-id nodes (Get/Set Agent Attribute, Get Agent Position/Offset, Form/Break Bond). Emitted on **all three** agent targets (JS / WASM `localGet(idxLocal)` / WebGPU `f32(idx)`) + in `AGENT_WASM_SUPPORTED_TYPES` + `AGENT_WEBGPU_SUPPORTED_TYPES`. (This one is a real node, not lowered.) **In `NEVER_INVARIANT`** ([loopInvariant.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/loopInvariant.ts)) — it has NO value inputs and emits the bare loop variable `idx`, so without it loop-invariance treats it as vacuously invariant and hoists it ABOVE the per-agent `for (let idx…)` decode (JS `idx is not defined`; WASM silently reads `idxLocal`=0 → always handle 0). Surfaces the moment Get Self Handle feeds a by-id node (e.g. Get Agent Position's `Reference` / Form Bond).
- **Make Vector** / **Break Vector** / **Vector Op** (Add/Subtract/Scale/Dot/Cross/Length/Normalize/Distance/Negate/Lerp/**Rotate (2D)**/**Rotate Around Axis (3D)**) — Vector Op + Break Vector are multi-output (in `MULTI_OUTPUT_TYPES` for the editor; the compiler never sees them). Vector Op's `hiddenPorts` shows ports per op (B for binary ops, Scalar for scale, T for lerp, `Axis` for rotateAxis, `Angle°` for both rotations, `value` for Dot/Length/Distance else `result`). **The two rotations take DEGREES** (`Angle°`, inline widget) — matching every other user-facing angle surface (the FOV nodes' Half-angle°, sprite compass degrees), while the Expression node's raw `sin`/`cos` stay radians; the lowering multiplies by π/180 (`DEG_TO_RAD`, exported from [VectorOpNode.ts](src/modeler/vpl/nodes/VectorOpNode.ts)) and then uses the already-lockstepped `sin`/`cos` arithmetic ops, so both rotations run on **all three targets, cell + agent, 2D + 3D, with zero per-target emit**. A positive angle rotates **from +X toward +Y = CLOCKWISE on screen** (rows/Y grow downward — the same convention Sense Hemifield's `cross = hx·dy − hy·dx ≥ 0 ⇒ Left` uses). **Rotate** spins the XY plane about Z and passes Z through unchanged (available in 2D AND 3D — in 3D it IS a rotation about the Z axis). **Rotate Around Axis** is Rodrigues (`v·cosθ + (k̂×v)·sinθ + k̂(k̂·v)(1−cosθ)`) with the axis normalised through the SAME guarded divide `normalize` lowers to, so a **zero axis ⇒ k̂ = (0,0,0) (÷0→0) ⇒ v·cosθ** — documented, well-defined on every target; it is offered ONLY in a 3D model (the CaNode dropdown filters it on `is3dModelLike`, and a stale `rotateAxis` config stays selectable + carries a `nodeValidation` badge). cos / sin / (1−cos) / the normalised axis / the axis dot are each ONE synthesized node reused per component (structural sharing — accessor-CSE is off in async agent mode). Verified by [scripts/test-vector-rotate.mjs](scripts/test-vector-rotate.mjs) — hand-computed VALUES on JS + a real instantiated WASM module in Node, bit-identical, plus **geometric invariants asserted on the compiled output** (length preserved, axial component preserved, signed turn == the requested angle) so it isn't a mirror of the lowering; negative-controlled against a sign flip and a 1−cos mutation. A permanent `[synthetic] Vector Op rotate2d + rotateAxis` entry in [scripts/parity-agent-wasm.mjs](scripts/parity-agent-wasm.mjs) guards the agent-graph JS↔WASM parity.
- **Make Color** / **Break Color** (`makeColor`/`breakColor`) over `[r, g, b, a]`.

### All-target lowering ([expandComposites.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/expandComposites.ts)) — the key design
A shared pre-compile graph transform rewrites every composite node into plain **`arithmeticOperator` + `getConstant`** scalar nodes BEFORE any target compiles — exactly the pattern of `expandMacros` / `collapseReroutes` / `injectLinkedOutputMappings`. Because the output is ordinary scalar nodes whose JS/WASM/WebGPU emit is already verified by every math-heavy model (Gray-Scott, MNCA, chemistry), vectors run natively on all targets with NO per-target vector code. The SAME deterministic transform runs in ALL 5 compiler front-ends, so the lowered graph is identical across targets and parity is inherited from the scalar primitives.
- **Lowering, by node:** Make Vector/Color → its output's component sources ARE its scalar inputs (pass-through). Break Vector/Color → each scalar output resolves to one component of the input composite. Vector Op → a small tree of `arithmeticOperator` nodes per component (add/sub/scale/cross/normalize/negate/lerp) or one scalar result (dot/length/distance). `lengthOf` = √(Σ component²); normalize divides each by the shared length (the `/` op's ÷0-guard makes a zero vector normalize to zero).
- **Recursive component resolution** (`vecComponentsOf` / `scalarSourceOf` / `resolveScalarInput` / `resolveVecInput`, memoised + cycle-guarded): a vector value bottoms out at a real scalar source or a literal, through any nesting (Vector Op → Vector Op), Break→Make round-trips, and shared values (one Vector Op result → many consumers synthesises once). Literals connect as an inline `_port_*` when the target port has an inline widget, else a synthetic `getConstant`.
- **Wired into all 5 front-ends** after `collapseReroutes`: JS `compileGraph` + `compileAgentGraph`, `compileGraphWasm`, `compileGraphWebGPU`, and BOTH `flattenAgentGraph`s (WASM + WebGPU) — the agent flatten is shared by the gate + the emitter, so a vector agent graph LOWERS to arithmeticOperator/getConstant (which ARE in the agent allowlists) and the gate now ACCEPTS it (runs on WASM/WebGPU, no JS clamp). Hot-path no-op when the graph has no composite nodes (every non-vector model + the 8 agent samples are byte-identical).

### Port wiring + UX
- `isValidConnection` ([GraphEditor.tsx](src/modeler/vpl/GraphEditor.tsx)): a composite port connects ONLY to the SAME composite type — never to a scalar or `any` port (so the lowering always has a well-defined producer). `portsCompatible` handles the suggestion layer (`a === b`).
- Distinct pin colours: vector = teal (`.handleVector`), color = pink (`.handleColor`) in [CaNode.module.css](src/modeler/vpl/CaNode.module.css) + `portHandleClass`. Vector Op op-dropdown UI in CaNode.
- **Apply Force "Vector input" mode** (`config.vectorInput`, default off): an additive `force` vector port that, when on, replaces the X/Y/Z component ports (`hiddenPorts`). `expandComposites` lowers it to the existing fx/fy/fz scalar ports (sets `vectorInput` false + wires the resolved components), so vector mode runs on **all** agent targets — `applyForce.compile` + the WASM/WebGPU emitters are component-only (no per-target vector path).
- Catalogue: **113 selectable** node types (116 − 3 hidden macro), **40 agent** nodes. *(Later raised to **115 selectable** / **42 agent** by the Agent Output-Mapping Graphs + Sprites milestone — `agentOutputMapping` + `setAgentSprite`.)*

### Verified (cross-target, runtime — NOT JS-only)
All 10 Vector Ops compile clean on JS/WASM/WebGPU (grid) + correct JS values (add=4, dot=11, cross=0, length=2.236, normalize=0.447, distance=2.828, negate=−1, lerp=2, scale=2, subtract=−2); **WASM grid runtime** (length model → all cells 5) + **WebGPU grid runtime** (add+break → all cells 4) via the real worker; wired Make Vector input → 5, Break→Make round-trip → 13; the **agent gate now returns `true`** for a reachable vector graph on BOTH WASM + WebGPU (was JS-clamped), Apply Force vector mode emits the lowered `_agentForceX[idx] += _v__vec0`; colour Make/Break works; Game of Life byte-identical on all 3 targets (lowering is a no-op for non-vector graphs); all 8 agent samples (+ synthetic 3D-field) still JS↔WASM bit-parity; tsc + build clean.

### Stored `vector` attribute + variable type (branch `absorb_old_automatosgt`) — the STORAGE composite
The Make/Break-Vector nodes above pass a vector on a WIRE; this adds a vector as a **stored** cell-attribute / agent-attribute / Local-Variable type, so a model can persist a per-cell / per-agent direction (a flow field, a facing/orientation, an accumulated force) as ONE named thing instead of hand-maintaining `fooX`/`fooY`[/`fooZ`] scalars. The canonical motivation was **agent orientation as a vector** (not just a compass angle) and dropping the per-component force-accumulator boilerplate.
- **Schema ([types.ts](src/modeler/vpl/types.ts), additive):** `AttributeType += 'vector'` + `Attribute.vectorDims?: 2|3`; `VariableDataType += 'vector'` + `Variable.vectorDims?: 2|3`. Old files load unchanged (no migration). Offered for **cell + agent** attributes and **scalar** Local Variables — NOT model attributes (they take the color-split path) and NOT array variables. The 3D option (`Vector (3D)`) is offered only when `vectorDimsForModel(model) === 3`.
- **The design = LOWER TO SCALAR-FLOAT COMPONENTS (the storage analogue of `expandComposites`).** A `vector` attr/var is rewritten to `dims` scalar `float` components (`<id>_vx`/`_vy`[/`_vz`]) BEFORE any target compiles, so **every downstream layer (all 5 compilers, the worker SoA, save/load, indicators) sees ONLY scalar floats — zero new per-target emit, zero new value-runtime type.** The ONE compiler-facing transform is **`lowerVectorAttrs(nodes, edges, model)`** in [vectorAttr.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/vectorAttr.ts): it (a) rewrites every VALUE read that references a vector — the own `getCellAttribute`/`getVariable`, the **neighbour reads** `getNeighborAttributeByIndex`/`getNeighborAttributeByTag`, and the by-id agent read `getAgentAttribute` — into a **Make Vector** over per-component reads (with the shared value input — the NI `index` / the `agentId` — **fanned out** to every component reader, reusing the ONE source node), (b) rewrites every FLOW write — the own `setAttribute`/`setVariable`, the **neighbour writes** `setNeighborAttributeByIndex`/`setNeighborhoodAttribute`, and the by-id agent write `setAgentAttribute` — into a **Break Vector** + a **linear flow-splice** (`do → set_vx → set_vy [→ set_vz] → next`, shared value input fanned out), (c) does a **config-slot expansion** of `moveSelfToNeighbor` (each vector payload slot → its scalar-component slots, `payloadCount` grows, `_attr_${i}_default` re-baked), and (d) reassigns `model` to the component-expanded attrs/variables. It runs AFTER `expandMacros`/`collapseReroutes` (so it sees a flat graph) and BEFORE `expandComposites` (so the Make/Break it synthesizes get lowered to scalar arithmetic like any other vector wire). It BAKES `_resolvedTagIndex` on synthesized `getNeighborAttributeByTag` readers + `_attr_${i}_default` on the move clone, so WASM/WebGPU (which have no JS pre-pass and never see the JS-mutated config for these freshly-created nodes) read the right tag/default. **Hot-path no-op** when the model has no vector attrs/vars (returns the same arrays — every existing model byte-identical). The set of lowered node types is exported as **`VECTOR_LOWERED`** (consumed by the validation guard).
- **The unified TYPE-DRIVEN ports (no dedicated Get/Set Vector nodes).** Every node whose `value` port carries a stored attr/var — the own `getCellAttribute`/`setAttribute`, the neighbour reads `getNeighborAttributeByIndex`/`getNeighborAttributeByTag`, the by-id agent read/write `getAgentAttribute`/`setAgentAttribute`, the neighbour writes `setNeighborAttributeByIndex`/`setNeighborhoodAttribute`, and `getVariable`/`setVariable` — becomes vector-aware: when the picked attribute/variable is a vector, that `value` port's `dataType` flips to `vector` (and Set drops its inline number widget). The shared resolver **`vectorPortDims(nodeType, config, model): 2|3|null`** ([vectorAttr.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/vectorAttr.ts) — keyed off `VECTOR_ATTR_PORT_NODES`; returns null for every other node type, so effectivePorts/CaNode call it GENERICALLY) is consulted by BOTH [effectivePorts.ts](src/modeler/vpl/effectivePorts.ts) (the port-shape source the drag/drop + drop-menu read) AND `isValidConnection` ([GraphEditor.tsx](src/modeler/vpl/GraphEditor.tsx), which resolves src/tgt vector-ness from each node's live config + enforces the composite `vector`↔`vector` exact-match). So dragging a vector attr/var onto the canvas gives the ordinary Get/Set node with a vector port, and it connects only to Make/Break/VectorOp/another vector attr. (The earlier dedicated `getVectorAttribute`/`setVectorAttribute`/`getVectorVariable`/`setVectorVariable` nodes were REMOVED from the registry + deleted.)
- **The ABI-mirror discipline (the silent-corruption class).** Every memory-LAYOUT + worker-message site that iterates attributes must see the SAME component expansion the compiler used, or its offsets desync (the `+64-cell` corruption). `expandVectorAttributes(attrs)` / `expandVectorVariables(vars)` (deterministic) is called at: [wasm/layout.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/wasm/layout.ts) `computeLayoutFromModel`, [webgpu/layout.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/webgpu/layout.ts) `computeWebGPULayout`, both agent layouts (`compileAgentGraphWasmForModel` / `compileAgentGraphWebGPUForModel` via `expandVectorAttributes(agentAttrsOf(model))`), and [SimulatorView.tsx](src/simulator/SimulatorView.tsx)'s worker `init` + `updateIndicators` messages (`attributes`/`agentAttributes` expanded before `toAttrDefMsg`). Variables ride the compiled step fn (`lowerVectorAttrs` reassigns `model.variables`/`agentVariables` before `buildVariableJS`), so no worker message carries them.
- **Facing/orientation via composition (no dedicated `facing` config):** an agent's heading is just a vector agent-attribute wired through Get Self Attribute → Break Vector → the `Get Agents In View` / `Sense Hemifield` **wired heading** input. So the FOV Sensing nodes get a real facing source with zero new machinery.
- **Save/load:** the `.gcaproj` stores the raw `vector` attr (schema round-trips); the worker + any embedded `.gcastate` only ever see the expanded float components (`ATTR_TYPE_MAP` never receives a `vector` — `serializeSimState` iterates the WORKER state, whose buffers are already component-keyed, so they serialize as `float64`). `attrsStructurallyEqual` ([SimulatorView.tsx](src/simulator/SimulatorView.tsx)) compares `vectorDims` (defense-in-depth: a 2D↔3D dims change re-lays-out the SoA → full worker reinit, even if `defaultValue` somehow didn't change alongside).
- **Simulator peripherals (all vector-aware):** the cell inspector ([InspectCellPopover.tsx](src/simulator/InspectCellPopover.tsx)) + the agent-state inspect popover recombine a vector's components into a `(x, y[, z])` readout (`decodeVectorFromValues`); the Manual Brush / seed-config / agent-Edit panels ([ManualBrushPanel.tsx](src/simulator/ManualBrushPanel.tsx)) render a labelled X/Y[/Z] widget, and every brush set-builder in SimulatorView splits a vector into per-component `{attrId, value}` sets via **`encodeAttrSets`** (the vector id itself never exists in the worker; its paint guard would silently skip it). The CaNode value-port handle renders teal (`portHandleClass` `vector`) via a `vectorPortDims` retype mirroring effectivePorts; a vector `setVariable` drops its inline number widget.
- **Coverage (v2) — SINGLE-vector reads/writes lowered; array-of-vectors + comparison still badged.** `lowerVectorAttrs` lowers everything in `VECTOR_LOWERED`: the OWN-cell/OWN-agent/OWN-variable Get/Set, the **neighbour reads** (`getNeighborAttributeByIndex`/`getNeighborAttributeByTag`), the **by-id agent read/write** (`getAgentAttribute`/`setAgentAttribute`), the **neighbour writes** (`setNeighborAttributeByIndex`/`setNeighborhoodAttribute`), and **`moveSelfToNeighbor`** — so a cell/agent can read a neighbour's / another agent's vector, write one, and transfer one, all correctly. **Verified end-to-end on JS + WASM + WebGPU through the REAL worker** (a neighbour `getNeighborAttributeByIndex(flow).x` read returns the actual east-neighbour value, torus-wrapped, 0 mismatches on all three targets; the own vector Set seeds `flow` via `initEvent → Make Vector → setAttribute`). Still NOT lowered (no vector representation — a vector array/comparison isn't a value shape the compilers have): **array-of-vectors reads** (`getNeighborsAttribute`/`getNeighborsAttrByIndexes`/`getAgentsAttribute`), `filterNeighbors` (scalar comparison), `updateAttribute` (inc/dec/max/min undefined on a vector), and the **field-bridge** nodes. Those emit `r_<id>[…]`/`w_<id>[…]` against the component-expanded buffer that has no `<id>` array (crashes at run time), so `detectMissingConfig` ([nodeValidation.ts](src/modeler/vpl/nodes/nodeValidation.ts)) badges any node NOT in `VECTOR_LOWERED` that references a vector attr via `config.attributeId`. Workaround: read the vector via Get (Self) Attribute / Get Neighbor Attr / Get Agent Attribute + Break Vector (or Get + Vector Op + Set for `updateAttribute`).
- **Adversarial-review hardening (all confirmed + fixed):** (1) the guard above was extended to `moveSelfToNeighbor`'s `attr_${i}` slots (it only checked `attributeId`). (2) A vector is a **scalar-only** type: the Local-Variables **Kind** dropdown resets a vector variable's type to Decimal when switched to Array (an `{kind:'array', dataType:'vector'}` would expand away yet still list in Set Array Element → `_var_<id> is not defined`); `expandVectorVariables` / `vectorPortDims` / `lowerVectorAttrs` also skip an array-kind vector (`isScalarVectorVar`) as defense-in-depth for hand-edited files. (3) The **Sub-attribute** editor is hidden for a vector cell attr (the components don't carry `parentAttributeId`/`parentValues`/`undefinedValue`, so it was a silent no-op). (4) The Type dropdown keeps showing **Vector (3D)** when the attr/var is *already* `vectorDims===3` (a 3D→2D model switch otherwise misreported it as "Binary").
