Verified in-app: renderer draws the outline (0→522 amber px→0); the geometry builder's axis mapping / radius / sphere / rect / anchor are exact; a real agent-brush drag sets a 216-vert sphere outline (bounded).

#### Agent brush: Push / Pull replace Bond (branch `updates`)
The `bond` brush mode (drag a disc, auto-glue every pair inside it already within `formDistance × contact`) was **REMOVED** — it only ever did anything on a bonded model, needed the agents to already touch, and Glue covers the deliberate case. In its place two modes that work on **every** agent model and give a *physical* way to interact with a running population: **Push** / **Pull**. Plan + illustrated mockup: [docs/PLAN_AGENT_PUSH_PULL_BRUSH.md](docs/PLAN_AGENT_PUSH_PULL_BRUSH.md)/`.html`.
- **The law.** For each live agent within `radius` of the brush centre, `d` = torus-shortest distance: `falloff = 1 − d/radius` (1 at the centre, 0 at the rim) · `step = intensity · dt · falloff`; push `x += step·outward`, pull `x −= min(step, d)·outward` (the `min` is what stops an overshoot past the centre), then wrap (torus) / clamp (bounded). **Contrast Move**: Move translates a whole SHAPE footprint rigidly by the drag delta; Push/Pull act over a RADIAL disc with a magnitude that depends on closeness, and keep acting while the button is held even if the cursor never moves.
- **`Intensity` is WORLD UNITS PER SECOND at the centre** and the SENDER pre-multiplies by the frame `dt` (clamped to 100 ms) — without that a 144 Hz display would push 2.4× faster than a 60 Hz one for the same setting. Persisted as `agentNudgeIntensity` in `genesisca_sim_settings` (default 10).
- **POSITION ONLY — no velocity kick (deliberate).** A kick would feel more like a force but it ACCUMULATES: at momentum 0.9 a sustained hold converges to ~10× the per-frame step, and at momentum 1.0 (Particle Life) boundedness depends entirely on the model's own graph-side friction. A displacement is well defined for every Motion mode (`static`/`velocity`/`force`), every momentum value and every compile target — the same contract Move already has. The write is `x` AND `xNext` (the `moveAgents` discipline; writing only `x` lets the next position commit snap the agent back).
- **ONE worker message, ONE handler, every target**: **`nudgeAgents { x, y, z?, radius, strength, torus, activeViewer }`** (`strength` SIGNED — `+` outward = push, `−` inward = pull — and already dt-scaled). It mutates the CPU agent store exactly like `moveAgents`, so **JS / WASM / WebGPU all work by construction**, and it joins **`AGENT_GPU_DEFER_TYPES`** (deferred during an in-flight GPU readback + sets `agentGpuUploadPending`, so a resident batch re-uploads the nudged positions). **2D and 3D share the handler** — `z` is read only when `worldDepth > 1`, and the 3D brush passes the plane-picked cell (the agent world IS the grid frame 1:1). An agent EXACTLY at the centre has no outward direction: push gives it a DETERMINISTIC golden-angle direction from its id (a 2D angle / a Fibonacci-sphere direction in 3D) so a pile on the cursor still explodes outward reproducibly; pull leaves it (`min(step, d) = 0`).
- **A LOOP, not a per-pointermove post** (`startNudgeLoop`/`stopNudgeLoop`/`nudgeTickRef`, shared by the 2D and 3D handlers): the press starts an rAF loop that posts at most ONE message per frame from the last cursor centre; a drag only re-aims `nudgeCenterRef`. So holding still keeps pushing and a 1 kHz pointer stream cannot flood the worker. Released on pointer-up (2D `handleMouseUp`, 3D `onUp` via `active === 'agentNudge'`).
- **They ignore the brush SHAPE** — a radial force needs a centre and a radius, so `NUDGE_BRUSH_MODES` always act over a plain disc (2D) / ball (3D) of `agentBrushRadius`; the panel shows **Radius + Intensity** instead of the shape row. **Because the shape is fixed, Ctrl+LMB-drag becomes TWO-AXIS in these modes: horizontal → Radius, vertical → Intensity (UP = stronger).** `agentsInRadiusAt` / `agentsInRadius3dAt` (originally Bond's scan collectors) SURVIVE as the effect-region collectors for the highlight.
  - **Both resize state machines take a dedicated FIRST branch** (`isResizingBrush.startIntensity` in the 2D `handleMouseMove`, `resizeStart.intensity` in the 3D gl-canvas `onMove`) that runs *before* the per-shape chain, so the selected shape is irrelevant — a ring-shaped brush in Push drags radius+intensity and leaves the ring width alone. That branch REPLACED the old `'circle'` substitution, so every other mode's per-shape math is byte-unchanged. Radius keeps the shared `round(dx / 5)` feel; intensity goes through `nudgeIntensityFromDrag` (below), with the sign convention every other secondary axis uses (up = more).
  - **THE VERTICAL AXIS IS MAGNITUDE-PROPORTIONAL, NOT LINEAR** (`nudgeIntensityFromDrag`, 2026-08-07 — the user reported *"why clamp to 200? I have been using it to 1000 even"*). The ceiling is **`NUDGE_INTENSITY_DRAG_MAX` = 10000**, i.e. four decades, and the shipped `start − round(dy / 5)` would have needed **50 000 px** to cross it while making the low end hypersensitive. The drag now moves in **`u = ln(1 + v / NUDGE_INTENSITY_FLOOR)`** space (`log1p`/`expm1`, floor **1**), stepping `u` by `−dy / NUDGE_INTENSITY_EFOLD_PX` (**150 px per e-fold**) and clamping `u ≥ 0`:
    - `v ≫ floor` ⇒ `du = dv / v`, so a fixed pixel travel is a fixed **RELATIVE** change — **measured ×2.74 at 100 and ×2.72 at 1000 for the same 150 px**, i.e. genuinely the same feel at every magnitude (10 px ≈ ±7% anywhere: 10→11, 1000→1069).
    - `v ≪ floor` ⇒ `du ≈ dv / floor`, a fixed **ABSOLUTE** step. **That linear floor is the whole reason for the `+1`**: a pure `v · exp(−dy/K)` can neither REACH 0 (it approaches asymptotically) nor ESCAPE it (`0 × e = 0`). Measured: 400 px down from 10 lands exactly on **0**, and 50 px up from 0 gives **0.4**. Full 0→10000 travel is **1382 px**; 10→10000 is 1022 px — one long gesture, and gestures COMPOSE because the law is relative (verified round-trip: 10 → 80 → 10 exactly).
    - Rounding is **one decimal below 10, whole units above** (`NumberField` here has no `integer` prop, so decimals commit), which keeps 1–20 finely adjustable without showing `1069.3` at the top.
  - **ONE ceiling, shared by the field and the drag** — `NUDGE_INTENSITY_DRAG_MAX`(10000) is the panel `NumberField`'s `max`, the drag clamp (via the shared `clampNudgeIntensity`), AND the clamp on the persisted value at load. Without the load clamp a legacy `agentNudgeIntensity` above the cap would be SNAPPED DOWN by the first pixel of a retune drag; without the field `max` a typed value could sit outside the range the drag can express. **Ctrl+LMB opens a resize, never a nudge**, so a drag retunes the NEXT hold rather than one already in flight.
- **Visuals**: the cursor is the effect ring — **SOLID for Push, DASHED for Pull** — plus 8 radial ticks with a chevron at the leading end (outward / inward), on the negative-silhouette layer; every agent inside the disc is ringed (**amber** push / **teal** pull) through the same area-highlight path Remove/Move/Edit use. 3D draws the volumetric ball outline + the same per-agent rings.
  - **THE ARROWS CARRY THE STRENGTH** (same round): with a 4-decade range the number alone is unreadable at a glance, so the arrows are centred on `NUDGE_ARROW_MID`(0.56 R) and grow OUTWARD FROM IT — half-length `nudgeArrowHalf` interpolates 0.10 R → 0.34 R over **`nudgeStrengthCue` = log10(v) / log10(10000)**, so **each decade is a quarter of the range** and 10 / 100 / 1000 / 10000 are visibly distinct (measured spans 0.40–0.72 R, 0.34–0.78, 0.28–0.84, 0.22–0.90 — a 3.4× length ratio end to end). Growing from the MIDDLE is what makes **both** chevrons move in both modes. The chevron head (`0.09 + 0.09·cue` of R, capped 9 px) and the shaft width (`1.5 + cue`) grow with it; the RING keeps `lineWidth 1.5` so it always reads as the radius alone.
  - **The cue is LIVE AT ALL TIMES, not only mid-drag** — `drawCursorLayer` reads `agentNudgeIntensityRef.current`, and both resize branches assign that **ref BEFORE `setAgentNudgeIntensity`** (the documented ref-leads-state discipline): the same handler calls `draw()`/rebuilds the 3D outline before React re-renders, so without the lead the arrow would lag one mousemove. A value typed into the PANEL has no pointer event behind it, so a small effect (`[agentNudgeIntensity, agentBrushRadius]`) schedules a **cursor-layer-only** redraw — otherwise a parked cursor kept showing the previous footprint.
  - **3D gets the same cue cheaply**: `buildBrushOutline3dSegs` gained an optional **`innerRing`** (a plane-only circle, no great circles — one 36-segment arc), and the nudge branch passes `rad · (MID − half)` so it SHRINKS as the intensity grows, mirroring the 2D arrows reaching further in. Every other shape passes `undefined` ⇒ the outline is byte-identical.
- **`push`/`pull` are in `AGENT_BRUSH_MODES_NEEDING_STATE` for their HIGHLIGHT ONLY** — the EFFECT is entirely worker-side (a centre + a radius, never an id list), but the ring reads the CPU snapshot. The 3 s idle backstop caps that cost. **`add` must stay OUT of that set** (it is the default mode and reads nothing) — pinned by `verify-agent-render.mjs`'s hover-pin block, whose set literal must be updated deliberately when a mode is added.
- **Removed with the mode**: `scanBondPairsAt`, `scanBondPairs3d`, `flushBondBatch`, `pendingBondPairs`, the `'agentBond'` drag state, the bond scan-ring cursor and the Bond radius field — plus the **`formBondBatch`** worker message entirely (its `case`, its interface, its `WorkerMsg` union member and its defer-set entry), since nothing else posted it. Glue/Cut still post single `formBond`/`breakBond` and keep their `resolveMaxBonds === 0` gating (`BOND_BRUSH_MODES` is now `{glue, cut}`); Push/Pull are **ungated**.
- **Verified in the real UI** (paused, so the brush is the only mover): the push law is exact to **8e-14** (60 agents inside r=40 all displaced by exactly `2·(1 − d/40)` outward, direction preserved, **0** agents outside the radius moved); pull likewise, with **9 of 60 clamped and 0 overshoots**; a real hold-and-release on the canvas posts **one nudge per frame while held and exactly 0 after release**; a paused pull moved **93/93 agents inward, 0 outward, 0 outside**, collapsing r≤5 from 8 → 88 agents with the total inside the radius unchanged; a sustained push evacuates the interior and packs everything at **exactly d = radius** (where the falloff is zero). Per target: **WebGPU** (Particle Life 2D + 3D — the 3D ball moved 270/270 outward with **269** also moving in z, the one exception being the agent exactly on the z-plane), **WASM** (Growing Graphs, bonded: all 10 seeds pushed 39.8 → 392.9 of a 400 radius), **JS** (a Boids probe with `agentTarget:'js'`: 50/50 outward, r≤10 6 → 0). On the bonded model the mode row reads **add remove move edit push pull glue cut** with no `bond`, and the Alt+wheel cycle walks exactly those eight. **0 fresh console errors** on a clean load exercising both modes.

### Verified
Force determinism (2 overlapping agents relax to the exact contact distance; a blob to a stable packing, 0 NaN); ~7000 steps/sec for 350 agents (the spatial hash); tension-axis division geometrically exact ((1,0)/(0,1) for horizontal/vertical stretch) with partner bonds partitioned; the headline "Morphogenesis — Growing Tissue" sample (12→1500 cells, ~5 bonds/agent, packed bonded sheet); the closed feedback (secrete→decay→sample round-trip). The three breadth samples: **Boids** self-organizes from disorder (velocity polarization 0.008 → 0.99 — a coherent flock); **Differential Tissue** grows 5→257 across 7 maturity stages with a STABLE stem pool (5) + self-limiting growth (specialization, not a blob); **Chemotaxis** (WASM field + JS agents, 0 errors) builds the field (max ~30) + aggregates agents from spread (178 bins) into clustered streams (99 bins, 2× density). **Scale**: the spatial hash keeps the JS engine O(N) — **2000 boids** (the heaviest per-agent work: neighbour query + 7 accumulators + force) run at **174 steps/sec** (5.7 ms/step), interactive; so the agent loop is NOT a JS bottleneck for realistic counts (Phase F's WASM port raises the ceiling past ~10k, it doesn't fix a bottleneck). Lattice path byte-identical on every PR (Game of Life / Life3D, all 3 targets) — the agent tier is additive + gated on `topologyMode.agents`.

### Phase F — PR6b-1: the WASM agent-loop ARCHITECTURE SKELETON (branch `agents_floating_cells`)
The FIRST internal split of capstone PR6b — proves the WASM agent loop ARCHITECTURE (memory sharing + the per-agent loop + dispatch + a few emitters) on a deterministic model BEFORE the large emitter port (PR6b-2 neighbour access → Boids; PR6b-3 field + division → Tissue).
- **A SEPARATE, minimal agent-WASM compiler** [src/modeler/vpl/compiler/agentWasm/compile.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/agentWasm/compile.ts) — `compileAgentGraphWasm(nodes, edges, model, agentLayout)` → `{ bytes, pages, supportedTypes }`. It REUSES the pure lattice ENCODER (`../wasm/encoder.ts`) but emits its OWN self-contained module — NO coupling to the lattice `WasmCompileCtx`/layout. The lattice WASM compiler (`wasm/compile.ts`/`wasm/layout.ts`) is **byte-unmodified** (proven: `compileAll` lattice bytes string-equal before/after on GoL/Life3D/snake/Gray-Scott/Boids/Tissue/Chemotaxis). Front-end = the SAME `expandMacros → collapseReroutes → canonicalizeAccessorEdges` the JS agent compiler runs.
- **The module**: `import "env" "mem"` = the wasmBacked AgentStore memory (PR6a — reads/writes hit the SAME bytes the JS engine reads at the `computeAgentMemoryLayout` baked offsets); `import "env" "pow"/…/"tanh"` = the 7 host math funcs (same funcIdx convention as the lattice, POW=0..TANH=6, NUM_IMPORTED_FUNCS=7); **`export "behaviour"(highWater: i32)`** → the per-agent loop `for (idx=0; idx<highWater; idx++) { if (alive[idx]==0) continue; const colorIdx=idx*4; <value DAG + linear flow chain> }`. **AW-HASH minimal**: the supported set needs no neighbour query, so `behaviour` takes ONLY `highWater` (no hash-array copy yet — `getNearbyAgents` is excluded by the gate; PR6b-2 adds it).
- **The minimal emitter set** (reads/writes the AGENT offsets, NOT the lattice offsets): `behaviourStep` (myX/myY[/myZ]/myRadius/myArea/myAge value-outs via `f64.load` at the x/y/z/radius/age offsets + idx*8; myZ gated on `is3dModel`), `getSelfPosition` (X/Y[/Z]), `getRadius`, `applyForce` (read-modify-write `+=` into forceX/forceY[/forceZ]), `setTargetRadius` (`f64.store` into targetRadius); PLUS the layout-agnostic value/flow utility on the f64 stack/locals: `getConstant` (number/bool), `arithmeticOperator` (Math, incl. the host transcendentals + the `/`÷0→0 guard), `statement` (Compare, numerical), `logicOperator` (AND/OR/XOR/NOT), `conditional` (if/else), `sequence` (transparent). Single canonical supported set `AGENT_WASM_SUPPORTED_TYPES`.
- **The gate** `isAgentGraphWasmSupported(model)` — TRUE iff Agents enabled AND EVERY (flattened) agent-graph node is in the supported set (+ Compare numerical-only, Get Constant number/bool-only). The central, honest predicate `agentTargetOf(cfg, wasmSupported)` consults: `agentTarget==='wasm'` resolves to `'wasm'` ONLY when supported, else clamps to `'js'` (the clamp stays the safe default). PR6b-2/3 widen `AGENT_WASM_SUPPORTED_TYPES` with no other change.
- **Dispatch** ([sim.worker.ts](src/simulator/engine/sim.worker.ts)): SimulatorView's `compileAgentModel` resolves the target + compiles the bytes (it has the model) and ships `agentTarget`/`agentWasmBytes` in the init + recompile messages (mirroring lattice `wasmStepBytes`). The worker, when `agentTarget==='wasm'`, backs the store on a `WebAssembly.Memory` (`createAgentStore({ wasmBacked:true })`, the SAME `computeAgentMemoryLayout` the compiler used), `instantiateAgentWasm`s the module against that memory, and in `runAgentStep` calls `agentBehaviourWasmFn(highWater)` INSTEAD of the JS `agentBehaviourFn` — **the force pass / structural phase below is UNCHANGED** (reads the same views). Any WASM failure → null the fn → JS fallback. `initAgents`/reset/recompile re-instantiate against the fresh memory (the orphan-WASM discipline: a fresh `WebAssembly.Memory` drops the old fn).
- **Sample**: [scripts/gen-agent-wasm-drift.mjs](scripts/gen-agent-wasm-drift.mjs) → `public/models/Agent WASM Drift Test.gcaproj` — 16 compact-seeded agents spring toward the world centre (`(centre − pos)·k → applyForce`), no RNG / neighbours / bonds, momentum 0, 2D. The deterministic JS↔WASM parity vehicle (`agentTarget:'wasm'`).
- **Verified**: tsc -b + `npm run build` clean; lattice WASM bytes + JS-agent behaviourCode byte/string-identical before/after (7 models); the gate correctly accepts the drift model + rejects Boids (PR6b-1 only); **JS↔WASM bit-parity** — END-TO-END through the real worker: JS-target vs WASM-target runs → bit-identical x/y across all 16 agents (0 mismatches, 0 NaN, 0 errors).

### Phase F — PR6b-2: the WASM agent loop runs Boids (widened emitter set; branch `agents_floating_cells`)
The SECOND internal split of capstone PR6b. Widens the SEPARATE [agentWasm/compile.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/agentWasm/compile.ts) so the **Boids — Flocking** sample runs on the WASM agent target with JS bit-parity. The lattice WASM compiler (`wasm/compile.ts`/`wasm/layout.ts`/`wasm/encoder.ts`) stays **byte-unmodified** (proven: `git diff` on `src/modeler/vpl/compiler/wasm` + `webgpu` is EMPTY; lattice GoL/Life3D compile clean on all 3 targets). The compiler now uses the byte-stable **`WasmEmitter`** abstraction (`../wasm/emitter.ts`, imported not modified) for clean local allocation + reuses the Expression AST emitter (`../expression/emitWasm.ts`).
- **Widened emitter set** (all read/write the AGENT offsets, mirroring the JS agent compiler 1:1): neighbour access — **`getNearbyAgents`** (fills a per-node scratch i32 id-array via the 3×3[×3] hash-bin stencil over the in-memory CSR hash + the all-pairs fallback, torus-wrapped exactly like the JS emit), **`forEachInArray`** (loops the scratch array, exposing element=agent-id + index as i32 locals), **`getAgentOffset`** (torus-shortest dX/dY[/dZ] + Distance via the world-bound fold), **`getVelocity`** (self when Agent unwired, else a neighbour Vx/Vy[/Vz]), **`getAgentPosition`** (X/Y[/Z]), **`getAgentRadius`**; **`getVariable`/`setVariable`** (SCALAR Local Variables = f64 function-locals, reset to initialValue at loop top — the boids cohesion/alignment/separation accumulators); **`expression`** (parsed AST → `emitWasm`); **`getRandom`** (float/integer/orientation/bool — NOT options mode); plus the PR6b-1 set (behaviourStep/getSelfPosition/getRadius/applyForce/setTargetRadius/getConstant/arithmeticOperator/statement/logicOperator/conditional/sequence).
- **AW-RNG** (B13 — the RNG-stream-divergence blocker): the shared xorshift32 `_rs` lives in an agent-memory cell (`layout.rngStateOffset`). The worker writes the global `rngState[0]` into the cell BEFORE the WASM `behaviour` call; the loop reads it once at function top (`_rs = u32[off] || 0x12345678`, mirroring JS exactly), advances per `getRandom` (same 13/17/5 constants on the in-register local), stores back at the end; the worker reads it back into `rngState[0]`. So a JS-target run and a WASM-target run advance the IDENTICAL stream. `getRandom` is emitted-once-per-agent (cached) → the RNG advances the same number of times as JS.
- **AW-HASH** (the keystone): the per-step spatial hash (`binStart`/`binAgents`) is **copied into reserved agent-memory views each step** (S10 — an O(nBins + liveCount) copy); the hash DIMENSIONS (valid flag + nBinsX/Y/Z + binSizeX/Y/Z + fieldW/H/D + torus flag) ride the **behaviour ARG list** (signature `(highWater, hashValid, nBinsX, nBinsY, nBinsZ : i32, binSizeX, binSizeY, binSizeZ, fieldW, fieldH, fieldD : f64, fieldTorus : i32)` — mirrored in `runAgentStep`, the ABI-mirror discipline). **Reserve bound + fallback**: `computeAgentMaxHashBins(W,H,D,range,defaultRadius,nbrQ)` (shared by compiler `agentMaxHashBinsForModel` + the worker `initAgents`) reserves `binStart` for the worst-case bin count (smallest bin edge, hard-capped 2²⁰); a per-step **fits-check** (`nBins+1 ≤ maxHashBins+1`) falls back to the JS behaviour fn for that step (warns once) — never silently wrong. `getNearbyAgents` writes its id-array to a per-node scratch slot (`AGENT_NEARBY_SCRATCH_SLOTS=4` reserved buffers of `maxAgents` i32; >4 nodes → gate rejects → JS). Both the RNG cell + hash + nearby-scratch are APPENDED to `computeAgentMemoryLayout` (existing offsets byte-identical → the drift-test path unaffected).
- **The gate** `isAgentGraphWasmSupported(model)` (the single source of truth `agentTargetOf` consults) now additionally requires: ≤ 4 `getNearbyAgents` nodes; every `forEachInArray.array` source is a `getNearbyAgents`; only SCALAR Local Variables (array variables + setArrayElement are PR6b-3); `getRandom` not options-mode. Field nodes / division-event / structural writes / `getCellAttribute` stay OUT → Chemotaxis (`secreteToField`) + Tissue (`getCellAttribute`) cleanly clamp to JS.
- **DEV `setRngSeed` worker message** (test-only, never sent by the app): forces the shared seed so a JS-target run + a WASM-target run advance the identical stream (the parity vehicle).
- **Verified**: tsc -b + `npm run build` clean; lattice byte-identity (zero `git diff` on `wasm`/`webgpu` compilers + GoL/Life3D compile clean ×3 targets); Boids `isAgentGraphWasmSupported===true` (2675-byte module, 11 node types); Chemotaxis/Tissue clamp to JS + run 0-error; **JS↔WASM bit-parity** — TWO pristine standalone workers (compact-seeded → deterministic, same RNG seed, momentum 0.9 full flocking), **N=200 steps, 260 agents → 0 diffs on x/y/vx/vy, maxAbs 0, 0 NaN** (positions bit-identical to full f64 precision); the PR6b-1 drift test still bit-exact (0 diffs/60 steps). NB: the parity test MUST use pristine standalone workers — the app-owned worker's `useEffect` re-init + the unserialized vx/vy (getState/loadState don't round-trip velocity, a PR4 gap) contaminate a same-worker JS-then-WASM comparison.

### Phase F — W1: the WASM FORCE PASS (the boost lever; plan `docs/PLAN_AGENT_WASM_WEBGPU.md`)
W1 ports the agent **force integrator** — the engine code that, even on the WASM agent target, ran in JS — to WASM. It is the HOTTEST per-step agent code (the per-neighbour-pair double loop): the 3×3(×3) hash-stencil neighbour pass (soft-sphere repulsion/adhesion + density) → bond springs → velocity integration (momentum, maxSpeed, drag, dt) → `xNext/yNext[/zNext]` → growth ramp. The handoff's PR6 intentionally kept it in JS to minimise the WASM surface; W1 is the deliberate delta.
- **A SECOND export `forcePass` in the SAME agent module** ([agentWasm/compile.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/agentWasm/compile.ts) `emitForcePass`): a faithful byte-for-byte port of `runAgentStep`'s force loop ([sim.worker.ts](src/simulator/engine/sim.worker.ts)), reading/writing the wasmBacked AgentStore at the `computeAgentMemoryLayout` baked offsets — the SAME memory the JS engine reads (zero glue). It runs RIGHT AFTER the behaviour (same step), reusing the in-memory hash already copied in for `getNearbyAgents` (no extra copy). f64 throughout ⇒ JS↔WASM bit-exact. **The structural phase + the hash build STAY in JS** (run once per step, not per neighbour-pair); `swapPositions` (a copy-into under wasmBacked views, B10) commits the new positions as before.
- **2D vs 3D** is a SEPARATE verbatim code path (the `if (is3d)` split mirrors the JS loop — NOT a branchless always-0-dz body — so the 2D arithmetic + stencil count are identical). The hash path skips the alive check (`buildSpatialHash` only bins alive agents); the all-pairs fallback adds it. Density counts regardless of bonding; the soft-sphere force + bond springs + growth-ramp magnitude are gated on the resolved `bonding`/`growthRate` (which the worker already resolves with the `usesBondingPhysics` toggle).
- **Mirrored scalar-config ABI** (`FORCE_PASS_PARAMS` ↔ the worker's `agentForcePassWasmFn(...)` call in `runAgentStep` — the param↔arg pair, the silent-desync class): `(highWater, hashValid, nBinsX, nBinsY, nBinsZ : i32, binSizeX, binSizeY, binSizeZ : f64, dtOverEta, muR, muA, range, momentum, maxSpeed, growthRate : f64, W, H, D : f64, bonding, torus : i32)`. `dtOverEta = dt/eta` is PRECOMPUTED (one division, bit-identical to JS's per-iteration `(dt/eta)` since the operands are step-constant). `bonding` gates BOTH the soft-sphere force (JS `engineForces`) AND the bond springs; `growthRate` carries the bonding gate (0 when off).
- **The torus position wrap uses a host `env.fmod = (a,b)=>a%b` import** — the EXACT JS `%` (fmod). WASM has no f64 rem opcode, and reconstructing `a - trunc(a/b)*b` rounds twice (drift). A "skip the wrap when n ∈ [0,span)" fast path is ALSO not bit-exact (for a non-power-of-2 span, JS's `(n+W)` rounds, so `((n%W)+W)%W ≠ n` in the low bits even for in-range n — verified: it diverged at ~1e-12). The unconditional host-fmod is the only bit-exact path. `fmod` is an 8th func import at funcIdx `NUM_IMPORTED_FUNCS` (=7), appended AFTER pow..tanh (0..6) so those indices are unchanged; the two module funcs are then `behaviour` (funcIdx 8) + `forcePass` (funcIdx 9), exported by name (the funcIdx shift is invisible to the worker, which calls by name). An inline musl-style i64 fmod (avoids the host call) is deferred — it needs ~15 new i64 encoder ops, and the wrap is once per agent, not per neighbour pair.
- **Worker dispatch** ([sim.worker.ts](src/simulator/engine/sim.worker.ts) `runAgentStep`): `instantiateAgentWasm` now returns `forcePass` too (`agentForcePassWasmFn`, null on a behaviour-only module — nulled wherever `agentBehaviourWasmFn` is). After the WASM behaviour ran AND the in-memory hash was copied in this step (`forcePassReady`), the worker calls `agentForcePassWasmFn(...)` INSTEAD of the JS force loop (`if (ranForceWasm) {} else if (is3d) {...} else {...}`). Any WASM force-pass failure → null the fn + run the JS loop this step. The hash-overflow / behaviour-fallback paths set `forcePassReady=false`, so the force pass only runs when its in-memory hash is valid.
- **Verified** (a Node esbuild-bundled parity harness — DOM-free; the worker's force loop copied verbatim as the JS reference): **12/12 bit-parity variants — 0 mismatches, maxAbs 0, 0 NaN** over 60 steps × 200 agents across {2D, 3D} × {hash stencil, all-pairs fallback, torus, clamp, soft-sphere ON/OFF, maxSpeed cap, growth ramp grow+shrink}; an **end-to-end** `behaviour(WASM)+forcePass(WASM)` vs `behaviour+jsForceLoop` test — 0 diffs over 50 real steps (2D + 3D). `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit` + `npm run build` clean. Lattice + JS-agent **byte-identity by construction** (only `agentWasm/compile.ts` + `sim.worker.ts` touched — the lattice/JS-agent compilers are untouched; `git diff --stat` = 2 files).
- **HONEST perf finding (the lever is small on this engine).** The plan hypothesised ~2–4× from the force pass. The measured **force-integrator-only** speedup (Node V8, hash build excluded) is **~1.0–1.25×**: ~1.25× in the clamp case, ~1.05–1.09× torus (the host-fmod boundary crossing — once per agent — erases part of the win), ~0.99× (a wash) for 3D-torus 2000 agents, up to ~1.15–1.17× at 10k. V8 already JITs this tight monomorphic numeric loop near-optimally, so the WASM win is modest — consistent with the plan's "neither target fixes a current bottleneck; both raise the ceiling," but BELOW its force-pass hypothesis. The port is bit-exact + zero-regression infrastructure (and worker-V8 / very-large-counts may differ from Node), but it is NOT the CA-grid-level speedup the goal sought for the FORCE LOOP specifically. (NB: the HEAVY-RULE benchmark below shows the boost DOES materialise for a heavy per-agent BEHAVIOUR rule — the force loop is just the wrong place to look.)

### Phase F — WASM AGENT WHOLE-TARGET PORT: full WASM agent coverage + JS bit-parity + the heavy-rule boost (branch `continue_agents`)
The full-coverage WASM agent push — `isAgentGraphWasmSupported` now accepts the ENTIRE agent-graph catalogue (the reject set is ZERO — WASM is Turing-complete + f64, so no node is un-portable), so a user picks the WASM agent target and models freely with **JS↔WASM bit-parity** (the f64 gold standard, UNLIKE WebGPU's f32/statistical parity). Touches ONLY `agentWasm/compile.ts` + `agentEngine.ts` + `sim.worker.ts` + `SimulatorView.tsx` (+ an `i32.trunc_sat` encoder const) — **lattice grid (2D+3D, all 3 targets) + the JS-agent + the WebGPU-agent compilers are byte-identical by construction** (`git diff --stat` vs the merge base touches none of them).
- **The WASM module = the BEHAVIOUR loop ONLY** (mirrors the WebGPU G4/G5 decision): the `divisionEvent` + `agentInit` roots stay JS-on-CPU (target-independent — the worker runs `agentDivisionFn`/`agentInitFn` over the SAME wasmBacked memory the WASM behaviour reads/writes, bit-exact). The gate checks ONLY the BEHAVIOUR-REACHABLE node set (`behaviourReachableNodeIds` = the `behaviourStep.do` chain + its transitive value cone), so a Tissue graph runs on WASM even though its divisionEvent subtree uses CPU-only nodes. `AGENT_WASM_CPU_ROOT_TYPES` (divisionEvent/agentInit/createAgent/addAgentToWorld) documents the JS-on-CPU set.
- **Added emitters** ([agentWasm/compile.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/agentWasm/compile.ts)): the **field bridge** (sampleField/fieldGradient[central-diff]/readCellsUnder[r-disk]/affectCellsUnder/secreteToField[bilinear splat] — 2D, torus-folded), the **agent-array tier** (getAgentsAttribute gather / filterAgents / joinAgents[union+intersection] / pickRandomAgent / pickNRandomAgents[partial Fisher-Yates] / getBondedAgents, all skipping empty(-1)/dead/oob ids; aggregate[sum/product/min/max/average/median[insertion-sort]/and/or] / groupOperator[+ weightedRandom + uniform random + index/position] / groupCounting / groupStatement over arrays — scratch via a per-agent bump pointer), `getCellAttribute`/`getAgentAttribute`/`setAttribute`/`updateAttribute` on the agent SoA (typed by `agentAttrKind`), the **structural-WRITE** nodes (divideAgent/formBond/breakBond/killAgent → request-flag stores into shared agent memory — the heavy mutation is the CPU structural phase), the **setters** (setVelocity/setAgentAttribute/setAgentsAttribute/setAgentPosition/Radius/Type — range+alive guarded), the **bond/self reads** (forEachBond[ragged bond loop]/getCurvature/getBondDegree/neighbourDensity), the **universal** value/flow nodes (switch[conditions+value, firstMatch+independent]/loop/valueSwitch[OP_SELECT relay]/getModelAttribute/lookupInteraction/interactionTableMap/proportionMap/interpolation/colorScale/categoricalColor/getColorConstant/arrayElement/arrayLength + getConstant tag + getIndicator/setIndicator/updateIndicator[ALL ops incl toggle/next/prev — the agent loop is SEQUENTIAL so these are well-defined, unlike WebGPU's parallel writers] + setCellLooks[plain, writes the agent colors buffer; glyph rejected — no per-agent glyph SoA]), and **array Local Variables** + setArrayElement.
- **External regions in agent memory** ([agentEngine.ts](src/simulator/engine/agentEngine.ts) `AgentLayoutExtras`): the cell field arrays (`_field_<id>`), model attributes, indicators, lookup tables ride NEW reserved regions appended to `computeAgentMemoryLayout` (after the PR6b-2 hash region, so existing offsets are byte-stable). The worker copies them IN before the WASM call (`copyAgentExternalRegionsIn`) and the field deposit + indicators back OUT after (`copyAgentExternalRegionsOut`) — Decision D-FIELD. **Layout lockstep (the +64-cell bug)**: the store's layout MUST equal the compiler's — same `maxHashBins` (both via `computeAgentMaxHashBins(W,H,D,range,dr,nq)`) + same extras; the worker derives `fieldTotal` from the LIVE grid dims, the compiler from the model — they agree. A mismatch shifts the field region and the WASM reads cell `idx + (regionΔ/8)` (the symptom: a noise field gives a grossly-wrong sample while a LINEAR field masks it — linear bilinear is exact regardless of which bracketing cells). `buildAgentLayoutExtras(model)` is the SINGLE source both call.
- **Sync agent mode under wasmBacked**: a distinct `attrWriteOffset` region (the WASM behaviour reads `attrOffset`, writes `attrWriteOffset`); `swapAgentAttrs` COPIES-INTO under wasmBacked (the B10/AW-SWAP view discipline — a reference swap would orphan the baked offset). `primeAgentAttrWrite` clones read→write before; `swapAgentAttrs` copies write→read after. (Async mode aliases write=read, byte-identical to before.)
- **Three parity bugs the JS↔WASM harness caught + fixed** (the gold-standard verification surfaced each): (1) **`emitLogic` UPPERCASE op** — `LogicOperatorNode` stores `'OR'`/`'AND'`/`'XOR'`/`'NOT'`; the emitter matched lowercase so OR/XOR/NOT fell through to AND (GoL-on-agents all-die, the SAME bug the WebGPU port hit); now `.toLowerCase()`s. (2) **field DOUBLE-wrap** — `emitSampleFieldAt`/`emitSecreteToField` wrapped (x,y) PAIRS, double-wrapping a corner coordinate shared between two samples; now `emitFieldWrapCoord` wraps each axis ONCE. (3) **field sample-before-deposit ORDER** — JS sink-hoists pure values to cell-top so a field read sees the PRE-deposit field; the WASM `preEmitAgentValues` pass (the WASM analogue of the WebGPU one, with `AGENT_VALUE_NO_HOIST` excluding RNG/mutable-storage/array-producer/forEach-element nodes — field reads ARE hoisted) now hoists the pure non-volatile value cone to agent-loop-top, matching JS exactly. (4) **`i32.trunc_sat_f64_s`** (a new encoder const, additive) for the f64→i32 value conversions — a NaN/Inf intermediate (aggregate.max over an empty array → -Inf; an expression with sin/sqrt) made the trapping `i32.trunc_f64_s` throw `float unrepresentable in integer range`; the saturating version is NON-trapping (NaN→0 like JS `x|0`) and bit-identical to plain truncation for finite in-range values (so the verified parity is preserved).
- **Verified — JS↔WASM BIT-PARITY on ALL 8 agent samples** (`scripts/parity-agent-wasm.mjs` — two stores, plain-JS + wasmBacked, same seed + hash + external regions, behaviour-fn-level): **0 mismatches over 150 steps, 64 agents** on Drift Test / Boids / Chemotaxis / GoL-on-agents / Ant Necrophoresis / the 3 Tissues (the force pass is W1-bit-exact; the structural phase is target-independent CPU → full-pipeline parity by composition). `scripts/check-agent-wasm-gate.mjs`: all 8 GATE✓ COMPILE✓ INST✓. `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit` + `npm run build` clean. **Browser-verified** (the worktree dev server on :5180, cross-origin module import into the running Chromium): all 5 agent samples GATE+COMPILE+INSTANTIATE in the REAL browser WASM engine, and the Chemotaxis field bridge is **BIT-IDENTICAL** (browser JS engine vs browser WASM engine, 20 steps, 0 mismatches).
- **PERF — THE BOOST MATERIALIZES for heavy rules** (`scripts/bench-agent-behaviour.mjs` — a chromatography-in-agents-style HEAVY per-agent rule: nearby gather → 3 aggregates → a Lookup Table → 2 expressions → 2 compares → 2 conditionals, the BEHAVIOUR fn only): **WASM vs JS = 5.0× at 500 agents / 2.8× at 2000 / 2.1× at 8000**. So the user's hypothesis HOLDS: WASM pulls ahead of JS as per-agent RULE COMPLEXITY grows, exactly like the CA grid. The trivial Boids force loop was a wash (W1 — V8 JITs a tight monomorphic numeric loop near-optimally), but a heavy behaviour rule (megamorphic typed-array reads, many branches, a lookup table) is where the JS interpreter overhead shows and WASM's compiled bytecode wins 2-5×.
- **The FINAL `isAgentGraphWasmSupported` reject set — EMPTY (zero node bans).** The only clamp-to-JS is the structural per-node array-scratch-slot budget (`> AGENT_NEARBY_SCRATCH_SLOTS=4` simultaneous getNearbyAgents producers → JS, never silently corrupted) — a capacity gate, not a node ban. WASM has NO precision/mode exclusions (f64 + sequential), so median/uniform-random/toggle-indicators/async-attrs ALL work (unlike WebGPU's f32/parallel fundamentals). Stop Event now runs natively on the WASM agent behaviour (see "Agent Stop Event"), and so does **Set Agent Sprite** (see its own section). `setCellLooks` glyph is the one documented JS-side carve-out (no per-agent glyph SoA; clamps via the behaviour-reachable gate).

### Phase F — PR7 G1+G2+G3: the WebGPU agent-loop COMPILER + force shader (branch `agents_floating_cells`)
The SEPARATE WebGPU agent-loop compiler — the GPU sibling of `agentWasm/compile.ts`. Emits a WGSL `behaviour` module (G1+G2) + a standalone WGSL force-pass module (G3) over a GPU agent SoA. **The per-step runtime wiring + `agentTargetOf` enable (G3-runtime+G6) are NOW DONE** — see the next section. The Boids agent loop runs end-to-end on WebGPU (live in-browser flock verified, polarization 0.998).
- **A SEPARATE, additive compiler** [src/modeler/vpl/compiler/agentWebgpu/](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/agentWebgpu/) — `layout.ts` (`computeAgentWebGPULayout`: the GPU agent SoA = 7 strided storage buffers for the Boids subset, under the 8-binding floor so no `requiredLimits` raise; SEPARATE from the WASM `AgentMemoryLayout` — the GPU never shares memory, the worker uploads/reads back), `compile.ts` (`compileAgentGraphWebGPU` + `isAgentGraphWebGPUSupported`), `forcePass.ts` (`emitAgentForcePassWGSL`). Touches NO lattice/grid WebGPU + NO existing agent JS/WASM path → lattice + JS-agent + WASM-agent byte-identity BY CONSTRUCTION (`git diff --stat` = only the DEV harness).
- **G1+G2 — the behaviour shader.** `dispatchCells` 2-D tiling, `highWater` a CONTROL UNIFORM (not baked — baking forces a per-gen recompile), the alive-skip + `idx>=highWater` guard. Universal nodes via f32 WGSL-string emit (reusing the lattice `emitWgsl` + select-divide-guard); the ~12 agent-node WGSL emitters (getNearbyAgents hash stencil + forEach + getAgentOffset torus fold + getVelocity/getAgentPosition/getAgentRadius + applyForce + setTargetRadius + setVariable). Per-agent PCG RNG keyed by `idx` (the lattice grid model — statistical parity, NOT bit-exact). Front-end = the SAME `expandMacros → collapseReroutes → CSE` the JS agent compiler runs. **Reconciled to the current base** (the prior 019375f reference pre-dated the Generic Agent Platform): the gate + all var sites read `model.agentVariables` (NOT the cell `variables`); the Compare op reads `cfg.operation` (the StatementNode key) NOT `operator` (a latent reference bug that would have emitted `==` for every non-equality Compare).
- **G3 — the WGSL force pass** ([forcePass.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/agentWebgpu/forcePass.ts)): the GPU sibling of `runAgentStep`'s force loop + `agentWasm` `emitForcePass` — the 3×3 hash-stencil neighbour pass (soft-sphere + density, torus-wrapped, all-pairs fallback) → velocity Euler (momentum/maxSpeed/dtOverEta) → wrap/clamp into the appended GPU `xNext`/`yNext` fields → age + growth ramp. Its own `ForceControl` uniform mirrors the WASM `FORCE_PASS_PARAMS` ABI. **`xNext`/`yNext` APPENDED to `AGENT_GPU_F32_FIELDS`** so the behaviour shader's field bases stay byte-identical (re-verified: 5780 chars, compiles clean with the new fields). 2D-only, f32. **Bond springs + division + the hash BUILD stay CPU/JS** (the GPU SoA carries no bond store; the gate excludes bonded/division/field models, so for the Boids headline the force pass is exact).
- **The gate** `isAgentGraphWebGPUSupported(model)` — TRUE iff Agents enabled AND not 3D AND EVERY (flattened) agent-graph node ∈ `AGENT_WEBGPU_SUPPORTED_TYPES` (the Boids subset, ≤ 4 `getNearbyAgents`, scalar-vars-only, no options-mode getRandom, every forEach array source = getNearbyAgents). Mirrors the WASM gate + a 3D rejection. (G6: `agentTargetOf` now widens to `'webgpu'` when this gate passes — see the next section.)
- **Verified**: tsc clean; `compileAll(Boids).agent.webgpu` emits a 5780-char shader with exactly the 11 Boids node types; **both** the behaviour shader AND `emitAgentForcePassWGSL` compile with **0 errors + 0 validation errors** on a real `device.createShaderModule`/`getCompilationInfo`; `isAgentGraphWebGPUSupported(Boids)===true`, `(Tissue/Chemotaxis)===false` (getCellAttribute/secreteToField + 3D clamp to JS). DEV harness ([compileHarness.ts](src/dev/compileHarness.ts)) gained an `agent.webgpu` surface.
- **THE SCALE BENCHMARK (the headline) — JS vs WASM, force integrator.** `scripts/bench-agent-force.mjs` (esbuild-bundled, DOM-free) times the force-pass hot loop (hash build excluded) at 2k/10k/50k/100k agents (customForces / Boids case): **JS vs WASM is a WASH at every scale — 0.99× / 0.90× / 0.98× / 1.03×** (JS steps/s 5590 / 866 / 99 / 33). V8 JITs the tight monomorphic loop near-optimally (consistent with W1's ~1.0–1.25×); the agent loop is O(N) via the spatial hash so it is NOT a JS bottleneck at interactive counts. **WebGPU is intentionally absent** — its per-step whole-SoA upload+readback (CPU-built hash) is a fixed overhead that dominates BELOW ~10k agents, so WebGPU for agents is a wash-or-REGRESSION at interactive counts and only possibly breaks even at the very largest counts (needs the wired runtime to measure). The milestone's honest conclusion: there is no agent-loop speedup to be had from a faster target at the counts that matter — the spatial hash already won that on JS.

### Phase F — PR7 G3-runtime + G6: the WebGPU agent RUNTIME (Boids end-to-end; branch `agents_floating_cells`)
The runtime that makes the WebGPU agent target SELECTABLE + RUNNABLE — the GPU sibling of `instantiateAgentWasm` + the WASM `behaviour`/`forcePass` dispatch in `runAgentStep`. Boids flocks end-to-end on WebGPU (live verified: velocity polarization `|Σv|/Σ|v|` climbs 0.01 → 0.998 over ~200 steps, 260 agents, 0 worker errors, agents render + move).
- **A SELF-CONTAINED agent WebGPU runtime** [src/simulator/engine/agentWebgpuRuntime.ts](src/simulator/engine/agentWebgpuRuntime.ts) — its OWN device + buffers + the two compute pipelines (behaviour + force), SEPARATE from the grid's `webgpuRuntime.ts` (so a model can run a WASM grid + WebGPU agents, the Boids case). `createAgentWebGPURuntime(behaviourShader, forceShader, layout)` acquires a device, compiles + validates both WGSL modules up front, allocates 8 buffers, builds the two bind groups (behaviour: 7 bindings agentF32 rw / agentI32 r / agentAlive r / hashBins r / control uniform / rngState rw / agentColors rw; force: 4 bindings agentF32 rw / agentAlive r / hashBins r / forceControl uniform — DIFFERENT binding indices, each shader its own bind-group layout over the SAME underlying buffers), + the two pipelines. Helpers: `uploadAgentSoA` (pack the CPU AgentStore f32/i32/alive SoA into the strided GPU buffers each step), `uploadAgentHash` (the CPU-built CSR hash → the hashBins buffer; returns false on overflow → JS fallback), `uploadAgentControl`/`uploadAgentForceControl` (the two uniforms, field order MIRRORS the shader structs + the WASM `FORCE_PASS_PARAMS` ABI), `dispatchAgentStep` (behaviour then force in one command buffer, `dispatchCells(maxAgents,64)` 2-D tiling), `readbackAgentStep` (read the f32 SoA back + commit `xNext/yNext → x/y` + `vx/vy/radius/density/age` into the CPU store — the JS `swapPositions` analogue), `seedAgentRng` (seed the per-agent PCG ONCE at creation; the GPU advances it in place across steps, so re-seeding every step is NOT done — that would freeze the sequence). f32 + per-agent PCG ⇒ statistical parity, NOT bit-exact (the documented WebGPU constraint). 2D-only. **`destroyAgentWebGPURuntime` releases the GPUDevice** (`dev.destroy()`, mirroring the grid's `destroyWebGPURuntime`) — `createAgentWebGPURuntime` requests its OWN adapter+device per build, so every in-session rebuild (soft recompile / agent-target flip / reset) that tears down the prior runtime WITHOUT a `worker.terminate()` would otherwise leak a heavyweight device; a full model LOAD terminates the worker and reclaims devices regardless, so this is an in-session correctness fix (not the cross-load recording slowdown).
- **`runAgentStepWebGPU()`** ([sim.worker.ts](src/simulator/engine/sim.worker.ts)) — the GPU sibling of `runAgentStep`'s WASM dispatch (ASYNC: the readback awaits a `mapAsync`). CPU prep (reset forces, build the spatial hash, prime the sync attr buffer) → upload SoA + hash + the two control uniforms → `dispatchAgentStep` → `swapAgentAttrs` → `readbackAgentStep` → the CPU structural phase (a no-op for Boids: the gate excludes bonds/division/field). Returns whether the GPU ran (false → the caller runs the JS `runAgentStep()` for that step — hash overflow / device failure are never silently wrong). The bond springs + division + the hash BUILD stay CPU/JS (the GPU SoA carries no bond store); for the Boids headline the GPU force pass is exact.
- **The step-batch async branch** (sim.worker.ts `step` handler): the sync `for` loop can't `await`, so a JS/WASM grid + WebGPU agents model (Boids) routes to an async COPY of the batch loop when `agentTarget === 'webgpu' && agentWebgpuRuntime` — it awaits `runAgentStepWebGPU()` per step, runs the cell `runStep()` synchronously (the grid is JS/WASM here), then the colour pass + `sendColors`. The pre-existing sync JS/WASM-agent loop is UNTOUCHED (the new branch is gated + early-`break`s before it). (A WebGPU GRID + WebGPU agents model would route through the existing `webgpuActive` async branch — but Boids uses a JS/WASM grid.)
- **`agentTargetOf(cfg, wasmSupported, webgpuSupported)`** ([centerBased.ts](src/model/centerBased.ts)) gained a 3rd arg: a `'webgpu'` config resolves to `'webgpu'` ONLY when `isAgentGraphWebGPUSupported(model)`, else clamps to `'js'` (the always-runnable fallback — NOT 'wasm'). The worker-side `resolveAgentTarget` (sim.worker.ts) is the safety net mirror: `'webgpu'` demotes to `'js'` if either shader is missing from the message.
- **Build/dispatch lifecycle**: SimulatorView's `compileAgentModel` resolves the target (`isAgentGraphWebGPUSupported`), compiles the behaviour shader (`compileAgentGraphWebGPUForModel`) + the force shader (`emitAgentForcePassWGSL`), and ships both WGSL strings + the layout dims (`agentWebgpuMaxAgents`/`MaxHashBins`) in the init + recompile messages (mirroring the WASM `agentWasmBytes` path). The worker `buildAgentWebGPUIfNeeded()` (async, monotonic build-token guarded — the orphan-on-reinit discipline) builds the runtime; `initAgents()` drops a stale runtime (a re-alloc invalidates it); reset/recompile rebuild. Any device/compile/dispatch failure nulls the runtime → the JS behaviour fn + JS force loop run.
- **The Properties radio** (PropertiesPanelContent.tsx) WebGPU agent option is now ENABLED (not `disabled`) + its hint reflects live support (`isAgentGraphWebGPUSupported(model)`): "runs on WebGPU (the Boids node subset, 2D)" when supported, else "falls back to JS (bonds / division / field stay CPU)".
- **Byte-identity** (verified `git diff --stat` vs the compiler-merge base `8d7c919`): the lattice grid compilers (`compile.ts`/`wasm/`/`webgpu/`) + the agent JS/WASM compilers (`compileAgentGraph`, `agentWasm/`) + the agent WebGPU COMPILER (`agentWebgpu/`) are ALL UNTOUCHED — the only diff is `centerBased.ts` (the 3rd `agentTargetOf` arm), `PropertiesPanelContent.tsx` (the radio), `SimulatorView.tsx` (the webgpu compile path in `compileAgentModel`), `sim.worker.ts` (the additive webgpu-agent branch, gated on `agentTarget==='webgpu'`), + the new `agentWebgpuRuntime.ts`. So lattice + JS-agent + WASM-agent behaviour is identical by construction for every non-WebGPU-agent model.
- **Verified**: `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit` + `npm run build` clean; live in-browser (Boids, agentTarget `webgpu`, WebGPU available) — gate `isAgentGraphWebGPUSupported===true`, `agentTargetOf===webgpu`, shader 5780 chars; 260 agents flock (polarization 0.01→0.998 over 200 steps, stable over 400+ steps, 0 worker errors), render as cyan dots, the Properties WebGPU radio is enabled + selected.
- **STILL TODO:** G4 (structural round-trip → Tissue), G5 (field bridge → Chemotaxis), PR7c (zero-copy / atomics) — clamped to JS by the gate. A HEAVY-per-agent-rule benchmark to show a WASM/WebGPU win (the simple Boids force loop is O(N) via the hash, so no agent-loop speedup from a faster target at interactive counts — the upload/readback overhead means WebGPU is a wash-or-regression below ~10k agents; it only helps at very large counts or with much heavier per-agent compute). *(All since DONE — G4/G5 below, the heavy-rule benchmark in the WHOLE-TARGET PORT, and PR7c residency in the perf round on `optimize`, which removes the per-gen upload/readback for eligible models.)*

### Phase F — PR7 G5: the WebGPU agent FIELD BRIDGE (Chemotaxis end-to-end; branch `agents_floating_cells`)
The closed agent↔grid morphogen feedback (Decision D-FIELD) now runs on the WebGPU agent target — **Chemotaxis - Aggregation** flocks-and-aggregates on WebGPU. Additive over the G3-runtime; the lattice grid + JS/WASM-agent + the **Boids WebGPU** path are byte-identical (the field buffers are created ONLY when the model has agent-accessible cell attrs → a no-field Boids shader stays 5780 chars).

The 5 field-node WGSL emitters — `sampleField` / `fieldGradient` (central-diff) / `readCellsUnder` (r-disk aggregate via `fieldSampleBilinear`); `affectCellsUnder` (r-disk) + `secreteToField` (4-cell bilinear splat via `fieldDepositCell`) — mirror the JS emitters' 2D math (f32, statistical parity).

The worker's `runAgentStepWebGPU` ([sim.worker.ts](src/simulator/engine/sim.worker.ts)) does the CPU round-trip: upload the field BEFORE the dispatch, read the deposit back into `readAttrs[id]` AFTER (gated on `fieldReadLen||fieldWriteLen > 0`) so the cell CA step incorporates it. `isAgentGraphWebGPUSupported` now accepts the 5 field nodes; the worker derives the field spec from `fieldSpecs` (= `cellFieldAttrsOf`; readWrite subset = `cellFieldWriteAttrsOf`), the SAME order the shader compiled against.

### Phase F — PR7 G4: the WebGPU agent STRUCTURAL ROUND-TRIP (Tissue end-to-end; branch `agents_floating_cells`)
The CPU structural phase (bonds / division eigensolve / death / auto-bond) + the division-event fn are **target-INDEPENDENT** (pure CPU/TS in [sim.worker.ts](src/simulator/engine/sim.worker.ts) `runAgentStructuralPhase`/`runDivisionEvent` + [agentEngine.ts](src/simulator/engine/agentEngine.ts) `divideAgent`) and run unconditionally. So G4 = (a) emit the structural-WRITE nodes on the GPU as per-agent REQUEST-FLAG stores + (b) read the request buffers back to CPU before the structural phase, mirroring how G5 added the field round-trip. **Morphogenesis - Differential Tissue** (division + bonds + maturity differentiation) now runs on the WebGPU agent target. The eigensolve + the divisionEvent fn stay JS on every target (NO WGSL division shader).
- **Request buffers ride the existing `agentF32` (binding 0) — ZERO new bindings** ([agentWebgpu/layout.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/agentWebgpu/layout.ts)): the 9 structural-request fields (`divideRequest`/`divideAxisX`/`divideAxisY`/`divideAsym`/`bondFormReq`/`bondFormL`/`bondFormK`/`bondBreakReq`/`killRequest`, `AGENT_GPU_REQUEST_FIELDS`) are appended to `AGENT_GPU_F32_FIELDS` AFTER `xNext`/`yNext` (so the force-shader bases stay byte-identical), stored as f32 (flags are small ints / an agent-id+1, exact ≤2²⁴; the axis/asym are float). The behaviour-shader emitters ([agentWebgpu/compile.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/agentWebgpu/compile.ts) `compileFlowNode`): `divideAgent`→`agentF32[drBase+idx]=1.0` + axis (`0.0` when unwired → the engine resolves the tension axis: `divideAgent` resolves it whenever the axis is non-finite OR `(0,0)`, so `0.0` is behaviour-equivalent to the JS path's NaN default — and MUST NOT be a NaN literal/bitcast, see the gotcha in Verified) + asym; `formBond`/`breakBond`→`(target|0)+1` + restLength/stiffness; `killAgent`→`1.0`.
- **User AGENT attributes on the GPU** ([layout.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/agentWebgpu/layout.ts) `agentAttrIds`/`agentAttrBase`): each `agentAttrsOf` id gets its own `agentF32` run appended after the request fields. `getCellAttribute`→`agentF32[attrBase+idx]` (f32; int/tag/bool round-trip exactly); `setAttribute`→write back with `round(...)` for int/tag/bool. `computeAgentWebGPULayout` gained a 4th `agentAttrIds` param; the SimulatorView compile (`compileAgentGraphWebGPUForModel`, uses `agentAttrsOf(model)`) + the worker rebuild (`buildAgentWebGPUIfNeeded`, uses `store.attrSpecs`) derive the SAME ordered list (the layout-match invariant).
- **Universal nodes Tissue's behaviour uses** (new emitters): `categoricalColor` (multi-output palette select, shares the lattice `readCategoricalEntries`/`readCategoricalDefault`); `setCellLooks` (per-agent packed `agentColors[idx]` = `r|g<<8|b<<16|a<<24`, PLAIN mode only — a glyph setCellLooks clamps to JS; the `__current__`/any mapping writes unconditionally since the agent loop has one viewer); `neighbourDensity`→`agentF32[densityBase+idx]`; `getBondDegree`→`f32(bondCount)`.
- **Runtime** ([agentWebgpuRuntime.ts](src/simulator/engine/agentWebgpuRuntime.ts)): `uploadAgentSoA` zeroes the request runs each step (a fresh per-step request slate) + uploads the agent attrs from `s.attrRead`; `readbackAgentStep` now ALSO copies the f32 SoA back into the engine's CPU request arrays (`s.divideRequest`/`s.bondFormReq`/…, flags rounded to int), the agent-attr runs into `s.attrWrite` (int kinds rounded), and the packed `agentColors` (a 2nd `copyBufferToBuffer`) into `s.colors`. The worker's `runAgentStepWebGPU` reorders to **dispatch → readback (attrs→attrWrite) → swapAgentAttrs (→attrRead) → structural phase** (the swap MUST follow the attr readback; in async agent mode `attrWrite` aliases `attrRead` so the swap is a no-op and the readback lands directly in `attrRead` — Tissue is async).
- **The gate checks ONLY the BEHAVIOUR-REACHABLE node set** (`behaviourReachableNodeIds` — the `behaviourStep.do` flow chain + its transitive value cone): the `divisionEvent` + `agentInit` roots are compiled SEPARATELY on CPU/JS (target-independent), so a Tissue graph whose divisionEvent subtree uses a node the shader can't emit (e.g. an extra `setAttribute`/`expression` on a daughter) still runs on WebGPU. The compiler's defensive loop + the getNearbyAgents-slot assignment are likewise scoped to reachable nodes. (Mirrors how the JS/WASM compilers walk one root at a time.)
- **`migrateForHarness`** ([compileHarness.ts](src/dev/compileHarness.ts)) now runs `migrateAgentAttributeSplit` + `migrateVariableScopeSplit` (mirrors LOAD_MODEL) — so the dev harness sees the split agentAttributes (Tissue's `maturity` moves cell→agent), matching the loaded model.
- **Byte-identity**: lattice grid + JS/WASM-agent + the no-structural-node Boids/Chemotaxis WebGPU shaders are unchanged (the request/attr runs only EMIT when a structural / Get-Set-Attribute node is reached; the layout's bigger `f32Len` is a buffer-size change, not a shader-string change). The force shader reads only the leading static fields, whose bases are unchanged.
- **Verified**: tsc + `npm run build` clean; the Tissue WebGPU shader compiles (gate `true`, target `webgpu`; `maturity` read/write at `agentF32[46200u+idx]`, the `divideRequest` flag store + NaN axis, the categorical palette select, `agentColors[idx]=` packed write, `neighbourDensity` read all present); Boids + Chemotaxis still gate `true` / compile with no request emit; the engine structural primitives consume the request values (the `(0,0)` GPU axis → the eigensolve resolves a finite tension axis on a bonded cluster, division grows the store, bonds partition, daughter inherits maturity). **LIVE-verified in the browser** (`agentTarget:'webgpu'`): gate `true`, target `webgpu`, behaviour shader compiles + builds with NO fallback; Tissue **GROWS 5 → ~305 agents** (bonds 5 → ~841, self-limiting at ~290-305 = contact inhibition), **maturity differentiates** (the categorical green-stem→magenta-mature coloring renders), 0 worker errors; Boids (0.998) + Chemotaxis (aggregation) re-verified still run on WebGPU (no regression — the structural emit is gated). **GOTCHA (the bug live-verification caught — the headless check could not):** the unwired divide axis MUST emit `0.0`, NOT a NaN — `bitcast<f32>(0x7fc00000u)` has no literal `nan` in the shader STRING (so a string scan passes), but **WGSL/Naga CONSTANT-FOLDS the bitcast into a NaN constant and rejects it** at `device.createShaderModule` ("value nan cannot be represented as 'f32'"), so the behaviour shader silently failed to build and **fell back to JS**. Any future "magic sentinel" in a WGSL agent/grid emitter must be a representable f32 (the engine's `non-finite OR (0,0)` check makes `0.0` the safe sentinel here). A passing TS-compile / shader-string check is NOT proof a shader RUNS — only a real `device.createShaderModule` (i.e. a browser run) is.

Fixed the operand order.
- **Verified — JS↔WASM bit-parity on ALL 9 agent samples** (8 shipped + a SYNTHETIC 3D-field model built in-memory by [scripts/parity-agent-wasm.mjs](scripts/parity-agent-wasm.mjs)'s `build3DFieldModel`, exercising ALL 5 field nodes in 3D): 0 mismatches over 150 (+ 300) steps, 64 agents, incl. the readWrite `field_` arrays (so the 3D secrete splat + affect scatter write bit-identical cells too). A six-agent review swept the agent engine, the three agent compile targets, the ~42 agent nodes, the 3D grid/renderer, the UI lifecycle, and the docs; every confirmed finding was fixed. Verified: tsc + `npm run build` clean; ALL 21 library models compile clean across JS/WASM/WebGPU (sweep via the dev harness); the 9-entry JS↔WASM agent parity harness = 0 mismatches; `check-agent-wasm-gate.mjs` all ✓. The load-bearing changes:
- **Agent state persists in `.gcastate` / Save-Project-with-grid** (was silently dropped — a hand-seeded agent board vanished on save/load). `SimulationState.agents?: SerializedAgentState` (+ `activeAgentViewer?`), base64-generic over the worker `AgentStatePayload` via `serializeAgentState`/`deserializeAgentState` ([fileOperations.ts](src/model/fileOperations.ts)); `applySimulationState` forwards it to the worker `loadState`; a state WITHOUT an agent payload re-seeds the agent layer (loadState else-branch) instead of keeping the old population. **⚠ `serializePreset` is a SECOND writer of the same `SimulationState` and it did NOT inherit this** — see the preset bullet in the Simulator section; when adding a board-state field, wire BOTH serializers. `AgentStatePayload` also gained `vx`/`vy` + the 3 sprite arrays (zeroed-then-loaded on deserialize — momentum models keep their motion; loading over a running session can't inherit stale slot velocities).
- **Async read-after-write hazards now cover AGENT roots on all three targets** ([asyncWriteHazard.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/asyncWriteHazard.ts) gained the agent reader/writer tables + synthetic `__agentVelocity__`/`__agentPosition__`/`__agentRadius__` keys): a behaviour `Set Attribute → read later in flow` reads post-write instead of a hoisted stale snapshot (async agent mode; division events ALWAYS — the division ABI's `w_` block now ALIASES attrRead, fixing sync-mode division writes being clobbered by the next step's `primeAgentAttrWrite`). JS pins via the existing volatile machinery; the agent WASM/WebGPU compilers consume the SAME shared `computeVolatileHoist` emitBefore plan (`ctx.hazardPinned`/`hazardEmitBefore` — emit ONCE at the LCA, NOT re-emit-per-use, which diverged on multi-use reads with a write between uses; the Ant pickup-then-drop shape caught it). Field reads stay a loop-top snapshot on every target (JS `routeValueEmit` forces them to CELL_TOP on agent roots so branch-sinking can't see a same-step deposit the WebGPU fieldRead snapshot can't). The agent WASM/WebGPU branch emitters also clear the volatile cache at conditional/switch/loop BRANCH boundaries (a getVariable-derived value cached from one branch left the sibling reading a stale local on WASM / an unresolved name on WGSL).
- **Agent flow-DIAMOND value scope — `enterCacheScope`/`exitCacheScope` (agentWasm + agentWebgpu)**: the branch-boundary `clearVolatileCache` above covers VOLATILE (forEach-element-derived) values but NOT the general class. `compileFlowChain` has NO visited guard (the documented "flow graphs are DAGs, not trees" discipline), so a flow **DIAMOND** — a node reached from >1 SIBLING branch (a `conditional` `then` AND `else` both flowing into a shared downstream chain; also `switch` cases, or two nodes' flow-outs targeting the same node) — inlines that shared node's body ONCE PER branch walk. A value in the shared body that is NOT hoisted to function-top by `preEmitAgentValues` (an impure cone — canonically a **getRandom-tainted expression**, since getRandom is in `AGENT_VALUE_NO_HOIST`) emits its `let`/`local.set` + caches inside the FIRST branch's block; the SECOND branch's walk hits the cache and references the first block's `let` — on **WebGPU** an out-of-scope WGSL "unresolved value" compile error (→ silent JS fallback), on **WASM** a stale function-scoped local reused (the else branch never re-draws its random) = silently wrong + a broken RNG stream (JS↔WASM parity break). **Fix**: a per-flow-block cache-scope snapshot/restore — `enterCacheScope` (snapshot value+array cache keys) on entering a `{…}` flow block (conditional then/else, switch cases+default, loop/forEach/forEachBond body), `exitCacheScope` (drop entries ADDED inside the block) on exit — so a shared body re-emits its non-hoisted values in each sibling branch's own scope. The snapshot is taken BEFORE the entry `clearVolatileCache` (volatile handling unchanged); pure cross-branch values pre-exist at snapshot time (function-top hoisted) → survive → **byte-identical** for models with no diamond (check-compile-identity: all library models unchanged). The **JS agent compiler needs no equivalent** — it uses the lattice sink analysis, which emits each value at the LCA of its uses (a diamond's shared getRandom lands ABOVE the branch, in-scope for both). Guarded permanently by the `[synthetic] Flow diamond` entry in [scripts/parity-agent-wasm.mjs](scripts/parity-agent-wasm.mjs) (conditional → shared getRandom chain; proven to FAIL without the WASM fix). When adding ANY new block-scoped flow emit to an agent compiler, wrap its body in enter/exitCacheScope — a diamond into it will otherwise reuse a first-branch local.
- **WASM agent emitter fixes** (all silent-wrong before): Compare `between`/`notBetween` (fell through to `==`), Math `%` (fell through to `+`; now host `env.fmod` + the ÷0 guard — `FMOD_FUNC_IDX` is module-scope), options-mode Get Random (fell into the float branch; now emits array-pick + Fallback, inputs resolved BEFORE the RNG advance), bool-mode Get Random (double i32→f64 convert = module VALIDATION failure → silent JS fallback), `filterAgents`/`joinAgents` `count`-port standalone consumption (threw → silent JS clamp; now the lattice count-dispatch pattern), pickRandomAgent resolves its input array BEFORE the RNG advance (chained-RNG-producer order), getConstant orientation-clamp/faceLabel parity. - **By-id reader guards on ALL THREE targets** (Get Agent Position abs+rel / Offset / Radius / Attribute + wired Get Velocity): `-1` (the empty sentinel — Pick Random Agent on an empty set) / out-of-range ids yield 0 instead of `undefined→NaN` position math (JS) or adjacent-memory reads (WASM); unwired reader ids default to `-1`. WASM = `emitAgentIdGuard` (ok flag + clamped safe id + `OP_SELECT`, eager-load-safe); WebGPU = `emitAgentIdGuarded` + `select()`. `forEachBond.currentLength` is torus-folded + 3D-aware on all targets (a seam bond read ≈ W − actual and "break over-strained bonds" severed every seam bond; WebGPU already folded 2D — JS/WASM caught up, all three gained the z arm).
- **Worker lifecycle fixes** ([sim.worker.ts](src/simulator/engine/sim.worker.ts)): the cell Init Event runs BEFORE the agent Init Event on load AND Reset (D-FIELD ordering — a Create-Agent rule that reads the field sees the seeded substrate); `runAgentStepWebGPU` resets `forceZ` (a JS fallback step left a permanent phantom z-force in 3D) and DEFERS mutation messages arriving during its awaited readback (`AGENT_GPU_DEFER_TYPES` + `flushDeferredAgentGpuMsgs` — a mid-step move/seed/paint was clobbered by the readback); `agentAddToWorld` only commits ids staged by THIS Init Event's Create Agent (ghost slots / free-list double-alloc); `currentAgentHash` is invalidated in `initAgents` + after the auto-bond rebuild (it reuses the same per-store scratch arrays); a throwing agent OM colour pass removes itself (was one error post per step); the `createAgent` msg carries `z`; daughter B inherits sprite state in `divideAgent`; the recompile message now ships `agentLayoutExtras`/`agentWebgpuLayout`/`agentWebgpuUsesI32Write`/usage flags (a live target flip to WASM rebuilt the store WITHOUT the extras the module was compiled against — the baked-offset corruption class); the agent Init ABI carries a trailing `_agentZ` in 3D (Set Agent Position's z write threw `_agentZ is not defined` — the canonical 3D spawn recipe crashed) + `zNext` syncs after init; the division ABI carries `_bondRestLength`/`_bondPartnerEpoch` (For Each Bond in a division event crashed on the missing param).
- **3D fixes**: `coords3d` is seeded (`coords` with dl=0) on the dimension flip to 3D AND on LOAD_MODEL, and the JS NI pre-pass `packCoord` falls back to `coords`+dl=0 like the worker (a 2D-authored neighbourhood in a 3D model packed all-INVALID_NI while the sim kept running it, and the slice editor showed 0 cells + clobbered on first click); the agent sphere pick maps back through the alpha-sort permutation (`agentInstOrder` in [gl3d.ts](src/simulator/render/gl3d.ts) — with Alpha blend on, kill/move/inspect hit the WRONG agent); `pick()`/`pickAgent()` respect the Layers Show toggles (no killing invisible agents); Ctrl+C/V/X was gated OFF in 3D (it silently corrupted layer-0 cells at a bogus 2D-projected position) — **since superseded by the layer-aware, brush-plane-anchored region clipboard, see "Shape-aware cell copy/paste"**; the 2D `handleMouseMove` bails in 3D (the hover-coords chip showed garbage); the idle agent-hover pick is rAF-throttled + canvas-rect-gated (was a full pick-FBO render + synchronous readPixels stall per raw window-wide pointermove).
- **Model lifecycle / UX**: `REMOVE_AGENT_MAPPING` cascades `clearDeletedId('mappingId')` (dead compiled pass + dangling picker); `UPDATE_AGENT_ATTRIBUTE` gained the Compare-tag `_port_x/y/y2` remap + a type-change linked-agent-mapping palette reset + `agentVariables` initialValue remap / tag-detach (REMOVE detaches too); `REORDER_AGENT_ATTRIBUTES` reducer + panel wiring (the drag handle was a silent no-op; a reorder forces the full reinit via `attrsStructurallyEqual`); `ADD_AGENT_MAPPING` seeds Standalone when no eligible agent attribute exists; the agent seed-config merge iterates `model.agentAttributes` keyed on `agentAttrSig` (it iterated CELL attrs — persisted seed config never survived a reload and cell edits wiped it); agent-graph compile errors surface in the compile-error banner (`[agents] …` — "No Behaviour Step node" was console-only) and agent OM compile errors are collected into `compileAgentGraph().error` instead of swallowed; the panel-drag drop menu applies `isNodeAvailable` (it offered lattice-only/async-only nodes the other menus hide); `behaviourStep`/`divisionEvent`/`agentInit` are singleton-enforced like Step/Init (`SINGLETON_NODE_TYPES` covers add/connect/paste/quick-add — a duplicate root was silently dead); a cross-graph clipboard renders a DISABLED "Paste (from X graph)" item instead of a silent no-op; Seed Pattern (compact/scatter) + Bond Rest Length got Properties rows; agent views got a Description field (feeds the viewer-tab tooltip) + "+ Add Agent View" works with zero agent attrs (Standalone); the Variables panel no longer spuriously auto-selects on a Cells↔Agents swap and agent tag variables bind AGENT tag attributes; `neighborIndex` is hidden from the agent-attribute type dropdown; `Neighborhood3DEditor` remounts per selection (`key={selected.id}` — stale form state overwrote neighbourhood B with A's spec); a glyph setCellLooks in a 3D model gets a validation badge (glyphs aren't rendered by the voxel view).
- **Parity-harness discipline**: [scripts/parity-agent-wasm.mjs](scripts/parity-agent-wasm.mjs)'s `buildArgs` mirror was missing the 3 sprite args (every trailing arg shifted — `_field_*` landed undefined), masking real-looking failures. The agent-loop ABI now has THREE mirrors: `buildAgentLoopParams` (compile.ts) ↔ `buildAgentLoopArgs` (sim.worker.ts) ↔ the harness `buildArgs` — edit ALL THREE together.
- **Agent `sequence` emitters walked NONEXISTENT ports** (found via a user gravitation model): both agent compilers' `case 'sequence'` walked `then0`/`then1` keyed on a nonexistent `sequenceCount` — the real ports are **`first`/`then`/`then_2`…** keyed on `extraCount` — so ANY Sequence in an agent behaviour silently dropped its ENTIRE downstream chain on WASM AND WebGPU (JS was fine → "works on JS only"). Sneaky because the gate/reachability walk the EDGE MAP (prefix scan), so every node still gate-passed + compiled — only the emitter's flow walk missed. Fixed in both; the parity harness's synthetic model now routes its agent chain through a Sequence for permanent regression coverage. **When adding a flow construct to the agent compilers, copy the port ids from the NODE DEF / asyncWriteHazard's walk — never guess.** No shipped sample used an agent-graph Sequence, which is why 9/9 parity passed while user models broke — sample coverage ≠ catalogue coverage for FLOW shapes.
- **WebGPU-agent perf posture surfaced in the UI**: the Properties WebGPU agent radio hint now states the per-step CPU↔GPU upload/readback cost (agents + cell fields) — below ~10k agents, and especially for field models (Ant Necrophoresis / Chemotaxis), JS/WASM is usually FASTER; WebGPU wins only at very large populations / very heavy per-agent math. This is the documented benchmark reality, not a bug.
- **Agents-only world resize at scale (the 600×600×400 hang)** — an agents-only (Grid Cells OFF) 3D model froze on resize to large volumes and never concluded, on every target. FOUR compounding worker causes, all fixed in [sim.worker.ts](src/simulator/engine/sim.worker.ts):
  1. **The nbr-table reservation** — `computeMemoryLayout` reserved per-cell neighbour index tables (`total × nSz × 4` bytes; a Moore-3D nbh at 600×600×400 = 144M cells ≈ 15 GB, past the wasm32 4 GiB address space) even though `gridCellsEnabled === false` means `buildNeighborIndices` + the cell step never run. `initGrid` now passes `gridCellsEnabled ? neighborhoods : []` into the layout, so an agents-only world allocates only attrs/colors/scratch. Also wrapped `initGrid()` in the init handler with try/catch → a genuinely-too-big world posts a clear `Grid allocation failed for W×H×D…` error instead of a silent dead worker.
  2. **Static colours shipped every step** — with no colour pass, the (huge) unchanged `colors` buffer (144M cells × 4 B ≈ 576 MB/step) was copied + transferred on every `stepped`. New module flag `colorsDirty`: set by `runStep`, `writeDefaultColors`, a mapping fn actually running in `runColorPass`, the WebGPU colours readback, and the loadState restore; when `!gridCellsEnabled && !colorsDirty`, `sendColors` posts the stepped message WITHOUT `colors` (agents payload + indicators still ride). SimulatorView's stepped handler keeps the last buffer when `msg.colors === undefined`. Grid-ON models are untouched (the skip requires `!gridCellsEnabled`). The post-batch `runColorPass()` is also gated on `gridCellsEnabled` (2 sites) — the cell graph of an agents-only model still has an (empty) Step root, so `stepFn` exists and used to re-dirty the colours every batch.
  3. **`generation` never advanced** — the batch loops only incremented via `runStep`, so an agents-only model was stuck at gen 0 (end conditions, the transport display, and "is it even running?" all broken). All 3 batch loops (sync, webgpu-agents, webgpu-grid) now `generation++` when agents stepped but the cell step was skipped.
  4. **Lattice-target instantiation ran with a mismatched layout** — the lattice WASM module / WebGPU runtime bake nbr offsets the worker layout no longer reserves. `init` + `recompile` + `setUseWasm`/`setUseWebGPU` now gate lattice-target bring-up on `gridCellsEnabled` (agents-only runs the agent target only; the AGENT WASM/WebGPU targets are unaffected — their layout is separate).
  Verified live at 600×600×400 gridCells:false: JS agents gen 0→20 at **6.75 ms/step**, WASM agent target gen 0→20, 0 per-step colours ships, 0 errors (was: frozen forever); grid-ON regression checks — WASM GoL ships colours 5/5 steps gens 1..5, WebGPU GoL direct-render unchanged.
- **Agents-only per-cell layout eliminated entirely (round 2 — the 500³ / 5000×500×500 failure).** Even after the nbr-table skip, an agents-only world still reserved **9 bytes/cell of inert engine regions** — colors (4) + the always-reserved async orderArray (4) + the markCellUpdated skip flag (1) — so 5000×500×500 (1.25e9 cells ≈ 11.25 GB) threw `WebAssembly.Memory(): value 171662 is above the upper bound 65536`. (The error names WebAssembly on ALL targets because **`wasmMemory` is the single backing store every target's JS views sit on** — it's the container allocation, not the WASM compile target.) Fix: `computeMemoryLayout` ([wasm/layout.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/wasm/layout.ts)) gained a trailing `gridCells = true` param — when false, the colors / glyph / order / skipped regions are 0 bytes, the sync attr-WRITE region aliases the read region, and initGrid also drops the variegated orientation inputs; **per-cell memory for an agents-only world = its CELL ATTRIBUTES only** (kept — the agent field bridge reads/deposits through `readAttrs`; the shipped agent samples have zero cell attrs post-migration, so cost ≈ 0). Compile-side callers (`computeLayoutFromModel`) never pass the param → lattice layouts byte-identical. Worker guards: `writeDefaultColors`/`runStep`/`runColorPass` early-return when `!gridCellsEnabled` (mutation-handler tails could otherwise loop a huge `total`); the order/skipped views + `colorsDirty` are grid-gated; `sendColors` also skips on `colors.length === 0`; the allocation-failure message now explains the shared backing store + the 4 GiB cap + (grid-off) "per-cell storage is the cell attributes only". **SimulatorView renders agents WITHOUT a colors buffer**: the 3D draw no longer early-returns on `colorsRef === null` (voxel upload skipped, stale instances zeroed via `r.instanceCount = 0`), and the 2D draw's `!colors` early-return is waived for agent models (blit + glyph-fallback ImageData guarded by `colors.length >= w*h*4`). Verified live: 500³ AND **5000×500×500 (1.25 BILLION cells)** grid-off run gen 0→20, agents render (5 sphere instances, 0 voxels), 0 errors; grid-ON regressions clean (WASM GoL colours 5/5, async Amphiphile 5/5, Ant Necrophoresis grid+agents+field 5/5); parity harness 0 mismatches.

### Set Agent Sprite on the WASM agent target (branch `updates`)

`setAgentSprite` was the **single genuine node gap on both agent targets** — it wrote five
PLAIN JS arrays (`spriteIds`/`spriteFrames`/`spriteSpeeds`/`spriteRotations`/`spriteScales`,
the ONE field group C9 described as having "no baked byte on any target"), so it had no WASM
emit and a sprite-driving **Behaviour** graph clamped the whole model to JS. It now emits on
WASM; the generated capability matrix reads **`agentGapsWasm: 0`**.

- **The enabler is the memory, not the emitter.** `computeAgentMemoryLayout` gained a sprite
  block — 4 f64 runs + 1 i32 run, `maxAgents` each — **appended after EVERY existing region**
  and reserved **only when the C9 `sprites` gate is on**. So a sprite-free model's layout is
  byte-identical, and a model that DOES carry sprites shifts no offset already baked into a
  module. `createAgentStore` returns VIEWS over those bytes when `wasmBacked`, plain arrays
  otherwise — which is what makes the WASM write and the JS `advanceAgentSprites` advance the
  same state. `AgentMemoryLayout.spritesReserved` is the emitter's C9 SAFETY CATCH (the shape
  of `layout.f64[name] === undefined`): gate off ⇒ every sprite facet is dropped, while the
  ALPHA facet survives because it writes `colors`, which is always allocated.
- **`env.atan2` is a CONDITIONAL import** (`AGENT_ATAN2_FUNC_IDX = NUM_IMPORTED_FUNCS + 3`),
  added ONLY when a reachable Set Agent Sprite uses the VECTOR rotation mode — the one facet
  needing an inverse tangent, which WASM has no opcode for. **Adding an import shifts the
  module's own function indices**, so making it conditional (and appending it LAST) is what
  keeps every model that does not use it byte-identical — the same conditional-arity
  discipline as `forcePassParamsFor(chargeOn)`. `usesAtan2` is scanned BEFORE emit, exactly
  like `viewerGuardIds`. The host object supplies `atan2` unconditionally (free — WebAssembly
  only looks up imports the module DECLARES).
- **Facet-for-facet mirror of the JS node**, including the two subtleties: an unwired `Agent`
  targets the current-loop agent UNGUARDED (it is live by construction) while a wired one takes
  the range-only guard the other by-id setters use; and the alpha byte is CLAMPED to [0,255]
  before `i32.store8`, because `store8` truncates where the JS `Uint8ClampedArray` clamps.
- **WebGPU clamped at the time, deliberately** — the sprite buffers had no GPU-side mirror,
  and adding one meant new runs + a per-generation round-trip for a pure DISPLAY layer. That
  clamp is **GONE**: see “Set Agent Sprite on the WebGPU agent target” below.
- **Gates**: `check-compile-identity` 29 models byte-identical; a permanent
  `[synthetic] Set Agent Sprite (all facets, self + by-id, vector rotation)` entry in
  [parity-agent-wasm.mjs](scripts/parity-agent-wasm.mjs) with a **VALUE invariant** that
  recomputes the expected state independently (parity alone would pass if BOTH targets wrote
  nothing) — negative-controlled twice by source mutation (a doubled scale write, and forcing
  the layout gate off); the harness's store comparison gained the five sprite arrays;
  `gen-capability-docs --check` regenerated. **Verified in the real UI**: the user's sprite
  boids model's chip flips `agents JS` → `agents WASM`, the bird sprites still render (30
  distinct colours in a 147-px blob — a textured sprite, not a flat disc) and animate, and an
  interleaved A/B shows WASM neutral-to-marginally-faster (2.69/2.71 vs 2.72/2.74 ms/frame at
  100 agents — as documented, the WASM win needs a heavy per-agent rule or a large population).

### Set Agent Sprite on the WebGPU agent target (branch `updates`)

The LAST agent-target node gap. `setAgentSprite` emitted on JS and WASM but not on the GPU
(no sprite mirror there), so a **behaviour-reachable** Set Agent Sprite clamped a
WebGPU-target model to JS — the C1 readout literally said *"the agent graph uses a node the
WebGPU agent shader does not emit (setAgentSprite)"*. It now emits; the generated capability
matrix reads **`agentGapsWebgpu: 0`** and the reject set is the documented fundamentals only.
**There was never a fundamental incompatibility** — sprite state is per-agent, own-slot (or
spawn-handle / range-guarded by-id) writes, exactly the parallel-safe shape every other agent
setter has. It was an effort-scope decision, and this closes it.

- **Five `agentF32` RUNS, no new binding** (`AGENT_GPU_SPRITE_FIELDS` in
  [agentWebgpu/layout.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/agentWebgpu/layout.ts)): `spriteIds` /
