  `spriteFrames` / `spriteSpeeds` / `spriteRotations` / `spriteScales`, one run each, **APPENDED
  AFTER every existing run** (including the P3 bond-form request runs) and reserved **only when
  the C9 `sprites` gate is on**. Appending last is what keeps a sprite-free model's bases — and
  therefore its emitted shader — byte-identical; riding `agentF32` is what keeps the Naga
  stripped-binding discipline out of it entirely. `AgentWebGPULayout.spritesReserved` is the
  emitter's C9 SAFETY CATCH (the mirror of the WASM layout's flag): gate off ⇒ every sprite
  facet is dropped, while the ALPHA facet survives because it writes `agentColors`, always
  allocated. **This also wires `agentFieldGating.ts` site 3**, which that file's header had
  claimed (`AgentWebGPUExtras.fieldGates`) but nothing implemented, because the group had no GPU
  run at all. `AgentWebGPUExtras.sprites` defaults to **OFF** when absent — deliberately
  inverting `normalizeFieldGates`' absent⇒on convention, because every other optional block in
  that file is absent⇒off and the two callers that pass no extras (SimulatorView's minimal
  render-only layout, the worker's fallback) compile no shader.
- **f32, and that is honest for this group.** `spriteIds` is a slot INDEX (exact in f32 far past
  any plausible sprite count, rounded on readback) and the other four are DISPLAY quantities the
  renderer already consumes as f32 — a frame counter, compass degrees, a size multiplier. Same
  statistical-parity stance as the rest of the WebGPU agent SoA.
- **THE CPU STAYS AUTHORITATIVE BETWEEN GENERATIONS, so the round-trip is a PAIR.**
  `advanceAgentSprites` ticks `frame += speed` once per generation, `initAgentSlot` clears a
  recycled slot and `divideAgent` hands a daughter its mother's sprite — all CPU. So
  `uploadAgentSoA` **SEEDS** the five runs from the store and `readbackAgentStep` /
  `readbackAgentFrame` copy them back. **Both halves are mandatory together**: the shader writes
  only the TICKED facets, so an un-seeded run would be read back as 0 and clobber the CPU value
  (a `spriteId` of 0 means "no sprite" ⇒ the agents silently render as plain discs). ONE
  predicate — **`spriteRunsActive(rt)`** = `rt.usesSpriteWrite && layout.spritesReserved` —
  gates the plan, the fill, the writeBuffer, both readbacks and the spawn-reconcile overlay, so
  they cannot drift; `buildF32ReadPlan` adds the runs under that SAME predicate, keeping the
  "the plan covers exactly what crosses the bus" invariant `compactBase` throws for.
- **`usesSpriteWrite` is set by a SPRITE-RUN write only, never by the ALPHA facet alone** (alpha
  writes `agentColors`, which every path already round-trips) — so an alpha-only node costs no
  extra traffic and does not block residency.
- **THE SPAWN RECONCILE OVERLAYS SPRITE STATE.** A newborn goes through `initAgentSlot`, which
  CLEARS sprites — so a Set Agent Sprite on a Create Agent handle would be lost. The reconcile
  now copies the five GPU values for `[hw, cursor)` exactly as it already does for the agent
  attributes and `targetRadius`.
- **RESIDENCY IS BLOCKED, narrowly and by DESIGN** (`residencyModelBlockers` key `sprites`,
  mirrored model-side in `residencyFactsFromModel`). A resident batch encodes N generations into
  ONE submit with NO CPU touch point, so the per-generation `advanceAgentSprites` tick could not
  interleave with the shader's writes. The term is `usesSpriteWrite`, **not "the model has
  sprites"**: a model whose sprite state is set in an Agent Output Mapping (or not at all) keeps
  residency exactly as before. Advancing frames GPU-side in `posCommit` was considered and NOT
  taken: sprite models are draw-bound and can never take the GPU direct-render path anyway (see
  the section below), so the win would be nil.
- **DELIBERATELY NOT EMITTED IN AN AGENT OUTPUT MAPPING MODULE** (`agentSubsetSupported`'s new
  `scope: 'behaviour' | 'om'` param). An OM module is dispatched ONLY inside
  `dispatchResidentBatch`, while every other path colours agents through the CPU
  `runAgentColorPass` — and the sprite round-trip is keyed on the BEHAVIOUR flag, so an OM-only
  write would simply be lost. Rejecting it keeps today's OM semantics EXACTLY (an OM with a
  sprite node ⇒ `omSupported: false` ⇒ the CPU overlay, where the node has always worked) and
  costs nothing user-visible: an OM-only usage never clamped the agent TARGET in the first place.
- **Gates**: `check-compile-identity` — **29 models, and the ONLY diff is `Boids - Flocking`'s
  `agent.webgpu.shader` / `agent.webgpu.error`** (empty + "unsupported node 'setAgentSprite'" →
  a real shader), i.e. the single shipped model that carries a sprite; every other model is
  byte-identical on every surface. A new
  [scripts/test-agent-sprite-webgpu.mjs](scripts/test-agent-sprite-webgpu.mjs) (50 checks, seven
  tiers: layout / gate / emit / C9 catch / OM scope / residency / runtime source invariants),
  **negative-controlled three ways by source mutation** — dropping the OM reject, dropping the
  sprite `writeBuffer` (caught by the 6-site count), and reserving the runs unconditionally.
  `gen-capability-docs --check` regenerated. `test-engine-resolve`'s WASM-accepts/WebGPU-refuses
  asymmetry case was built on this very node, so it is rebuilt on the CONTRACT (Statistical ⇒
  WebGPU, Exact ⇒ WASM) — that took the suite from 7 failures to 1, the remainder being the
  PRE-EXISTING `Boids - Flocking` contract-re-inference case (the shipped file carries
  `reproducibility: 'statistical'` with an explicit `agentTarget: 'wasm'`) plus the pre-existing
  SKIP of the deleted `Cubic GRA.gcaproj`. **BOTH are since resolved** (2026-08-05): the
  re-inference check was the HARNESS over-asserting — a declared contract may legitimately
  differ from the inference when the engine is pinned explicitly (C5 makes that a note, never
  an error), so the strip case now asserts against `inferContract` and the declared value is
  what the round-trip preserves; and the Cubic GRA cases were retired rather than skipped.
- **Verified on the REAL GPU** (in-browser; the pane is occluded, so pixel evidence comes from
  `getImageData` rather than a screenshot): the reporter's sprite boids model on
  `agentTarget: 'webgpu'` flips the C1 readout from `✗ WebGPU — … does not emit
  (setAgentSprite)` to **`✓ WebGPU  running`**, the chip reads `agents WebGPU`,
  `getDiagnostics` reports `agentEngineActive: 'webgpu'` with **`fallbackEvents: []`** (no
  silent demotion) and `residency.eligible: false` with the sprite blocker as its first reason.
  Sprite ids reach all 100 agents (`spriteIds = 1`) and **frames ADVANCE every generation**
  (0.005 → 1.706 over 13 generations; **608 generations with 0 worker and 0 console errors**,
  frames finite at ~153–158). Cross-target: the same model on WASM reaches 1.73 vs the GPU's
  1.71 at generation 13 — statistically equivalent, as documented. Pixels: a single agent's
  blob is a 20×20-px region with **90 distinct colours** (993 distinct over 27.5 k lit pixels
  for the whole flock) — textured sprite art, not a flat disc. **All facets on the real device**:
  a synthetic probe wiring `dirX = handle - 3`, `dirY = 2` produced rotations matching the
  hand-computed `atan2(id-3, -2)·180/π` **exactly on all 8 agents (max error 0)** and
  identically on WASM; the alpha facet round-tripped 200; and a **by-handle spawn** wrote the
  newborn's `spriteId 1` / rotation 135° / scale 3.5 through the reconcile overlay. Regressions:
  **Particle Life** (non-sprite, WebGPU) still reports `residency eligible + engaged` with
  `directRender: agents`, and the shipped **Boids - Flocking** on WASM still runs 260 agents with
  sprites (2271 distinct colours) and 0 errors.

#### Sprite models are DRAW-bound, and Glow is now a real cost on them
Measured on a 100-agent sprite boids model at FPS ∞ / G/F 1 (1900×1000 pane, 100 Hz display):
the whole frame is **~2.2 ms**, essentially all of it main-thread DRAW — the agent step for
100 boids is noise. So switching the agent engine moves this class of model very little; what
moves it is the overlay. Two consequences worth remembering:
- **A sprite model can never take the GPU direct-render path** (`agentRenderModelTermsOk`
  excludes sprites), so it always pays the CPU overlay + the per-frame snapshot.
- **Glow went from INERT to ~+21% per frame on this class of model.** Before the CPU-overlay
  glow pass (`drawAgentGlow`), ticking Glow on a sprite/CPU-overlay model did nothing at all
  (the checkbox even read "Glow (WebGPU direct render)"). Measured on the same model:
  master **2.164 → 2.220 ms** with Glow on (inert, noise), current **2.227 → 2.699 ms**
  (+0.47 ms). That is the feature working as intended, but note the trap: **`agentGlow` is a
  PERSISTED per-user setting (`genesisca_sim_settings`), not a model property**, so a user who
  enabled Glow while trying it on another model silently carries that cost into every agent
  model afterwards. It is the first thing to check when an agent model feels slower than a
  build that predates the CPU glow pass.

### Agent Stop Event (all 3 agent targets — branch `absorb_old_automatosgt`)
A **Stop Event** node in the agent BEHAVIOUR graph now pauses the simulation on every agent target (JS + WASM + WebGPU); it was a JS-only carve-out. The `_stopIdx` (1-based, offset by the cell stop count via `stopIdxBase`) is baked by the JS `compileAgentGraph` (runs first in SimulatorView) on the original nodes — `expandMacros` passes top-level nodes by reference, so the WASM/WebGPU agent compilers read the same baked config (exactly like the cell grid).
- **JS**: unchanged — the behaviour writes the shared `_stopFlag[0]` via the ABI's `_stopFlag` param.
- **WASM**: `computeAgentMemoryLayout` ([agentEngine.ts](src/simulator/engine/agentEngine.ts)) **appends** a 4-byte `stopFlagOffset` cell (always reserved → existing offsets byte-stable, verified: parity + gate + ABI audit unchanged). `stopEvent` ∈ `AGENT_WASM_SUPPORTED_TYPES` with an emitter mirroring the cell WASM (`if i32.load(stopFlagOffset)==0 { i32.store(stopFlagOffset, stopIdx) }`).
- **WebGPU**: a dedicated `stopFlag` atomic<u32> storage buffer (**binding 13**, gated on the `usesStop` flag like `usesSpawn`/binding 12), `atomicCompareExchangeWeak(&stopFlag, 0u, stopIdxU)` in the shader; `resetAgentStopFlag` seeds it to 0 before each dispatch, `readbackAgentStep` returns it, `runAgentStepWebGPU` merges it into `stopFlag[0]`.
- **The ordering fix (also fixes a pre-existing JS-agent bug)**: the agent step runs BEFORE the cell step in every batch loop, and `runStep`/`runStepWebGPU` reset the shared `stopFlag` at their top (finalizeStepWebGPU even OVERWRITES it from the GPU) — which clobbered an agent stop in a grid+agents model. New `drainAgentStop()` ([sim.worker.ts](src/simulator/engine/sim.worker.ts)) reads the agent stop source (JS/WebGPU → `stopFlag[0]`; WASM → the memory cell) + clears both; each batch loop **captures** it before the cell step and **surfaces** it after `generation++` (so the paused generation matches the cell-stop semantics). Gated on `agentStore && simulateAgents` → cell-only models are byte-identical.
- **Verified** (real worker, all 3 targets): an agents-only `behaviourStep → stopEvent` fires "AGENT STOP FIRED" at gen 1 on JS / WASM (gate accepts, module emits it) / WebGPU (real-GPU shader compiles + the atomic + readback merge, 0 errors); a **cell-only** stopEvent still fires (unregressed); a **grid+agents** agent stop fires (the clobber fix). tsc + build + parity (11 samples) + WASM gate + ABI audit all green.

### Cross-Agent Write Semantics (branch `sim_agent_fixes`) — sync-overwrite gate + Apply Force To Agent
The agent form of the CA grid's **Fundamental #4 (Writability)**, plus the commutative force sibling it enables. **The throughline: OVERWRITE writes race across agents; ACCUMULATE writes don't** — so the two get opposite rules. Plan + Impact Map + mockup: [docs/PLAN_CROSS_AGENT_WRITES.md](docs/PLAN_CROSS_AGENT_WRITES.md) / [IMPACT_MAP_CROSS_AGENT_WRITES.md](docs/IMPACT_MAP_CROSS_AGENT_WRITES.md) / `.html`. All additive/gated — lattice + every non-touched agent model byte-identical (JS↔WASM parity re-verified on all samples).
- **Part A — cross-agent OVERWRITE writes are async-only.** `setAgentAttribute` / `setAgentsAttribute` / `setAgentPosition` / `setAgentRadius` write ANOTHER agent's slot; in **sync** agent mode (double-buffered attrs) that collides with the target's own self-update (lost update, order-dependent, a genuine data race on parallel targets). A single **compile-time gate** in `compileAgentGraph` ([compile.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/compile.ts), right after `buildAdjacency`) rejects them when `centerBased.agentUpdateMode === 'sync'` AND the node is reachable from the **behaviour** root (a BFS over `flowOutputToTargets` — init/division roots are sequential one-time / structural-phase, never the parallel self-update loop, so NOT gated) AND the target isn't a one-hop **`createAgent` handle** (spawn configuration: the staged newborn isn't concurrently written — the exemption that keeps unified spawning working in sync mode). The JS compile always runs first in SimulatorView, so its error short-circuits ALL targets (no per-target copy needed). **In ASYNC mode the cross-agent overwrites are legal but SEQUENTIAL-order-dependent, which the parallel GPU cannot honour** — so `isAgentGraphWebGPUSupported` ([agentWebgpu/compile.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/agentWebgpu/compile.ts)) rejects any behaviour-reachable member of the same 4-type set whose id input is WIRED to a non-`createAgent` source (unwired = `-1` = guarded no-op; a spawn handle is thread-owned — both race-free): such a model clamps to JS/WASM, where the sequential agent loop gives a well-defined write order. This closed a real hole — before this gate an async cross-agent-overwrite model silently EMITTED on WebGPU with racy last-writer-wins visibility. (NB the earlier "WebGPU is sync-only" phrasing here was WRONG — the WebGPU agent target runs `agentUpdateMode:'async'` models fine [Tissue is async]. The follow-on claim that on the GPU "the mode only governs CPU-side buffering + residency eligibility, since a parallel dispatch always gives snapshot-reads + thread-own-writes regardless" was ALSO wrong, and is what PX fixed: thread-own-writes is only snapshot semantics for an agent's OWN slot — reading a NEIGHBOUR's attribute out of the same run someone else is writing is a race. Sync now allocates a distinct write run + commits it per generation; see the PX section.) `setVelocity` is self-only (no id input) → untouched.
- **Part B — `applyForceToAgent`** ([ApplyForceToAgentNode.ts](src/modeler/vpl/nodes/ApplyForceToAgentNode.ts)): add a force vector to another agent by id (`force[target] += f`), the cross-agent counterpart to Apply Force. **Commutative** (`+=` onto the per-step-zeroed force buffer the integrator consumes AFTER the whole behaviour pass) → **race-free in BOTH sync and async** (order doesn't matter for a sum; no collision with the target's own Apply Force). Newton's 3rd law, custom pairwise / Coulomb laws, action-at-a-distance. Ports mirror Apply Force (`fx/fy/fz`, `fz` 3D-only) + an `agentId`; range+alive guarded (live-agent guard in behaviour/division, `_agentMaxAgents` range-only in init); `AGENT_NODE_REQUIREMENT` → `motion: 'force'`. **(Note the corrected Apply Force semantics: it ACCUMULATES `+=` onto a buffer zeroed each step — `s.forceX.fill(0,0,hw)` — then the fused pass seeds from it and the engine adds its own soft-sphere/springs on top; a single call ≈ "set from 0", N calls sum. Not "set the force".)**
- **All three targets** (the ALL-TARGET rule — no JS-only clamp): **JS/WASM** — a plain guarded `+=` (the behaviour loop is SEQUENTIAL, no atomics; WASM `forceAddAt` = the arbitrary-target sibling of `forceAdd`, in `AGENT_WASM_SUPPORTED_TYPES`). **WebGPU** — the parallel scatter CONTENDS (many threads add to the same target → lost-update race on the read-modify-write), so it goes through an **f32-bitcast atomic-CAS** (`forceScatterAdd`, the EXACT `fieldDepositCell` pattern) into a dedicated `forceScatter : array<atomic<u32>>` buffer (**binding 14**, gated on the new `usesForceScatter` flag like `usesSpawn`/`usesStop`), X/Y[/Z] regions strided by `maxAgents`; the runtime `clearBuffer`s it each step ([agentWebgpuRuntime.ts](src/simulator/engine/agentWebgpuRuntime.ts)), and the **force pass** reads its own slot (no contention → plain `bitcast<f32>(forceScatter[i])`, **binding 4**, gated) and folds it into the self-force seed. Self Apply Force stays a plain non-atomic write (each thread owns its slot). `usesForceScatter` threads compile-result → SimulatorView (`emitAgentForcePassWGSL(layout, usesForceScatter)`) → init/recompile msg → `createAgentWebGPURuntime` usage — same plumbing as `usesSpawn`. A no-scatter (Boids) shader is byte-identical (no binding 14/4, no helper).
- **Array broadcast — `applyForceToAgents`** ([ApplyForceToAgentsNode.ts](src/modeler/vpl/nodes/ApplyForceToAgentsNode.ts)): add the SAME force to EVERY agent in an id array (feed Get Nearby / Bonded / Filter Agents). **Pure editor sugar with ZERO new per-target emit** — a shared pre-compile transform **`expandForceToAgents`** ([forceToAgentsExpand.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/forceToAgentsExpand.ts)) lowers it to **`For Each In Array → applyForceToAgent`** (the sanctioned "lower to primitives" pattern — `expandComposites`/`expandMultiAttrs`/`lowerVectorAttrs`), so it reuses the single node's JS/WASM/WebGPU emitters ENTIRELY. Wired into all three agent front-ends right after `collapseReroutes` (JS `compileAgentGraph` + both `flattenAgentGraph`s), so the agent-target GATE inspects the flattened graph (`forEachInArray` + `applyForceToAgent`, both supported) — `applyForceToAgents` needs NO supported-types entry. Bit-parity inherited from the two verified primitives; semantically identical to the hand-built For-Each pattern. Hot-path no-op when unused.
- **Verified**: tsc + `npm run build` clean; Part A gate (real compiler — sync→error, async→compiles, `createAgent`-handle→exempt); Part B **JS↔WASM bit-parity** ([scripts/parity-agent-wasm.mjs](scripts/parity-agent-wasm.mjs) `buildApplyForceToAgentModel` pairwise scatter + `buildApplyForceToAgentsModel` array broadcast, 30 steps, 0 mismatches) + WGSL generation + the lowering ([scripts/test-cross-agent-writes.mjs](scripts/test-cross-agent-writes.mjs), Parts A/B/C, 2D+3D); **real-GPU** (in-browser) — both behaviour + force shaders `createShaderModule` with **0 errors** (2D+3D, single node AND the array node's scatter-CAS-inside-forEach), the runtime BUILDS (bind groups match pipeline layouts) and a real `dispatchAgentStep` runs with **0 validation errors**. Catalogue → **143 selectable / 47 agent**.

### Agent action TARGETING — optional id, default self (branch `polishing`)

User report: *"We have no way to 'kill' an agent from its id now? not even the 'self'?? … only
the 'kill agent' that destroys the current evaluated agent? that is very limiting … it should
all be consistent in providing either an id or assuming self, unless there is a strong
technical reason not to."* Plus the same for Set Velocity, *"following the example of the node
'Get Velocity' that the user can provide an agent or leave empty for the 'self'."*

**THE CONVENTION, now uniform: an agent action either takes an OPTIONAL `Agent` id whose
UNWIRED state means SELF, or has a by-ID sibling node.** The id port is always
`{ id: 'agentId', label: 'Agent', dataType: 'integer' }` — literally Get Velocity's port, so
the read and write halves of every pair look the same.

**THE BYTE-IDENTITY DISCIPLINE (inherited from Form Bond's `agentA`, and non-negotiable):
wiredness is read from the EDGE MAP and resolved BEFORE anything is minted** — `em.allocLocal`
changes the WASM module bytes even for an *unused* local, and `fresh()` shifts every later WGSL
name. Unwired therefore emits the historical statement byte-for-byte on all three targets
(`check-compile-identity`: 29 models, every surface unchanged).

#### The three nodes that gained the optional id
| node | unwired | wired | gated? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Kill Agent** | `_killRequest[idx] = 1` | `_killRequest[target] = 1` — PREDATION ("consume" a neighbour) | **NO** — see below |
| **Set Velocity** | `_agentVX/VY[idx] = …` | writes that agent's velocity (knock-back) | **YES** — cross-agent OVERWRITE |
| **Set Target Radius** | `_agentTargetRadius[idx] = …` | makes ANOTHER agent grow/shrink | **YES** — cross-agent OVERWRITE |

**WHY A WIRED KILL NEEDS NO GATE — the commutativity argument, and it is the load-bearing
reasoning here.** A kill is a **flag set to a CONSTANT** (`killRequest[t] = 1`) consumed once by
the CPU structural phase at the end of the step. Setting the same value is **IDEMPOTENT and
ORDER-INDEPENDENT**: N agents all electing to eat the same target produce the identical result
in any order, and it cannot collide with that target's own self-update (nothing ever writes the
flag back to 0). That is exactly the argument that exempts **Apply Force To Agent**'s
commutative `+=`. So `killAgent` is deliberately **NOT** in `CROSS_AGENT_OVERWRITE`
(compile.ts' synchronous-mode gate) and **NOT** in the WebGPU agent gate's wired-non-spawn
reject set — verified, not assumed: a kill-only model's `isAgentGraphWebGPUSupported` returns
**true** and it runs natively on the GPU. On WebGPU the store is a plain **non-atomic** write of
`1.0` into another slot's `killRequest` run — a benign race, because every racing writer writes
the identical value — and `readbackAgentStep` already rounds it (`>= 0.5 ? 1 : 0`).
**Set Velocity / Set Target Radius are the opposite**: last-writer-wins overwrites, so they join
the same machinery as Set Agent Attribute / Position / Radius (the set is now **six** types in
both gates). For an order-independent way to influence another agent's motion, Apply Force To
Agent works in both modes on every target.

**Guards** mirror the by-id setters exactly: range-only (`< _agentMaxAgents`, WASM's shared
`emitGuardedAgentWrite`, WGSL's `< i32(control.maxAgents)`) in the init/behaviour roots — the
unified-spawning relaxation that lets a staged Create Agent handle be configured — and
range+alive elsewhere. For the kill, range-only is *provably equivalent* to range+alive because
the structural phase separately gates on `alive[i]`, and a recycled slot is cleared by
`initAgentSlot`.

**⚠ THE INIT-ABI ASYMMETRY THIS EXPOSED (a real trap):** `deriveAgentAbi`'s **init** kind carries
`_agentZ` but **NOT `_agentVZ`**, and `_killRequest` is **loop-only**. So a wired Set Velocity in
the Agent Init Event (a legitimate "seed a newborn's velocity on its handle" use) would have
emitted an undefined `_agentVZ` in 3D — it now **drops the z half in the init root** (the C9
"no param ⇒ no write" safety-catch shape) rather than widening the ABI. Kill Agent stays
unconditionally init-invalid either way. `nodeValidation`'s `AGENT_SELF_ONLY_WHEN_UNWIRED`
makes that badge WIRING-aware for the two conditional nodes.

#### THE AUDIT — every agent action node's targeting (the sweep behind the convention)
| node | targeting | why |
|---|---|---|
| Apply Force / **Apply Force To Agent** / Apply Force To Agents | self / **by id** / array | complete trio already |
| Set Attribute (Self) / **Set Agent Attribute** / Set Agents Attribute | self / **by id** / array | complete trio; the by-id half is *named* "(by ID)" and its unwired `-1` no-op is load-bearing for the spawn idiom |
| **Set Agent Position** / **Set Agent Radius** | by id (required) | by-ID half of a documented pair; `Get Self Handle` is one wire away, and their unwired no-op is the spawn-handle idiom. **Left required deliberately** — defaulting them to self would silently retarget existing graphs |
| **Kill Agent** | **optional id ⇒ self** | ✅ this change — had NO by-id sibling |
| **Set Velocity** | **optional id ⇒ self** | ✅ this change — had NO by-id sibling |
| **Set Target Radius** | **optional id ⇒ self** | ✅ this change — Set Agent Radius sets the CURRENT radius, so the GROWTH TARGET was unreachable for any other agent |
| Set Agent Sprite | optional id ⇒ self | already the convention |
| Form Bond | optional `agentA` ⇒ self + `targetAgent` | already (lowers to the Form Between encoding when wired) |
| Form Bond (paired) / Transfer Bond | two / three explicit ids | inherently multi-party |
| **Break Bond** / Set Bond Attribute / Rewire Bond | self-anchored pair | **the one real remaining gap** — see the follow-up below |
| Divide Agent | self only | dividing another agent by id would need the Division Event (which runs per-DAUGHTER of the divider) to answer "whose event is this?", plus a partition spec chosen by an agent that is not the mother. A semantic redesign, not a port |
| Add Agent To World / Create Agent | by handle | a handle IS the target; "self" is meaningless |
| affectCellsUnder / secreteToField / sampleField / fieldGradient / readCellsUnder | self position | the node's identity is "the cells **under this agent**"; a by-id variant is a plausible future node, not a port on these |
| moveSelfToNeighbor etc. | — | lattice nodes, out of scope |

#### FOLLOW-UP (recorded, deliberately NOT half-shipped): `Break Bond Between (a, b)`
Break Bond is self-anchored (`self ↔ targetAgent`), so a third party cannot cut an edge it is
not part of. The encoding is already reserved: per the [bondRequestQueue.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/bondRequestQueue.ts)
lane table, Form Between negates the BREAK lane and Transfer negates the FORM lane, leaving
**both lanes negative** as the one free combination. Sketch: `bl = −(a+2)`, `fl = −(b+2)`;
decode it in `drainAgentBondRequests` **before** the two existing sign branches; whole-op
pre-check (`a↔b` must exist, both live/in range) so **I5** holds; emit on all three targets
through the shared `emitBondRequest`. It is compiler + engine + drain work touching the
invariant harness, so it wants its own pass rather than a rushed rider on this one.

- **Verified.** Byte-identity **29/29, every surface**. Harnesses: `parity-agent-wasm`
  (JS↔WASM bit-parity, all samples + a new permanent `[synthetic] By-id targeting` entry),
  `verify-graph-rewrite` **533**, `test-agent-abi` **607**, `test-c9-gates` **413**,
  `audit-agent-layout`, `test-cross-agent-writes`, `parity-agent-force` **43**,
  `check-agent-wasm-gate`, `gen-capability-docs --check`. The new synthetic splits the
  population into hunters + prey + BYSTANDERS and recomputes every expected number from the
  agent's HANDLE, so a by-id write that spills onto an untargeted slot is caught;
  **negative-controlled both ways** — WASM-only dropping the kill guard fails PARITY
  (`killRequest[0] js=0 wasm=1`), while making BOTH targets write self (which parity cannot
  see) fails the VALUE INVARIANT.
- **Real UI** (a "Consume" model: each agent knocks back every neighbour within r=3 and eats the
  one within 1.6, with a `self < other` tie-break): from ONE pinned seed **JS and WASM produce
  the IDENTICAL series 400 → 248 → 245 → 244 → 244** with 240 agents carrying the by-id
  knock-back velocity (read via `readAgents` — the render snapshot's `vx` is a length-0 array
  unless velocity is REQUESTED, the documented trap); the same model on the WebGPU agent target
  correctly **clamps to JS** (`isAgentGraphWebGPUSupported` false, chip `⚙ agents JS⚠`) with
  identical results; a **kill-only** variant runs **natively on the real GPU** (chip
  `⚙ agents WebGPU`, no fallback, 400 → 248) — the commutativity claim, demonstrated; and the
  same model in SYNCHRONOUS agent mode produces the named compile-gate error. 0 console errors.

### Agent-engine performance review round (branch `optimize`, 2026-07-22)
A measured, phase-profiled review of "Particle Life struggles before 50k" — full findings + prioritized fix list in **[docs/PERF_REVIEW_AGENT_ENGINE.md](docs/PERF_REVIEW_AGENT_ENGINE.md)**. **The FOLLOW-ON project (GPU-resident agent RENDER + residency widening, phases A1→F) is planned and session-orchestrated via [docs/HANDOFF_GPU_AGENT_RENDER.md](docs/HANDOFF_GPU_AGENT_RENDER.md)** (master runbook: invariants, phase sequence, per-phase handoffs, status board) — new sessions execute one phase each; read the master's §0/§3 before touching this area. What SHIPPED in the round:
- **Resize → agent-compiler dims desync FIXED** (the `[agents] spatial hash (N bins) exceeds the WebGPU reserve (M)` error after a simulator Resize): `compileAgentModel` now takes the SAME dims-overridden **`dimsModel`** the grid compilers get (both call sites — init + soft recompile). Before, the agent WASM/WebGPU layouts baked the MODEL dims while the worker ran LIVE dims: WebGPU → permanent silent per-step JS demotion after any resize-to-larger; WASM → a store↔module offset desync of every region after the hash reserve (nearby-scratch/model-attrs/**lookup-tables**/fields — silent wrong-offset reads, the baked-offset corruption class). Defence-in-depth: the init/recompile messages ship **`agentWasmLayoutSig`** (`{maxHashBins, totalBytes}` of the compiled layout) and `instantiateAgentWasmIfNeeded` REFUSES to instantiate on a mismatch (loud error + safe JS-on-views fallback). Browser-verified: WASM + WebGPU targets at 600×600 run clean post-resize.
- **WebGPU agent scratch arrays capped** (`AGENT_GPU_ARRAY_CAP = 2048` in [agentWebgpu/compile.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/agentWebgpu/compile.ts)): the per-thread `var<function>` array-producer slots were sized at **maxAgents** — WGSL zero-inits function-address-space vars, so 50k maxAgents = 200 KB of private memory zeroed PER THREAD per dispatch (measured 415 ms/gen on a Pascal → 190 ms with the cap). Slots are now `min(maxAgents, 2048)` (+ fill guards in nearby/join); maxAgents ≤ 2048 models emit byte-identical shaders; a >2048-member query TRUNCATES (documented GPU capacity bound). **Never size a per-thread WGSL array by maxAgents.**
- **[scripts/bench-agent-engine.mjs](scripts/bench-agent-engine.mjs)** — the per-phase agent-engine profiler (real `.gcaproj` + real instantiated WASM; phases: hash/behaviour/force/snapshot/clone at N ∈ {2k,10k,50k} at shipped + user densities; `MODEL=` env override). THE measurement tool for agent perf work — rerun it after any engine change.
- **Measured truths to keep in mind**: the per-pair physics is >99% of an agent generation (hash/snapshot/args are noise) — cost ∝ N × density × queryRadius², so the pair count (not the compile target) is the lever; WASM ≈ 1.1× JS on gather-heavy workloads. (The Help tab's Bond-Graph Agents § Performance now carries the user-facing version of this guidance.)
- **The "WebGPU wrong dynamics" bug — RESOLVED (async step-batch re-entrancy, commit 8173f25).** Boids plateaued at ~0.03–0.45 polarization on the WebGPU agent target with zero errors; an exhaustive primitive-probe session found nothing because **the GPU physics was correct all along** — the state-roundtrip experiment (loadState the SAME agent state into both targets) showed a single GPU step matches JS to 1.4e-5 (pure f32) and strictly-SEQUENTIAL batches flock 0.378→0.998. The corruption trigger was **queuing multiple `step` messages at once**: the async WebGPU batch loops yield to onmessage at every `await`, so a queued `step` started a CONCURRENT batch interleaved with the running one (stale CPU uploads racing fresh GPU results). The sync JS/WASM loop can't be interleaved — which is why only the GPU paths broke. **Fix** ([sim.worker.ts](src/simulator/engine/sim.worker.ts)): while an async step batch is in flight the worker **defers EVERY incoming message** and replays them in order when the batch settles (`asyncStepBatchInFlight` + `deferredDuringAsyncBatch` + `endAsyncStepBatch`), restoring the synchronous path's semantics; plus permanent GPU diagnostics (`device.onuncapturederror`, `device.lost`, `pushErrorScope('validation')` around the dispatch). **Any future async worker batch loop must set/clear this flag.** Verified: the previously-failing overlapped-burst pattern flocks 0.223→0.998 on the GPU.
- **Density-scan skip (commit 50e6f96, all 3 targets)**: the fused force pass ran its full neighbour scan UNCONDITIONALLY just to count `density`, even when engine physics is off and nothing reads it — ~70% of the behaviour's cost wasted on custom-force models. Now compile-side **`agentUsesDensity`** (a macro-aware scan for `neighbourDensity`/`divideAgent` in [SimulatorView.tsx](src/simulator/SimulatorView.tsx), shipped in init/recompile) gates the scan: `doScan = engineForces || usesDensity` in the JS force loop (both 2D+3D arms), a **`doDensity`** WASM forcePass param (index 25 — the ABI is now 26 params; [agentWasm/compile.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/agentWasm/compile.ts) wraps the scan in an `ifThen` on `bonding|doCollision|doDensity`), and a WGSL `ForceControl.doDensity` field (u[24], `FORCE_CONTROL_BYTES` 96→112). Measured: 50k@600² force 449→**2.8 ms**, total 1123/994→**589/544 ms/gen** (~1.9×). [scripts/parity-agent-force.mjs](scripts/parity-agent-force.mjs) gained density-skip + density-only combos (6 total, bit-exact).
- **PR7c GPU RESIDENCY — SHIPPED (commit 614bbee).** For eligible models the WebGPU agent target now runs **whole frames resident on the GPU**: the spatial hash is built ON-GPU (clearBuffer → atomic count → a single-workgroup two-level exclusive scan [256 threads × ≤256-bin chunks] → atomic scatter with cursors), a whole gens/frame batch is encoded in **ONE queue submit** (per gen: hash passes → behaviour → force → **posCommit** — a compute pass that commits xNext→x AND zeroes the force accumulators GPU-side; a same-buffer copyBufferToBuffer is a validation error, hence compute), and the CPU reads back once per FRAME (`readbackAgentFrame`). `agentGpuUploadPending` (set by every mutation message — the AGENT_GPU_DEFER_TYPES set ∪ loadState/reset/setRngSeed/importImage — and initAgents) re-uploads the SoA only when the CPU touched it (CPU-side force zero before that upload — **per-step force accumulators MUST be zeroed each generation**; the resident path does it in posCommit). **Eligibility** (`agentResidentEligible` in [sim.worker.ts](src/simulator/engine/sim.worker.ts)): behaviour-scoped compiler flags **`usesStructural`/`usesRadiusWrite`** (set by the GPU emitters in [agentWebgpu/compile.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/agentWebgpu/compile.ts) — behaviour-scoped so an Init-Event spawn like Particle Life stays eligible) + agents-only + async attrs + no field/springs/growth/spawn/stop/indicators/positional; anything else falls back to the per-gen GPU path unchanged. Runtime lives in [agentWebgpuRuntime.ts](src/simulator/engine/agentWebgpuRuntime.ts) (`ensureAgentResident` — 4 extra pipelines with explicit bind-group layouts, `computeResidentHashParams` coarsens the bin edge ×1.3 to fit maxBins, `dispatchResidentBatch`). Measured: Boids **~0.4 ms/gen** (flocks 0.105→0.998); 50k Particle Life @600² **~20 ms/gen** (29× the 1030 ms pre-review WASM baseline, ~10× the per-gen GPU path); mutation round-trip exact (moveAgents lands + integrates).
- **P2 render + snapshot (commit 463077a)**: `stampBatchedTile` draws sub-2px batched opaque discs as `rect()` splats (`SPLAT_MAX_RAD = 2`) instead of moveTo+arc subpaths; `snapshotAgentsForRender` ships **Float32** copies (render precision — the store stays f64) and gates **vx/vy on `includeSprites`** (the sprite orientToVelocity heading is their only consumer; measured 45→17 B/agent, per-frame snapshot+clone 5.4→2.2 ms at 50k). The worker transfer list gates the length-0 placeholders on `length > 0` — they SHARE one ArrayBuffer, and listing a duplicate in a transfer list is a DataCloneError. gl3d's `AgentSnapshot3D` types follow. Measured: 50k stepped-handler (snapshot consume + draw) median **25 → 9.6 ms**.

### THE ACTIVE WINDOW — per-generation agent GPU traffic tracks the POPULATION, not `maxAgents` (2026-07-31, user-reported)

**`maxAgents` is a user-set CEILING, and every per-generation CPU↔GPU transfer was sized by it.** A model that grows to ~2 000 agents under a 60 000 ceiling therefore moved **~15 MB of mostly-dead slots EVERY generation**. A bonded / structurally-rewriting model (a GRA rule — rewiring IS the point) can never be residency-eligible, so it *always* pays that per-generation round-trip. Reported as *"on wasm the processing is much faster than on webgpu (roughly 2x)"* — it was worse than 2×, and it got worse with N.

**Measured on the reporter's 3D Cubic GRA, same 60 000 ceiling:** `47.4 ms/gen → 10.9 ms/gen` (**~4.4×**) at a LARGER population (N 1830 → 2486). Confirmed as the cause first by changing ONLY the ceiling (60000 → 4000 gave 47 → 10 ms/gen), with WASM as the control (insensitive: 6.5 → 5.1, since it works in place on `wasmMemory` and has no round-trip). Before the fix the gap widened with N — 1.9× at N≈100, **7.4× at N≈1900** — which is backwards for a GPU and is the tell that the cost was ceiling-bound, not work-bound.

- **`AgentWebGPURuntime.gpuActiveHigh`** ([agentWebgpuRuntime.ts](src/simulator/engine/agentWebgpuRuntime.ts)) is the window; `agentActiveWindow(rt, highWater)` is the ONE resolver every transfer calls. **It only ever GROWS** — a slot the GPU has written must keep being refreshed, or its stale request-queue lanes get read back and **drained** on a later generation. Slots it has never covered are still the zero the buffer was created with, which is exactly the "no requests, not alive" state the reconcile expects. That monotonicity IS the correctness argument; do not "optimise" it by shrinking on reset.
- **It must cover the post-dispatch SPAWN CURSOR, not just `highWater`**: a spawning behaviour bump-allocates slots ABOVE highWater via the atomic cursor and the reconcile reads `[hw, cursor)`. So `readbackAgentStep` reads that ONE u32 **first** (a 4-byte round-trip) and sizes everything else from it. A non-spawn model skips the extra round-trip — its window is exactly `highWater`.
- **Upload**: per-RUN `writeBuffer` of each strided run's live prefix (~30–50 small writes) replaces one whole-buffer write; the CPU zero-fill tails become `[hw, window)` instead of `[hw, maxAgents)`. Same for the alive mask, the colours, and the bond store (`bondStoreUpload`, a reused staging array instead of a fresh `Int32Array(bondStoreLen)` per generation).
- **Readback needs COMPACTION, not a prefix.** The f32 SoA is a set of STRIDED runs (run r at `f32Base[r] .. +maxAgents`), so the live prefixes are scattered across the whole buffer and a windowed readback cannot be one copy. `buildF32ReadPlan` copies each run's prefix into its own slot of a COMPACTED staging buffer and maps only `totalElems`. **EVERY run is planned** (the same field lists the upload walks), not just the ones the reader touches, and **`compactBase` THROWS on an unplanned base** — returning 0 would silently read a neighbouring run's values. Every read site is rebased through `CB(...)`, including the spawn reconcile's attribute read.
- `readbackAgentFrame` (the resident once-per-frame path) gets the same window + plan.
- **Gotcha this exposed in the harness**: `blockAfter(src, /export async function readbackAgentStep\(/)` returned the function's `Promise<{…}>` RETURN TYPE, not its body, so three checks passed vacuously. `blockAfter` now searches for the body brace from the END of the match.
- **Guarded** by the **B13** block in [scripts/verify-agent-render.mjs](scripts/verify-agent-render.mjs) (13 checks: monotonic + ceiling-clamped window; no whole-buffer write/copy remains; the plan covers every run; the unplanned base throws; the cursor-first sizing; every base rebased; the resident path and the bond store windowed). **Negative-controlled** — reverting the window to the ceiling, or making an unplanned base return 0, each fails exactly the check that names it.
- **Verified on the real GPU**: the reporter's model holds the cubic invariant (deg 3/3, `E = 3N/2`), 0 dangling, 0 asymmetry at every sample through 1200 generations of heavy spawning + rewiring; **Game of Life on Agents matches Conway CELL-FOR-CELL over 1024 agents for 3 consecutive generations** on non-trivial boards (234→243→213→171 alive, 0 mismatches — the value-level oracle for the windowed attribute readback); Particle Life (resident path) still shows its **6 species colours**; Growing Tissue keeps 7228 bonds with 0 dangling through division; Boids/2D unchanged. 29 models byte-identical; 14 gates green.

### Why a BONDED model can never be GPU-resident (the two agent GPU paths)

There are **two** WebGPU agent paths, and which one a model gets is the single biggest performance fact about it:

| | resident | per-generation |
|---|---|---|
| submits | **ONE** for the whole gens/frame batch | one per generation |
| CPU work between generations | **none** | upload → dispatch → readback |
| readback | once per FRAME | once per GENERATION |
| eligibility | `agentResidentEligible` | everything else |

**Residency's entire value is that N generations are encoded into ONE queue submit with NO CPU touch point between them.** So *anything* that needs the CPU BETWEEN generations disqualifies a model — by construction, not by omission.

**The structural phase — bond form/break/rewire, division, death, auto-bond, the stale-bond sweep — is CPU/JS on EVERY target by design.** A shader can only *request* those ops (it writes flags into the P4 request queue); applying them is serial data-structure surgery, not per-agent parallel math:
- the bond store is **ragged**, with per-agent capacity, a free list and epoch-stamped slot recycling. Removing a bond compacts by swapping with the last slot (`moveBondSlot`), which moves **both** endpoints' rows.
- **division** partitions a mother's bonds between two daughters via a closed-form eigensolve, then rewires every partner.
- `partner` / `restLength` are **CPU-owned** — the shader never writes them (P3), so they would need uploading + reading back each generation regardless.

Hence the two INDEPENDENT terms in [`agentResidentEligible`](src/simulator/engine/sim.worker.ts): **`s.maxBonds === 0`** (no bond store to sync) and **`agentGraphResidencyClean`** (= `!usesStructural && !usesRadiusWrite`, i.e. no Divide / Form / Break / Rewire / Kill reachable from the behaviour root). The other terms exclude features for the same reason — field bridge, sync-attr swap, positional projection, spawn reconcile, stop drain, indicator accumulation all need per-generation CPU.

**For a GRA rule this is not incidental — THE REWIRING IS THE MODEL** — so `Cubic GRA`, `SDCA`, `Life on Bonds` and every Morphogenesis Tissue can never satisfy either term. They are not "failing" residency; they are a different class of simulation.

**Lifting it** would mean porting the structural phase itself to the GPU: a parallel bond-store allocator/compactor, a GPU division partition, and conflict resolution for concurrent rewires of a shared edge — plus its own answer for invariant **I5** (a rejected op leaves the graph EXACTLY as before), which today is trivially satisfied because the CPU applies ops one at a time. Not scheduled.

**Until then the per-generation path is the middle ground and it is a real one**: behaviour + force still dispatch on the GPU, only the round-trip is per generation — and THE ACTIVE WINDOW (above) made that round-trip's cost track the live population instead of the `maxAgents` ceiling (measured 47.4 → 10.9 ms/gen). At small populations WASM can still win, because a CPU target has no round-trip at all.

### Direct agent render — GPU-side, free-when-idle (A1 + A2 + A1.5 + C + D; branch `optimize`)
The **WORKER renders agents into a transferred OffscreenCanvas**; the main thread just blits it 1:1 (`ctx.drawImage(agentRenderCanvasRef, 0, 0)`, the grid direct-render seam). **A1** feeds the render from the resident/per-gen GPU SoA (WebGPU-target models). **A2** widens this to CPU (JS/WASM) targets: the worker builds a lightweight **render-only** WebGPU surface and uploads the CPU store's positions/colours each frame, then presents on the SAME pipeline — the sim keeps running on the CPU, only the DRAW moves to the GPU (see the A2 subsection below). The per-frame CPU pipeline (readback → snapshot → postMessage → Canvas2D `drawAgentsOverlay`) runs **ONLY while a feature needs it** — free-running cost ≈ one `drawImage`. Additive/gated — every non-eligible model keeps today's CPU-overlay path byte-for-byte. Handoff: [docs/HANDOFF_GPU_AGENT_RENDER_A1.md](docs/HANDOFF_GPU_AGENT_RENDER_A1.md) (+ the master [HANDOFF_GPU_AGENT_RENDER.md](docs/HANDOFF_GPU_AGENT_RENDER.md) / [IMPACT_MAP](docs/IMPACT_MAP_GPU_AGENT_RENDER.md) / [PLAN](docs/PLAN_GPU_AGENT_RENDER.md)). Touches ONLY [agentWebgpuRuntime.ts](src/simulator/engine/agentWebgpuRuntime.ts) + [sim.worker.ts](src/simulator/engine/sim.worker.ts) + [SimulatorView.tsx](src/simulator/SimulatorView.tsx) — **NO compilers / gl3d / agentEngine / JS-WASM paths** (`git diff --stat` = 3 files), so byte-identity holds by construction.
- **FP-1 — the render is a VIEW of engine-owned state.** `AGENT_RENDER_WGSL` reads ONLY `agentF32[x/y/radius]` + `agentAlive` + the packed `agentColors` (r|g<<8|b<<16|a<<24) — fields every agent model has, so **zero compiler changes**, graph-agnostic. Instanced disc quads (`draw(4, highWater × copiesX × copiesY)`, triangle-strip): the VS decomposes the instance index into `(agent = inst % highWater, copy = inst / highWater)` → torus tile offset from the RenderView, world→screen via `scalePx/oxPx/oyPx`, degenerate off-screen quad for dead/alpha-0 agents. FS = disc SDF (premultiplied) + optional outline rim (matches the 2D `stampBatchedTile` ×0.60 band); a SECOND entry-point pair (`vsGlow`/`fsGlow`) draws the **additive halo** on the glow pipeline. **The drawn radius is floored at 1.2 px** (`max(ar*scalePx, 1.2)` — audit M2) to match the CPU overlay's `Math.max(1.2, r*scale)` at all three draw sites; without it a sub-pixel agent (zoomed out / large world) vanished on the fast path while the CPU path still drew a dot. Two pipelines (plain premultiplied-over / glow additive) — with Glow on BOTH draw, halo first, core over it (see the Glow section). `presentAgentsEncode` patches the uniform's `highWater` from the caller's value each present (the camera message can't know the free-mode highWater), so the instance decomposition always matches the draw.
- **THE DISC EDGE IS ANTIALIASED — analytic coverage, ALWAYS ON (no toggle).** `fsMain` used to end the silhouette with a bare `if (d > 1.0) { discard; }`, a BINARY edge: **measured on a real device with the shipped shader (radius 12), 0 partial-coverage pixels and 0 distinct partial alphas**, the centre scanline stepping 255 → 0 in one pixel — while the CPU overlay's Canvas2D `arc` fill produced **2084 partial pixels over 54 alpha levels** on the same app. **That inconsistency IS the user-reported "the contours of the agents appear serrated"**: an overlay model looked smooth, a direct-render one (Particle Life, and every E2 composite model) looked jagged. Now `pxw = max(fwidth(d), 1e-5)` and `cov = clamp((1 - d)/pxw + 0.5, 0, 1)` give a one-pixel coverage ramp centred on the true silhouette (cov = 0.5 exactly at `d == 1` — the same half-in/half-out coverage a rasterizer computes), folded into **BOTH the alpha AND the premultiplied rgb** (alpha-only would leave a bright rim fringe). After: **100 partial pixels / 30 alpha levels, and the coverage-weighted area lands on πr² to within 0.02 % (448 → 452.30 vs 452.39)** — proof the ramp is *calibrated*, not merely blurred — with the fully-opaque body **BIT-IDENTICAL** (verified 0 differing pixels, max channel delta 0, at radius 12 and 26, glow on and off).
  - **`fwidth` MUST be taken BEFORE any discard** — WGSL requires derivative builtins in uniform control flow.
  - **THE QUAD CARRIES A ONE-PIXEL PAD, and the pad and the uv rescale are a PAIR.** The quad CIRCUMSCRIBES the disc, so they are tangent at the four axis points and the ramp's outer half would be clipped exactly there (four hard notches). `padded = half + 1.0` grows the geometry and `out.uv = corner * (padded / half)` rescales so `d == 1` still marks the DRAWN radius; **`out.radPx` stays the UNPADDED radius** so the outline band does not move. Padding without the rescale shrinks the disc; rescaling without the pad restores the notches.
  - The **outline band** is feathered with the SAME derivative (`mix(1.0, 0.60, t)`), matching the antialiased `stroke()` the CPU overlay draws instead of a second hard step inside the body. **`fsGlow` needs no ramp** — its falloff already reaches zero continuously at `d == 1`, so the halo was never aliased; its discard just trims the pad ring.
  - **ONE module (`buildAgentDiscPipelines`) feeds A1, A2 and the E2 composite**, so all three inherit the edge policy and cannot drift. **The CPU overlay is untouched** (already coverage-antialiased), and capture rides along for free (view scope reads the display; the simulation scope re-renders with Canvas2D arcs).
  - **3D sphere impostors are NOT covered.** Both `agentRenderSphereWGSL` (worker, free mode) and gl3d's `SPHERE_FS` (frame mode) end the silhouette with `discard`, and **MSAA does not help a discard edge** (the fragment is killed for all its samples), so gl3d's `antialias: true` buys nothing there. The correct fix is **multisampling + alpha-to-coverage** (`alphaToCoverageEnabled` / `gl.SAMPLE_ALPHA_TO_COVERAGE`) — order-independent and depth-write-safe, unlike alpha blending, which would need back-to-front sorting and would halo against `frag_depth`. It MUST land on BOTH renderers at once (the free/frame flip has to stay seamless), so it is a separate change; the 2D fix above is what the report was about.
  - Guarded by the **B15** block in [scripts/verify-agent-render.mjs](scripts/verify-agent-render.mjs) (10 source invariants), **negative-controlled by SOURCE MUTATION — 7 mutations, 7 caught**: revert the ramp to the hard discard, move `fwidth` after the discard, drop the pad, drop the uv rescale, shift `radPx` to the padded radius, fold coverage into alpha only, drop the outline feather.
- **FP-2 — the CPU never NEEDS per-frame agent state; FEATURES do.** Worker readback POLICY: `agentUiSync` (default ON) — when ON the resident batch reads the GPU state back each frame and `sendColors` ships the render snapshot (picks/hover/inspector/recording read it, `drawAgentsOverlay` is STILL skipped — only the DATA flows); when OFF the resident batch SKIPS `readbackAgentFrame`, sets `agentStoreStale`, and `sendColors` ships **no `agents` payload** — just an `agentLiveCount` scalar (the stats chip). The batch presents INSIDE `dispatchResidentBatch`'s single submit (GPU-authoritative — posCommit ran, so `agentF32[x]` is current); the per-gen path + mutations present via `presentAgentsFromStore` (uploadAgentSoA + **uploadAgentColors** [syncs the CPU-set colours for a fresh/mutated agent] + presentAgentsOnce). `agentBatchPresented` flags the internal present so `sendColors` doesn't double-present.
- **`uploadAgentSoA` MUST seed `agentColors` (the transparent-agents trap, fixed 2026-07-23).** The per-gen + resident SoA-upload path uploads positions/attrs but NOT colours; `readbackAgentStep` then OVERWRITES `s.colors` from the GPU `agentColors` buffer. A model whose agent behaviour has **NO colour node** (no Set Cell Looks, no Agent Output Mapping — Boids/Chemotaxis rely on the per-slot `DEFAULT_AGENT_COLOR`) never writes `agentColors` in the shader, so without a seed the readback pulls the buffer's uninitialized ZEROS back → fully-transparent, INVISIBLE agents on the CPU overlay AND the composite. So `uploadAgentSoA` now calls `uploadAgentColors(rt, s)` at its end (idempotent — a colour-writing shader overwrites the seed GPU-side; only supplies the default when nothing writes). This was the symptom-1 root cause of the WASM-grid+WebGPU-agent Chemotaxis "no agents" report — a field-coupled WebGPU-agent model is NOT render-eligible (CPU overlay), so it read the never-seeded buffer.
- **E2 single-canvas composite is RE-ENABLED, redesigned at DISPLAY resolution (2026-07-25).** The original E2 rendered both layers into ONE grid-sized (`W×H`) canvas with the agent camera at world resolution (`scalePx=1`), letting the main-thread blit scale it — so a radius-1 agent was a ~1px disc that became a CELL-SIZED BLOCK once scaled to the display (the user's "agents become a blob of cells" on WebGPU/WebGPU). The **display-res redesign** renders BOTH layers at DISPLAY resolution through the camera into a **display-sized** canvas: the grid layer is a fullscreen triangle whose FS **inverts the camera** (display pixel → world coord `(fragCoord−oxPx)/scalePx` → cell `floor(wx)/floor(wy)` → grid `colorsBuf`, NEAREST = crisp CA cells), and the agent discs render through the **SAME display-res camera** as the A1 render — so agents stay CRISP DISCS at any zoom. See the "E2 — single-canvas composite render" subsection for the full design; the `agentComposite` gate is live again.
- **The one-shot rule — ONE place** (the load-bearing correctness): at the TOP of `self.onmessage`, if `agentStoreStale` and the message reads/mutates agents (`AGENT_GPU_DEFER_TYPES ∪ {getAgentState, getState}`) → block via the existing `asyncStepBatchInFlight` deferral, `await readbackAgentFrame`, clear the flag, then REPLAY the (now-fresh) message. So **no CPU consumer ever sees stale state** — it pays a one-shot readback (~2 ms @50k). `getState` (save) is fresh for free (also fixes the pre-existing agent save-freshness gap). Verified with a hostile test: `moveAgents` / `getAgentState` fired mid-free-run reflect post-readback state exactly.
- **The DUAL of the one-shot rule — no PRESENT may ever WRITE a stale CPU store back to the GPU (`42a44a0`).** `presentAgentsFromStore` `uploadAgentSoA`s the CPU store before presenting, so a present fired while `agentStoreStale` OVERWRITES the live diffused GPU state with the stale ≈last-synced frame — reverting the sim (the Particle-Life "brush-remove a hole, play, then a re-attach/refocus jumps back to the post-brush frame and freezes" report; the audit-B1 hazard realised on a present path). The one-shot rule keeps CONSUMERS fresh; this keeps PRODUCERS from clobbering. **`presentAgentsIfActive()` is now present-only (`presentAgentsOnce`, no upload) whenever `agentStoreStale`** — so EVERY present site is safe by construction (the `setAgentCamera` handler's explicit stale branch is now redundant-but-harmless; `refreshAgentDisplay` [tab-refocus] no longer reverts). Companion: `attachAgentCanvas` (display resize / re-attach) previously force-cleared `agentStoreStale = false`, LYING that the CPU was fresh on a re-attach to the still-authoritative GPU compute runtime → its present then uploaded the stale store; it now `await ensureAgentStoreFresh()` instead (read the GPU down if stale — a no-op on a fresh/rebuilt runtime or a CPU target), so the present's upload is an identity. **Rule for any new agent present path: never upload when `agentStoreStale`; present-only or `ensureAgentStoreFresh()` first.** Verified in-browser (WebGPU agent target, 1800 particles, free mode): mean per-agent advance over a 2.5 s window was 59.1 with no refresh vs 54.1 while spamming `refreshAgentDisplay` (ratio 0.92 — a revert would have collapsed the refresh run toward zero).
- **The gate** (all GENERAL properties, evaluated in SimulatorView at init/recompile; mirrors the grid's placement): `topologyMode.agents && gridCells === false && !is3D && agentResult.agentTarget === 'webgpu' && transferControlToOffscreen supported && (model.sprites?.length ?? 0) === 0 && !agentMetaballs.enabled && (model.agentMappings?.length ?? 0) === 0`. (**D relaxes the `gridCells === false` term to `gridCells === false || (agentDecoupled && !is3D)`** — see the D subsection; a 2D field-decoupled grid+agents model qualifies.) **NOT coupled to `agentResidentEligible`** — the per-gen GPU path renders too (the SoA is uploaded there). **The Agent-Output-Mapping exclusion is a deliberate ADDITION to the handoff gate** (see the A1 Completion Report): OM colours are computed CPU-side by `runAgentColorPass` into `s.colors`, NOT into the GPU `agentColors` the render reads, so an OM model keeps the CPU-overlay path where its colours stay correct. **A1.5 LIFTS this for a WebGPU-target model whose OM graph compiles to GPU colour passes** — the OM term becomes `agentMappings.length === 0 || agentOmGpuSupported` (see the A1.5 subsection). Sprites / metaballs / 3D / a non-webgpu target likewise fall back to today's path (function first). **BONDS are a shared exclusion in BOTH dimensions** (`resolveMaxBonds(model.centerBased) === 0` — audit H1, originally a 3D-only term): the GPU pass draws discs/spheres only and `draw()` skips `drawAgentsOverlay()` under direct render, which is the SOLE bond renderer — a bonded model would silently lose its bond lines (the shipped 2D Tissue samples did) and the `showBonds` Layers toggle would become a no-op. Emitting bond lines in the GPU pass (a line pipeline + the bond-pair buffer) is a real render feature, not a wiring repair — recorded as a follow-up.
- **Attach lifecycle** (clones the grid seam): the worker posts `agentRuntimeReady` when `buildAgentWebGPUIfNeeded` installs the runtime → SimulatorView `maybeAttachAgentCanvas` (transfer a DISPLAY-pixel-sized OffscreenCanvas, post `attachAgentCanvas`) → worker `setupAgentDirectRender` (validates the WGSL module async, builds pipelines, presents once) acks `agentRenderStatus{active}` → SimulatorView commits the placeholder as the blit source + sends the initial camera. `agentRuntimeReady` resets the active flag first (covers soft-recompile re-attach, since the runtime rebuild drops the old render pipeline); a display RESIZE re-attaches with a fresh canvas (transferred dims are fixed); tab-refocus posts `refreshAgentDisplay`. `agentRenderActive`/`agentStoreStale` reset on every runtime teardown (initAgents / buildAgentWebGPUIfNeeded / step-fail). **A re-attach REUSES a layout-matching render-only surface** (audit H3): every real display-size change re-attaches (once per frame while a splitter is dragged), and building a fresh surface there orphaned three `maxAgents`-sized buffers AND a shared-device reference that could never be released — so the attach handler reuses `agentRenderRuntime` when `maxAgents`/`gridDepth`/`f32Len` match and destroys a stale-layout one first (`buildAgentDiscPipelines`/`setupAgentSphereRender` likewise destroy the previous render-view uniform). **The gate's two MODEL-dependent terms are re-evaluated on a SOFT recompile** (audit M1): `sprites` + `agentMappings` are deliberately NOT in `needsFullInit` (a reinit would reset the grid + re-seed the population), so the once-computed gate went stale — adding a sprite kept direct render on (sprites never drawn) and adding a GPU-unsupported agent OM kept it presenting behaviour colours. `agentRenderModelTermsOk()` (module-scope, ONE source) feeds both the init gate and a soft-recompile refresh of `agentRenderModelTermsOkRef`, which `maybeAttachAgentCanvas` consults exactly like the metaballs suppression (detach/re-attach, no worker teardown). **A `recompile` is in the one-shot staleness set** (audit M3): the rebuild drops every GPU buffer, so a free-mode soft recompile used to REWIND to the last synced frame — the dispatcher now reads the GPU state down first, and the rebuild's `agentGpuUploadPending` re-seeds the new runtime from it (lossless).
- **Camera** (`setAgentCamera`, present-only): SimulatorView `computeAgentRenderView` reuses the exact 2D draw math (scale/pan/infinity tile range, cap 256 copies) + `agentOutlines` + `agentGlow` + `bg2d` (the shader clears with the bg, so `draw()` skips the CPU bg fill under direct render). rAF-coalesced + deduped (a plain step doesn't move the camera, and each `setAgentCamera` triggers a present — a per-frame post would double the render cost).
- **The UI-sync driver** (`setAgentUiSync`): ON iff a feature is (or may be) reading agent state — paused (`!playing`), recording, a pinned/sweep inspector, an edit target, the vision-cone display, a **state-reading** agent brush / inspect hovering (below), or metaballs suppressing direct render. Debounced OFF ~300 ms (brush strokes don't thrash). Re-evaluated per-frame in the stepped handler (catches hover-during-play) + on the state-signal effect.
- **THE HOVER TERM IS MODE-AWARE, AND PASSIVE HOVER MUST NEVER PIN** (user-reported: *"just having the cursor on top of the simulation drags the performance down … even if the user is not actually interacting … when it doesn't even change the highlight"*). The term used to be a bare `brushTarget === 'agents' && agentCursorWorldRef != null` (+ the 3D `glPointerOverRef` twin), described here as already narrow because it "ANDs an armed agent brush". **It was not narrow at all: an AGENTS-ONLY model FORCES `brushTarget` to `'agents'`** (there is no grid layer to point at, and an effect pins it), so it reduced to "the cursor is somewhere over the canvas" — and the **DEFAULT brush mode `add` reads NOTHING** from the snapshot (`agentSeedInShape` / `agentSeedPoints` / `agentSeedInLine` scatter points by pure geometry, and its cursor is the shape silhouette). Resting the cursor therefore held the per-frame GPU readback + snapshot ship forever. **Measured on Particle Life (WebGPU agents, free-running, ~1800 agents): worker turnaround median 4.1 → 9.5 ms, mean 5.4 → 19.9, p90 5.7 → 89.2 ms, throughput −25%, with a snapshot on 487 of 487 frames instead of 0.** Two guards now, and **both** are needed:
  1. **`agentHoverNeedsState()`** — the ONE predicate the term consults. True iff the model has agents AND (the **Inspect toggle is on or Shift is held** — those pick through `pickAgentAt` / gl3d's colour-id FBO on *any* agent model, so this arm is deliberately NOT gated on the brush target) OR (the brush targets agents AND its mode is in **`AGENT_BRUSH_MODES_NEEDING_STATE`** = remove/move/edit/glue/cut/bond — every mode except `add`, because each of those draws a hovered-agent ring or an area highlight, or runs an id scan on the press). **`shiftDownRef`** is a new dimension-agnostic window keydown/keyup latch (the pre-existing `glShiftDownRef` is 3D-canvas-scoped and stays the grid driver's signal): arming on the MODIFIER rather than the press is what keeps Shift+LMB inspect correct in `add` mode, where nothing else would have armed the snapshot (measured re-arm → fresh snapshot ≈ one worker round-trip, 4–6 ms, vs >100 ms for a human press).
  2. **THE IDLE BACKSTOP (`AGENT_HOVER_IDLE_MS` = 3000, `noteHoverActivity()`)** — a cursor motionless for 3 s is not interacting, so the pin drops even in a state-reading mode (the user asked for exactly this fallback). Called from every activity source: the raw 2D `mousemove` (**BEFORE `scheduleHoverWork`**, so an aiming movement re-arms synchronously in the same event), the 2D `mousedown`/`wheel`, the 3D `onMove`/`onDown`/`onWheel`/canvas-enter, and Shift-down. It is a **trailing timer** (a raw move stream is 125–1000 Hz, so the hot path is one timestamp write; the armed timer re-checks the stamp when it fires). **On expiry it CLEARS `agentHoverIdRef` + `agentAreaHoverIdsRef`** — those rings are drawn from the LIVE snapshot every frame, so leaving them would drift off the agents they name; the pure-geometry footprint silhouette stays. **Documented residual:** a press after ≥3 s of a *literally* motionless cursor in a state-reading mode acts on a snapshot up to one debounce older than live. Any pixel of movement re-arms first, so only a perfectly still pointing device reaches it.
  - **Verified after the fix** (real UI, real worker): resting the cursor in `add` mode is **identical to cursor-off** (median 4.2 vs 4.0 ms, p90 5.8 vs 5.6, **0 snapshots of 634 frames**); `remove` mode pins while moving and releases at t ≈ 3.0 s (`hoverActive` false) → UI-sync OFF at t ≈ 3.6 s (after the 300 ms debounce) → back to baseline (median 4.8 ms, 0/688 snapshots); a single mousemove re-arms **synchronously** (`uiSyncOn` false→true in the same event); Shift-down in `add` mode flips the pin ON; Shift+LMB still opens the agent inspector; the Remove/Area highlight rings still draw while moving; 3D behaves the same on the gl canvas. **`window.__agentRenderState()` (DEV) exposes `uiSyncOn` / `hoverNeedsState` / `hoverActive` / `idleForMs`** so a probe can tell the hover pin apart from any other want-term. Pinned by the **B14** block in [scripts/verify-agent-render.mjs](scripts/verify-agent-render.mjs) (15 checks; negative-controlled — dropping the mode predicate, the idle flag, or the visual clear each fails exactly the check that names it). **NB the `blockAfter` anchors must STOP before the arrow's `{`** — it searches for the next `{` *after* the match, so including it scans an inner block (three checks passed vacuously until this was fixed).
- **Glow** is a simulator Graphics option (`genesisca_sim_settings.agentGlow {on,size,intensity,steepness,core}`, sanitized on load) — a checkbox + Size/**Core**/Intensity/Falloff sliders in the agent common-controls, **rendered in BOTH dimensions** (the block is no longer `!is3D`-gated; its four tooltips swap per dimension). **In 2D it renders on BOTH agent paths** — the direct-render/E2 shader pipeline here AND the CPU overlay (see "CPU-overlay glow" below), which is what makes it work on the models the direct-render gate excludes (bonded / sprites / metaballs / field-coupled). **In 3D it is a DIFFERENT TECHNIQUE — a dual-Kawase bloom — see "3D agent glow" below.** **Its 2D shape is a SOLID CORE + a halo that ACCUMULATES EXACTLY AND IS COMPRESSED ONCE — see the next three sections.**
- **Verified in-browser** (the pane reports hidden, so protocol + worker state + DOM, NOT composited pixels — the compositor is suspended while occluded, so `drawImage(transferredCanvas)` / screenshots can't be read; the render pipeline is proven by `agentRenderStatus:true` [WGSL compiled 0 errors, both pipelines built, the present executed] + 0 GPU errors over 900 gens + the identical battle-tested grid blit): a WebGPU-agent Boids ENGAGES direct render; free mode ships `hasAgents:false`+`agentLiveCount` while gen advances; UI-sync ON re-ships the snapshot; the hostile staleness test (`moveAgents`/`getAgentState` mid-free-run) reflects post-readback state; `getState` is fresh; Boids flocks to **polarization 0.9991**; the stats chip reads the free-mode count; a JS-target model does NOT engage (CPU path unchanged); no re-attach storm. tsc + `npm run build` + `parity-agent-wasm` (18) + `parity-agent-force` (7) all green.

#### CPU-overlay glow — the Canvas2D sibling of the WGSL glow pipeline (branch `updates`)
**The reported bug**: *"the Glow option is not working for the Growing Graphs rule, no matter if it's webgpu or wasm"*. Glow lived ONLY in `AGENT_RENDER_WGSL`, and the direct-render gate excludes any model with `resolveMaxBonds(model.centerBased) > 0` (the GPU pass draws no bond LINES — audit H1), so **every bonded model** — `Growing Graphs`, `Cubic GRA`, `SDCA`, `Life on Bonds`, all three Morphogenesis tissues — took the CPU overlay and the checkbox did nothing **on any agent target** (the target is irrelevant; the *render path* is what decides). Same for sprites / metaballs / a field-coupled model.
- **`drawAgentGlow`** ([SimulatorView.tsx](src/simulator/SimulatorView.tsx), module-level, next to `sanitizeAgentGlow`) mirrors the WGSL halo FS over a disc of radius `radPx + glowSize`. **Each sprite is blitted into an off-screen ACCUMULATION scratch, and the whole layer is tonemapped once on the way to the display** — see "ACCUMULATE EXACTLY, COMPRESS ONCE" below; it was per-agent `'lighter'` onto the display, then per-agent `'screen'`, before that. Uses the SAME `Math.max(1.2, r*scale)` radius floor as every other draw site.
- **THE SPRITE CACHE IS THE WHOLE POINT.** A `createRadialGradient` per agent per frame is unusable at the ~10k-node scale a GRA model reaches, so the profile is baked ONCE into a 2R×2R canvas per **(colour quantised to 5 bits/channel, integer glow radius)** — the glyph-tile-cache pattern. 5-bit quantisation (≤3/255 error, invisible in a halo) is what collapses a **Color-Scale agent viewer** (hundreds of distinct colours) to a handful of sprites. Cache cap **1024**, evicting **oldest-first** (never a wholesale clear, which would thrash into one canvas per agent); measured headroom: `Growing Graphs` at its 10k cap groups into **224** distinct (colour, radius) discs. `R > 128` (a very zoomed-in view) draws uncached — a 256×256 sprite that few agents on screen would share. The cache is keyed on `intensity|steepness` and dropped wholesale when a slider moves.
- **`intensity > 1` used to be reproduced by MULTI-PASS** — a Canvas2D alpha caps at 1 while the GPU's `intensity * …` saturated only in the framebuffer, so the sprite was baked at `intensity/ceil(intensity)` and blitted `ceil(intensity)` times ('lighter' is truly additive). **SUPERSEDED TWICE and gone for good**: repeated passes COMPOUND rather than sum under both screen and the log encoding, and it is unnecessary — the sprite now bakes an UNBOUNDED radiance into a bijective encoding, so any intensity rides ONE pass. **The `min(1, …)` clamp it was later replaced by is also gone** (it was the plateau disc — see below).
- **Draw order: bonds → HALO → discs.** *(Superseded the original bonds → discs → glow; see the solid-core section below for why.)* The halo sits UNDER the bodies, so discs / sprites / the goo blob land on top of it untouched.
- **Per-agent alpha 0 is skipped** (the GPU VS culls those quads too); other alphas ride `ctx.globalAlpha`, written only when it CHANGES. Infinity mode tiles exactly like the disc pass; off-screen agents are culled by the same box test.
- **`renderSimulationFrame` calls the SAME helper**, so a simulation-scope screenshot / recording carries the glow (this closed one arm of the documented simulation-scope fidelity gap — sprites + metaballs remain).
- **Cost, MEASURED** (real UI, `Growing Graphs` paused at its 10 004-node cap, one full redraw forced by a zoom click, canvas ops instrumented): glow OFF = 224 `fill` + 10 004 `rect` + 1 `stroke` ≈ **7.0 ms**; glow ON = the same **+ 10 004 `drawImage` = 30.5 ms** ⇒ ~**3 µs/agent**, ~38 ms/frame total. Verified that the blend mode is NOT the cost (an in-page A/B put the composited blend within 5 % of `'source-over'` — it is per-call dispatch overhead, so neither downscaling the layer nor batching by colour would help). At the shipped model's 6 g/s the sim still dominates; on the display it caps ~26 fps at 10k agents. Opt-in, documented in Help; **glow OFF is byte-identical** (the pass is skipped entirely — the instrumented op counts match exactly). **The HDR rework re-measured this at +8 %** — 14.59 → 15.74 ms on the same model at 4 896 agents — because the accumulation is the same N blits plus ONE extra layer blit (see the flush finding below).
- **Verified in the REAL UI** (visible pane): `Growing Graphs` (WASM agents) grown to 10 004 nodes glows — lit pixels 2 838 → 6 532 and total luminance 1.14 M → 4.12 M on the display canvas at 1 180 nodes, and the 10k render reads as a glowing nebula; `SDCA` (**WebGPU** agents, bonded ⇒ CPU overlay) glows with bonds + discs still drawn; a simulation-scope screenshot goes 11 998 → 74 530 lit pixels with glow on; `Particle Life` reports `directActive: true`; 0 console errors.

#### THE SOLID CORE — glow is a core + a halo, not one falloff (branch `updates`)
**The reported problem**: *"the glow shouldn't be a single circle … at least the falloff shouldn't be like that, because it gets impossible to visualize well both clusters of agents AND barely-visible isolated agents. We should be able to have a 'core size' that is a colour that won't be added out or faded out."* A single additive falloff from the centre forces a choice: lower the intensity so clusters stay legible and a lone agent is a dim smudge; raise it so a lone agent reads and clusters blow to white. Both halves of that trade come from the SAME cause — **the agent's own colour was being produced additively**, so it scaled with intensity and accumulated with its neighbours'.
- **THE SHAPE (both paths): an OPAQUE core with the halo UNDER it.** `coreR = radPx + core*glowSize` (so `core ∈ [0,1]`, `0` = the agent's own disc — the default, and the historical body size), `R = radPx + glowSize`. The core is drawn **source-over** (premultiplied on the GPU, a plain fill on the CPU) so it can be neither added out by a neighbour's halo nor faded out by a low intensity. The halo's falloff is **remapped over the BAND** `[coreFrac, 1]` (`t = clamp((1-d)/(1-coreFrac))`, `g = intensity·pow(t, steepness)`) instead of `[0,1]` — the whole dynamic range lands outside the body rather than being spent inside it. Inside the core the profile plateaus at `intensity` (invisible under an opaque body; it keeps the curve continuous at the core edge and reads correctly under a TRANSLUCENT agent).
- **GPU** ([agentWebgpuRuntime.ts](src/simulator/engine/agentWebgpuRuntime.ts)): the module now has TWO entry-point pairs over ONE shared `buildVert(vi, inst, halo)` — `vsGlow`/`fsGlow` (quad half = `R`, screen-blended) and `vsMain`/`fsMain` (quad half = `coreR`, premultiplied-over + the outline rim). **Both `presentAgentsEncode` and `presentCompositeEncode` draw the halo pipeline THEN the plain one** when `rt.renderGlow`; before, glow SELECTED the glow pipeline INSTEAD of the plain one, so a glowing agent had **no opaque body at all** — that is the GPU half of the bug. Using two entry points rather than a pass flag in the uniform keeps the uniform written once per present. `rt.renderGlow` now also requires `glowSize > 0 && glowIntensity > 0` (a halo that would contribute nothing is skipped; the core pass always draws — it IS the body). `out.radPx` carries the DRAWN body radius (`half`), so the outline rim hugs whatever silhouette the user sees; with glow off `half === radPx`, byte-identical.
- **`RenderView.glowCore` is APPENDED LAST** (struct + `fl[21]`), so every pre-existing member keeps its offset — the `ForceControl.motionMode` / VoxelView precedent. The struct grows 84 → 88 B inside the unchanged 96-B `RENDER_VIEW_BYTES`; `verify-render-uniform-layouts` pairs struct ⇄ writer by offset and stays green.
- **CPU** ([SimulatorView.tsx](src/simulator/SimulatorView.tsx)): `drawAgentGlow` MOVED from the end of `drawAgentsOverlay` to right after the bond layer, so the halo goes down BEFORE the bodies (that reorder alone is the CPU half of the fix — the halo used to blend onto the discs and wash them). It now runs two sub-passes: the halo, then — **only when `core > 0`** — an opaque core disc of radius `coreR`, batched one path+fill per distinct RGBA. At the default `core = 0` the second pass is skipped ENTIRELY, which is what keeps sprites and the metaball blob untouched (their own body draws on top of the halo and IS the core). `renderSimulationFrame` was reordered the same way.
- **The sprite cache carries the core**: `glowCoreFrac(R, size, core)` derives the core fraction from R (radPx = R − size), so the cache KEY stays (quantised colour, R) and `size|core` merely ride the `glowSpriteSig` that invalidates it. An explicit gradient stop is added AT the core edge so the plateau boundary is sharp regardless of where the 32 uniform stops fall.
- **⚠️ NEVER PUT A BACKTICK IN A WGSL COMMENT** — `agentRenderWGSL` is a TS template literal, and one in a comment terminates it (`TS1005: ';' expected`, ~50 lines away from the real cause).
- **VERIFIED IN THE REAL UI (visible pane), by PIXELS, on both paths.** The decisive test is transform-free and colour-agnostic: **every fully-opaque body pixel must be BIT-IDENTICAL between glow ON and glow OFF.**
  - **CPU overlay** — `Growing Graphs` (WASM agents, bonded ⇒ overlay), paused at 3 896 agents: **53 220 / 53 220 body pixels identical (100.0000 %, 0 differing)** while the halo lights 65 461 new pixels (76 609 → 142 070) and raises luminance 63 % (28.4 M → 46.4 M). **At the MAXIMUM intensity 3.0 the cores are STILL 100 % identical** (52.6 M luminance) — the old glow would have blown every one of them to white. Isolated-agent close-up (10 seeded nodes, radPx 17.09): the core reads its exact colour `(16,10,60,255)` at r = 0 / 8 / 14 on all ten, the halo appears only outside (α 73 → 29 → 1 → 0 across r = 19 → 30).
  - **Core slider** — at `core = 0.6` the measured solid radius per agent is 20.5–22 px against the predicted `17.09 + 0.6·8 = 21.89`.
  - **GPU direct render** — `Particle Life` (WebGPU agents, `directActive: true`): **44 358 / 44 358 body pixels identical, max channel delta 0**, halo 44 358 → 92 769 lit px. The pre-fix shape would have left **zero** opaque pixels; measured `opaqueON = 44 387 ≈ opaqueOFF = 44 358`. At `core = 0.75` the solid area grows ×1.84 (44 387 → 81 777 opaque px) and **100 % of the 2.70 % of disc pixels that changed are still fully opaque** — a NEIGHBOUR's enlarged solid core covering them, never an additive wash.
  - **E2 composite** — `Chemotaxis` (WebGPU grid + WebGPU agents, `compositeActive: true`): all on-screen agent cores bit-identical ON vs OFF, all gained a halo just outside the disc.
  - **Metaballs** (CPU overlay, `directActive: false`) render the goo blob with a halo and no disc artifacts; the **simulation-scope screenshot** carries the halo with cores at their exact colour. 0 console errors throughout.

#### ACCUMULATE EXACTLY, COMPRESS ONCE — the glow architecture (branch `updates`, 2026-08-07)
**Reported twice.** First: *"Find a better way to blend the glow halos to avoid this oversaturated look and contrast artifacts where there is a high density."* That round replaced pure-additive with **screen** (`1 − (1−p)^N`), which helped. Then: *"it's gotten better but still not good enough. Use as reference the way that our Particle Life reference code solves it. Theirs looks much more well treated both in 2D and 3D."*

**THE LESSON — a per-pair blend is MEMORYLESS, so no operator can fix this.** Additive gives `min(1, Np)`, screen gives `1 − (1−p)^N`; both are functions of the RUNNING RESULT, both live in `[0,1]`, and both exhaust 8 bits after ~4 overlaps for any `p` bright enough to see ONE halo. **The plateau is a property of the ARCHITECTURE, not of the operator.** The reference (studied under `SandboxScience-master/`, technique reimplemented — no code copied) does not blend halos against each other at all: it renders every particle's glow quad **additively into an `rgba16float` HDR target** and compresses the accumulated sum **once**, in a fullscreen compose pass (`assets/particle-life-gpu/shaders/render/particle_render_glow.wgsl` + `.../compose/compose_hdr.wgsl`, wired in `components/particle-life/ParticleLifeGpu.vue`). Both our 2D paths now do the same.

- **THE HALF NOBODY EXPECTED — the clamp WAS the worst artifact.** Under screen the emitted value had to be clamped (`dst = 1 − src`, so `> 1` SUBTRACTS the backdrop), and `min(1, intensity·t^steepness)` gives every agent a hard-edged, fully-saturated **PLATEAU DISC** wherever the profile reaches 1: at the shipped Intensity 3 that is the **outer 42 % of the band radius**, identical on every agent, before any overlap. Removing the clamp is the single most visible half of this fix — and it is only *possible* because the accumulation is no longer where the compositing happens.

**GPU** ([agentWebgpuRuntime.ts](src/simulator/engine/agentWebgpuRuntime.ts)) — three new pieces beside `ensureAgentDepthTex`: `GLOW_HDR_FORMAT = 'rgba16float'` (renderable AND blendable), `ensureGlowHdrTex`/`destroyGlowHdrTex`, and `encodeGlowHdrPass`.
