  reproducibility the `wasm` target was chosen for).

## Agent Capability Profiles (branch `absorb_old_automatosgt`)

Decompose the monolithic agent engine into **opt-in capability modules** so a model declares only the capabilities it needs and its EDITOR SURFACE (palette nodes, Behaviour-Step ports, agent Edit-panel rows, inspector fields) shows only its paradigm's machinery — a social-graph or particle author never sees morphogenesis nodes. Universality by **composition**, not by piling every feature onto one fixed agent. Spec/audit trail: [docs/HANDOFF_AGENT_CAPABILITY_PROFILES.md](docs/HANDOFF_AGENT_CAPABILITY_PROFILES.md) (authoritative) + [PLAN](docs/PLAN_AGENT_CAPABILITY_PROFILES.md) + [ANALYSIS](docs/ANALYSIS_AUTOMATOSGT_AGENTS.md). **STEP 0 + STEP 1 shipped (the entire clarity win, editor-surface); STEP 3 (Bonds SoA gate) + the physics-capability ENGINE wiring (Collision / Bonds=Physics / Growth now gate real engine behaviour — the honest-controls pass) shipped on top, all byte-identical for existing files; the remaining SoA memory-compute gating (STEP 4/6) + net-new STEP 5 nodes are the secondary win.**

### The honest core (always allocated) + the gate-able capabilities
- **Core (never SoA-gated before the deferred STEP 6):** the slot **id** (= the array index) + `alive` + `colors` + position (`x,y[,z]` + the `Next` double-buffer) + velocity (`vx,vy[,vz]`) + force (`forceX,forceY[,forceZ]`) + `radius` + the always-on i32 reductions `lineage`/`epoch`/`bondCount` + the user's agent attributes. **Motion & Body are always-allocated in v1** (there is no `Static` integrator path yet) — their toggle is a palette/port gate only; SoA-gating them is the deferred XL STEP 6.
- **Capabilities (gate-able on top of core):** Motion (static/velocity/force), Body, Collision (off/**soft**=springy repulsion force / **positional**=rigid no-overlap constraint — two GENUINELY different models), Bonds (off/data/physics), Auto-bond, Growth, Division, Lifespan, Population (birth/death), Sensing, Orientation, Field coupling, Appearance. **The PHYSICS capabilities (Collision / Bonds=Physics / Growth) now drive the ENGINE, not just the editor surface** — see "Physics-capability engine wiring" + "Positional (hard) collision" below.

### The profile is the single source of truth ([src/model/agentCapabilities.ts](src/model/agentCapabilities.ts))
- **Schema** ([types.ts](src/model/types.ts)): `AgentCapabilities` + `MotionMode`/`CollisionMode`/`BondsMode`; `CenterBasedConfig.agentCapabilities?` (additive — absent ⇒ inferred).
- **7 presets** (`AGENT_PRESETS`): Particle · Boids · Vivarium · Morphogenesis · Social Graph · CA-on-Agents. `Full ≡ Morphogenesis` (deep-equal — a STEP 1 gate). `matchAgentPreset` flips to `'custom'` on any edit that stops matching.
- **Mode-aware dependency closure** (`computeCapabilityClosure`): auto-enables hard deps (Collision=soft ⇒ Body + Motion=Force; Bonds=physics ⇒ Motion=Force; Growth/Division ⇒ Body; Auto-bond ⇒ Bonds=physics; Population.Birth ⇒ Motion). `applyCapabilityEdit` ALSO cascades REMOVALS (Body off ⇒ drop Growth/Division/Collision; Motion below Force ⇒ demote physics bonds / soft collision).
- **Node→capability requirement table** (`AGENT_NODE_REQUIREMENT`, `nodeSatisfiesCapabilities`): the ONE source consumed by BOTH the palette gate AND the migration widening. A node not listed is core/universal (Behaviour Step, Get Self Position, Get/Set Agent Attribute-by-id, the array-tier plumbing) — always available when Agents is on. Only nodes that should VANISH when their capability is off are listed (Divide Agent→division, Apply Force→motion=force, Get Radius→body, Form Bond/For Each Bond→bonds, Secrete To Field→fieldCoupling, …).
- **Usage-widened migration** (`inferAgentProfile` / `migrateAgentCapabilities`, wired into LOAD_MODEL + `migrateForHarness`): **minimal base + engine-physics signal (`usesBondingPhysics` ⇒ collision/body/force, `autoBond` ⇒ physics bonds) + node-usage widen + Body-for-any-moving-model, then closure.** **DELIBERATE DEVIATION from the handoff's config-base-Full** — this is provably safe (the widen uses the SAME requirement table as the gate, so it can NEVER hide a node the graph uses) AND honest/tight (a maxBonds>0 model that never touches bonds no longer shows the whole morphogenesis palette). Verified: shipped Boids infers `motion/body/sensing` only; Tissue infers full physics+division. A fresh Agents-topology enable seeds the friendly `defaultAgentCapabilities()` = Boids.
- **Footprint estimate** (`estimateAgentFootprint`): the per-agent byte readout enumerating the SAME field groups STEP 3's profile-driven `computeAgentMemoryLayout` will gate (v1 is a display-only what-if — the engine still allocates the full struct).

### The three enforcement gates (all read the resolved profile)
1. **Palette** ([nodeValidation.ts](src/modeler/vpl/nodes/nodeValidation.ts) `isNodeAvailable`): hides a capability-off node from palette / quick-add / connection-drop (within the existing `bondGraph`+Agents-graph branch).
2. **Badge** (`detectCapabilityRequirements` → CaNode amber `!`): INFORMATIONAL in v1 (the compiler still emits unconditionally, so a placed violator keeps working; the badge guides the user). Covers macro internals via `countMacroSubgraphIssues`. Becomes BLOCKING from STEP 3.
3. **Ports/rows**: `BehaviourStepNode` `hiddenPorts` hides Radius/Area (Body) · Bond Degree (Bonds) · Age (Lifespan); the Properties [AgentCapabilitiesSection.tsx](src/modeler/panels/AgentCapabilitiesSection.tsx) preset picker + toggles + live footprint; SimulatorView's `agentEditPanelAttrs` + the inspector popover filter geometry rows to enabled capabilities.

### STEP 0 — shared layout-agnostic ABI descriptor ([src/modeler/vpl/compiler/agentAbi.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/agentAbi.ts))
The three CPU-side agent-ABI mirrors (compile.ts `buildAgentLoopParams`/`buildDivisionParams`/`buildAgentInitParams` NAME strings, the worker's `buildAgentLoopArgs`/`buildDivisionArgs`/`buildAgentInitArgs` VALUE arrays, the parity harness `buildArgs`) now ALL derive from ONE source — `deriveAgentAbi(kind, shape[, profile])`. Each field bundles its param NAME + a `get(store, rt)` value resolver, so name and value are defined together and the four sites **cannot desync in order** (the "3D dimsModel/total" desync class). The descriptor takes a lightweight `AgentAbiShape` (primitives — `is3d`/`agentAttrs`/`fieldAttrs`/`hasLookupTables`) so the worker (which keeps no model) derives it from its own state (`agentAbiShapeOfStore` + `agentAbiBaseRt`). `buildAgentAbiParams` (names) + `buildAgentAbiArgs` (values, used by BOTH worker + harness). An optional per-field `gate(profile)` is wired but a **no-op in STEP 0** — the descriptor is currently profile-unaware, so the output is byte-identical to the pre-refactor mirrors (this is the prerequisite that makes STEP 3+ field gating a one-place change). `is3dModelLike` (niCodec) — NOT `is3dModel` (compile.ts) — avoids a circular import.

### Verification (every SoA-touching step must re-pass these)
- `node scripts/parity-agent-wasm.mjs` — JS↔WASM 0 mismatches on all 9 agent samples (the harness now CONSUMES the shared `buildAgentAbiArgs`, so it verifies the loop-args path the worker uses).
- `node scripts/test-agent-abi.mjs` — proves `buildAgentAbiArgs` for loop/division/init is element-for-element identical to the old hand-written builders (2D/3D × ±lookup × ±hash); covers division+init, which parity never runs.
- `node scripts/audit-agent-layout.mjs` — the 4-site field-order audit (compile params === descriptor per kind; 2D a strict prefix of 3D; no dup names; valid cTypes). The cross-target SoA field-SET arm (CPU `AGENT_*_FIELDS` vs WebGPU `AGENT_GPU_*_FIELDS`) activates in STEP 3 when the layout becomes profile-gated.
- `node scripts/test-agent-capabilities.mjs` — 67 asserts (preset stability, Full≡Morphogenesis, migration never hides a used node on any shipped sample, gating, removal cascades, footprint ordering).
- Browser-verified: the Properties panel renders (Boids 141 B, Social Graph 125 B); Growing Tissue seeds (init) + grows 12→1500 agents over 203 steps (division + loop) with 0 errors — so all three descriptor-derived ABI paths run at runtime.

### STEP 3 — first real SoA gate: Bonds (SHIPPED)
The Bonds capability is AUTHORITATIVE for the ragged bond store. `resolveMaxBonds` ([centerBased.ts](src/model/centerBased.ts)) is profile-aware — `bonds === 'off'` ⇒ **0** regardless of the config's `maxBonds` ceiling, riding the already-tested maxBonds=0 code path (pure-force models). So a Boids/Chemotaxis/Ant model that never forms bonds no longer pays `28·maxBonds·maxAgents` for a store it never touches (~112 KB at 2000 agents), while a bonded tissue keeps its store. **Byte-identical output** for any bond-free model (the compiled per-agent code loops `b < bondCount[idx]` = 0 and never indexes the 0-length store). The GPU layout's maxBonds now also goes through `resolveMaxBonds` (was a direct read — the desync fix); the auto-bond scan is gated on `s.maxBonds > 0`; the load-state stride check (M1) rejects a mismatch only when the saved state HAS bonds. `scripts/test-bonds-allocation.mjs` asserts it. Verified: parity 0 mismatches; Boids on WebGPU (resolvedTarget=webgpu, effMaxBonds=0) flocks 0.999. Field coupling needs no SoA change (agentAccess already prunes the `_field_` signature). **The badge stays INFORMATIONAL** (a placed capability-off node still compiles as a no-op — making it blocking would error a leftover node that would work if the capability were re-enabled).

### Physics-capability engine wiring (Collision / Bonds=Physics / Growth — SHIPPED) — the honest-controls pass
The v1 milestone was "editor-surface only", but that left several EXPOSED capability MODES driving nothing in the engine — a **false choice** (the user-reported bug: a pure gas with **Collision = positional** but "Use bonding physics" OFF had its agents pass through each other, because the soft-sphere repulsion was gated on the coarse legacy `usesBondingPhysics` bundle). The fix DECOUPLES that bundle into per-capability engine resolvers in [centerBased.ts](src/model/centerBased.ts), each with a **legacy fallback so a profileless config is byte-identical**:
- **`usesEngineCollision(cfg)`** = `agentCapabilities ? collision !== 'off' : usesBondingPhysics(cfg)` → the soft-sphere **REPULSION** (volume exclusion). So Collision runs independently of bonding — a gas collides without cohesion/springs.
- **`usesEngineSprings(cfg)`** = `agentCapabilities ? bonds === 'physics' : usesBondingPhysics(cfg)` → the bond **SPRINGS** + the auto-bond scan. Makes the Bonds dropdown's **Data-vs-Physics a REAL distinction** (Data bonds are force-free connectivity edges; only Physics bonds spring). Previously Data and Physics unlocked the same nodes AND ran the same springs → a pure false choice.
- **`usesEngineGrowth(cfg)`** = `agentCapabilities ? growth : usesBondingPhysics(cfg)` → the growth **RAMP** (radius → targetRadius). So ticking Growth + placing Set Target Radius actually ramps (was a silent no-op without the legacy toggle).
- **Adhesion** (the free-agent cohesion `muA`) stays on `usesBondingPhysics` — it has no capability control (a numeric knob, not an exposed MODE).
- **All three targets:** JS `runAgentStep` gates springs on `springs`, growthRate on `usesEngineGrowth`; the WASM force pass adds a **`doSprings`** param (index 24, after `doCollision` at 23) gating the spring block — adhesion keeps `P.bonding`; growth rides the worker's `growthRate` arg (0 when the Growth capability is off, no bytecode change). The **WebGPU force pass has NO springs** (bonds are CPU-only on WebGPU — nothing to gate; it only got `doCollision`, correctly). `doCollision`/`doSprings` on WASM + `ForceControl.doCollision` on WebGPU were verified for ABI/slot consistency by adversarial review.
- **Byte-identity preservation:** `inferAgentProfile` widens `bonds→physics` (when `bonds !== 'off'` under `usesBondingPhysics`) and `growth→true` (when `growthRate > 0` under `usesBondingPhysics`), so a MIGRATED legacy bonding file reproduces its old spring/growth behaviour exactly (the resolvers read the SEEDED inferred profile after LOAD_MODEL). Verified (adversarial review): all 8 shipped agent models resolve collision/springs/growth to the SAME value the old `bonding` gate produced — or differ only where inert (no bonds → 0-length store → springs no-op; `growthRate === 0` → ramp no-op). The ONE non-byte-identical case (intended, matches no shipped model): a hand-constructed legacy file with the engine OFF + `growthRate > 0` + a Set Target Radius node used to freeze the ramp (a dead node); it now ramps — the previously-silent node starts working. Runtime: Growing Tissue still grows 12→768 with ~7260 bonds + the radius ramp; JS↔WASM force-pass parity ([scripts/parity-agent-force.mjs](scripts/parity-agent-force.mjs), 4 gate combos, 0 mismatches) + collision separates an overlapping blob 13×; WebGPU real-device shader compile (0 errors, 2D+3D) + end-to-end GPU dispatch (minPairDist 0.047→0.619 collision-on vs 0.047 off, matching JS/WASM exactly).

**`positional` collision — a REAL second model (see "Positional (hard) collision" below).** The honest-controls pass initially FOLDED `positional`→`soft` (it was a phantom — no distinct algorithm existed) and offered only Off / Volume exclusion. That fold was later REMOVED when positional was implemented for real: `computeCapabilityClosure` no longer collapses it, the dropdown restores **Off / Soft-sphere / Positional**, and `usesSoftCollision`/`usesPositionalCollision` gate the two distinct engine paths.

**Hidden dead rows (honest-core: never expose a toggle that unlocks nothing):** the Properties panel filters `HIDDEN_CAP_ROWS_V1` = { `populationBirth` (gates no dedicated node — the unified Create Agent / Add Agent To World spawning is always available in BOTH the Init Event and the Behaviour graph, ungated) }. **`orientation` is now UN-hidden** — it gates the FOV **`facing` heading source** (see "FOV facing heading source" below). Rows/schema/presets stay intact (a preset that sets them still matches; the footprint counts them); only the render is filtered — remove a key when its feature lands. Trimmed the Sensing description's FOV over-promise + rewrote the Motion segmented-control labels as the palette gate they are (the engine always integrates velocity in v1; a Static/Velocity integrator is the deferred STEP 6).

### Positional (hard) collision — a genuine second collision model (SHIPPED, all 3 targets, 2D+3D)
`Collision = positional` is a RIGID, no-overlap position-projection constraint — the distinct alternative to `soft` (the springy repulsion FORCE). Plan + illustrated mockup: [docs/PLAN_POSITIONAL_COLLISION.md](docs/PLAN_POSITIONAL_COLLISION.md)/`.html`.
- **Two real models now:** `soft` = a penalty force `μ_R·(d−s)` (transient overlap, non-penetrating only in the stiff limit — needs Motion=Force); `positional` = after integration, overlapping pairs are projected apart to EXACTLY touching (zero overlap, billiard-ball — works under any Motion since it edits positions). Adhesion/springs/growth orthogonal.
- **Algorithm** — `resolvePositionalCollisions` in [agentEngine.ts](src/simulator/engine/agentEngine.ts) (next to `buildSpatialHash`): a **Jacobi** position projection. Each of `positionalIterations` (config, default 2, live-tunable) sweeps reads the sweep-START positions, sums a **half-overlap push** `0.5·(s_ij−d)·(x_i−x_j)/d` per overlapping neighbour (torus-shortest, hash stencil + all-pairs), and applies all corrections at once → **order-INDEPENDENT** (identical across targets). Reuses the dead `forceX/Y[/Z]` buffers as the accumulator (**NO new per-agent SoA**); inlined interaction (V8-optimal, mirrors the force pass); the hash is rebuilt ONCE per step (sub-contact corrections rarely cross bins). A single sweep resolves an isolated pair exactly; dense packing converges over a few (the iteration knob).
- **CPU post-step on ALL targets** — the projection is target-independent CPU/JS, EXACTLY like the agent **structural phase** (bonds/division). ONE implementation, no WASM export + no GPU shader: called in `runAgentStep` between `swapPositions` and the structural phase (JS + WASM run the SAME fn over the wasmBacked memory VIEWS ⇒ **bit-identical**), and in `runAgentStepWebGPU` after `readbackAgentStep` (which already commits GPU positions to the CPU store — no extra readback; the next `uploadAgentSoA` returns the non-overlapping positions to the GPU). WebGPU's f32 force pass ⇒ f32-precision read-back positions ⇒ statistical parity (the documented WebGPU-agent stance, no worse than the CPU structural phase).
- **Gate change:** the soft-sphere repulsion moved `usesEngineCollision` → **`usesSoftCollision`** (`collision==='soft'`) at both force-pass sites, so a positional model runs the projection INSTEAD of the soft force. `collisionMode`/`usesSoftCollision`/`usesPositionalCollision` in [centerBased.ts](src/model/centerBased.ts) are the single source (legacy fallback `usesBondingPhysics ? 'soft' : 'off'`, never `positional`).
- **Byte-identical for shipped/legacy** — the inference only ever produces `soft`/`off` (never `positional`), and `usesSoftCollision` == the old `usesEngineCollision` for those. Only a hand-set `collision:'positional'` file changes (it used to fold to the soft force; now it runs the hard constraint — the intended fix). Verified: [scripts/test-positional-collision.mjs](scripts/test-positional-collision.mjs) (2D+3D torus/bounded resolve 0.01→1.0 exactly; wasmBacked bit-parity 0 mismatches; 0-iter no-op) + browser JS (off leaves overlap 0.7 vs positional→contact 2.0) + real-GPU WebGPU (routes to the webgpu target, 1.577→2.0, 0 errors). UI: the Collision dropdown restores Off / Soft-sphere / Positional + a Positional Iterations field (`AgentCapabilitiesSection`).

### Long-range CHARGE — the force that opens a grown graph (L1, SHIPPED; all 3 agent targets, 2D+3D)
The agent engine had **no force with reach beyond contact distance**, so any model whose bonds rest far past `sij = ri + rj` collapsed. **Measured** on K4 → 1200 nodes grown by triangle split through the real force loop: **99.2 % of nodes had an unrelated node inside contact distance** and unrelated nodes sat ~16× closer than bonded partners. The pair law repels only below `sij` (1.8 for `Cubic GRA`), **ATTRACTS** from there to `interactionRange × sij` (3.96), and is zero beyond — while bonds rest at 5. **Widening `interactionRange` does NOT help** (measured, row 3 of the sweep): it widens the *search*, not the force, and past `sij` the sign flips to adhesion. **This is not a tuning problem.** Design authority: [IMPACT_MAP_GRAPH_LAYOUT_CADENCE.md](docs/IMPACT_MAP_GRAPH_LAYOUT_CADENCE.md) · phase doc [HANDOFF_GLC_L1_CHARGE.md](docs/HANDOFF_GLC_L1_CHARGE.md).
- **The law**: `f_ij = k · (1/(1+d²) − 1/(1+maxDist²)) · (p_j − p_i)` for every pair within `chargeMaxDist`, **in addition to** soft-sphere + springs. `k < 0` repels. The `− min_c` term takes the force continuously to zero at the cutoff instead of stepping.
- **A FINITE cutoff suffices *at L1's measured scale*** (DC1): quality saturates by ~8× the bond rest length and an unbounded cutoff merely INFLATES the layout (bond 3.25× rest) without improving separation, so charge is **one extra term in the fused pair loop all targets already have**, reusing the existing uniform hash. ⚠️ **C10 MEASURED THE OPPOSITE AT SCALE and shipped the tree as an explicit option** — see "Charge RANGE" below. L1's sweep ran at N = 1200 in a very sparse 4000-wide world; in a world scaled to the POPULATION the cutoff law degrades as N grows while the tree does not, and at an 8×-rest cutoff the widened stencil is actually *slower* than the tree. Read the two together: a finite cutoff is right for a small or sparse model, the tree for a growing one.
- **Capability + config**: `AgentCapabilities.charge: 'off' | 'on'` (default **off**; `computeCapabilityClosure` requires `motion: 'force'`, and `applyCapabilityEdit` drops it when Motion falls below Force). `CenterBasedConfig.chargeStrength` (default −3) + `chargeMaxDist` (**absent ⇒ a DERIVED `8 × bondRestLength`**, DC6 — deliberately NOT a world-absolute constant). Resolvers in [centerBased.ts](src/model/centerBased.ts): `usesCharge` / `chargeStrengthOf` / `chargeMaxDistOf` / `chargeBinEdgeOf` / **`chargeParamsOf`** (the precomputed `{doCharge, chargeK, chargeMaxD2, chargeMinC}` — precomputing cutoff² + minC in ONE place, like `dtOverEta`, is what makes JS↔WASM bit-parity hold). `usesCharge` has **no legacy fallback** (charge is net-new, so a pre-L1 file can only resolve to off).
- **THE TRAP — the hash bin edge.** `binEdge = max(range·2·maxR, neighbourQueryRadius)`, and the force pass only ever sees pairs within ONE bin of its 3×3(×3) stencil. **`chargeMaxDist` MUST join that max** or every pair past one bin is invisible and the force is **silently truncated** — plausible-looking, wrong physics, no error anywhere. `chargeBinEdgeOf` (0 when off ⇒ the max is unchanged ⇒ byte-identical) joins it at all THREE hash sites: `runAgentStep`, the per-gen WebGPU `runAgentStepWebGPUInner`, and `computeResidentHashParams` (the resident batch). **Safe for the reserve by construction** — the reserve is computed from the SMALLEST edge and a LARGER edge yields FEWER bins; **`computeAgentMaxHashBins` must NOT be widened** (it is baked into the agent memory layout, so changing it would shift every offset past the hash region). The positional-collision projection keeps the NARROW `collisionBinEdge` (it only needs contact distance).
- **FOUR force surfaces, all of them** (the term goes in BEFORE the soft-sphere's own much-smaller `rmax` cutoff rejects the candidate — riding inside it would clip charge to the contact radius): **JS** [sim.worker.ts](src/simulator/engine/sim.worker.ts) — the SEPARATE verbatim **2D and 3D** arms × (stencil + all-pairs) = 4 sites; **WASM** [agentWasm/compile.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/agentWasm/compile.ts) `emitForcePass`; **WebGPU** [agentWebgpu/forcePass.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/agentWebgpu/forcePass.ts) canonical body; and **the B1 bin-sorted MIRROR body** in the same file — a term added to only one of the two GPU pipelines diverges *only* for models that engage the mirror. The shared `chargeTerm(is3d)` helper emits both GPU bodies so they cannot drift. Charge also joins every **scan gate** (`doScan = doForce || doDensity || doCharge`) — a pure charged gas has no soft-sphere, no springs and no density consumer, so without that the whole neighbour pass would be skipped.
- **The conditional-arity contract (WASM)**: the param list is part of the module's type section, so declaring charge params unconditionally would change EVERY agent model's bytes. `forcePassParamsFor(charge)` **appends** a 4-param block (`doCharge:i32, chargeK, chargeMaxD2, chargeMinC:f64` at indices 26-29) ONLY when `usesCharge`, so a charge-off module is byte-identical; indices 0..25 never shift. The worker **always passes all 30 args** — the WebAssembly JS API ignores arguments past a function's arity, which makes the dangerous direction (a module that DECLARES them while the worker omits them ⇒ `undefined` ⇒ NaN ⇒ poisoned forces) structurally impossible. **Asserted, not assumed** (`parity-agent-force.mjs` checks `forcePass.length` 26 vs 30 and calls the 26-param export with 30 args).
- **WebGPU gates at RUNTIME instead** (`fc.doCharge`): the shader text is not compile-identity-checked, the branch is on a uniform (perfectly coherent), and one shader then serves both states so toggling charge never rebuilds a pipeline. `ForceControl` grew 25 → 29 scalars; **`FORCE_CONTROL_BYTES` 112 → 128**. It is now **registered in [verify-render-uniform-layouts.mjs](scripts/verify-render-uniform-layouts.mjs)** — it had been excluded on the grounds that its members are "baked into the shader from the compiler's layout", which is true of the agent `Control` uniform but WRONG for `ForceControl`: a fixed hand-written WGSL field list in one file plus a hand-written table of LITERAL indices (`u[0]`, `fl[6]`, …) in another is exactly the drift pair that harness exists for, and it feeds BOTH GPU force pipelines. (Registry entries gained an optional `structFile` for the two-file case.)
- **Measured layout fix** ([scripts/probe-graph-layout.mjs](scripts/probe-graph-layout.mjs), now driving the **REAL** WASM force pass over a real `createAgentStore` — it used to carry its own copy of the force loop, which cannot gate the product): overlap **99.2 % → 0.2 %**, nnb/bond **0.18 → 0.81** at the default 8× cutoff. The probe now **asserts** this (including that the charge-off baseline is STILL jammed — if that stops failing, the probe has stopped measuring the bug) and exits non-zero.
- **3D costs several times more — keep the cutoff tighter there.** The stencil is a 3×3×3 VOLUME, so candidates grow with the CUBE of the cutoff. Measured on a uniform packing at spacing = rest: 2D 124 cand/agent (1.8 ms/tick) at 4× rest and 427 (5.4 ms) at 8×; **3D 813 (11.8 ms) at 4× and 1728 (23.8 ms) at 8×** — at 8× in 3D the stencil already covers the entire population, i.e. it degenerates to all-pairs with none of the extra quality. **Start 3D at ~4× the bond rest length.**
- **Verified**: 29 library models byte-identical; `parity-agent-force.mjs` **20 checks** (11 new charge combos — charge on/off × 2D/3D × torus/bounded × collision on/off × charge-only — all 0 JS↔WASM mismatches) + the arity contract + **the bin-edge trap test with a live negative control** (at 0.9× cutoff the widened edge feels the force while the pre-L1 edge reads exactly 0); real GPU — all 8 shader variants (2D/3D × mirror × scatter) compile 0 errors / 0 validation errors, a real dispatch matches the analytic force to 2.2e-8 (f32) and is exactly antisymmetric, and **the B1 mirror and canonical pipelines are BIT-IDENTICAL with charge on** (maxDiff 0 over 8 agents); a live in-browser A/B on the shipped `Cubic GRA` (WASM agent target, 240 generations, 0 worker/console errors) — overlap **99.8 % → 14.3 %**, nnb/bond **0.07 → 0.467**. **That residual 14.3 % is the SECOND, independent cause** the impact map identified (§1.4): at 2278 agents a 220×220 torus gives 4.6 units/agent against a bond rest of 5 — the world is SATURATED and no repulsion strength can open it. Enlarging/unbounding the sample worlds is **L3's** scope (DC7).
- **Negative-controlled**: dropping the `− chargeMinC` term from the WASM emit makes every charge parity combo fail (1500-3000 mismatches); dropping one charge write from `uploadAgentForceControl` makes the uniform harness report `unwritten: chargeMaxD2@108`.

### Charge RANGE: Cutoff | Global (deterministic Barnes–Hut) — C10 / P11a (branch `GRA`)

`CenterBasedConfig.chargeRange?: 'cutoff' | 'global'` (absent ⇒ `cutoff` ⇒ **byte-identical**, no migration) + `chargeTheta?` (default 0.9, clamped `[MIN_CHARGE_THETA 0.1, MAX_CHARGE_THETA 1.5]`). Phase spec [HANDOFF_CLARITY_SIMPLIFICATION.md](docs/HANDOFF_CLARITY_SIMPLIFICATION.md) §C10, implementing [PROPOSAL_CLARITY_SIMPLIFICATION.md](docs/PROPOSAL_CLARITY_SIMPLIFICATION.md) **P11 item 1**; impact map + plan [PLAN_CLARITY_C10.md](docs/PLAN_CLARITY_C10.md)/`.html`.

**This is a different LAW, not a speed-up of the same one.** `global` drops the cutoff entirely (`min_c = 0`) and sums **every** pair through a Barnes–Hut octree; a model that switches follows a different trajectory and its `.gcaproj` records the choice, exactly as changing any other physics parameter does.

- **Approximate ≠ nondeterministic.** Same positions ⇒ same Morton codes ⇒ same order-canonical traversal ⇒ **bit-identical forces** on the CPU engines, so a fixed seed still replays and an Overseer sweep still reproduces. θ changes *which* law you run, not whether it repeats.
- **GLOBAL TAKES AN OPTIONAL CUTOFF (a later follow-up, shipped).** `chargeMaxDist` under
  `chargeRange:'global'` truncates the tree sum exactly the way the reference implementation
  (`calcMultibodyForce`) does: the coefficient becomes `1/(1+l²) − 1/(1+R²)` so it reaches zero
  CONTINUOUSLY at `R`, and nodes / whole leaves / individual points beyond `R` are culled at the
  same NODE granularity the reference uses. **Why it matters:** the far field of N distant nodes
  sums to ≈ `N/l`, which GROWS with the population — so the un-cut law inflates a *growing* graph
  without bound. **`chargeGlobalMaxDistOf` resolves absent/0 to `Infinity`, deliberately**: `l² <
  Infinity` is always true and `1/(1+Infinity) = 0`, and `x − 0 === x` bit-exactly, so the culled
  arithmetic COLLAPSES to the un-culled one with no second code path and no cross-target drift.
  (Contrast `chargeMaxDistOf`, the CUTOFF law's resolver, which derives `8 × rest` when unset —
  global has no derived default because "every pair" is the law C10 shipped.) Per target: **JS**
  emits the cull unconditionally (behaviour-identical at Infinity); **WASM** gates it at COMPILE
  time on a finite cutoff (`allocLocal` + instructions change the bytes, so an un-cut global model
  stays byte-identical — the `chargeOn` precedent) and allocates its `mass` temporary only then;
  **WGSL** gates at RUNTIME on the uniform (its text is not identity-checked, and `chargeMaxD2`
  uploads as f32 `Infinity`). `chargeBinEdgeOf` is UNCHANGED — global still never widens the hash
  stencil, because the octree carries it. Covered by 8 new `parity-agent-force` combos
  (2D/3D × torus/bounded × tight/loose × θ) plus a VALUE invariant asserting a world-sized cutoff
  is INERT (1.0% off the un-cut law), a tight one CHANGES the answer (98%), the traversal tracks
  the TRUNCATED sum far better than the un-cut one (37% vs 99%), and the result is MONOTONE in R.
  **Negative-controlled by source mutation**: disabling the WASM cull emit fails all 8 combos.
- **THE BENCHMARK GATE decided this ships enabled, and it inverted L1's prediction.** [probe-graph-layout.mjs](scripts/probe-graph-layout.mjs) grows the GRA blob at N ≈ 2.5k / 5k / 20k in a world scaled to the population (`side = √(N·(rest·1.45)²)`), same ticks + seed + splits, and compares the tuned 8×-rest cutoff against θ = 0.9 global. Global wins on **every** axis at **every** size — and is **cheaper**:

  | N | nnb/bond (cutoff → global) | overlap % (cutoff → global) | ms/tick (cutoff → global) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 2 500 | 0.53 → **0.83** | 16.9 → **4.2** | 7.15 → **4.33** (0.61×) |
  | 5 000 | 0.47 → **0.82** | 37.9 → **4.9** | 22.43 → **13.77** (0.61×) |
  | 20 000 | 0.37 → **0.81** | 82.1 → **4.4** | 254.74 → **186.35** (0.73×) |

  **The SHAPE is the point**: the cutoff law DEGRADES as N grows (nnb/bond 0.53 → 0.37, overlap 17 % → 82 %) while global holds flat (0.83 → 0.81, ~4 %). A finite cutoff cannot open a graph that outgrows it, however it is tuned — which is exactly the "new capability, not a speedup" claim. It is *cheaper* because at an 8×-rest cutoff the bin edge IS the cutoff, so the 3×3 stencil sweeps a 120×120 area in a dense world while the tree stays O(N log N). Six gate assertions in the probe hold this permanently. (No shipped model is retuned — the shipped-configs-are-deliberate rule.)
- **THE SEAM: ONE TypeScript build, three traversals.** `buildAgentOctree` ([agentEngine.ts](src/simulator/engine/agentEngine.ts)) builds the tree once per generation into plain typed arrays; JS reads them directly, the WASM force pass reads a COPY at baked offsets in the shared agent memory, and WebGPU reads an upload. The BUILD is where two implementations would drift (bbox reduction, float→int quantization, sort tie-break, split order) and it runs once per generation; the TRAVERSAL is the hot part and is pure arithmetic over shared bytes — the shape the force pass already keeps bit-identical. Exactly the `buildSpatialHash` precedent (built in TS, copied into WASM memory, uploaded to the GPU).
- **Determinism rests on four STRUCTURAL facts** (not on care): Morton quantization is a pure function of the positions; **the sort is ORDER-CANONICAL** — a stable LSD radix (3 × 10-bit passes) seeded from an id-ordered array realises `(morton, id)` order with no comparator, so no sort algorithm can change it; the build is a deterministic DFS with a **node-count CAP that degrades a node to a LEAF** (a leaf is *more* exact, so the cap can never make a result wrong — only slower — and it bites in the same place every run); and the traversal is a fixed-order skip-link walk (`nodeI` ascending, leaf points in sorted order), so the f64 accumulation order matches on JS and WASM.
- **Layout**: `AgentLayoutExtras.chargeTreeNodes` (from the shared `agentOctreeNodeReserve(maxAgents)` = `maxAgents + 64`) reserves 10 regions appended AFTER every existing one — 3 sorted-position runs (`maxAgents` f64 each) + 7 node runs (cx/cy/cz/ext f64, start/end/next i32). **0 ⇒ zero bytes ⇒ every cutoff/off model's layout, and therefore its WASM bytes, is unchanged.** The WebGPU side puts the tree in its OWN two buffers (bindings **7**/**8**, declared only when nodes are reserved — the Naga stripped-binding discipline), so the agent SoA runs are untouched.
- **WASM conditional arity gains a THIRD value**: 26 (charge off) / 30 (cutoff) / **32** (global, appending `treeNodeCount:i32, chargeTheta2:f64`). `emitForcePass` emits the tree traversal **INSTEAD of** the pair term (never both — `chargeParamsOf.doCharge` is FALSE under global, which is what stops the force being counted twice). The worker always passes all 32; extras past a module's arity are ignored, so the dangerous direction stays structurally impossible.
- **`chargeBinEdgeOf` returns 0 under global** — the stencil carries no charge, so widening it would be pure cost (and in 3D the candidate count grows with the CUBE of the edge). `doScan` is unchanged in shape; global simply does not join it, so a pure global-charge gas skips the neighbour pass entirely.
- **f64 ASSOCIATION ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING — the parity harness caught a real bug here.** JS evaluates `1 + a + b [+ c]` strictly left-to-right; folding it as `1 + (a + b + c)` in the WASM emit diverges by an ULP that the integrator amplifies (it surfaced as 4 mismatches in **2D bounded** while torus and 3D happened not to). Any new emitted arithmetic must mirror the JS ASSOCIATION, not just the value.
- **GPU residency is a BLOCKER under global** (`residencyModelBlockers` key `chargeGlobal`): the tree is CPU-built per generation, which is precisely the per-generation CPU touch point residency exists to remove. Surfaced in C1's readout and C3's diagnostics. **A GPU tree BUILD is a recorded follow-up, not a hidden gap.**
- **Self-interaction is not excluded** (the reference behaviour): a node containing the agent can pass the θ test, because the centre of mass can sit up to ≈ `extent·√3` from a contained point. Leaf-level self is *exactly* zero (`d = 0 ⇒ c·d = 0`), so the error is confined to the far field — which is what θ names. θ is clamped rather than validated (it is part of a declared law a file records, so it must resolve, never throw).
- **The tree is 3D-native**; a 2D model is the `z = 0` slice, so the octree degenerates to a quadtree with a constant z bit-plane — ONE build path, no 2D special case.
- **Torus**: every delta (node COM and leaf point) takes the SAME minimum-image fold as every other engine force. A node straddling the seam has a large extent, so it fails θ and is descended to leaves where the fold is exact — it degrades gracefully rather than silently.
- **Verified**: 29 library models byte-identical on every surface; `parity-agent-force` **34 checks** (13 new global combos — 2D/3D × torus/bounded × θ 0.3/0.9/1.4 × collision on/off × global-only — all 0 JS↔WASM mismatches) plus the 32-param arity contract and a **VALUE invariant** proving the tree approximates the exact all-pairs sum (rel err **0.013 % at θ = 0.2** vs **3.76 % at θ = 1.4**, so θ genuinely controls accuracy — parity alone would pass a traversal that summed zero on both targets); `audit-agent-layout` **347 checks** (the tree regions on both targets, proven failable by a source mutation that overlaps two runs); real GPU — **all 12 force-shader variants compile 0 errors**, and a real dispatch matches the CPU traversal to **2.6e-6 max relative error** (mean 2.1e-7 — pure f32) with 0 validation errors; in-browser on a global-charge `Cubic GRA` (WASM agents): 6 → 26 agents over 120 generations, every agent moving, and the **cubic invariant intact (min deg = max deg = 3, E = 39 = 3N/2)**, 0 console errors; the Properties row flips Cutoff ⇄ Global bidirectionally, hiding the cutoff field under Global and swapping the C2 pipeline detail to `k = −10 · GLOBAL (Barnes–Hut θ = 0.9)`.

### STEP 5 — Get Age + Get Agents In View + Sense Hemifield (SHIPPED); Spawn / Orientation remaining
**Get Age** ([GetAgeNode.ts](src/modeler/vpl/nodes/GetAgeNode.ts)) is the Lifespan capability's palette node — reads `_agentAge[idx]` (a byte-clone of Get Radius; JS + WASM + WebGPU emitters, `NEVER_INVARIANT` + `NEVER_PURE`).

**Get Agents In View** (STEP 5b — [GetAgentsInViewNode.ts](src/modeler/vpl/nodes/GetAgentsInViewNode.ts)) is the directional-FOV node — the array of nearby agents inside a heading-relative **vision cone** (the Sensing capability's second node; it un-hid the Sensing FOV description). **Zero new SoA/ABI:** the cone test rides the SAME 3×3(×3) spatial-hash gather as Get Nearby Agents (`emitNearbyFill` on WASM + WebGPU was PARAMETERIZED with an optional cone, NOT cloned — getNearbyAgents keeps `cone=null` ⇒ byte-identical). Membership = `dot(heading, offset) ≥ cosHalf·|heading|·|offset|` (the division-free rearrangement of `cosA ≥ cosHalf`); `cosHalf = cos(halfAngle·π/180)` is a **compile-time literal** (`viewCosHalf`, no runtime `cos` ⇒ JS↔WASM bit-parity, no host-cos import); `|heading|²==0` (a still agent under the velocity source) ⇒ **omnidirectional** (the ÷0 guard); `halfAngle ≥ 180°` ⇒ an omni compile-time fast-path. Config: `halfAngle` (deg) + `headingSource` (**velocity** default / **wired** X/Y/Z — a `facing` source lands with Orientation, deferred to avoid an unbacked option). 2D + 3D (`hiddenPorts` hides the Z heading in 2D). **The 5 registration sites the parity harness caught** (the "half-wired feature" lesson): AGENT_WASM/WEBGPU_SUPPORTED_TYPES, AGENT_ARRAY_PRODUCERS (×both), the array-dispatch case, **AGENT_VALUE_NO_HOIST** (else the pre-emit tried to hoist it as a value → "unsupported value node"), and the **nearby scratch-slot budget** (else `slot·maxAgents·4` = `undefined·… = NaN` → `i32Const(NaN)` "leb128s: non-finite NaN"). Verified: JS 0-mismatch vs an independent cone calc (66% cull); JS↔WASM bit-parity ([scripts/parity-agent-wasm.mjs](scripts/parity-agent-wasm.mjs) `buildFOVModel` synthetic, 30 steps); WebGPU real-GPU shader compile (0 errors) + end-to-end (0 mismatch, 65% cull); Boids (getNearbyAgents on WebGPU) unregressed (polarization 0.998).

**Sense Hemifield** (STEP 5b — [SenseHemifieldNode.ts](src/modeler/vpl/nodes/SenseHemifieldNode.ts)) is the Braitenberg **LEFT / RIGHT** sensor — a MULTI-OUTPUT value node (`Left Count` + `Right Count`) that runs the SAME FOV-cone gather as Get Agents In View but, instead of an id array, SPLITS each in-view neighbour by the sign of the heading-relative **cross product** (steer by `Left − Right`). It carries `getAgentOffset`'s registration footprint (MULTI_OUTPUT_TYPES + NEVER_INVARIANT + the accessorCSE never-pure list + the asyncWriteHazard reader-seed/read-keys + AGENT_WASM/WEBGPU_SUPPORTED_TYPES + a value-emitter case on each compiler) **PLUS two id-ARRAY outputs, `Left Agents` / `Right Agents` — see the next bullet.** Reuses `viewCosHalf`/`viewHeadingExprs` from Get Agents In View so the cone math is IDENTICAL, and the WASM/WebGPU emitters reuse the SHARED `emitHashStencil`/`emitAllPairs` (no gather drift). The split: **2D** `cross = hx·dy − hy·dx`; **3D** `cross = det[heading, offset, up]` = `select(hx·dy − hy·dx, hz·dx − hx·dz, upY)` with `up = +Z` normally, swapped to `+Y` when the heading is near-vertical (`upY = hz² > 0.81·hm2`, computed once per agent — det[h,o,+Z] reduces to the 2D form). `cross ≥ 0` ⇒ LEFT (a deterministic tie toward Left); a zero heading ⇒ omnidirectional cone ⇒ all Left. Config `halfAngle` (default **90°** = a 180° front hemisphere) + `headingSource` (velocity/wired). Verified: **tsc**; **JS logic** ([scripts/test-hemifield-logic.mjs](scripts/test-hemifield-logic.mjs)) — 5 hand-verified + independent-re-implementation cases (2D omni / 2D cone-60 / heading-rotation / 3D up-swap / 3D no-swap), all L/R exact; **JS↔WASM bit-parity** ([scripts/parity-agent-wasm.mjs](scripts/parity-agent-wasm.mjs) `buildHemifieldModel` synthetic storing BOTH outputs so a L/R swap is caught, + all 8 samples unregressed); **WebGPU real-GPU** — 2D (no `select`) + 3D (`select` with the verified operand order) shaders compile with 0 device errors.

  - **The two id ARRAYS make it a CONDITIONAL array producer** (so a rule can ACT on a side, not merely measure it: `Left Agents` / `Right Agents` feed For Each In Array / Get Agents Attribute / Filter Agents / Aggregate). **THE COST RULE: only a CONSUMED array port costs anything** — an unconsumed side emits no declaration, no scratch, no push and (on WebGPU) no `var<function>` slot, so a counts-only graph compiles to EXACTLY the pre-arrays code on all three agent targets (`check-compile-identity`: 29 models byte-identical, incl. the shipped `Boids — Hemifield Vision`).
    - **ONE predicate decides it everywhere.** `hemifieldArraysUsed(nodeId, edges)` / `hemifieldArraySlotCount` (exported from [SenseHemifieldNode.ts](src/modeler/vpl/nodes/SenseHemifieldNode.ts)) derive consumption from the FLAT EDGE LIST — the one input every front-end AND every gate has — so the JS emit's injected `_leftAgentsUsed`/`_rightAgentsUsed` config flags (the `_indexesConnected` precedent, injected by `compileRoot`), the WASM/WebGPU emitters, the WebGPU array-producer BUDGET and the WebGPU slot ASSIGNMENT all get the same answer by construction. Both compilers stash the flat edges on their ctx (`ctx.flatEdges`) purely so the emitters can ask that same question from that same input.
    - **THE COUNT *IS* THE ARRAY INDEX AND THE LENGTH**: the push rides the SAME branch as the count bump and uses the count as its write index, so `leftAgents.length === leftCount` holds by construction and the arrays partition EXACTLY the set the counts count (asserted in both harnesses). On WebGPU the push is capped at `AGENT_GPU_ARRAY_CAP` like every other GPU array producer, so past the cap the ARRAY truncates (`len = min(count, cap)`) while the COUNT stays exact — the documented GPU capacity bound.
    - **SCRATCH BUDGET, per target.** **WASM**: the arrays ride the general per-agent BUMP-POINTER slab (`allocScratch`, capacity `highWater`) — the same region getBondedAgents / filterAgents / getAgentsAttribute use — so they do **NOT** consume one of the `AGENT_NEARBY_SCRATCH_SLOTS` (4) baked-offset buffers and the WASM capacity gate is unchanged. **WebGPU**: one `var<function>` slot per CONSUMED port (0/1/2, keyed `${nodeId}:${portId}`), counted into the `AGENT_WEBGPU_NEARBY_SLOTS` (6) budget by the SAME `hemifieldArraySlotCount` the slot assignment uses.
    - **Registration deltas beyond the ports**: `senseHemifield` joins `AGENT_ARRAY_PRODUCERS` on BOTH agent targets, but ONLY for its array ports — a new **`isAgentArrayPort(nodeType, portId)`** guard keeps its scalar `leftCount`/`rightCount` off the array path (without it, a count wired into an `isArray` input would silently resolve to the whole id array). It is added to the array DISPATCH (`compileArrayNode`) on both targets, to the WebGPU array-source EDGE gate, and — **per NODE, not per type** — to both `isHoistable` predicates: a hemifield with a WIRED array port is an array producer and must emit at its use site, while a counts-only one keeps hoisting exactly as before (which is what preserves byte-identity).
    - **Verified**: `test-hemifield-logic.mjs` (11 checks) asserts array MEMBERSHIP by a `Σ 2^id` bitmask against an independent re-implementation (2D omni / 2D cone-60 / heading rotation / 3D up-swap) plus `length === count`, disjointness, and that a counts-only node emits NO array machinery; the `[synthetic] Hemifield (L/R counts + both id ARRAYS)` parity entry sums each side's ids through a For Each + Local Variable and carries a VALUE invariant recomputing all six outputs independently (**negative-controlled**: an identical off-by-one on BOTH targets passes parity and is caught by the invariant). **Real worker, all three agent targets** (JS / WASM / WebGPU, 40 agents): counts, sums AND lengths match an independent recompute from the read-back positions with **0 of 40 agents disagreeing** and identical L/R totals (351/276) on all three; the WGSL compiles + dispatches on a real device with 0 errors and `agentEngineActive: 'webgpu'`, 0 fallback events.
    - **A pre-existing bug fixed in passing**: `test-hemifield-logic.mjs` was STALE and failed 5/5 on HEAD — its ABI shape omitted C9's `gates` (and the bond-attr / generation blocks), so its arg list declared 9 more fields than the compiler's param list and every later arg shifted (the documented `AgentAbiShape` mirror rule). It now builds the store WITH `resolveAgentFieldGates(model)` and passes the matching shape.

Catalogue → **118 selectable / 45 agent**.

### STEP 4 + STEP 6 — SHIPPED (C9, branch `GRA`): profile-gated SoA fields + the Static integrator

Both former "Deferred XL" items landed as Clarity phase **C9** ([HANDOFF_CLARITY_SIMPLIFICATION.md](docs/HANDOFF_CLARITY_SIMPLIFICATION.md) §C9, plan + impact map [docs/PLAN_CLARITY_C9.md](docs/PLAN_CLARITY_C9.md)). **[src/model/agentFieldGating.ts](src/model/agentFieldGating.ts) is the ONE source of truth** for both — `resolveAgentFieldGates(model)` (which optional fields exist) and `agentMotionMode` / `motionIntegrates` / `motionAppliesForces` / `motionModeCode` (whether the engine moves anything).

- **STEP 4 — the four optional field groups are gated by CAPABILITY *OR USAGE*.** `sprites` (`spriteIds`/`Frames`/`Speeds`/`Rotations`/`Scales`, **36 B/agent**; at C9 the only group with no baked byte on any target — it has since gained a WASM region so Set Agent Sprite can emit there, appended after every other region, so the gating argument is unchanged), `age` (8 B), `targetRadius` (8 B), `density` (8 B). **Measured on the shipped library: 24 B/agent of f64 reclaimed on 6 models, 16 B on 5, 8 B on 3** — plus the 5 dropped sprite ABI params on ALL 14 (no shipped agent model has sprites).
  - **THE SAFETY CATCH — ONE uniform representation: a dropped field is a ZERO-LENGTH typed array, never `undefined`.** On a zero-length `TypedArray` **`a[i] = v` is a silent no-op**, so every engine WRITE (`initAgentSlot`, `divideAgent`'s daughter seeding, `paintAgents`, and the serialize `copyInto`, which already clamps to `min(dst, src)`) needs **no guard at all**; only READS do. The three agent compilers therefore emit the typed default: JS via `ctx.agentGates` in the node emitters + the `behaviourStep.myAge` preamble; WASM via `ctx.layout.f64[f] === undefined` (`gatedF64Read`, with the write emits skipped); WebGPU via `hasF32` / `gatedF32` over `layout.f32Base`. Engine-side, `getAgentState` reports `?? 0`.
  - **THE GATE IS USAGE-WIDENED, never capability-only** — `hiddenPorts` + the palette gate are cosmetic (the badge is informational), so a placed `Get Age` keeps compiling with Lifespan off. `age` = `lifespan || getAge || a WIRED behaviourStep.myAge`; `targetRadius` = `growth || usesEngineGrowth(cfg) || setTargetRadius || setAgentRadius`; `density` = **deliberately the NEIGHBOUR-SCAN predicate** (`neighbourDensity || divideAgent || usesSoftCollision || usesBondingPhysics || usesCharge`), because that scan is the field's only writer, so density-off implies the scan never runs and nothing writes it on any target; `sprites` = `model.sprites.length > 0 || setAgentSprite`.
  - **THE LOCKSTEP — the gates decide BYTE OFFSETS, and the resolved record is SHIPPED, never recomputed.** `resolveAgentFieldGates(model)` rides the init/recompile message as `agentFieldGates` (the `agentBondReqSlots` precedent) into `createAgentStore({ fieldGates })` and onto `store.fieldGates`; `computeAgentMemoryLayout` reads it off `AgentLayoutExtras.fieldGates` (which `buildAgentLayoutExtras` fills from the same resolver). It is ALSO in `needsFullInit` — a gate change re-lays-out the SoA, so a soft recompile would leave the store one shape while the freshly compiled module bakes another.
  - **THE `AgentAbiShape` MIRROR RULE (a real desync this phase hit and fixed).** The gates ride `AgentAbiShape.gates`, so **EVERY shape builder must carry them** — `agentAbiShapeOf` (compile.ts), `agentAbiShapeOfStore` (the worker, which reads `s.fieldGates`), and the parity harness's `shape`. Missing it at ONE site makes the param list and the arg list describe different field sets and every later arg shifts: the worker's builder was missing `gates`, and Ant Necrophoresis' Agent Init Event died with *"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '0')"* — `_rngState` had shifted off the end of the arg list. **`audit-agent-layout` CANNOT catch this** (it compares compile's params to the descriptor using the SAME shape), so tier D of [scripts/test-c9-gates.mjs](scripts/test-c9-gates.mjs) pins it as a source invariant over all three sites.
  - **The WebGPU agent SoA layout is deliberately NOT gated** (only its emitters carry the safety catch). Its runs are a transient per-generation mirror re-uploaded from the CPU store, not where agents live; gating them would additionally touch the windowed upload/readback plan (`buildF32ReadPlan`, whose `compactBase` THROWS on an unplanned base) for no memory win. Flipping it on later is a layout-only change — the emitters are already ready.
- **STEP 6 — `Motion: Static | Velocity | Force` now drives the ENGINE, not just the palette.** `force` (the default and every legacy file) is the historical integrator byte-for-byte. `velocity` integrates `x += v` with the velocity the graph SET and seeds NO engine force (so `Set Velocity` genuinely coasts — under force mode a momentum-0 model wipes it the same step). `static` moves nothing: the force accumulation, the integrate block **and the position commit** are all skipped.
  - **THE HAZARD (and the reason the two are skipped TOGETHER):** `Ant Necrophoresis` SHIPS `motion: 'static'` and moves its ants with `Set Agent Position`. Skipping the force pass while KEEPING `swapPositions` would copy the stale `xNext` over `x` and revert every graph write — the Ant section above warned that the inert pass "MUST run" for exactly this reason. So: JS skips `swapPositions`; the per-gen WebGPU path refreshes `s.xNext` from the live `s.x` before the upload (making the readback commit an identity); and the resident `posCommit` is compiled for the mode — under Static it writes `xNext = x` instead of `x = xNext`.
  - **Per target**: JS gates both the 2D and 3D integrate arms plus the commit; **WASM emits one of three COMPILE-TIME variants** (`emitForcePass(..., motionMode)`) rather than taking a runtime param — the motion mode is a MODEL property that cannot change without a recompile, which is exactly the reasoning behind `forcePassParamsFor(chargeOn)`, and it adds no ABI slot; **WebGPU** gates at RUNTIME on a new `ForceControl.motionMode` field (appended last, `FORCE_CONTROL_BYTES` unchanged at 128 — the `doCharge` convention, since the shader text is not identity-checked).
  - **Only the `bonding` / `springs` / `doCollision` / `doCharge` resolvers are additionally `&& doForces`** — the capability closure already forces `motion: 'force'` for soft collision / physics bonds / charge, so this only bites a hand-edited profile.
  - **The C2 pipeline panel reads the mode**: `Reset force accumulators` is off unless Motion = Force, and `Integrate & commit positions` is off under Static with the detail *"nothing moves — positions change only when your graph writes them"* (Velocity shows `x += v`).
- **Gate**: [scripts/test-c9-gates.mjs](scripts/test-c9-gates.mjs) — **413 checks** in four tiers: the 16-combination gated layout matrix × 2D/3D (exact byte savings, exact ABI-name drops, 2D-still-a-prefix-of-3D, zero-length store arrays that swallow writes), the safety catch on JS + a real WASM module, motion-mode POSITIONS through the reference integrator (force moves / velocity coasts ignoring the force / static frozen AND a mid-step position write survives), and the shape-builder mirror rule. Negative-controlled by SOURCE MUTATION (disabling the layout skip gives 38 failures).

- **STEP 5** — DONE (Population.Birth spawning via the unified Create Agent / Add Agent To World; the FOV `facing` heading source + Orientation-row un-hide — see above). **STEP 4 + STEP 6 are DONE too (C9 — see the section above), so the whole Agent Capability Profiles milestone has shipped.** The one deliberate carve-out is the WebGPU agent SoA layout, which stays ungated (its emitters already carry the safety catch).

## Grid Init Event (global procedural seeding — all 3 targets)

A SECOND cell-grid init entry-point, the free-form GLOBAL counterpart to the per-cell Init Event — the exact analogue of the **Agent Init Event**. The per-cell `initEvent` runs once for EVERY lattice cell (the engine loop is the outer loop, so it can only answer "should THIS cell be seeded?"); the new **Grid Init Event** (`gridInit`) runs **EXACTLY ONCE**, so the user wires a Loop (or nested Loops) inside its DO chain and writes ARBITRARY cells with **Set Cell (at Position)** — imperative seeding the per-cell init can't express (place N random seeds, draw a line/shape, seed the middle box). Additive/opt-in: a model without a Grid Init Event is byte-identical.

### The two nodes ([GridInitEventNode.ts](src/modeler/vpl/nodes/GridInitEventNode.ts) + [SetCellAtPositionNode.ts](src/modeler/vpl/nodes/SetCellAtPositionNode.ts))
- **`gridInit`** ("Grid Init Event") — a white `event` root, SINGLETON (in `SINGLETON_NODE_TYPES`), in `MULTI_OUTPUT_TYPES` (its value-outs resolve via `_v<id>_<port>`). Value-outs: `width` (W), `height` (H), and `depth` (D, hidden in 2D via `hiddenPorts`/`is3dModelLike`) — so seeding is grid-size-independent (seed the middle at `width/2`). `compile()` returns `''` (root; the compiler emits the once-only function). It has NO "current cell", so per-cell reads (Get Cell Attribute / Get Cell Position — which need `idx`) don't apply here — a runtime `idx is not defined` surfaces via the worker if misused (same caveat as the Agent Init Event's per-agent readers).
- **`setCellAtPosition`** ("Set Cell (at Position)") — an `output` flow node: `x`/`y`/`z` (z hidden in 2D) + `value` (the type-adaptive widget — bool/tag/number by the chosen attribute's type, same `effectiveWidget` swap + attribute dropdown as Set Attribute) + config `attributeId`. Its `compile()` evaluates each coordinate ONCE into an int local (a wired getRandom source would else advance the RNG twice), bounds-checks against the grid, and writes `w_<attr>[idx]` — 2D `idx = _cy*W + _cx`, 3D `idx = _cz*W*H + _cy*W + _cx` (picked by `ctx.is3d`). Out-of-range positions are skipped. **JS-only emit** (see below).

### The design — JS-executed once, on EVERY compile target (the Agent Init Event precedent)
`gridInit` compiles to **ONE JS function executed once in the worker (`runGridInit`), regardless of the model's compile target** — exactly like `agentInit`/`divisionEvent` (JS-on-CPU while the behaviour runs on WASM/WebGPU). So there is **NO WASM/WebGPU emitter** for these two nodes and no `expandX`-style lowering, yet the feature works IDENTICALLY on JS/WASM/WebGPU because the WASM/WebGPU **step** compilers only walk the `step`/`initEvent`/mapping roots — they NEVER see `gridInit` (not a root they look for) or `setCellAtPosition` (only reachable from `gridInit`). The seeding is a one-time pass, so nothing is lost by not using WASM/WebGPU. **This satisfies the ALL-TARGET rule** — the feature runs on all three targets; it is not a JS-only clamp of a step-hot feature.
- **Compiler** ([compile.ts](src/modeler/vpl/compiler/compile.ts)): emits `gridInitCode` (the `CompileResult.gridInitCode` field) right after the per-cell `initCode`, using the SAME `omParams` signature (called with `buildLoopArgs()`, like `initFn`) — no loop wrapper. Order: scratch decls → Local Variables (`buildVariableJS(model.variables)` — the scalar `let`s + array fills run ONCE, so a counter persists across the user's Loop) → the `_v<id>_width/height/depth = W/H/D` preamble (emitted BEFORE `preLoopValueLines` so a loop-invariant `width/2` sees them) → `_rs` → value/flow lines.
- **Worker** ([sim.worker.ts](src/simulator/engine/sim.worker.ts)): `gridInitFn` (eval'd in `compileFns`, alongside `initFn`; `gridInitCode` rides `InitMsg`/`RecompileMsg`). `runGridInit()` runs on Reset AND first load, AFTER `runInit()` (so a global seed is the final word), gated on `gridCellsEnabled`. Buffer discipline mirrors `runInit`: it runs right after `resetGrid`/`initGrid` (so `readAttrs === attrsA`), sync mode seeds the write buffer from the read buffer, runs the fn (which writes specific `w_<attr>` cells), then copies write→read; async mode shares one buffer. Under WASM the `r_`/`w_` params are views over `wasmMemory`, so writes land in the right region and the WASM step reads them; under WebGPU **a gridInit model always takes the CPU init path**: `runInit`'s GPU-init shortcut AND the reset handler's `useGPUInit` are both gated on `gridInitFn === null` — the Grid Init's seed is CPU-written, so the CPU must be the init authority end-to-end (per-cell init runs via the JS `initFn`, gridInit seeds on top, then the reset handler's `!useGPUInit` branch uploads the COMPLETE state; the WebGPU-ready handler's `uploadAttrs` covers first load). Without that gate, a model with BOTH events (the Accretor: per-cell `border` + gridInit seed) dispatched the GPU init, skipped the upload, and the seed silently never reached the GPU — Reset showed nothing (a user-reported bug, fixed + verified: Accretor-on-WebGPU Reset seeds asym/sym + grows; Life3D's initEvent-only GPU-init path unregressed). `hadInit`/`loadHadInit` include `gridInitFn` so the post-init colour refresh fires.
- **Gating**: both nodes are in `LATTICE_ONLY_TYPES` (hidden on the Agents graph); `detectMissingConfig` badges `setCellAtPosition` without an attribute; Show Code adds a "Grid Init Event (global, runs once on Reset)" section.
- **Verified** end-to-end through the REAL worker (`getState`): a model seeding the middle (`width/2`,`height/2`[,`depth/2`]) + a Loop-drawn line via a Local-Variable counter produces the EXACT same cells on **JS / WASM / WebGPU × 2D / 3D** (all 6 combinations identical: 2D `[[0,0]..[4,0],[7,7]]`, 3D `[[0,0,0]..[0,0,4],[4,4,4]]`); Reset re-runs it (a painted stray cell is cleared, the seeds return); both nodes render in the Modeler; hidden on the Agents graph; tsc + `npm run build` clean.
